articles.title: 'Hey Copilot, Outlook.com isn't working. Can you fix that?': Microsoft shows off AI troubleshooting a Windows 11 PC — and the haters are out in force
articles.text:
Microsoft shows off Copilot troubleshooting Windows 11 — but this will be for Copilot+ PCs only (and here's why that's a good thing)
New video clip is our first glimpse of AI-based 'local PC diagnostics' in action
- Windows 11 is bringing in a feature for Copilot+ PCs that will troubleshoot problems
- We've heard about this before, but Microsoft has shown off a new demo of the feature working in a video clip
- Because it uses the NPU, this 'PC diagnostics' functionality can stay local, and not tap the cloud, which is good news from a privacy perspective — but doubters remain
Microsoft is working towards a world where if there's a problem with your Windows 11 PC, Copilot will be able to help solve it (or it'll try to, anyway).
Windows Central reports that Microsoft's Ignite conference is underway, and the company has written a blog post about 'Building Windows for the next era of work' that touches on a whole host of topics pertaining to AI and Copilot.
While aimed at the business world, the 'local PC diagnostics' capabilities of Copilot will be usable by consumers, at least if they own a Copilot+ PC, as this feature will run by locally leveraging the NPU (and not via the cloud).
We knew that this was what Microsoft had been angling towards, but the below YouTube clip is the first time we've seen Copilot in action troubleshooting a PC issue — in this case, a problem with Bluetooth headphones.
The user must give the AI permission to access files and read system information, and then it runs a scan on the system (with no changes being made) in an attempt to find the root of the problem.
This can be a multi-step query session (a running troubleshooting conversation) on alternative fixes if the initially proposed solution doesn't produce the goods.
As you may have seen, Microsoft is working on integrating Copilot with the Windows 11 search box (in the taskbar), albeit as an opt-in choice (it won't be on by default, in other words).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Alongside this, Microsoft has a plan for allowing Copilot to deal with files on your local drives, so you can ask the AI in natural language to find, copy or rename files and so on.
As Microsoft puts it: "Tidying a cluttered Downloads folder or pulling project files together takes a sentence."
It's hard to imagine how that might go wrong.
These features are "coming soon" for Copilot+ PCs, we're told.
Analysis: steering clear of the cloud — but not the broader risks that some fear
The idea of Copilot troubleshooting a PC has mainly provoked a mixture of mirth and cynicism on social media. It's worth bearing in mind, though, that you must give Copilot explicit permission to carry out these tasks — and it's also good that the work is done locally. This is because if the AI was carrying out these tasks in the cloud, that would raise concerns around privacy and where the various bits of system information that Copilot is using might end up.
As for that negative reaction, it includes comments from those on Reddit such as: "Hey Copilot, Outlook.com isn't working. Can you fix that?" (A reference to the recent huge Microsoft outage, of course).
Another Redditor jokes about the best possible fix they could envisage for Windows 11: "So it [Copilot] can remove itself?"
Even if the AI is working locally, and on a read-only basis – without any ability to change system settings, so it's just providing advice – there will continue to be Windows 11 users who don't want anything to do with Copilot on their PC. A lot of that is down to much broader trust issues relating to AI in general, but it's also about Microsoft's penchant for bugs (with its monthly updates) — the combination of which is enough to make some folks feel very uncomfortable.

articles.title: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Tuesday added a critical security flaw impacting Perforce Puppet, an enterprise infrastructure-as-code (IaC) and configuration management platform, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing reports of active exploitation.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS score: 9.4), is a case of deserialization of untrusted data that could result in remote code execution.
"Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Puppet's report-processing code that allows a client with any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type through a PUT request," CISA said.
"If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability."
The shortcoming impacts the following versions -
- Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.0 before 2026.0.1
- Puppet Enterprise 2025.0.0 before 2025.12.1
- Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.0 before 2023.8.13
- Puppet Core 9.0.0 before 9.1.3
- Puppet Core 8.x before 8.22.2
It was addressed by Perforce Software on November 3, 2026, in the following versions -
- Puppet Enterprise 2026.0.1 (Puppet Core 9.1.3)
- Puppet Enterprise 2025.12.1 (Puppet Core 8.22.2)
- Puppet Enterprise 2023.8.13 (Puppet Core 8.22.2)
- Puppet Core 9.1.3
- Puppet Core 8.22.2
It's worth noting that the issue also affects OpenVox, an open-source implementation of Puppet, and has been resolved in the following versions -
- OpenVox Agent 9.3.0 and 8.32.0
- OpenVox Server 9.2.0 and 8.18.0
Alain Rödel, a security researcher at Neodyme AG, has been credited with discovering and reporting CVE-2026-115731 along with CVE-2026-115732 (CVSS score: 9.0), a critical certificate-name authorization bypass affecting both Puppet and OpenVox. The issues were discovered with artificial intelligence (AI) assistance and precise steering, the German cybersecurity company added.
"The impact highly depends on the Puppet server configuration and the orchestration protocols used, if any are enabled at all," Neodyme said in a report published this month. "Independent of the configuration, an attacker with RCE on a Puppet server can grab the CA signing keys and impersonate other hosts."
"Puppet is a powerful software, often with full access to a fleet of systems in a corporate network. Remote Code Execution on such a central and important system can lead to worst-case scenarios: Deployment of ransomware, mass data exfiltration, and potentially lateral movement to other parts of the network."
As of writing, there are no details on how the vulnerability is being weaponized in the wild. However, a Reddit user named transdimensia noted in a November 4 post that it was being exploited shortly after public disclosure.
"After finding a severely misconfigured CA in my fleet, I traced the actions backwards on a [CVE-2026-]115731 intrusion," the user said.
Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are advised to apply the fixes by December 1, 2026, to secure their networks under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk.

articles.title: Comment libérer de l’espace sur son PC avec ChatGPT ou Claude
articles.text:
Avant de désinstaller un jeu ou de vous lancer dans le tri de vos photos, demandez à ChatGPT ou à Claude ce qui encombre votre PC. Sur le nôtre, une démo avait laissé à elle seule près de 60 Go de fichiers dont on pouvait se passer.
On sait assez bien ce qui prend de la place sur un PC qu’on vient de monter ou d’acheter. Quelques années et quelques dizaines d’installations plus tard, on a une idée beaucoup plus vague de ce qui se cache sur le SSD. Au moment de faire le ménage, c’est souvent un jeu qui en fait les frais, pour la simple raison qu’on sait où le trouver et combien sa désinstallation va rapporter. On pense moins volontiers aux fichiers qu’un logiciel a mis de côté pour gagner du temps la prochaine fois qu’on l’ouvrira. C’est pourtant là qu’on a fait la plus belle trouvaille de cet essai.
L’idée nous est venue en demandant à Hermes, notre agent IA, de regarder ce qui remplissait le disque. Il nous avait proposé plusieurs lots de fichiers à nettoyer, en expliquant pour chacun ce qu’on pouvait gagner et ce qu’on risquait de perdre. On a voulu voir si l’on pouvait obtenir le même coup de main avec ChatGPT, plus accessible qu’Hermes. Voici comment s’y prendre sous Windows, avec ChatGPT ou avec Claude, que votre PC soit équipé d’un SSD ou d’un disque dur.
Peut-on le faire avec un compte gratuit ?
Si vous utilisez ChatGPT, votre compte gratuit suffit. La petite différence avec vos conversations habituelles, c’est qu’il faut ouvrir l’application Windows et y choisir Codex pour que ChatGPT puisse examiner les dossiers de votre PC.
- Assistant IA extrêmement polyvalent
- Fonctionnalités gratuites nombreuses
- Automatisation de tâches complexes
Si vous préférez Claude, l’outil équivalent s’appelle Claude Code et demande au minimum un abonnement Claude Pro. Si vous avez déjà cet abonnement, suivez le parcours Claude ci-dessous. Sinon, le parcours ChatGPT vous évitera de payer pour cet essai.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace
Lancer l’analyse avec ChatGPT
Ouvrez ChatGPT pour Windows, choisissez Codex et démarrez une conversation sur votre ordinateur. Copiez-y le message proposé un peu plus bas. Si l’application vous demande l’autorisation de lire un dossier, regardez lequel et donnez votre accord au fur et à mesure. À ce stade, il s’agit simplement de faire le tour du propriétaire.
Lancer l’analyse avec Claude
Ouvrez Claude pour Windows et cliquez sur « Code » dans la colonne de gauche. Sous la zone où vous écrivez d’habitude, choisissez « Local », puis « Ouvrir un dossier ». Dans la fenêtre qui s’affiche, cliquez sur « Ce PC », puis sur le disque « C: ». C’est là que Claude fera ses recherches. Vous pouvez maintenant lui envoyer le même message qu’à ChatGPT. Le guide de Claude détaille cette étape si les boutons se présentent autrement chez vous.
Le message à copier pour savoir ce qui prend de la place
Avant de commencer, ouvrez l’Explorateur de fichiers de Windows et cliquez sur « Ce PC ». Sous le disque « C: », vous verrez combien de place il reste. Notez le chiffre ou faites une capture d’écran pour pouvoir comparer après le ménage. Dans le message ci-dessous, on laisse de côté les documents personnels et les dossiers synchronisés en ligne, comme OneDrive. Le nom et la taille des fichiers suffisent pour ce premier tri, et une partie des informations communiquées à l’IA peut être traitée en ligne.
Le prompt :
Analyse mon disque C: pour repérer ce qui prend de la place et ce qui pourrait être nettoyé. Pour l’instant, ne supprime, ne déplace et ne modifie rien. Mesure les volumes avec les outils locaux disponibles, sans installer de logiciel supplémentaire.
Présente les principaux dossiers et fichiers volumineux, puis propose des lots de nettoyage numérotés, classés par priorité selon la place récupérable et les conséquences de leur suppression. Pour chaque lot, précise les emplacements, la taille mesurée, l’utilité probable des fichiers et la méthode de nettoyage. Demande-moi si j’utilise encore les applications avant d’en proposer la désinstallation.
Appuie-toi sur les noms, tailles et dates sans ouvrir mes documents personnels. Laisse de côté les dossiers synchronisés avec le cloud et les fichiers uniquement en ligne. Ne propose aucune suppression manuelle des composants Windows, des pilotes, des sauvegardes ou des fichiers de récupération.
Indique les zones que tu n’as pas pu examiner et les mesures incertaines, sans compter deux fois le même espace. Termine par tes recommandations et attends que je choisisse les lots à nettoyer.
La première réponse peut réserver quelques surprises. Sur notre PC, Codex a repéré deux gros fichiers que Windows utilise pour compléter sa mémoire et pour retrouver notre session au réveil de l’ordinateur. Ensemble, ils pèsent près de 35 Go. Ils expliquent donc une bonne partie de l’espace occupé, et on les a laissés là où ils étaient. Si un nom vous laisse perplexe, c’est justement le moment de poser la question qui manque à une simple liste de fichiers : « Si j’efface celui-ci, qu’est-ce qui changera la prochaine fois que j’utiliserai mon PC ? »
Ce qu’on a supprimé, et ce qu’on a préféré garder
Chez nous, le choix a été vite fait pour Electric Dreams, une démo d’Epic. À elle seule, elle avait laissé près de 60 Go de cache, autrement dit des données que le logiciel garde sous la main pour éviter de refaire le même travail au prochain lancement. On a autorisé Codex à vider ce cache ainsi qu’un second, puis à effacer de vieux fichiers temporaires et des comptes rendus de plantage. En revanche, on a tiqué devant un nom que l’on reconnaît moins facilement dans une liste : LLVM. Après explication, il s’agissait d’outils de développement logiciel, qui pouvaient encore être utiles sur cette machine. Pour les quelque 3 Go en jeu, on les a gardés.
Dans notre essai, on a répondu : « tu peux nettoyer les lots 1, 3 et 4. » et nous avons demandé des précisions sur la nature de LLVM. Reprenez les numéros qui correspondent à votre propre liste. Si la liste contient une application que vous n’utilisez plus, désinstallez-la depuis les paramètres de Windows, ou demandez à l’agent de le faire pour vous. Pour ses propres fichiers, Windows propose aussi des recommandations de nettoyage dans Paramètres > Système > Stockage.
Et si vous en profitez pour mettre à la Corbeille quelques vieux téléchargements, pensez à vérifier son contenu avant de la vider. Tant que les fichiers y sont, ils prennent toujours la même place sur le PC.
Après le nettoyage, retournez dans « Ce PC » sur l’explorateur Windows et comparez l’espace libre avec votre premier relevé. Chez nous, Codex annonce 63,9 Gio récupérés, soit environ 69 Go pour les trois lots réunis. Le détail qu’on retiendra, c’est que près de 60 de ces 69 Go dormaient dans le cache d’une seule démo. On aurait pu passer un bon moment à trier nos photos avant d’arriver au même résultat !

articles.title: GTA 6 Reportedly Plays Best on PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S Struggles
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
GTA 6 Reportedly Plays Best on PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S Struggles
Digital Foundry has published its detailed platform comparison for GTA 6 based on over 100 hours of testing. Rockstar has officially confirmed that every console targets 30 FPS, and even the PS5 Pro misses out on a 40 FPS or 60 FPS mode. The PS5 Pro, PS5, and Xbox Series X all render at 1440p, but only the PS5 Pro reconstructs that into a 4K-like image using PSSR. The other two get a softer spatial upscale through Rockstar's own TAA. The Pro is also the only version with ray-traced shadows, while the other consoles have to make do with RT global illumination and RT reflections only. 
In DF's technical analysis, the PS5 Pro was able to hold 30 FPS across roughly 75 hours of play, briefly dropping to 24 FPS in scenes with intense explosions. The base PS5 and Xbox Series X bounce between 30 FPS and the high 20s during combat and fast traversal, but they can also dip into the low 20s in very intense scenes. DF notes that the Xbox Series X feels slightly smoother thanks to Xbox's 120 Hz VRR container. The PlayStation does not benefit from VRR at all, since it only kicks in above 48 FPS. Still, Digital Foundry's verdict is that both versions look and play well. Then there's the Xbox Series S…Xbox's "little brother" console is the hardest to recommend for Grand Theft Auto 6. It renders at 720p and uses FSR 4 to reach roughly 1080p, which also makes GTA 6 the first Xbox Series game to ship with that upscaler. As for the framerate, much of the game reportedly runs in the mid-to-high 20s, and heavy explosions can even pull it down to around 20 FPS. Some very specific scenes saw the Series S dip to the high teens momentarily. Visually, the lighting, reflections, shadows, and textures are all a step below the other consoles, and apparently pop-in is also an annoyance. PC players are still in the dark about when GTA 6 is coming to the platform, with the latest rumors pointing to a Q1 2027 window.

articles.title: “La demanda de IA está creciendo. Creo que la industria estará bien”: Sam Altman sobre la salida de Jensen Huang de Nvidia
articles.text:
Sam Altman, director ejecutivo de OpenAI, sostuvo que la salida de Jensen Huang como CEO de Nvidia no frenará el avance de la inteligencia artificial (IA). “Es difícil imaginar la revolución de la IA sin Jensen y la compañía que ha construido”, declaró Altman durante el evento Silicon Valley & The World.
Aun así, descartó que su salida provoque una alteración en el mercado: “Hay tanta demanda, y está tan claro que la IA es real y que la gente quiere usarla y que los ingresos y la demanda están creciendo con tanta fuerza, que creo que la industria estará bien”.
La renuncia de Huang como consejero delegado se produjo tras conocerse una relación extramatrimonial con una presunta espía china. El cofundador de Nvidia dejó el cargo en medio de una campaña pública que reclama su restitución y de cuestionamientos desde Washington sobre el futuro liderazgo de la empresa.
Qué relación hay entre Nvidia y OpenAI
Nvidia comprometió hasta 105.000 millones de dólares para respaldar el proyecto de centros de datos de OpenAI en Ohio, sumado a otros negocios compartidos. Esa relación convirtió la salida de Huang en un foco de inquietud para los mercados, ante la posibilidad de que se revisaran compromisos vinculados a la expansión de la inteligencia artificial.
Altman consideró que la dimensión de la empresa permite sostener sus garantías financieras incluso sin su fundador al mando. “Nvidia es una empresa gigantesca”, enfatizó. “Creo que la gente sigue confiando mucho en sus garantías”.
El dirigente de OpenAI definió a Huang como un “héroe” personal y señaló que “los héroes tienen defectos”. Su respaldo estuvo acompañado por una referencia a su propia destitución temporal al frente de OpenAI en 2023, experiencia por la que dijo sentir una profunda empatía hacia la situación de Huang.
Cuál ha sido la postura de otros líderes tecnológicos sobre el caso de Jensen Huang
La cautela de Altman contrasta con la posición de otros referentes tecnológicos. Elon Musk, director ejecutivo de SpaceX y Tesla, Tim Sweeney, director ejecutivo de Epic Games, y Garry Tan, presidente de Y Combinator, firmaron una carta abierta para pedir a la junta directiva de Nvidia que reincorpore a Huang como consejero delegado.
La petición reunió más de 165.000 firmas, incluidas las de más de 7.500 empleados de Nvidia, una cifra equivalente a más del 15% de la plantilla. Entre los adherentes figura Travis Kalanick, cofundador de Uber, quien escribió que Huang “erró, sí, errar es humano, pero no creo que nada de lo que hizo alcance el umbral para separarlo de su compañía”.
Qué presión hace Silicon Valley para la restitución de Jensen Huang en Nvidia
Un aliado de Huang confirmó a Financial Times que un grupo de ejecutivos de Silicon Valley organizó un “cuartel de guerra” para impulsar su regreso y reunir respaldo en la Casa Blanca.
“Todos los que importan en el sector tecnológico fuera de los laboratorios de vanguardia admiran a Jensen”, afirmó esa persona, quien añadió que el propio Huang respalda esas gestiones.
La posibilidad de un reintegro de Huang a Nvidia enfrenta resistencia dentro del Gobierno de Estados Unidos. El secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, pidió una “reorganización drástica” en la conducción de Nvidia y sostuvo que la compañía debería buscar a su próximo director fuera de la empresa.
Hace poco, Huang manifestó que estaría dispuesto a retomar el cargo si la junta directiva considera que esa decisión beneficia a los accionistas, los empleados, Nvidia y Estados Unidos. “Si el consejo considera que mi regreso beneficia a los accionistas, a los empleados, a la empresa y a Estados Unidos, me sentiría honrado de atender esa petición y volver a ejercer como director ejecutivo”, señaló.

articles.title: CISA Urges Immediate Patching of Java4Shell Flaw That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has urged organizations to immediately patch a newly disclosed critical security flaw impacting Oracle Java.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 (CVSS score: 8.1), refers to a case of out-of-bounds write that can lead to denial-of-service (DoS) or remote code execution under certain conditions.
"This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as 'Java4Shell,' affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which is part of the Java Development Kit (JDK)," CISA said. "Specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow for unauthenticated remote code execution."
Patches for the flaw have been released by Oracle and OpenJDK. As of writing, there is no evidence the vulnerability has been exploited in the wild.
As reported previously by The Hacker News, Java4Shell can enable attackers without an account to execute arbitrary code on Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate, and with a login on Apache Kafka Broker, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker, under default settings.
Advisories for the flaw have been released by numerous security and software vendors, including Aikido, Amazon Linux, Blackpoint Cyber, Chainguard, Cisco Talos, Cycode, Datadog, Dynatrace, Endor Labs, Field Effect, Hadrian, Horizon3.ai, Miggo, Orca Security, Qualys, Rapid7, Red Hat, SentinelOne, Sophos, Tanium, Tenable, Upwind, VulnCheck, watchTowr, and Wiz.
In an update shared on November 18, 2026, the Keycloak team said an instance can be considered at risk if the following conditions apply -
- It runs an unpatched OpenJDK build from 17.0.6 onward, including unpatched OpenJDK 21 and 25 builds
- Its x86-64 host or virtual machine exposes the avx512vbmi CPU feature to Java
- The running JVM has Base64 intrinsics enabled and has not been limited to AVX2 with -XX:UseAVX=2
"The x86-64 Keycloak container images tagged 26.8.2-1 and 26.8.2-2 bundle an affected OpenJDK 21.0.13 build," the team said. "These image tags alone do not establish whether your deployment is exploitable: check the CPU feature and effective JVM flags."
"A Keycloak ZIP or TAR.GZ distribution started directly on a host can also be affected; the conditions depend on its Java runtime and CPU, not on whether it runs in a container."
Keycloak is also recommending that users run the below command to check the CPU feature on a host or virtual machine -
grep -m1 '^flags' /proc/cpuinfo | grep -qw avx512vbmi && echo 'AVX-512 VBMI available'
If the output of the command returns nothing, it indicates that the CPU does not expose AVX-512 VBMI and is not known to be affected by the flaw. Keycloak has released temporary mitigations that users can apply until it releases updated Keycloak and Keycloak Operator container images once patched OpenJDK builds are available for them.
"The vulnerability could be reached through a local Spring Boot application using Spring Security," Blackpoint Cyber researchers Sam Decker and Nevan Beal said.
"In this environment, approximately 28,000 unauthenticated HTTP requests carrying a malformed Base64 authentication value caused the JVM to terminate after roughly 20 seconds of sustained requests. Additional testing confirmed corruption of nearby Java objects and changes to live application data without necessarily causing an immediate crash."
CISA is recommending that organizations take the following steps -
- Identify affected Java installations.
- Review software inventory for JDKs and Java runtimes, including those bundled with third-party applications or included in container images and appliances.
- Apply relevant Java and vendor patches as soon as they are available.
"If immediate patching is not feasible, implement temporary compensating controls, such as restricting and validating Base64 input at the application boundary, enforcing input-size limits, and limiting unauthenticated access," CISA said.

articles.title: Can a VPN help you play GTA VI early?
articles.text:
Can a VPN help you play GTA VI early? The truth about risky purchases, quicker downloads, and early access rumors
The latest Grand Theft Auto (GTA) is nearly out in the US and UK, and after a 13-year wait, hype is at its peak.
Several VPNs have used the excitement to promote themselves as 'gaming VPNs' — offering higher download speeds, less latency and even early access.
The issue is a VPN will not help you access GTA VI early. What's more, there are no online elements at launch that require the 'improved ping' some providers claim.
Not all the claims are bogus. Higher download speeds are a possibility, and VPNs can help protect you from fake storefronts or phishing traps.
Here's everything you need to know.
Will a VPN give me safer downloads and help avoid scams?
Yes, for some.
While console gamers only have hours to wait for GTA VI to arrive, PC gamers have a far longer wait before they can play. As a result, lots of fake storefronts offering 'early PC access' are cropping up, keen to take advantage of eager PC gamers.
According to Surfshark, over 200 new GTA-themed domains had emerged by August, with more than a quarter appearing to contain scam links. NordVPN also found a 'scam kit' listed on the dark web for just $200 that contains everything someone might need to earn money maliciously from the launch.
VPNs can help protect you from dangerous sites in several ways.
Many come equipped with malicious link blocking or scam detection features, which can warn you of threats before a site loads.
You can also use email alias tools — offered by the likes of Surfshark, Proton and ExpressVPN — to mask your real email address if you're asked to sign up to any sites you're unsure of.
However, email security may be the least of your concerns if you've just submitted your credit card details to a scam site.
As usual, the best thing to do is to use common sense when approaching any site advertising GTA VI access: does the price seem too good to be true? Is it offering access to something earlier than you expected?
If the answer to either of these questions is yes, then steer clear.
NordVPN Complete: the best GTA VI VPN plan
Was: $4.49/month
Now: $3.99/month
NordVPN's Complete plan is the best way to keep yourself safe when buying and playing the new Grand Theft Auto. It includes scam detection and identity defense tools such as dark web monitoring to keep you safe from scam sites. It also has protocols quick enough to keep your gaming smooth (but secure) once GTA Online launches in 2027. Try it risk-free with NordVPN's 30-day money-back guarantee.
Can a VPN help me get faster download speeds?
Possibly. 
Grand Theft Auto VI is over 200GB to install, so it naturally takes a long time to download.
Some Internet Service Providers (ISPs) throttle your connection to preserve capacity for others when they spot a large download or during peak times.
In these specific situations, a VPN can help because it means your ISP can't determine what you're doing online. However, this is only likely to work if your connection is being significantly impacted.
For normal use, a VPN actually slows your internet connection because of the encryption overhead.
So for most, the best option is just to connect your console to your router via an Ethernet cable instead.
Can a VPN help me get GTA VI early?
No.
While in the past you could trick your computer or console into thinking you were in New Zealand by editing your time zone or connecting to a VPN, this method doesn't work these days.
Major game stores like Steam, PlayStation Store and Microsoft Store lock accounts to a specific region when you sign up. So, if you originally signed up from the UK, it won't make a difference if you connect to a router running a VPN.
While some people online have suggested creating a New Zealand-based account, it's worth remembering that you'd be violating the service's Terms of Service and could lose access to the game as a result.
Will a VPN improve online play?
Not yet.
GTA VI online is not available at launch. However, once it arrives, a VPN can help in a couple of ways:
- DDoS attacks: Previous online modes from Rockstar have left users' IP addresses exposed, leaving them vulnerable to DDoS attacks. With a VPN connected, your real IP address is hidden, which keeps you protected.
- Routing stability: Playing with a VPN connected to a local server can also help streamline ISP peering and remove packet loss issues so you don't experience an unstable connection when you're online.
How to stay safe
Keeping your personal data safe in the run-up to the GTA VI launch comes down to common sense.
Don't click links without checking they're safe, don't sign up for websites making promises they can't keep and don't let your excitement cloud your judgment about any supposed 'discounts' or early access opportunities.
A VPN can offer a useful extra layer of protection. NordVPN, for example, includes malicious link blocking and scam detection, as well as dark web monitoring for all your personal details.
Combined, that's everything you need to stay safe against malicious GTA VI links, which is why it's my recommendation if you're considering a VPN for launch day.
By signing up now, you'll also be protected for GTA Online when it eventually launches. NordVPN offers the security you need to protect against DDoS attacks and has fast connections to ensure lag-free gaming.
While a VPN won't give you exclusive early access to GTA VI, or guarantee faster downloads, it does give you the peace of mind that you're not being scammed and added security for the future.

articles.title: Latest NVIDIA Drivers Might Cause Excessive SSD Writing
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
Latest NVIDIA Drivers Might Cause Excessive SSD Writing
NVIDIA's latest GeForce Game Ready GPU drivers are reportedly causing excessive SSD writing on multiple systems. Users have been reporting numbers of up to 30 GB per hour of SSD writes, even when no typical writing activity is occurring. With driver version 621.01 installed, the NVIDIA Display Container process recorded less than 2 MB of writes while the PC was idle. However, with the upgrade to the version 621.14, released on November 4, the same five-minute check resulted in approximately 515 MB of writes. Another report indicates write activity as high as 30 GB per hour with the newer 621.24 driver. Reports collected by TroubleGrid and posts on NVIDIA's forums point to a binary log named nvlog.nvlgstg, stored in the NVIDIA Corporation folder under C:\ProgramData.
While this may seem minor, it's important to remember that systems can run for extended periods, and the writing can accumulate over time, potentially leading to SSD wear and tear. SSD lifespan largely depends on its ability to endure constant random writes, and forcing random writes onto an SSD will undoubtedly shorten its lifecycle. This is particularly concerning given the high cost of NAND Flash, as users are operating expensive SSDs that could undergo unnecessary wear. Users monitoring the file found that NVDisplay.Container.exe seemed to rewrite it repeatedly. GeForce owners can check their systems by opening the Disk tab in Windows Resource Monitor and looking for NVDisplay.Container.exe under Disk Activity. Disabling recording and overlay features reduced activity in some cases. Below resource monitor is an image from Wccftech.Some users report that reverting to version 621.01 reduced idle writes. Others found temporary relief by stopping the NVIDIA Display Container LS service, deleting the log, and restarting the service. However, leaving the service disabled can interfere with the NVIDIA Control Panel and NVIDIA App. If readers recall, AMD had a similar issue a few days ago with Radeon drivers causing excessive SSD writing, which has been fixed in a subsequent optional driver update. NVIDIA will likely follow with taht idea, which means we are expecting a new driver update soon.
Sources:
				TroubleGrind, 				via VideoCardz, 				Wccftech

articles.title: Cómo limpiar la lavadora por dentro y qué partes debes revisar después de cada uso según los fabricantes
articles.text:
Limpiar la lavadora por dentro cada uno o dos meses, o después de unos 30 lavados, ayuda a eliminar residuos de detergente, humedad y pelusas que pueden afectar el lavado de la ropa.
Fabricantes como LG, Samsung y Whirlpool plantean esta frecuencia como una guía para conservar el equipo y prevenir problemas de olor, drenaje o acumulación de suciedad.
El mantenimiento no se limita a una limpieza programada. Después de cada uso, dejar la puerta abierta y retirar restos visibles de jabón o suavizante reduce la humedad dentro del tambor y evita que los residuos se adhieran a la goma, al dispensador o a los conductos. Estas acciones toman pocos minutos y ayudan a revisar el estado del aparato.
Los residuos se acumulan en partes que el ciclo de lavado no limpia
La lavadora usa agua y detergente para tratar las prendas, pero ese proceso no elimina todos los restos que quedan en el interior. Fibras textiles, suciedad, producto sobrante y humedad pueden concentrarse en áreas que no están a la vista.
Con el tiempo, esa mezcla puede provocar malos olores, manchas en la ropa, dificultades para evacuar el agua y obstrucciones. El problema suele aparecer en la junta de goma, el cajón del detergente y el filtro de drenaje, tres zonas que requieren revisiones regulares.
Si el equipo tarda más de lo habitual en desaguar, deja residuos sobre la ropa o mantiene un olor persistente, conviene comprobar estas partes. Una inspección antes de que el problema avance puede evitar que la suciedad afecte otros componentes internos.
La frecuencia también depende del uso. Una lavadora que funciona todos los días, recibe cargas grandes o lava prendas muy sucias requiere una limpieza más regular que otra utilizada de forma ocasional.
La limpieza mensual cobra importancia cuando se lava a diario
Los fabricantes citados recomiendan una limpieza completa cada uno o dos meses o tras cerca de 30 ciclos. Si la lavadora se usa a diario, es conveniente revisar tambor, dispensador y filtros al menos una vez al mes.
Algunos modelos incorporan programas específicos para limpiar el tambor. Otros requieren seleccionar un ciclo vacío con agua caliente. El manual del aparato indica cuál es el procedimiento adecuado y qué productos se pueden emplear sin afectar los materiales.
Antes de utilizar vinagre, bicarbonato o blanqueador, es necesario revisar las instrucciones del fabricante. Estos productos pueden servir para determinadas limpiezas, pero no deben aplicarse de la misma manera en todos los modelos ni sobre todas las superficies.
El exceso de detergente también incrementa la acumulación. Respetar la cantidad indicada para cada carga evita que una parte del producto termine adherida al tambor, a los conductos o al dispensador.
Cinco partes de la lavadora necesitan revisiones periódicas
La limpieza interior se concentra en zonas concretas. Estas son las principales:
- Cajón del detergente: debe extraerse y lavarse con agua caliente y jabón para vajilla. Un cepillo pequeño facilita retirar residuos adheridos. También es necesario limpiar el compartimento donde encaja.
- Filtro de drenaje: suele estar en la parte frontal inferior. Se debe abrir con precaución y limpiar bajo el grifo. Conviene colocar una toalla o un recipiente, ya que puede salir agua retenida.
- Tambor: se puede repasar con un paño de microfibra. Algunos ciclos vacíos con agua caliente ayudan a reducir residuos y olores.
- Junta de goma: requiere agua tibia y jabón, sobre todo en los pliegues. Allí se acumulan humedad, cabellos, pelusas y restos de producto.
- Mangueras y conexiones: deben revisarse para detectar fugas, desgaste o señales de deterioro.
El vinagre blanco puede utilizarse para limpiar el tambor, aunque conviene evitar su aplicación reiterada sobre la goma. El contacto frecuente con este producto puede acelerar el desgaste de la junta.
Qué hacer después de cada lavado para evitar humedad y moho
Los cuidados posteriores a cada ciclo complementan la limpieza mensual. Al terminar el lavado, es aconsejable dejar abierta la puerta para que el tambor se seque y circule el aire.
También conviene retirar de inmediato los restos de detergente o suavizante que queden visibles en el cajón. Si se endurecen, resultará más difícil quitarlos y pueden impedir el paso adecuado de los productos durante el siguiente ciclo.
Una rutina de mantenimiento no elimina todas las averías, pero permite detectar señales antes de que afecten el desagüe, la higiene o el rendimiento. Revisar el manual, ventilar el interior y limpiar las áreas donde se acumulan residuos ayuda a conservar la lavadora en condiciones adecuadas para el uso diario.

articles.title: Pourquoi GTA 6 tourne à 30 fps sur toutes les consoles, même sur PS5 Pro : les explications de Rockstar
articles.text:
Rockstar vient de répondre à la question que se posent les joueurs sur console : pourquoi GTA 6 reste verrouillé à 30 images par seconde sans mode intermédiaire à 40 fps ? Tout se jouerait notamment dans les 33 millisecondes dont dispose le moteur graphique pour calculer chaque image. Décryptage.
Inutile de chercher un mode Performance dans les réglages de GTA 6 à sa sortie. Le jeu arrive le 19 novembre avec un seul mode graphique et la même cadence cible sur toutes les consoles, de la Xbox Series S à la PS5 Pro, en passant par la Series X et la PS5. À la veille du lancement, Rockstar a expliqué à TechRadar pourquoi il s’en tenait à 30 images par seconde (fps), y compris face à l’option intermédiaire des 40 fps.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Ce que Rockstar fait de ses 33 millisecondes
À 30 fps, le jeu doit livrer une image toutes les 33,3 millisecondes. À 40 fps, il lui faudrait en produire une toutes les 25 ms. Dix images de plus chaque seconde, c’est un gain de fluidité à l’écran, mais aussi un quart de temps en moins dans le budget de calcul par image. Sur les consoles de cette génération, certains jeux proposent ce compromis entre un mode Qualité à 30 fps et un mode Performance à 60 fps. À 120 Hz, chaque image d’un jeu qui tourne à 40 fps reste affichée pendant exactement trois rafraîchissements.
Pour Jonathon Ashcroft, vice-président senior chargé de la technologie chez Rockstar, le calcul dépasse la seule qualité d’image. Le studio doit répartir le travail entre le processeur central et le processeur graphique pour simuler le monde et produire son rendu. Les différents systèmes du jeu interagissent en permanence, et le studio juge que le temps disponible à 30 fps lui permet de préserver l’équilibre entre la simulation, le rendu et le gameplay.
Marc Chambers, directeur de la production technologique, souligne de son côté que les outils et la technologie du jeu ont été développés en interne. Rockstar a ainsi pu les adapter à ce qu’il voulait faire de son monde ouvert.
Sur PS5 Pro, les améliorations portent sur le rendu
Les rumeurs d’un mode à 40 fps avaient entretenu l’espoir d’une option plus fluide sur les consoles les plus puissantes. La PS5 Pro conserve la même cadence cible que la PS5 avec toutefois des améliorations visuelles propres à la console. Sony annonce une image plus nette grâce au PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) et des ombres calculées en ray tracing.
Pour les joueurs, la régularité de cette cadence d’affichage comptera autant que le chiffre annoncé. C’est en traversant Vice City à toute blinde qu’on saura si ces 30 fps se font oublier.

articles.title: Attackers Compromise Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI Package to Steal Cloud Credentials
articles.text:
Threat actors have compromised Microsoft's agent-framework package to push a credential stealer, according to reports from Aikido, Chainguard, Endor Labs, OX Security, SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Google-owned Wiz.
The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published 33 minutes apart on November 17, 2026, and are designed to run a credential stealer on every Python start. As of writing, both the release versions have been quarantined on the Python Package Index (PyPI) repository. It's unclear how the attacker managed to obtain publishing access.
Agent-framework is the meta-package for Microsoft Agent Framework, an open-source framework for building and orchestrating artificial intelligence (AI) agents using Python.
"Both versions install Python startup hooks that silently collect credentials, environment data, and cloud identity tokens, then exfiltrate them to a webhook[.]site endpoint," Socket said in a report.
Once either of the versions is installed, the package drops a .pth file in the site-packages root directory, which then gets executed automatically on every interpreter start, causing the credential stealer to run whenever Python is started in an environment, even if the package is not explicitly imported.
"Each wheel adds a .pth file to site-packages," Endor Labs said. "Python executes import lines in .pth files on every interpreter start, so the stealer runs on any Python launch in an affected environment, including pip itself, whether or not anything imports Agent Framework."
The names of the .pth files are below -
- agent_framework_meta.pth in version 1.26.1
- af_runtime_diag.pth in version 1.26.2
The "agent_framework_meta.pth" file contains a single import statement referencing "agent_framework_meta," which then launches the stealer payload. It's capable of capturing the following data -
- Environment variables based on substring-based matching
- Credential files associated with Azure CLI (~/.azure/*.json), .npmrc, pip.conf, .netrc, .git-credentials, .docker/config.json, Hugging Face, Microsoft Azure DevOps agents, and .env and JSON files
- Azure DevOps OIDC tokens
- Azure managed-identity tokens
- Azure instance metadata and retains up to 8,000 characters of the response
"Besides reading credentials already on disk, the code asks the platform to issue new ones," SafeDep said. "Rotating stored secrets does not cover those."
"In an Azure DevOps pipeline, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN and SYSTEM_OIDCREQUESTURI are enough to request a federated token for api://AzureADTokenExchange. On Azure compute, it asks the managed identity endpoint for an access token to each of these resources. It uses IDENTITY_ENDPOINT or MSI_ENDPOINT on App Service and Functions, and 169.254.169[.]254 elsewhere. It also pulls instance metadata."
It's worth noting that the Azure instance metadata service (IMDS) is a RESTful web service that runs on a local IP address ("169.254.169[.]254"), and provides information about the virtual machine, its region, tags, and the identity token.
All the collected information is saved into a JSON document, zlib-compressed, Base64-encoded, and sent via an HTTPS POST request to a hard-coded URL ("webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb").
Version 1.26.2, on the other hand, imports a new top-level module, af_runtime_diag.py, collects GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, and expands the search patterns used for harvesting credential-related environment variables.
Given that the package attracts about 190,000 downloads a month, users are advised to perform the following steps -
- Isolate affected hosts and runners
- Pin the package to the most recent safe version (1.26.0) and restore from a clean environment
- Check for exposure to the malicious versions between 8:35 and roughly 9:20 p.m. UTC on November 17, 2026
- Search proxy and DNS logs for requests to webhook[.]site/d381fd80-ec62-42ad-8f5c-d1b15103c9bb
- Rotate exposed credentials from a clean system
- Audit Azure identities and review sign-in and activity logs
- Audit GitHub Actions workflows that deploy to Azure
"The malicious agent-framework shows how attackers are targeting the AI developer ecosystem and the CI pipelines behind it," OX Security said. "While directly targeting an official Microsoft package, it seems that attackers found a way to hijack the wheel creation flow to add malicious logic inside."
Agent-framework is the second Microsoft-related PyPI package to be compromised this year. In May 2026, the threat actors behind TeamPCP pushed three malicious versions of durabletask, Microsoft's Python client for the Durable Task workflow execution framework, to distribute the Mini Shai-Hulud worm.

articles.title: Tor hit by major DDoS attack, forced to release emergency update to users
articles.text:
Tor hit by major DDoS attack, forced to release emergency update to users
Users are reporting slow and unresponsive Tor networks
- The Tor Project releases urgent updates after large-scale DDoS attacks overwhelmed relay operators across the network
- Attackers flooded relays with circuit requests, causing resource exhaustion, degraded performance, and lost relay functionality
- Maintainers say the attacks are ongoing and adaptive, urging operators to upgrade immediately and watch for further fixes
The Tor Project seems to be experiencing major Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks which have gotten so disruptive that they forced the release of an update in order to address it.
Now, Tor Project says “most relay operators” were affected by an ongoing DDoS attack.
“This release comes in rapid response to the ongoing DDoS attack on the network, which has affected most relay operators,” the patch notes read. “This is not an easy problem to address, as relays across the network are being overwhelmed by a massive flood of client circuits. We are actively evaluating additional defenses and so expect further releases in the near future.”
Second patch
Tor is a privacy-focused network that routes internet traffic through multiple relays (servers operated by volunteers), allowing users to hide their identities and online activities. The relays work by receiving and forwarding encrypted traffic between users and other parts of the network, and are divided into three categories: Guard (or entry) relays (the first point of contact between a Tor user and the network), Middle relays (these pass traffic between them and add layers of separation), and Exit relays (these send traffic from the Tor network back to the regular internet and the user’s final destination).
The patch brings Tor to version 0.4.9.17 and includes a series of security fixes, including, according to the patch notes, one “especially important for relay DoS defenses related to IPv6 handling."
The project now urges relay operators to upgrade to the latest version as soon as possible, and to keep an eye out for additional updates. It did not share any details about the ongoing DDoS attack.
This doesn’t seem to be the first patch the Tor Project released in response to the DDoS attacks, either.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Approximately three weeks ago, Tor version 0.4.9.15 was introduced, also in response to attacks.
This version, however, seems not to have worked properly. “Tor relay operators are reporting renewed denial-of-service (DoS) attacks despite security mitigations introduced in Tor 0.4.9.15 on October 28,” a Reddit user said in a thread on “renewed DoS attacks”.. “On November 9, one operator reported that two relays lost their HSDir flags after attacks caused severe CPU and memory exhaustion. Another operator reported similar activity on November 10, including thousands of circuit creation requests per second.”
The operator said the reports suggest whoever is behind these attacks managed to bypass Tor’s recent protections. “The full scope of the attacks and their impact on the wider Tor network are not clear,” they said.
Reddit activity
Reddit has quite a few threads from different Tor users complaining about nodes being saturated and the network being slow or outright unresponsive. On November 9, a person on the Tor Project’s forum said the attacker “successfully stripped the HSDir flag from two [of their] relays” in a few hours, and that one attack saw “high asymmetric egress and one saw high asymmetric ingress (although not nearly as much as the old attacks).”
Both relays lost their HSDir flags as a result.
At press time, no threat actors claimed responsibility for the attacks, so we don’t know who they are or what their motives are. What we do know is that the attacks appear persistent and adaptive, and that relay operators reported multiple waves of attacks and changes in attack patterns.
Whether or not the latest patch finally addresses the attacks in full, remains to be seen. The project maintainers seem to be confident about it.
“Thank you to all… except our attacker(s),” they said in conclusion.

articles.title: NVIDIA ferme publiquement la porte à un retour de Jensen Huang
articles.text:
On parle beaucoup d'un potentiel retour de Jensen Huang à la tête de NVIDIA. Mais le conseil d'administration n'a clairement pas l'air très chaud pour cette possibilité !
L'énorme polémique autour de la liaison de Jensen Huang avec une femme qui pourrait être une espionne chinoise n'a pas été éteinte par sa démission. Car de nombreuses personnes au sein de NVIDIA, ainsi qu'à l'extérieur - à l'instar d'Elon Musk - poussent pour que le fondateur de la boîte reprenne son poste de PDG. Mais pour le moment, ça ne semble pas avoir d'effet sur la direction.
Le président du conseil d'administration de NVIDIA réfute publiquement la possibilité d'un retour de Jensen Huang
Jensen Huang aimerait pouvoir reprendre les rênes de NVIDIA. Mais le conseil d'administration n'est clairement pas très chaud pour cette option, comme nous l'apprend une information de Reuters.
D'après ce dernier, le président du conseil d'administration de NVIDIA, Harvey Jones, a ainsi déclaré que la société ne réengagerait pas Jensen Huang. Une communication qui a eu lieu ce mardi 17 novembre, à l'occasion d'une conférence téléphonique avec les investisseurs.
NVIDIA a engagé le cabinet Heidrick & Struggles pour trouver un nouveau PDG
Preuve de sa volonté de tourner définitivement la page, il a aussi indiqué durant la même conférence qu'il ne répondrait pas aux questions relatives à Jensen Huang. Pour lui, l'avenir se trouve ailleurs, et il l'a montré en se faisant accompagner durant cette intervention de la patronne par intérim Colette Kress et du vice-président et directeur général chargé du calcul hyperscale et haute performance, Ian Buck.
Pour ce qui est du futur patron, NVIDIA a fait appel au cabinet de recrutement de renommé mondial Heidrick & Struggles afin de trouver un remplacement à Jensen Huang. « Nous souhaitons nommer le PDG, le PDG permanent, dès que possible, mais nous ne précipiterons pas cette nomination avant d’avoir trouvé la personne idéale » a assuré Harvey Jones. Alors, la porte est-elle définitivement fermée ?
Source : Reuters

articles.title: Los siete fundadores de Anthropic que están a punto de volverse multimillonarios con la salida a bolsa de la empresa
articles.text:
Anthropic, la empresa de inteligencia artificial que desarrolla Claude, prevé debutar el jueves en el Nasdaq bajo el símbolo “ANT”. Según The Wall Street Journal, cada uno de sus siete cofundadores posee participaciones valuadas en torno a USD 18.000 millones, tras obtener USD 250 millones en ganancias.
La compañía se constituyó formalmente en enero de 2021, después de que un grupo de exintegrantes de OpenAI la abandonara en diciembre de 2020 ante diferencias sobre los riesgos del desarrollo acelerado de la inteligencia artificial. En menos de seis años, creció hasta convertirse en uno de los laboratorios más influyentes del sector.
Sus siete cofundadores son todos millennials e incluyen dos hermanos, tres doctores, un experiodista y un estudiante que abandonó la universidad, con intereses que van desde la biología hasta el punk rock y la teología.
Dario Amodei, el CEO con doctorado en biofísica que dejó OpenAI para fundar Anthropic
Dario Amodei, de 43 años y director ejecutivo de Anthropic, es doctor en biofísica y realizó estudios de posgrado en la Facultad de Medicina de Stanford con foco en oncología. Pasó por Baidu y Google antes de que Sam Altman lo reclutara para OpenAI en 2016.
Con el tiempo, ambos discreparon sobre los riesgos del desarrollo acelerado de la IA, lo que derivó en la salida de Amodei y en la fundación de Anthropic, según The Wall Street Journal.
Daniela Amodei, presidenta y directora de la junta que aprendió a negociar con su hermano desde la infancia
Daniela Amodei, de 39 años y presidenta de Anthropic, estudió literatura en la Universidad de California en Santa Cruz y trabajó en política y en Stripe antes de sumarse a OpenAI, donde se desempeñó en gestión y como vicepresidenta de Seguridad y Políticas.
Hoy encabeza el enfoque en seguridad de la empresa, con especial énfasis en evitar que sus sistemas sean utilizados para desarrollar armas químicas o biológicas, según el diario.
Christopher Olah y la interpretabilidad: entender qué ocurre dentro de los modelos de IA de “caja negra”
Christopher Olah, de 34 años, lidera la investigación sobre interpretabilidad, la disciplina que busca comprender por qué los sistemas de IA —llamados de “caja negra” por la opacidad de sus procesos internos— funcionan de determinada manera. Abandonó la universidad sin graduarse y se convirtió en una referencia del campo.
Su trabajo lo llevó a organizar encuentros con líderes religiosos para debatir la posibilidad de que los sistemas de IA tengan alguna forma de conciencia, y a reunirse con el papa León XIV, quien advirtió que la tecnología podría generar nuevas formas de esclavitud.
Tom Brown, el arquitecto de acuerdos que conecta a Anthropic con el Pentágono y Silicon Valley
Tom Brown, de 39 años y director de computación de Anthropic, es graduado del MIT y codesarrolló junto a Dario Amodei uno de los conceptos técnicos que permite a los sistemas de IA comunicarse de forma conversacional. Su rol actual abarca la negociación de acuerdos de chips, la representación informal de la empresa en Washington y el manejo de vínculos institucionales delicados.
Según el diario, aprovechó su afiliación republicana para desactivar tensiones con la administración Trump y negoció directamente con el Pentágono para evitar que Anthropic quedara excluida del mercado estadounidense.
Jack Clark, el experiodista de tecnología que hoy define la política de IA en el Instituto Anthropic
Jack Clark, de 38 años, llegó a la inteligencia artificial desde el periodismo: fue reportero de tecnología en Bloomberg Businessweek antes de trabajar en comunicaciones de OpenAI y luego dirigir las políticas de Anthropic.
Hoy encabeza el Instituto Anthropic, un centro de estudios dedicado a comprender las consecuencias de los sistemas de IA potentes. Según The Wall Street Journal, Clark definió su posición con claridad en una conferencia en Bangkok: “la singularidad ya está aquí”.
Jared Kaplan, el físico de Harvard que escribió las leyes que gobiernan el crecimiento de los modelos de IA
Jared Kaplan, de 42 años y director científico de Anthropic, es físico teórico y docente en la Universidad Johns Hopkins desde 2012, donde sus intereses de investigación van de la gravedad cuántica al aprendizaje automático. Estudió física y matemáticas en Stanford antes de doctorarse en física en Harvard.
En 2019, como consultor de OpenAI, coautoró “Leyes de escalado para modelos de lenguaje neuronal”, artículo de referencia que establece cómo la capacidad de procesamiento, los datos de entrenamiento y las variables matemáticas de un modelo influyen en el desempeño de un sistema de IA: a mayor tamaño y entrenamiento, mejores resultados.
En Anthropic, Kaplan amplió este trabajo y desarrolló formas de gobernar sistemas de IA con una “constitución”: reglas predefinidas que orientan el comportamiento del modelo y limitan respuestas para evitar que se descontrolen.
Sam McCandlish, el arquitecto jefe que define los parámetros de los nuevos modelos de Claude
Sam McCandlish, de 36 años y arquitecto jefe de Anthropic, supervisa el desarrollo de los parámetros de los nuevos modelos: las variables matemáticas internas que determinan cómo aprende y responde un sistema de IA.
Doctor en física por Stanford, comparte con Kaplan la autoría del artículo sobre las leyes de escalado. Su trabajo define el núcleo técnico de cada nueva versión de Claude, según el diario.

articles.title: Typing 365 Turns PC Building, Technology and More into Typing Practice
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
Typing 365 Turns PC Building, Technology and More into Typing Practice
Typing faster is useful, but what if practice could also teach you something? Typing 365 is a free native Windows app that combines structured typing lessons, educational content, and competitive challenges.
With over 100,000 installs and nearly 4 million typing races completed worldwide, Typing 365 has grown into more than a speed test. Its Albums Store offers themed collections covering technology, science, history, psychology, and more.Build Your PC: A Free Album for First-Time Builders
The new Build Your PC album features 40 free typing exercises about desktop hardware. It covers motherboards, component compatibility, assembly, first boot, operating system installation, and troubleshooting.
Here's the idea in practice: instead of just reading a guide, you type passages such as "Before buying a CPU, check that its socket matches your motherboard and that the board's BIOS supports it." By the end of the album, you've practiced thousands of keystrokes while picking up the fundamentals of building a PC.
You might already know your way around a PC case, but it's an easy recommendation for students, first-time builders, or that friend whose build you always end up helping with.
Why a Native Windows App?
Browser-based typing sites are great for a quick test. Typing 365 is designed for consistent practice, combining a dedicated Windows experience with structured courses, progress tracking, and detailed performance statistics.
Beginners can start with Typing 101, a free course that gradually introduces keys before moving on to complete sentences. Other courses cover keyboard rows, punctuation, and speed development.
During practice, an on-screen keyboard and optional hand guidance support finger placement. The app tracks words per minute (WPM), characters per minute (CPM), accuracy, and mistakes. You can also turn your own notes or technical material into typing exercises.Find Your Weak Spots with PRO Analytics
The free app offers plenty of practice material, while Typing 365 PRO adds detailed analytics for users who want to improve their skills. View speed trends, session history, and keyboard heatmaps, or identify slow words, characters, and letter pairs for targeted practice.
PRO also unlocks exclusive albums, advanced courses such as Typing 102, which focuses on building typing speed, plus additional fonts, keyboard sounds, avatars, and customization options.
PRO is available through a monthly subscription or a one-time lifetime purchase, with US pricing starting at $2.99/month or $29.99 lifetime. Prices may vary by region.
Race Against Other Typists
Prefer competition? Join ranked typing races, compare your results with other players, and climb the global leaderboards. Whether you're chasing a personal best or a higher rank, every race offers a new challenge.
Practice in Five Languages
Typing 365 supports English, German, Spanish, Russian, and Arabic, allowing users to practice across languages and keyboard layouts.
From learning keyboard basics to understanding how a PC comes together, Typing 365 turns everyday practice into something worth your time.
Download Typing 365 for free from the Microsoft Store and start typing.
Typing 365 is available for Windows PCs, with optional premium albums and PRO features.

articles.title: Russian COLD RELIC Hackers Use Stolen Google Workspace Data to Breach Second U.S. Organization
articles.text:
The Russia-linked cyber espionage group known as Cold Relic (formerly COLDRIVER and UNC4057) has been observed weaponizing a single cloud compromise into a launchpad for a series of linked intrusions resulting in third-party compromise.
Google's Mandiant and Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said it investigated a 2026 compromise at a U.S.-based organization in which the adversary leveraged data, the corporate staff directory, and identities harvested from an earlier attack on another U.S.-based entity in late 2025.
Cold Relic, also tracked as Callisto, Gossamer Bear, and Star Blizzard, has a track record of orchestrating sophisticated phishing and malware campaigns to gain access information that may be of strategic importance to the Russian government.
The access is abused to register rogue multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices, passkeys, and MFA backup codes to establish long-term persistence and then conduct aggressive data collection and exfiltration operations targeting email, chat, and cloud storage repositories. In addition, the compromised access is used to target the victim's social and professional networks.
Attacks mounted by the threat actor have successfully compromised high-value targets, including government officials, defense contractors, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) across Europe and North America.
"Once Cold Relic compromises a target, it uses stolen emails and data to establish authentic pretexts and impersonate contacts when reaching out to subsequent targets," Google said.
According to the tech giant's cybersecurity and incident response teams, Cold Relic compromised the cloud productivity environment of an unspecified U.S.-based organization in late 2025. Initial access to the network was achieved by means of a residential proxy network located in close geographical proximity to the victim.
Using the stolen credentials of a Super Admin account and combining it with an MFA push notification fatigue attack, the threat actor is said to have gained access to the account after the victim accepted an MFA request. This was followed by the attacker registering their own device within the tenant to retain access. The threat actor was also observed using passkeys and MFA backup codes as alternate access mechanisms.
"Cold Relic used the privileges of the compromised Super Admin account to download the contents of the entire organization's cloud storage drive by both mass sharing files to a Cold Relic-operated email account and downloading files directly," Google explained.
"While operating inside the tenant of the victim organization, Cold Relic accessed the Admin Console, queried Admin security investigation and email audit logs to check defensive visibility, and viewed, modified, and deleted Alert Center notifications to remove forensic evidence of the initial intrusion."
These actions ultimately enabled the threat actor to export full employee lists and domain-wide data via the Google Takeout service using the Super Admin privileges. Following mass data theft, the attackers continued to maintain access over several months and perform additional activities -
- Sync email inbox via OAuth to external email clients.
- Re-authenticate using unrevoked attacker-enrolled passkeys that persisted across password and session resets and bypassed device registration controls.
- Target cloud drive document access related to credentials, email archives, personnel information, and other documents of interest.
Even after the attackers were ousted from the victim organization, Google said it observed Cold Relic using email accounts impersonating employees of the victim organization to target both internal employees and associates within the same professional circles as part of a renewed social engineering campaign.
The attack then moved to the next phase when the threat actor compromised a Microsoft Entra ID user account of a second U.S.-based organization that used Entra ID as its federated single sign-on (SSO) identity provider for Google Workspace.
By impersonating an employee at the first organization, the threat actor established communications with the target over a secure messaging app and then shared phishing links designed to harvest credentials and authentication tokens for Entra ID under the pretext of sharing a document containing details about a technical issue.
"Upon successful authentication using the stolen credentials, Cold Relic registered and used a new MFA device in the SSO solution to retain access to the user account throughout the intrusion," Google said.
"By impersonating someone known in the same professional circles as the new target, Cold Relic increased their chance of phishing success. Ultimately, in this case, Cold Relic was able to obtain credentials to the organization and perform bulk download of files accessible in the compromised user's cloud drive."
Upon successfully compromising the second organization, the messaging app account used to initiate the conversation had its profile name changed to a different persona. It's suspected that the new persona was likely used to target other organizations in the same professional network.
"Cold Relic's campaigns demonstrate the convergence of human-centric social engineering and cloud identity abuse," Google said. "By obtaining access to strategic personnel rosters and operational documents, Russian intelligence services turn legitimate business communications into attack vectors against trusted partners."

articles.title: Microsoft Defender va pouvoir protéger les systèmes vulnérables sans attendre l'installation d'un correctif
articles.text:
Microsoft présente Vulnerability Shielding, une nouvelle fonction de Defender capable d'appliquer des protections temporaires aux systèmes exposés à des failles de sécurité. En cas d'attaque, elle pourra même intervenir automatiquement pour couper la route aux pirates.
Les cybercriminels n'attendent pas que les entreprises aient terminé leurs mises à jour pour exploiter une faille de sécurité. Entre la publication d'un patch et son installation, plusieurs jours peuvent s'écouler, le temps de vérifier sa compatibilité avec les logiciels existants et d'organiser son déploiement sans perturber l'activité. Un délai dont les pirates savent profiter, et pendant lequel Microsoft entend désormais protéger les systèmes vulnérables grâce à Vulnerability Shielding, une nouvelle fonction de Defender présentée à l'occasion de l'Ignite 2026.
Faire barrage aux pirates sans corriger la faille
Plutôt que de laisser les machines exposées jusqu'à l'installation d'une mise à jour, Microsoft propose de leur appliquer des protections provisoires, adaptées à la vulnérabilité concernée. Pour cela, Vulnerability Shielding s'appuie sur l'intelligence artificielle et les données de sécurité de Defender pour identifier les failles exploitables, examiner la configuration des systèmes et déterminer comment empêcher les pirates d'en tirer parti.
Dans les faits, l'outil pourra restreindre les communications réseau, bloquer des chemins d'accès ou limiter certaines autorisations pour empêcher l'exploitation d'une vulnérabilité, tout en cherchant à préserver le fonctionnement des applications. Il ne s'agit donc pas de corriger la faille elle-même, mais de rendre son exploitation plus difficile en attendant l'installation du patch définitif.
Cette protection préventive s'appuie sur le Risk Reduction Agent de Microsoft Perception, chargé d'établir un plan d'action tenant compte des risques et des contraintes de l'entreprise. Pour aider les administrateurs à prendre leur décision, l'agent simulera les conséquences des protections envisagées à partir de 90 jours d'activité réelle. Aucune mesure ne sera appliquée sans leur validation.
En cas d'attaque, Defender pourra intervenir de lui-même
Mais Vulnerability Shielding ne se limitera pas à anticiper les attaques. La nouvelle fonction vient également renforcer Attack Disruption, le dispositif de Defender capable de détecter et d'interrompre automatiquement des intrusions en cours. Lorsqu'une attaque sera repérée, il pourra appliquer de lui-même des protections temporaires aux systèmes vulnérables.
L'objectif sera alors de bloquer les accès exploités par les pirates, mais aussi de leur fermer d'autres voies susceptibles de leur permettre de progresser dans le réseau. Pour choisir les restrictions à appliquer, Defender tiendra compte des vulnérabilités connues, des techniques d'attaque observées et des usages habituels des systèmes concernés, afin de préserver autant que possible les activités légitimes.
Ces protections auront vocation à rester temporaires. Une fois le correctif définitif installé, elles seront retirées automatiquement. Les administrateurs pourront également consulter les restrictions appliquées, exclure des appareils ou des applications et revenir sur une décision si nécessaire.
Vulnerability Shielding arrive en préversion publique, avec une première prise en charge des failles permettant l'exécution de code à distance sur les serveurs pour son volet préventif. La nouveauté s'adresse aux entreprises équipées des solutions de sécurité professionnelles de Microsoft, et non aux particuliers utilisant simplement l'antivirus intégré à Windows.
- Moteur de détection de dernière génération efficace et discret
- Intégration dans Windows 10 et Windows 11
- Pare-feu

articles.title: GTA 6 dev speaks on building a modern game while balancing Vice City’s nostalgic 80s vibes influenced by Miami Vice and Goodfellas — ‘Something we have talked about is being nostalgic for the present moment we are all in but also being nostalgic for GTA Vice City’
articles.text:
GTA 6 dev shares how Miami Vice, Heat, and Goodfellas are ‘touchstones’ for the latest game and how it channeled a sense of nostalgia of GTA Vice City — ‘I think the feeling of playing a movie that you get with GTA is one of the coolest things we do’
- Grand Theft Auto 6 senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries explains how Rockstar Games channeled the 80s vibes of GTA Vice City
- Humphries says GTA Vice City is "a game we all love and know sits in a special place for a lot of our fans"
- He reveals that media like Heat, Scarface, Goodfellas, and Miami Vice are "touchstones" for the studio's GTA games
Rockstar Games drew on some of the most iconic 80s gangster movies for Grand Theft Auto 6, influencing the studio's vision for a game that channels the nostalgia of playing GTA Vice City.
Responding to questions sent directly to Rockstar by TechRadar Gaming, senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries explained how the team made a game for 2026 while balancing the 80s vibe players know and love.
"Something we have talked about is being nostalgic for the present moment we are all in but also being nostalgic for GTA Vice City - a game we all love and know sits in a special place for a lot of our fans," Humphries said. "Vice City FM being the 80s station is a sort of nod to that."
The developer went on to reveal how Rockstar references a lot of classic gangster media from the 80s, which it uses to channel that style and vibe.
"There are movies that are touchstones for us whenever we start on one of these projects – Scarface, Heat, Goodfellas – but we also go back and watch Miami Vice, particularly the pilot," Humphries said. "Nothing on TV has ever been as cool as those 90 minutes.
"I think the feeling of playing a movie that you get with GTA is one of the coolest things we do.”

articles.title: General Motors planea usar 20% más robots en sus fábricas de Norteamérica para 2028
articles.text:
General Motors prevé aumentar 20% el uso de robots y otras formas de automatización en sus fábricas de Norteamérica hasta 2028, según dos personas con conocimiento del asunto citadas por la agencia Reuters. La automotriz busca contener el aumento de los costos laborales y los gastos de producir en territorio estadounidense.
La meta de 20% y la fabricación propia de robots no se habían divulgado antes, según Reuters. GM desarrolla sus equipos y los ensambla en su planta de Kokomo, Indiana. Su prioridad son los robots móviles autónomos, máquinas que trasladan piezas de un punto a otro dentro de las plantas sin conductor.
Las automotrices usan robots desde hace décadas para soldar paneles de carrocería o mover insumos entre estaciones. Ahora buscan sumar más robótica y más inteligencia artificial a la línea de producción para elevar la productividad, en un momento de costos más altos por las materias primas y por el traslado de las cadenas de suministro a Estados Unidos.
GM sigue comprando equipos de robótica a proveedores externos mientras desarrolla los propios. Según Reuters, la compañía declaró el año pasado que tenía unos 100 especialistas en robótica, ingeniería de IA y hardware dedicados a sistemas avanzados.
GM exige automatización a sus proveedores
Otras dos fuentes de la cadena de suministro dijeron a Reuters que GM pide a los fabricantes de autopartes que compiten por nuevos contratos que presenten planes para automatizar sus propias operaciones. La empresa califica esos planes con una tabla de puntajes y toma en cuenta el resultado al adjudicar los contratos.
GM no respondió de inmediato al pedido de comentarios de Reuters. Antes había afirmado que usa la automatización para mejorar la seguridad, la calidad y la eficiencia. “A medida que se intensifica la competencia global, seguimos poniendo estas tecnologías a trabajar de maneras que apoyan a nuestros equipos de manufactura”, señaló la empresa.
El sindicato United Auto Workers (UAW), que representa a unos 50.000 trabajadores de fábrica de GM, calificó la estrategia como una forma de recortar empleos. “Su idea de ser más eficientes es recortar a las mismas personas que crean su producto y sus ganancias”, dijo en un comunicado el vicepresidente del gremio, Ryan Hiestand.
“No necesitamos más robots para que GM haga otra recompra de acciones”, agregó Hiestand. En junio, el presidente del sindicato, Shawn Fain, había advertido en una convención que los frutos del trabajo se multiplicaron como nunca sin que los trabajadores los cosechen, y que si la IA se usa como cómplice de ese robo, “hay que detenerla”.
Costos laborales y presión política
Desde que el UAW logró ganancias récord en el contrato de 2023 con GM, Ford y Stellantis, las automotrices estadounidenses aumentaron la automatización para contener costos. GM calculó que ese contrato sumaría unos USD 575 por vehículo en costos laborales, y Ford estimó USD 900. Entonces, analistas ya preveían que las empresas recurrirían a más robots para compensarlo.
La política del presidente Donald Trump de traer trabajo industrial de vuelta al país también presiona los costos de producción. Las automotrices estadounidenses sostienen desde hace tiempo que sus costos laborales superan los de rivales extranjeros y los de competidores nuevos como Tesla, cuyas fábricas en Estados Unidos en su mayoría no tienen sindicato.
Laurie Harbour, socia de la firma de asesoría Wipfli especializada en el sector automotor, dijo a Reuters que el objetivo final es dedicar menos horas de trabajo a cada vehículo para ser más eficientes y rentables. Añadió que más automatización puede aliviar la escasez de mano de obra de las automotrices.
La automatización será probablemente un tema central en la próxima negociación del UAW con GM, Ford y Stellantis, cuyos contratos vencen en la primavera boreal de 2028, el mismo año fijado por GM para su meta de 20%.

articles.title: Sony Defeats UK PlayStation Store Lawsuit With Help From Physical Discs
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 18th 2026
Sony Defeats UK PlayStation Store Lawsuit With Help From Physical Discs
London's Competition Appeal Tribunal (CAT) unanimously dismissed the £1.97 billion ($2.6 billion) class action lawsuit against Sony on November 17, according to The Game Business. As a result, 12.2 million UK PlayStation users won't receive a payout. The claim was filed by consumer rights advocate Alex Neill in August 2022, accusing Sony of abusing a near-monopoly over digital PlayStation games and add-ons. He added that Sony funnels every purchase through the PlayStation Store, where it takes a 30% commission. The case went to trial back in March, and it covered everyone who bought digital PlayStation content in the UK between August 2016 and February 2026. Sony, however, came out on top on every issue. 
The tribunal rejected the argument that PlayStation owners are trapped in a market of their own. It argued that Sony competes in a "systems market" with other players like Xbox, Nintendo, and PC, with physical games also acting as a real alternative to the PlayStation Store. That last bit is quite interesting, to say the least, since Sony is actively phasing out physical disc production by 2028, moving to an all-digital future. It is ironic that the very medium that Sony is moving away from has helped it win a class-action lawsuit. The tribunal found that Sony wasn't dominant in any relevant market, and Neill couldn't show that Sony's margins were excessive, since console makers often sell their hardware at thin margins and rely on software sales to earn it back.Sony will also not be forced to let any rival storefronts onto its consoles, since the tribunal ruled it a security risk and noted that competition law places no such obligation on Sony. Although Sony won this round, this isn't the only class-action lawsuit against it. It still faces several similar class actions in Australia, the Netherlands, and Portugal, though those are at earlier stages. Alex Neill is also reportedly considering an appeal.
