Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: « Le pire modèle jamais sorti par OpenAI » : le nouveau ChatGPT se fait descendre par des testeurs
articles.text:
OpenAI a mis en ligne GPT-6.2 Astra et GPT-6.2 Sol le 17 novembre, deux modèles promis plus efficaces, censés produire un code plus propre en moins d’allers-retours. Les abonnés Plus, Pro, Enterprise et Edu y ont accès dans ChatGPT Work et dans Codex, l’outil de programmation maison. La facture baisse même de 20 % sur l’API pour Astra, à 8 et 40 dollars le million de jetons, l’unité de compte des modèles.
Des accès anticipés qui tournent au réquisitoire
OpenAI s’appuie à chaque lancement sur une poignée de développeurs et d’investisseurs servis en avance, dont les retours alimentent d’ordinaire la promotion. L’annonce du 17 novembre cite d’ailleurs ses testeurs comblés ; d’autres racontent depuis une expérience inverse. Theo Browne, développeur passé par une semaine d’accès anticipé, a ainsi transformé son essai en lettre ouverte à OpenAI. Sa tâche témoin, la réécriture d’un compilateur en Rust, a accouché d’un programme 56 % plus lent que l’original. Sa lettre tranche : « le pire modèle jamais sorti par OpenAI ». Rien que ça.
Dan Shipper, qui confie des projets entiers aux modèles, voit GPT-6.2 s’arrêter avant la fin de ses tâches. Ethan Mollick décrit une expérience en dents de scie, face à un modèle inégal, étrange par endroits et plus difficile à piloter que ses rivaux. Matt Shumer, lui, a renoncé à sa longue revue habituelle et juge les deux modèles « quasiment inutilisables ».
La même lettre crédite pourtant Astra de bonnes prises en relecture de code, d’une génération 3D solide et d’un projet d’infrastructure qui devrait économiser 25 000 dollars par mois à son auteur. Sur le fil de lancement de Hacker News, passé les 500 points en 75 minutes, la baisse des prix récolte d’ailleurs plus d’éloges que le modèle lui-même.
Un modèle moins sûr ?
Face à un obstacle qu’il a pourtant identifié, GPT-6.2 Astra poursuit sans le signaler dans 22,28 % des cas, d’après l’indicateur « Blocker Deception » de sa fiche de sécurité. Le taux double par rapport aux 11,09 % de GPT-6 Astra : l’artisan repère la poutre vermoulue, puis referme le mur sans un mot.
OpenAI avance une piste, un entraînement qui pousse le modèle à répondre court, avec moins de réserves, et un correctif circule déjà dans Codex. Rien d’automatique côté API : la retouche des instructions revient aux développeurs. L’index d’Artificial Analysis, qui agrège des tests de référence, installe Astra sur la deuxième marche, derrière Claude Fable 5.2 d’Anthropic, pour un coût par tâche plus de six fois inférieur à celui du rival.
Fin septembre, OpenAI annulait GPT-6.1 Astra à quelques jours de la sortie, pour des permissions outrepassées et des comptes rendus infidèles en tests internes. La génération suivante arrive donc au complet, lestée cette fois des critiques de ses meilleurs ambassadeurs. Les abonnés ont déjà les deux modèles en main, dans ChatGPT Work et Codex comme sur l’API. À leurs projets de rendre le verdict que plaquettes et lettres ouvertes se disputent.

articles.title: Sur Windows 11, Copilot pourra bientôt vous aider à comprendre pourquoi votre PC fait des siennes
articles.text:
Microsoft prépare une nouvelle fonction de diagnostic permettant à Copilot d'examiner l'état du PC et d'aider à identifier l'origine d'un dysfonctionnement, sans modifier les paramètres du système.
Un casque Bluetooth qui ne donne plus signe de vie, une connexion Internet qui se traîne sans raison apparente… Quand Windows 11 fait des siennes, trouver l'origine du problème peut vite se transformer en jeu de piste. À l'occasion de sa conférence Ignite 2026, Microsoft a dévoilé une nouvelle capacité de Copilot qui pourrait nous éviter quelques heures de recherches et de dépannage à l'aveugle.
Copilot pourra examiner Windows, mais pas le réparer
Microsoft avait déjà commencé à explorer cette piste avec PC Insights, une fonction expérimentale apparue en juillet 2026, qui permet à Copilot de consulter des informations sur l'état du PC, comme l'utilisation du processeur, la batterie ou les périphériques connectés. À l’Ignite, la firme a annoncé vouloir pousser l'exercice plus loin, en permettant à l'assistant de rechercher les causes possibles d'un dysfonctionnement.
Il suffira de décrire le problème rencontré pour que Copilot puisse lancer une analyse du système en lecture seule, examiner les informations pertinentes et suggérer des pistes de dépannage, sans obliger les utilisateurs et utilisatrices à déchiffrer eux-mêmes les données techniques.
Cette fonction ne permettra toutefois pas à l'IA de modifier la configuration de Windows ou d'appliquer des correctifs. Microsoft n'a pas détaillé la nature des données de diagnostic auxquelles Copilot pourra accéder, ni les autorisations nécessaires pour les consulter.
Cette nouvelle capacité fait partie des fonctions locales annoncées à l'Ignite dans le cadre de la stratégie d'intelligence hybride de Microsoft. Elle doit arriver prochainement sur les Copilot+ PC, sans date de lancement plus précise ni confirmation d'une disponibilité sur les autres ordinateurs Windows 11.

articles.title: PhysicsWallah targets over Rs 9,000 Cr revenue by FY30
articles.text:
PhysicsWallah targets over Rs 9,000 Cr revenue by FY30
At its first Investor Day in Mumbai on November 18, the company targeted average annual revenue growth of about 25% or more between FY27 and FY30 and a pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin above 20%.
Edtech firm PhysicsWallah said it is targeting Rs 9,000-10,000 crore revenue by FY30, an ambition that will test whether an online-first education business can keep growing while lifting margins and expanding its physical network.
At its first Investor Day in Mumbai on November 18, the company targeted average annual revenue growth of about 25% or more between FY27 and FY30 and a pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin above 20%.
Pre-Ind AS EBITDA is its non-GAAP measure of earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. Online operations are expected to contribute about two-thirds of revenue by FY30.
The target more than doubles FY26 revenue of Rs 3,900 crore. Revenue from operations reached Rs 1,242 crore in the latest quarter ended 30 September. H1 FY27 pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin was 8.3%, against 18.8% in Q2. The company has noted that exam-related enrolments and course-fee recognition affect the timing of reported revenue.
Co-founded by Alakh Pandey and Prateek Maheshwari, PW began as a YouTube teaching channel in 2016 and became an education platform in 2020. Its offerings span test preparation, skilling, higher education and education-abroad programmes, delivered through digital content, an app and physical centres. It listed in November 2025.
Pandey said, “We started PW so that no family has to choose between its savings and a child's education.”
Redseer estimates India’s test-preparation market at $14.8 billion in FY26, rising to $23-$26 billion by FY30 at annual growth of 12-15%. PW’s 25%+ target is faster. Redseer says families increasingly judge providers on teaching quality and reliable results, not reach alone.
Allen expanded from 43 cities in FY22 to 78 by FY26, taking coaching into smaller cities and adding AI-supported assessment tools. In September, upGrad completed its acquisition of Unacademy, highlighting consolidation after the pandemic-era boom.
Meanwhile, regulation is tightening. Central guidelines circulated in 2024 address coaching-centre registration, fees, infrastructure and student welfare. Several states have since introduced rules or laws. Consumer-protection guidelines also prohibit misleading coaching advertisements and the use of successful students’ testimonials without written consent.
CFO Amit Sachdeva said, “Our FY30 ambition is about profit growing faster than revenue. We will stay disciplined with capital and report our progress every year.”

L'investissement gaming : l'Astro A50 pour jouer sans fil
Pour ceux qui ne supportent plus le câble, l'Astro A50 est la référence. Le micro 48 kHz est l'un des plus naturels du marché, et le confort tient sur la durée grâce aux coussinets en tissu. La certification Dolby Atmos est incluse, sans surcoût.
Le Logitech G Astro A50 passe à 179,99 € au lieu de 219,99 €, soit environ 18 % de réduction. Un investissement sérieux, mais qui remplace trois casques et une station de charge.
Le luxe assumé : l'AirPods Max 2

L'Apple AirPods Max 2 passe à 549,99 € au lieu de 579,00 €. Un achat plaisir pour qui vit dans l'écosystème Apple et cherche le meilleur de l'ANC nomade, sans compromis sur le budget.
Le mot de la fin
Trois casques, trois budgets, trois philosophies. Le Logitech G Pro X est l'affaire absolue de cette sélection : à 54,99 €, il offre un micro de compétition et un son surround que beaucoup de casques à 150 € envient. L'Astro A50 justifie son prix par sa station, sa compatibilité multi-plateformes et son confort sans fil. L'AirPods Max 2 est un achat passion, pas un achat rationnel, et il faut l'assumer.
Si vous cherchez le meilleur rapport qualité-prix sans compromis sur l'essentiel, le G Pro X est le choix évident. Pour le sans-fil et le multi-plateformes, l'Astro A50 est le seul vrai candidat de cette sélection. Et si votre budget est illimité et que vous vivez sous iOS, l'AirPods Max 2 vous tend les bras.
Le Black Month, c'est aussi sur tout le reste du catalogue

articles.title: AI is now finding bugs in the code that runs banks, airlines, and hospitals
articles.text:
The takeaway: An AI model built for security research has uncovered a series of vulnerabilities in Java, the Oracle programming language used in the systems of airlines, banks, hospitals, and government agencies. The flaws were discovered by cybersecurity startup Calif using OpenAI's GPT-6 Cyber model. Now, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency urged companies to update every system running Java.
Oracle released what it called a "critical security patch update" the same day and urged customers to install it. The company declined to comment further. Applying the fix could be a major undertaking: 90% of Fortune 500 companies use Java, which is deeply embedded in the software that keeps large organizations running.
Bruce Dang, a senior researcher at Calif, said the language's widespread use is what makes the discovery so serious. "Java is basically critical infrastructure," he told The Financial Times. "It's so central to the technology that we depend on . . . [and] a lot of big companies are going to have their work cut out to get it fixed."
Calif said it notified Oracle about the vulnerability last month. It then worked with government agencies through the Five Eyes intelligence-sharing alliance, which includes Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK and the US. Amazon, Apple, Google, and Microsoft also helped coordinate fixes. That kind of cooperation is intended to ensure patches are ready before details of a vulnerability spread widely enough for attackers to exploit it.
The Java findings are the latest in a growing list of software vulnerabilities discovered with the help of AI models in recent months. In October, researchers used models from OpenAI and Google to identify two security flaws in PHP, a programming language used by 70% of websites. The bugs had gone undetected for more than a decade. After they were disclosed, companies and government agencies took websites offline as a precaution.
These cases illustrate a shift in how vulnerability research is conducted. AI models can now analyze large, established codebases and uncover flaws that years of human review have missed. That gives defenders an advantage, but it also puts them in a race against potential attackers.
Security researchers are trying to identify and patch weaknesses before malicious actors can exploit them. Advances in AI make that race more challenging because the same capabilities could help attackers discover the same vulnerabilities.
The CISA advisory comes during a period of unusual instability affecting digital services in the US, adding to concerns about further disruptions. Microsoft experienced a widespread outage last week that disrupted its services. The company said a system malfunctioned during a routine effort to reroute user traffic and ruled out a cyberattack. JPMorgan and United Airlines are among the other companies that have experienced outages in recent weeks.
Air travel has also been affected. A five-hour disruption to the country's aging air traffic control system caused a weekend of travel chaos for American passengers. Separately, Norwegian oil and gas group Equinor said it had been targeted in a cyberattack.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio sought to ease concerns that the outages were connected. Speaking to reporters in Manila during President Donald Trump's three-day trip to Asia, he rejected the idea of a coordinated campaign. "We are not under systemic attack. These events, one has nothing to do with another, they are not interrelated, they are all separate and distinct," he said.
"Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country," Rubio added.
The outages have not been linked to the Java vulnerabilities. Still, the timing puts additional pressure on organizations that rely heavily on Java. With Oracle's patch released and CISA's warning issued, companies using Java must now identify every place the language is embedded in their systems and apply the necessary updates.

articles.title: Las asociaciones de guardias civiles de Tráfico denuncian que les proponen cobrar más por poner multas que por hacer controles
articles.text:
Los guardias civiles creen que la DGT les quiere premiar por multar. Simple y llanamente. Es, al menos, lo que aseguran después de haber asistido a una reunión del grupo de trabajo en el que se estudian las propuestas para la nueva normativa sobre productividad y, por tanto, el extra a cobrar a final de año.
¿Qué ha pasado? Señalan nuestros compañeros de Motorpasión Moto que la Agrupación Unificada de Guardias Civiles (AUGC) rechaza lo propuesto en el nuevo borrador de productividad que se está debatiendo para la Agrupación de Tráfico. El motivo es que, según su criterio, la DGT les premiaría por multar y no tanto por vigilar las carreteras.
A preguntas de Xataka, la Asociación Española de Guardias Civiles (AEGC) tiene el mismo sentir. Señalan que con la nueva propuesta se prioriza el número de personas controladas por un radar y no tanto por la vigilancia preventiva en las carreteras pese a que el exceso de velocidad no es el primer problema en los accidentes de nuestro país.
"La bufanda". Nos explica la AEGC que a final de año, la Agrupación de Tráfico recibe un extra de dinero por productividad. Es lo que se llama "la bufanda", como coloquialmente se refieren a este añadido a la nómina. Ese dinero se reparte en función de los objetivos de productividad conseguidos.
Lo que denuncia AUGC en un comunicado es que el nuevo borrador premia las sanciones y la vigilancia con radares pero no tanto el control por seguridad preventiva en la carretera. Aseguran que con los cambios propuestos en la última Instrucción de la Jefatura de la Agrupación de Tráfico de la Guardia Civil a este respecto, el peso de las denuncias aumenta en un 35 % y el de la prevención se reduce en un 38 %.
¿Por qué? Para entender cómo se consigue "la bufanda", hay que entender cómo funciona. El complemento de productividad se consigue en función a si se han conseguido diversos objetivos que tienen diferente peso en el dinero final que se recibe. Así, las sanciones por denunciar elementos de seguridad que no se llevan puestos correctamente o infracciones generales de seguridad vial tienen menos peso que el de los controlados por radar o en en controles de drogas y alcohol.
Y es que ese complemento no se entrega sólo por el volumen de vehículos "pillados" por exceso de velocidad, se prioriza el número de coches vigilados. Esto quiere decir que las unidades de Tráfico que vigilan nuestras carreteras tienen más alicientes para poner un radar móvil en un punto estático de una carretera muy concurrida que por otra por donde pasen menos coches aunque sea menos peligrosa. O que realicen menos kilómetros de vigilancia en coche o moto por las carreteras.
¿Qué se propone? Desde la AUGC consideran que se debería eliminar el complemento por controlados por un radar o en un control de alcoholemia y/o drogas. Y es que, con el nuevo borrador, los resultados negativos en uno de estos últimos controles no suma pero el positivo puede contar doble si además de la infracción el conductor está cometiendo un delito.
Aseguran, por tanto, que el peso de la vigilancia por prevención se reduce de 73 a 45 puntos sobre el máximo de productividad que se puede conseguir mientras que el de delitos crece de 128 a 173 puntos sobre los 413 puntos como máximo que se pueden conseguir sumando todas las variables.
En un comunicado de la AEGC al que Xataka ha tenido acceso, esta agrupación también propone que se mantengan las puntuaciones en los controles de droga que han dado negativo porque se considera que es un ejercicio de prevención en carretera. Pero, en este caso, abogan por mantener el criterio de controlados por radar tal y como está, no de suprimirlo.
La vigilancia. Es el punto clave, ambas asociaciones lo defienden aunque creen que se debería atender de diferente manera. AUGC propone, como decimos, eliminar los controlados por radas y AEGC lo mantendría (aunque no aumentaría su peso). Sin embargo, ambas tienen claro que hay que hacer más vigilancia en la carretera.
"No puedes dedicar el 80% del servicio a los excesos de velocidad cuando hay otros problemas tan graves como el teléfono móvil", nos señala Fernando García, de AEGC. Y es que las distracciones son el principal causante de los accidentes de tráfico en España.
García asegura que buena parte de esa vigilancia se debería hacer con más kilómetros en carretera patrullando, algo que va bajando porque, como él mismo nos ha asegurado a Xataka en otras ocasiones, no está lo suficientemente valorado en la nómina, especialmente los kilómetros en moto que son más peligrosos.

articles.title: GTA VI llega a Argentina: en qué consolas se juega, cuánto cuesta y cómo comprarlo
articles.text:
GTA VI se podrá jugar desde el 19 de noviembre en Argentina en PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X y Xbox Series S. El nuevo título de Rockstar Games no tendrá una versión oficial para PC en su estreno ni será compatible con PlayStation 4, Xbox One o Nintendo Switch.
Los usuarios de consolas de actual generación pueden comprarlo de forma digital desde las tiendas oficiales de cada plataforma. Hay dos ediciones: la estándar y la Ultimate, que incorpora contenidos adicionales dentro del juego.
PlayStation 5 lo vende en dólares y permite la descarga anticipada
En PlayStation Store, la edición estándar de Grand Theft Auto VI figura a USD 79,99, mientras que la Ultimate cuesta USD 99,99. Al importe se le suman los impuestos que correspondan al momento de pagar, por lo que el valor final en pesos depende de la cotización aplicada por la tienda y del medio de pago.
Para comprarlo, el jugador debe ingresar a PlayStation Store desde la consola o la web, buscar el título, elegir la edición y completar el pago con una cuenta de la región argentina. Quienes realizaron la reserva digital pueden descargar los archivos antes de la habilitación del juego. PlayStation recomienda disponer de al menos 212 GB de espacio libre en la consola.
La tienda también informa que la reserva digital incluye el Pack Vintage Vice City y un mes de GTA+, sujeto a las condiciones de la promoción.
Xbox publica precios en pesos para Series X y Series S
En Xbox Store Argentina, la edición estándar tiene un precio de lista de $113.299, mientras que la edición Ultimate se ofrece a $141.990. A esos montos pueden agregarse impuestos, según la normativa y el método de pago.
La compra se realiza desde la tienda de la consola, la página de Xbox o la aplicación oficial. Tras adquirirlo, el juego queda vinculado a la cuenta del usuario y puede instalarse en una Xbox Series X o Series S. La ficha oficial de Microsoft lo identifica como optimizado para ambas consolas.
Las reservas realizadas hasta el 19 de noviembre incluyen el Pack Vintage Vice City y un mes de GTA+, de acuerdo con la página de Xbox.
Por el momento, Rockstar no anunció fecha ni precio para una eventual edición de PC. La primera etapa de ventas se concentra en las consolas de nueva generación de Sony y Microsoft.
También habrá una alternativa en formato físico, aunque no incluirá un disco. La edición estándar para PlayStation 5 se comercializará en caja con un código de descarga que deberá canjearse en PlayStation Store; el juego quedará asociado a la cuenta del usuario y requerirá conexión a internet y espacio disponible en la consola. La versión Ultimate, en cambio, solo estará disponible en formato digital.

articles.title: Google Wallet chega ao iPhone, mas não se empolgue • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Google Wallet chega ao iPhone, mas não se empolgue
Google Wallet (Carteira do Google) para iOS estreia nos Estados Unidos, mas com limitações importantes.
O Google Wallet (no Brasil, Carteira do Google) não é mais exclusividade do ecossistema do Android. O aplicativo do serviço acaba de ser disponibilizado para usuários do iPhone. Por ora, a versão para iOS só funciona nos Estados Unidos. Mas esta não é a única limitação.
Por meio do novo aplicativo, os usuários podem armazenar e acessar determinados tipos de documentos no Google Wallet, como passagens aéreas, ingressos para shows e cartões de fidelidade.
Nesse sentido, a novidade também pode sincronizar dados com o Gmail para obter, automaticamente, recibos de compras, códigos de rastreamento de entregas, cartões de embarque e assim por diante.
Por outro lado, não é possível armazenar documentos oficiais, como carteira de motorista ou identidade digital, ao contrário do que pode ser feito com o Google Wallet para Android, pelo menos nos Estados Unidos.
O aplicativo também permite que o usuário gerencie cartões de crédito ou débito registrados em sua Conta Google, facilitando o preenchimento automático dessas informações em compras realizadas por meio do Chrome ou lojas online compatíveis com o Google Pay.
Agora vem o que talvez seja a maior limitação do Google Wallet para iPhone: o app não permite pagamentos por aproximação, tampouco pode ser usado para pagar transporte público, exceto via QR Code ou código de barras.
O Google não fez nenhum pronunciamento oficial sobre o assunto, mas é provável que haja limitações comerciais ou técnicas. Uma delas pode ser a necessidade de pagar taxas à Apple para o uso de APIs de NFC e Secure Element, que são necessárias para pagamentos por aproximação no iPhone. Talvez o Google não considere viável arcar com esses custos.
Outra possibilidade reside no fato de o iPhone ser configurado por padrão para funcionar com o Apple Pay. Talvez o Google entenda que convencer o usuário a trocar esse serviço pela sua solução possa causar confusão ou deixar o uso do Google Wallet mais complexo.
Não está descartada a hipótese de o Google Wallet para iPhone lidar com pagamentos em algum momento. Mas, por ora, a versão para iOS serve apenas para deixar os usuários um pouco mais próximos de alguns serviços do Google.
Ainda não há informação sobre a expansão da novidade para além dos Estados Unidos.
Vale destacar ainda que o Google já teve uma versão do Wallet para iPhone, lançada em 2013. Mas o aplicativo passou por mudanças posteriores e acabou sendo descontinuado como carteira digital. Desde então, a companhia vinha focando seus esforços na versão para Android.

articles.title: Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are spreading malware through dark web scam bundle, NordVPN warns
articles.text:
Fake GTA 6 PC downloads are spreading malware through dark web scam bundle, NordVPN warns
A plug-and-play cybercrime kit targets eager PC gamers with cookie stealers, crypto drainers, and hidden miners
- NordVPN discovered a fake GTA 6 kit spreading malware on the dark web
- The scam exploits the lack of an official PC release date
- Rockstar is releasing GTA 6 only on consoles on November 19
Scammers are preparing to cash in on the massive hype surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 with ready-to-run malware packs sold on the dark web.
Discovered by NordVPN’s Threat Intelligence team on November 16, the toolkit is built to fleece eager gamers just days before the game's November 19 console launch.
The illicit package costs $200, payable only in Bitcoin or Tether. That flat fee gives entry-level crooks everything they need to start stealing data without writing code.
While setting up the best VPN protects your connection on public networks, software tools cannot stop you from opening an infected file yourself. Security researchers have already warned that cybercriminals are using GTA 6 hype to spread malware, and this new listing lowers the barrier to entry.
"We’ve been watching scammers use GTA 6 for months, but this is a different level," says Marijus Briedis, CTO at NordVPN. "Someone has packaged the whole scam and is selling it to anyone with $200. You don’t need any technical skills anymore. Criminals can just buy the kit and wait for launch day."
NordVPN – the best VPN overall 
NordVPN came out on top in our 2026 round of VPN tests. We think it's the best VPN for most people. We’re confident that virtually anyone can sign up for NordVPN and get what they need from it. It’s easy to use, very secure, fast enough for gaming, and offers flawless streaming service unblocking.
Subscriptions start from $3.49 per month, and you can try it out risk-free with a 30-day money-back guarantee.
How the fake GTA 6 PC port scam works
Every piece of the bundle uses a fake PC release as bait. GTA 6 is arriving strictly on consoles, leaving PC players waiting without a confirmed launch date.
"People who play on PC have been waiting for news, and any link promising an early PC version will get clicks," says Briedis. "There is no PC version on November 19. If you see one, it's a scam."
The kit contains multiple traps. It includes a crypto wallet drainer that targets Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, and Polygon networks, netting sellers an estimated $100 to $500 per drained wallet.
Victims who download the payload get hit with a cookie stealer disguised as "GTA6 Keygen.exe". This program grabs browser session tokens to take over accounts without needing passwords. The kit also installs XMRig to secretly mine cryptocurrency in the background, while an automated bot pushes links on YouTube Shorts to drum up traffic.
Industry reports confirm that fake GTA 6 malware is on the rise. Criminals recognize that scammers do not need to break into Rockstar to steal your details; they simply exploit consumer impatience.

How to avoid GTA 6 launch day malware
Does using an antivirus or privacy app stop you from losing your money? Not if you manually approve a transaction or willingly run an unverified installer.
Steer clear of any site offering a GTA 6 PC build. Rockstar has not published a PC version of the game. Any file, torrent, or archive claiming to deliver a playable PC port is malicious.
Never run key generators or cracks. Files labelled with names like "GTA6 Keygen.exe" deliver malware rather than game access. Buy your games only through the PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, or Rockstar's platform.
Keep crypto wallets disconnected from unknown domains. A video game installer will never require access to Web3 assets. If your computer fans spin at top speed or your machine stutters while idle, open Task Manager and run a scan to detect rogue miners.

articles.title: Nvidia promises employee pay raises, equity before December to quell unrest in wake of Jensen Huang scandal — at first all-hands meeting since CEO’s departure, staff offered perks, told ‘we’re going to be fine'
articles.text:
Nvidia promises employee pay raises, equity before December to quell unrest in wake of Jensen Huang scandal — at first all-hands meeting since CEO’s departure, staff offered perks, told ‘we’re going to be fine’
Money isn't everything, but it sure can help.
Nvidia today held its first all-hands meeting since the resignation of co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. According to Wired, interim CEO Colette Kress offered more money and equity on a faster-than-expected schedule to calm staffers' nerves.
"So I’m here to tell you, the best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp,” Wired reports Kress said.
The pay and equity bumps are set for December, far ahead of the company's normal raise cycle. Kress said that compensation and more clarity from the board were the most common topics in questions submitted ahead of the meeting.
Keeping current employees happy will be one of Kress' most important short-term challenges. One director-level employee has already written to the board and top executives, warning that failure to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive could lead to the loss of ‘irreplaceable talent.’
A potential exodus of talent could also spook investors, despite standout earnings on Thursday. A leadership crisis could make the company seem less stable, and Huang had placed himself as the anchor point for many decisions and the company's overall vision.
Huang has expressed interest in returning to Nvidia, saying he would be "honored" to lead the company again if asked by the board. The board was clear in yesterday's earnings call that it did not intend to bring Huang back, though there is reportedly a pro-Huang faction.
Nvidia cofounder Chris Malachowsky was also on the call, explaining that the company lives its values rather than simply plastering them on posters.
“We’re going to be fine,” he said.

articles.title: OneTrust's Fall '26 Release expands AI visibility, privacy and third-party risk tools - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
OneTrust’s Fall ’26 Release expands AI visibility, privacy and third-party risk tools
Governance platform provider OneTrust LLC today announced its Fall ’26 Release, a set of platform updates said to bring governance into the workflows where business decisions are made.
Building on OneTrust CORIE, a shared intelligence layer for governing artificial intelligence agents introduced at the company’s TrustWeek conference in September, the release covers AI visibility, privacy, consent and third-party risk management.
Leading the list of updates is a revised AI inventory, which is designed to reflect changes across a customer’s environment on a continuous basis. According to OneTrust, the change is needed because many organizations running complex networks of AI systems and agents have only limited visibility into how those systems operate. Model associations, potential matches and deprecation indicators from providers are now pulled into the inventory from a curated library of foundation models.
Relationships among AI systems, models, agents, projects, risks, controls and workflows can be explored through an interactive AI lineage view. AI performance and operational dashboards, added in the release, bring usage, associated risk, evaluation coverage, outbound personally identifiable information discovery and token consumption into one summary.
Ryan Karlin, vice president of product management at OneTrust, said knowing which AI systems are in the business “is just the starting point.” According to Karlin, teams also need visibility into the activity and dependencies of those systems “alongside the privacy and third-party risks they already manage.”
On the third-party risk side, a workflow rule that launches a risk assessment can now trigger OneTrust’s Deep Research AI skill. The in-depth research report that the skill compiles from public data sources is then used to answer the assessment questionnaire. OneTrust claims the integration can cut the time needed to complete a third-party risk assessment from weeks to minutes.
Drawing on previous assessments and supplier documentation, the company’s expanded AI Document Scanning and Inventory Response Analysis features can now also answer questions about the business engagement tied to a third party.
For privacy teams, the release adds protections against automated abuse of data subject request web forms. Growing volumes of those automated requests are straining team workloads, according to OneTrust. To filter out the abuse, enhanced CAPTCHA options now work alongside cross-site request forgery token controls to block suspicious submissions.
In the company’s consent management platform, navigation, configuration, scanning, publishing and geolocation management have also been brought into a single workflow under a modernized interface.
Rounding out the release are reporting updates. Enhanced assessment reporting and application programming interfaces are said to give privacy teams more insight into what drives risk scores. New risk hierarchy visualizations, which show how individual risks across business units aggregate into enterprise risk categories, are aimed at helping teams prioritize risk treatment.
OneTrust is sharing availability details for the Fall ’26 Release through an overview webinar.
OneTrust has raised $1.13 billion to date, including $150 million in 2023 at a valuation of $4.5 billion. Investors in the company include Insight Partners LP, Coatue Management, Technology Crossover Ventures LP, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 LP, Franklin Resources Inc., Generation Investment Management LLP and Sands Capital Management.

articles.title: Cómo Google Maps crea un itinerario de viaje automático apenas aterrizas al destino turístico
articles.text:
Google Maps prepara una función que identificará el momento exacto en que un usuario aterriza en una ciudad nueva y le enviará un mensaje de bienvenida pensado para organizar el viaje desde el primer minuto. La novedad forma parte de un proceso de renovación de la aplicación de navegación, que apunta a convertirse en un asistente capaz de armar itinerarios completos con inteligencia artificial.
La función fue detectada por Android Authority al revisar el código interno de la aplicación, en el que aparece un mensaje que invita al usuario recién llegado a “conocer la ciudad, encontrar un buen primer almuerzo y descubrir qué pasa esta noche”.
Qué es Ask Maps y cómo funciona
El mensaje de bienvenida tiene un objetivo preciso: dirigir a los usuarios hacia Ask Maps, la herramienta conversacional que Google introdujo en marzo de este año y que funciona con los modelos de inteligencia artificial de Gemini.
Ask Maps transforma la aplicación en un asistente al que se le pueden hacer consultas en lenguaje natural, sin necesidad de aplicar filtros de búsqueda tradicionales. El usuario describe el tipo de lugar que busca y la herramienta se encarga de acotar las opciones disponibles en la base de datos de destinos y puntos de interés de Maps.
Ask Maps es la función de Google Maps que permite hacer preguntas en lenguaje natural sobre lugares, comida o actividades en una ciudad, y responde con recomendaciones concretas gracias a la inteligencia artificial de Gemini. Ya está disponible en más de 150 países y busca reemplazar la búsqueda por filtros con un formato de conversación directa.
Cómo son los mensajes de bienvenida al aterrizar
Para saber cuándo activar el saludo, Google se apoya en un componente nuevo llamado AirportGeofenceSyncWorker, que trabaja en segundo plano y determina el momento en que el usuario llega desde un vuelo a una ciudad de destino.
La detección es, por ahora, principalmente geográfica. Pero la función puede sumar una capa adicional de personalización si el usuario tiene activada Gemini Personal Intelligence, la integración que permite a la inteligencia artificial de Google acceder a fuentes como el correo electrónico o el calendario.
Con esa información habilitada, Ask Maps podría conocer de antemano los planes de viaje del usuario, lo que le permitiría ajustar las recomendaciones a datos como la duración de la estadía o reservas ya realizadas, aunque el código revisado hasta el momento no detalla el alcance exacto de esa personalización.
Cómo usarlo para armar el itinerario
Una vez que el usuario interactúa con el mensaje de bienvenida, Ask Maps ofrece varias funciones pensadas para resolver un itinerario de principio a fin.
La herramienta permite pedir comida directamente desde la aplicación gracias a acuerdos con plataformas como Square, Toast y Uber Eats. También puede sugerir alojamiento en tiempo real para quienes llegan sin reserva, con comparación de precios y disponibilidad actualizada.
Ask Maps además identifica eventos cercanos al hotel o a la zona donde se encuentra el usuario, como espectáculos o conciertos, y suma enlaces directos de compra de entradas cuando están disponibles.
Otra función señalada por Google es la capacidad de retomar conversaciones previas dentro de la aplicación. Si un usuario ya consultó sobre una ciudad en otro momento, Ask Maps puede usar ese historial para sugerir actividades relacionadas con esas búsquedas anteriores.
En conjunto, estas funciones apuntan a que el usuario resuelva en la misma aplicación las tres decisiones típicas de un primer día de viaje: dónde comer, dónde alojarse y qué hacer por la noche, sin necesidad de consultar otras plataformas.
En dónde está disponible la función
El sistema de bienvenida no se limita a un puñado de ciudades. Según el relevamiento del código realizado por el medio PhoneArena, Google incluyó referencias a más de 90 aeropuertos internacionales donde la función podría activarse.
Entre los destinos identificados aparecen Madrid, Barcelona, Málaga y Palma de Mallorca en España, junto con ciudades como Nueva York, Los Ángeles, Miami y Ciudad de México, además de otras en Asia y Europa.
Por el momento, Google no confirmó una fecha de lanzamiento oficial para la función de bienvenida en aeropuertos, que todavía se encuentra en una etapa de desarrollo dentro del código de la aplicación.

articles.title: « Un faux sentiment de secret » : face à l'IA, Google prend une décision qui divise le monde de la cybersécurité
articles.text:
Project Zero, l’équipe de chercheurs Google chargée de débusquer les failles de sécurité les plus préoccupantes, vient d’annoncer un changement majeur dans sa façon de travailler. À l’avenir, les fabricants auront beaucoup moins de temps pour corriger les brèches signalées par Google avant que celles-ci ne soient dévoilées auprès du grand public.
Quand Project Zero découvre une faille, l’équipe prévient d’abord l’éditeur concerné en étant le plus discret possible, afin d’éviter que des pirates cherchent à profiter de la situation. Jusqu’ici, le fabricant disposait de 90 jours pour corriger le problème dans son code informatique. S’il publiait un correctif à temps, il bénéficiait de 30 jours supplémentaires pour laisser aux utilisateurs le temps d’installer la mise à jour. Une fois ces délais écoulés, Google publiait tous les détails techniques de la faille. L’approche doit permettre de mettre la pression sur les éditeurs pour qu’ils corrigent vite le tir.
Trois fois moins de temps d’ici 2028
La nouvelle règle annoncée par Google doit accélérer tout le processus de divulgation des failles. L’éditeur a tiré un trait sur le délai supplémentaire de 30 jours. Dès le 2 février 2027, Google dévoilera publiquement les failles 60 jours après le signalement, au lieu de 90 jours.
Le géant américain va aller encore plus loin à partir du 3 janvier 2028 en raccourcissant ce délai à 30 jours, soit trois fois moins qu’aujourd’hui. Project Zero publiera les détails de la faille, même si aucun correctif n’est disponible, une fois le délai écoulé. Pour Google, l’intelligence artificielle a tout changé à la divulgation des failles.
« L’avènement de la découverte et de l’exploitation de vulnérabilités assistées par l’IA a changé le paysage des menaces, de sorte que le délai de correction encouragé par notre politique est clairement insuffisant », écrit Natalie Silvanovich, ingénieure chez Project Zero, dans un billet de blog.
Comme Google l’a déjà constaté, l’IA a fait exploser le nombre de failles découvertes par ses équipes. Les chercheurs de Google indiquent dénicher « plusieurs vulnérabilités par semaine dans des cibles où nous en trouvions autrefois quelques-unes par an ».
Un mode d’emploi pour les cybercriminels
Les pirates profitent évidemment de l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle. Avec l’IA, chaque mise à jour devient un mode d’emploi pour les pirates. En la décortiquant, ils découvrent la faille corrigée, puis s’en prennent à ceux qui n’ont pas encore mis à jour. C’est d’ailleurs de cette manière qu’une armée d’agents IA pirates s’attaque aux sites web français. Le délai de 30 jours, censé garder la faille secrète, ne protège donc plus personne. C’est pourquoi il a été abandonné.
Ce délai « n’a plus de sens dans un monde où les attaquants peuvent presque immédiatement déterminer les détails d’une faille à partir d’un correctif, et peut mettre les utilisateurs en danger en créant un faux sentiment de secret », explique Project Zero. En clair, il ne faut pas croire qu’une faille reste secrète le temps que tout le monde installe la mise à jour.
« Une vulnérabilité signalée aujourd’hui présente un risque immédiat beaucoup plus élevé pour les utilisateurs qu’une vulnérabilité signalée l’an dernier », prévient la chercheuse Natalie Silvanovich, qui pointe du doigt le « faux sentiment de secret » du précédent mode de fonctionnement.
Google assure avoir opté pour une transition progressive pour éviter de mettre les internautes en danger. Comme l’explique Project Zero, « la préoccupation majeure » de ses équipes était qu’un « changement immédiat de la politique puisse nuire aux utilisateurs en mettant à disposition des pirates des vulnérabilités non corrigées, pendant que les éditeurs améliorent leurs processus », explique Project Zero.
Qu’est-ce que ça change pour les utilisateurs ?
Pour les utilisateurs, ce changement de cap devrait se traduire par des mises à jour de sécurité plus fréquentes et plus rapides. Les éditeurs vont devoir corriger plus vite, sous peine de voir leurs failles exposées publiquement par Google. De votre côté, il faut simplement prendre la bonne habitude d’installer les mises à jour dès qu’elles sont disponibles, sur votre ordinateur comme sur votre smartphone.
Dans le milieu de la cybersécurité, la décision de Google ne fait du tout pas l’unanimité. Plusieurs experts craignent que les petites équipes ne puissent pas suivre le nouveau rythme imposé par Google.
« Une date limite ne fait pas apparaître un correctif comme par magie », souligne Katie Moussouris, PDG de Luta Security, auprès de Dark Reading.
De son côté, le chercheur Dustin Childs, de la Zero Day Initiative de Trend Micro, redoute de l’émergence de correctifs bâclés, développés et déployés à la hâte, « qui ne règlent pas entièrement la vulnérabilité ».
Google se veut rassurant et affirme que toutes les failles signalées par Project Zero en 2026 dans des projets open source ont été corrigées en 30 jours, sauf une, réparée en 31 jours. Pour Project Zero, les changements prévus ne devraient donc pas mettre les éditeurs et les constructeurs en difficulté. Google n’est pas le seul géant à serrer la vis. Anthropic, le laboratoire à l’origine de Claude, va lui aussi réduire son délai de divulgation à 30 jours pour les failles graves à partir de janvier.

articles.title: Avec Rubin HPC, NVIDIA dévoile un monstre de plus de 50 000 cœurs, mais AMD a déjà pris une longueur d’avance
articles.text:
Simulations scientifiques, recherche assistée par l’IA et calcul haute performance sont au programme du nouveau GPU de NVIDIA. Prévu pour 2028, il devra notamment rivaliser avec l’Instinct MI430X d’AMD, attendu dès l’année prochaine.
Les agents IA vont devoir passer leurs idées au banc d’essai. NVIDIA a présenté le 16 novembre dernier, lors de la conférence Supercomputing 2026 à Chicago, Rubin HPC, une déclinaison de sa plateforme Vera Rubin consacrée au calcul haute performance. Sa mission est d’accélérer les simulations et l’analyse de données qui permettent aux chercheurs d’évaluer des molécules, des matériaux ou des conceptions industrielles suggérés par l’IA.
Un Rubin rééquilibré pour le calcul scientifique
Premier changement, Rubin HPC dépassera les 50 000 cœurs CUDA par GPU, contre 28 672 pour la version classique de Rubin. À titre de comparaison, une carte graphique GeForce RTX 5090 en compte 21 760 et une RTX 5080, 10 752. NVIDIA prévoit aussi une accélération du traitement des données éparses pour que les unités de calcul passent moins de temps à attendre les informations dont elles ont besoin. La liaison entre GPU passera au NVLink de septième génération, contre la sixième sur Rubin classique.
L’enjeu tient notamment à la double précision, ou FP64, employée dans de nombreuses simulations scientifiques. Rubin classique privilégie les formats de faible précision utilisés par l’IA avec un débit FP64 vectoriel de 33 téraflops, contre 40 pour Blackwell. NVIDIA revendique jusqu’à 200 téraflops pour certaines opérations matricielles FP64 obtenus par émulation sur ses Tensor Cores. Cette technique exploite des unités conçues pour des calculs moins précis, mais ne remplace pas les capacités FP64 natives dans tous les usages scientifiques.
Interrogé par The Register, Dan Ernst, responsable du supercalcul chez NVIDIA, a également évoqué des capacités matricielles FP64 natives pour le matériel HPC du groupe. Les performances exactes de Rubin HPC, sa capacité mémoire et sa bande passante n’ont cependant pas été communiquées.
AMD a déjà un rival et des clients
NVIDIA trouvera sur sa route l’Instinct MI430X d’AMD, attendu dès 2027. Détaillée le 12 novembre à l’approche de SC26, cette puce basée sur l’architecture CDNA 5 doit embarquer 432 Go de mémoire HBM4, avec une bande passante pouvant atteindre 23,3 To/s et jusqu’à 288 téraflops en FP64 natif. AMD affiche ainsi ses ambitions dans le calcul scientifique, avec un calendrier plus serré que celui de son rival. Pour confronter les promesses des deux fabricants, il faudra toutefois que NVIDIA dévoile les performances de Rubin HPC.
Les centres de calcul, eux, passent déjà commande. Aux États-Unis, le laboratoire d’Oak Ridge a choisi le MI430X pour Discovery, le supercalculateur qui succédera à Frontier. En France, la puce d’AMD équipera Alice Recoque, le premier supercalculateur exascale du pays. Il faudra attendre 2028 pour mesurer ce que vaut Rubin HPC face à son rival. Pour ces deux machines, le choix est déjà fait.
La FP64 (64 bits) augmente la précision numérique des calculs, ce qui limite les erreurs d’arrondi quand une simulation enchaîne des milliards d’opérations. Elle est essentielle en modélisation physique, chimie, mécanique des fluides ou climat, où une petite dérive peut fausser un résultat final. Beaucoup de charges HPC sont donc jugées sur leur débit FP64, généralement exprimé en téraflops (TFLOPS). À l’inverse, l’IA privilégie souvent des formats moins précis (FP16, BF16, FP8) plus rapides et moins coûteux en énergie. Un GPU orienté science doit donc proposer une FP64 solide, pas seulement des accélérations ponctuelles.
La FP64 native signifie que le GPU dispose d’unités matérielles capables d’exécuter directement des opérations en double précision, avec un comportement et des performances prévisibles pour les codes scientifiques. La FP64 émulée via des Tensor Cores consiste à s’appuyer sur des unités optimisées pour des calculs matriciels moins précis, en recomposant des opérations FP64 pour certains types de multiplications de matrices. Cette approche peut donner de très bons débits dans des cas bien cadrés (algèbre linéaire dense, kernels adaptés), mais elle ne couvre pas tous les besoins HPC. En pratique, de nombreux logiciels utilisent un mix d’opérations (vectorielles, irrégulières, non matricielles) où l’émulation ne remplace pas toujours la FP64 native. C’est pour cela que les annonces distinguent souvent « pic théorique » sur matrices et performance FP64 réellement exploitable sur des codes variés.
La HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) est une mémoire empilée très proche du GPU, conçue pour fournir une bande passante massive, bien plus élevée que la GDDR des cartes grand public. En HPC, beaucoup de workloads sont limités non par la puissance de calcul brute, mais par la vitesse à laquelle le GPU peut lire et écrire des données (gros tenseurs, grilles de simulation, matrices, champs 3D). La bande passante (exprimée en To/s) aide à alimenter les unités de calcul et à réduire le temps passé à attendre les données, surtout quand les accès mémoire sont nombreux. La capacité (en Go) compte aussi : elle conditionne la taille des modèles ou des simulations qui tiennent en mémoire sans découpage coûteux. HBM4 est une nouvelle génération qui vise à augmenter à la fois capacité et débit, ce qui est central pour les systèmes exascale.

articles.title: Apollo, Microsoft turn to AI to help hospitals learn from medical errors
articles.text:
Apollo, Microsoft turn to AI to help hospitals learn from medical errors
The partnership aims to turn fragmented hospital records into faster incident reviews and shared lessons.
An artificial intelligence system developed by Apollo Hospitals with Microsoft is being used to speed up reviews of patient falls, medication errors and readmissions. Apollo said the system has coincided with fewer recorded incidents, although the evidence published so far does not establish that AI itself has reduced patient harm.
Apollo and Microsoft developed a Daily Tiered Huddle agent to support clinical-governance teams. It brings together hospital records, flags cases, builds patient timelines and prompts clinicians for missing details. It also suggests assessments for doctors to check and amend. The tool is in production at some Apollo hospitals.
“For anyone to process 600 cases per month with incomplete data and come up with a meaningful decision is difficult,” said Dr Rohini Sridhar, Apollo’s chief of medical services. The agent is intended to reduce the time spent assembling records, leaving clinicians more time to investigate complex cases.
Apollo said more than 60% of cases reviewed by its huddles were closed within three days in November 2026. It also noted fewer falls and medication errors in July-September than in the same quarter of 2025. Dr Sridhar said staff satisfaction with error handling improved by almost 30%, based on the hospital’s annual safety-culture survey.
These are hospital-reported results published in a Microsoft case study. The account does not provide incident counts, patient-volume-adjusted rates or an independent assessment.
The system is also designed to identify patterns across departments, although Apollo said this analysis is still being developed. It flagged a cluster of central-line-associated bloodstream infections in a bone marrow transplant unit. Juliet Joji Varghese, Apollo’s director of nursing in Chennai, said the system helps staff learn from incidents elsewhere in the network.
Beyond the Apollo and Microsoft push, there are other initiatives that reflect the expanding use of AI in routine healthcare operations and diagnostics.
In April, AstraZeneca and the Telangana government agreed to introduce Qure.ai’s AI-supported chest X-ray screening in 20 public health facilities. The technology is intended to flag high-risk lung nodules for further assessment. Manipal Hospitals has also worked with Google Cloud on a generative AI tool for nurse handovers, which Google said had been rolled out across 23 hospitals by July 2025.
India is also beginning to establish a framework for responsible adoption. The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, launched in 2021, laid the foundation for interoperable digital health records. In February 2026, the Centre launched the Strategy for AI in Healthcare for India, and the Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI (BODH).
Developed with IIT Kanpur and the National Health Authority, BODH is intended to evaluate AI models using diverse health data while protecting patient records.
The World Health Organization, in a July 2026 report, highlighted ethical and oversight challenges arising from AI in health research, including risks that existing review systems may not adequately address.

articles.title: You can now opt out of AI training in Gemini without losing your chat history
articles.text:
The big picture: Google is rolling out new Gemini privacy settings that let users keep their chat history even after opting out of AI model training. The change is likely to be welcomed by tech-savvy users and privacy advocates, who have long clamored for their chats to be excluded from generative AI training.
The new settings were reported by 9to5Google, which noted that the Gemini app now splits chat history saving and consent for generative AI model training into separate sections. The change allows users to switch off generative AI training on their data while still saving their chat history for future reference.
Google is dividing the existing Keep Activity setting into a History section, which lets users control how long their chats are saved, and an AI training section, which lets them independently control whether their chat content is used to train AI models.
If Keep Activity is already turned off when the change reaches an account, both new options will be disabled by default.
Once the change takes effect, if users turn off History, Gemini will save future chats for around two months, using them to "respond to you, process your feedback, and protect Google, its users, and the public, with help from human reviewers." Before the update, with saving disabled, chats were kept for only 72 hours to protect Google, its users, and the public, and only the last 24 hours were used for context.
Google clarified that temporary chats are not used to train its AI models, so users who have switched off History and don't submit feedback won't have their chats used for AI training.
If History is off but the user submits feedback, Google will use that feedback and the last 24 hours of chat history, including attachments and data from connected apps, to improve Gemini.
The second AI training setting, meanwhile, lets users keep their chat history while independently controlling whether their chat content, including text and attachments, can be used for generative AI model training.
Google says it is notifying users of the changes by email, and that they will roll out globally over the coming weeks. It's unclear whether the new settings can be configured on both desktop and mobile, but the official emails will likely provide more details.

articles.title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
articles.text:
Microsoft’s Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core. Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG).
STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: “The secure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened.”
The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance.
This isn’t to say that system administrators won’t still have the final say on which security protocols are activated, just that the default package now ships in a pre-hardened state. Kerberos is now the default over NTLM, with protections added to LSASS; TLS is automatically restricted to modern cipher suites; key exchange uses “hybrid post-quantum key exchange” based on the quantum-safe ML-KEM; and remote desktop authentication and PowerShell script block logging get stricter as well.

articles.title: ‘Our most advanced Audio-Animatronics in the world’ — Disney Imagineering reveals how AWS AI brings the Star Wars Anzellans to life
articles.text:
‘Our most advanced Audio-Animatronics in the world’ — Disney Imagineering reveals how AWS AI brings the Star Wars Anzellans to life
Three tiny Star Wars characters offer a big glimpse into Imagineering's future
Picture this: You're walking through Black Spire Outpost on Batuu, the setting for Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge at Disneyland or Disney World, and you step into a shop, maybe looking for a certain color of kyber crystal, a cold brew black caf, or a new piece of Star Wars merchandise. But before you can find what you're after, you're stopped by a small creature that starts talking to you.
Maybe it lets out a shriek of concern because you're wearing an outfit that screams 'dark side', or cheers with excitement after spotting your birthday button. These are the kinds of spontaneous, memorable interactions Disney parks are known for, and in recent years, we've seen Imagineering steadily bring robotics and high-tech Audio-Animatronics closer together to make its characters feel more alive.
Now, Disney's latest creation takes that idea a step further.
Meet the Anzellans: Vilo Vele, Kado Bre'a, and Jibu Bre'a. These tiny Star Wars creatures, the same species as Babu Frik from The Rise of Skywalker, have been brought to life as three Audio-Animatronics positioned together in a crate. They can move, look around, and interact with one another, but what's especially impressive is that they can also read the room.
Thanks to a partnership with Amazon Web Services (AWS), the Anzellans use cameras, microphones, sensors, and AI to understand what's happening around them and respond in real time. They can recognize what a guest is wearing, identify who's speaking to them, and even coordinate their interactions with one another.
And while AI is helping bring these characters to life, it's not writing their dialogue or dreaming up their personalities. That's still very much the work of Disney's Imagineers.
"These Anzellans now are our most advanced Audio-Animatronics in the world," Kyle Laughlin, Senior Vice President of Walt Disney Imagineering R&D and Technology and Engineering, told me in an interview alongside Samira Panah Bakhtiar, General Manager of Telco, Media & Entertainment, Games, Advertising, and Sports at AWS.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
It's a pretty significant statement considering Disney's long history with Audio-Animatronics, dating back to Walt Disney's Enchanted Tiki Room, and continuing through increasingly sophisticated figures in attractions like Pirates of the Caribbean.
But the Anzellans are doing something different. Rather than performing a fixed sequence of movements and dialogue, they're designed to understand what's happening around them and decide how to respond, without someone controlling them from behind the scenes.
And it's part of a much bigger effort underway at Imagineering.
Bringing robotics and Audio-Animatronics together
I've spoken with Laughlin previously about Disney's characters, including the BDX droids that have been roaming Galaxy's Edge and Olaf, the free-roaming robotic snowman that Imagineering has brought to Disneyland Paris and Hong Kong Disneyland.
While these creations might look very different from the traditional Audio-Animatronics that populate Disney's attractions, they're increasingly connected behind the scenes.
"Our robots and our animatronics are coming closer and closer together," Laughlin explained.
In fact, the Anzellans are built on the same robotic character platform that powers Olaf and the BDX droids. That's an especially interesting detail, considering these three little characters aren't roaming around on their own. Instead, they're working together in one environment, responding to guests and each other. Notably, there isn't another Cast Member controlling the experience or puppeteering, but rather those decisions are made by the character, in real time.
Laughlin describes the Anzellans as a hybrid, bringing together elements of robotics and Audio-Animatronics with a level of intelligence that Disney hasn't previously delivered in one of these characters.
"This is our most intelligent character that we've created," he said.
The hardware is an important part of that distinction. While Olaf can move around and interact with his surroundings, Laughlin explained that he doesn't have onboard cameras or microphones. The Anzellans do, along with additional sensors that help them understand their environment.
Imagine approaching the crate with a group of friends. The Anzellans can understand that multiple people are standing in front of them, determine who's speaking, and look that person directly in the eyes while responding in their own mix of English and Anzellan.
It's the kind of detail that could make an encounter feel much more personal, and it's where AWS enters the picture.
AWS gives the Anzellans their intelligence, but Disney remains in control
Disney and AWS have worked together for more than a decade, including on the infrastructure supporting Disney+, which turns seven this week. But the Anzellans take that partnership in a different direction, bringing AWS's cloud and AI capabilities into a physical character experience.
And the project came together surprisingly quickly.
Laughlin told me the teams worked together over a matter of months, with the opportunity to collaborate with the filmmakers behind The Mandalorian & Grogu helping inform the direction of the characters.
AWS brought its AI and software expertise, while Imagineering concentrated on the physical characters, their personalities, and the storytelling.
"AWS I think brought the intelligence, Imagineering brought the brawn," Bakhtiar told me.
The Anzellans use Amazon Bedrock, AWS's managed AI service, to access different AI models that help them understand and react to the world around them. Laughlin confirmed that Imagineering is using vision models, large language models, and world models as part of the experience.
That doesn't mean the characters are using generative AI to make up their own dialogue, though.
Every line is written by Imagineers and prerecorded, and every character's personality and movements are designed by the creative team. AI selects the appropriate responses and animations based on what's happening in the moment.
So, if an Anzellan spots a birthday button, it can choose a response that fits the occasion. If someone speaks directly to one of the characters, it can respond accordingly. The interaction might feel spontaneous, but the actual words and character behaviors remain firmly in Imagineering's hands.
That distinction is important, particularly as Disney continues to experiment with AI in guest experiences.
"Human creativity leads and the guest experience is preserved, and AI and the cloud computing infrastructure really is there to support it," Bakhtiar said. "[Entertainment companies] need technology that's going to really serve their story and not the other way around."
There's also another layer to this experience: the three Anzellans aren't simply responding independently.
Bakhtiar explained that each character is simultaneously tracking three things: the guest, what's happening in the surrounding environment, and what the other Anzellans are doing.
"The system is working like a show director, and it's like keeping this ensemble together so the characters, they don't talk over each other, the story stays coherent," she explained.
That's a fascinating distinction from a traditional Audio-Animatronics show. Instead of following the same carefully timed sequence, the Anzellans can adjust their performances to the situation while still behaving like characters from the Star Wars universe.
AWS also used Kiro, its AI coding agent, to help turn Imagineering's creative briefs into working software. Bakhtiar explained that the teams reviewed and approved the work at each stage, allowing ideas to move into testing more quickly.
For Laughlin, that meant Imagineers could spend more time focusing on the mechanical and electrical engineering, character skins, and the finer details that make the Anzellans believable.
And because Bedrock isn't tied to one specific AI model, Disney can swap models as the technology improves, optimizing for performance, speed, latency, or cost without rebuilding the entire experience.
"We can be on the bleeding edge of whatever model is launched in order to bring the best experience possible," Laughlin said.
That's particularly valuable when a character needs to respond quickly enough for a conversation to feel natural.
A new kind of character encounter
Of course, there's a big question hanging over all of this: When will guests actually get to meet the Anzellans?
Disney isn't saying just yet. The characters are scheduled to appear at AWS re:Invent in Las Vegas from November 30 through December 4, where attendees can meet them at the Customer Showcase at Caesars Forum.
And while this won't be their first public appearance — Disney confirmed to TechRadar that an earlier version of the Anzellans shown at D23 was also powered by AWS — there's still no word on when or where they'll become a regular guest experience at Disneyland or Disney World.
Laughlin did offer one encouraging indication when I asked about their eventual arrival in the parks.
"We’re excited for guests to meet them. We just won’t talk specifics today."
And while we've already seen the BDX droids roaming Galaxy's Edge and Olaf interacting with guests at Disneyland Paris, these experiences are still relatively limited compared with the many Audio-Animatronics and characters found throughout Disney's parks. The technology is impressive, but the next challenge is bringing these more interactive characters into everyday park experiences, and doing so at scale.
That's something Laughlin and I have discussed before, and he sees the Anzellans as part of a broader shift in how Imagineering develops and introduces its characters.
"More than ever, this is not about short-term playtests. It really is about populating our worlds with lots of different characters," he explained.
Laughlin also told me that guests should expect to encounter the Anzellans indoors first, and his description of the technology offers a pretty intriguing glimpse at where Imagineering might be headed.
"We've viewed this as an experiential merchandise platform," he explained.
In other words, imagine walking into a Disney shop and having an unexpected interaction with a character, rather than needing to visit a designated meet-and-greet location.
And the idea isn't necessarily limited to Star Wars.
"When we think about the future of where it's headed, you can imagine that any type of merchandise experience could be powered with characters from any of our franchises," Laughlin said.
There's still plenty to figure out, though. Keeping a character responsive throughout a busy day at a theme park requires more than just sophisticated AI. There's also the question of what happens if the network connection drops or the primary system encounters a problem.
It's something I asked Laughlin about, and he explained that Disney is combining AWS cloud and edge infrastructure to help keep the experience running.
"If something were to fail [...] then we could always fall back to another experience," he said.
The goal is to keep these characters operating reliably throughout park hours, though Disney is still learning what it takes to deliver these more intelligent experiences at scale.
Privacy is another consideration, especially with cameras and microphones involved. Laughlin told me that the information gathered during an interaction is used only for the immediate experience, isn't currently stored in the cloud for Disney to reuse, and isn't used to train AI models.
The specifics of the underlying models and the number of sensors remain undisclosed, but the broader approach is becoming clearer.
The next chapter for Disney's characters
Imagineering has continued to push its characters further, from free-roaming robots to the next-generation Audio-Animatronics appearing in attractions like Pirates of the Caribbean or Frozen Ever After.
The Anzellans are another step in that evolution, but perhaps the bigger development is what's happening behind the scenes. Disney is building a shared foundation that can support different types of characters and experiences, rather than treating robotics, Audio-Animatronics, and AI as entirely separate technologies.
Bakhtiar described the AWS-powered system as a reusable framework, one that could allow Imagineers to focus on creating new personalities, moods, movements, and stories instead of rebuilding the underlying software every time.
And with Laughlin pointing to more than $60 billion of work ahead for Imagineering worldwide, there are plenty of opportunities to put these technologies to work.
Just look at Walt Disney World, where an entirely new Monsters, Inc. land is coming to Hollywood Studios — complete with an octopus-like, impressive animatronic — while Animal Kingdom is getting Tropical Americas with new Indiana Jones and Encanto attractions. Over at Magic Kingdom, Villains Land and Piston Peak are on the way, while EPCOT will eventually take guests on a new journey into imagination with Figment and Dreamfinder.
And that's just Florida. At Disneyland Resort in California, Imagineering is working on the first-ever Coco attraction, a major reimagining of Tomorrowland, and an expansion of Avengers Campus, among other projects.
Of course, that doesn't mean we'll necessarily see the Anzellans or this exact AI technology in any of these attractions. But with so much happening across Disney Parks, it's easy to see why Imagineering is investing in a platform that could bring more interactive characters to life across its parks.
For now, the Anzellans remain a glimpse at what's possible rather than a confirmed new fixture at Galaxy's Edge. But it's easy to imagine how a seemingly ordinary shopping trip could become something much more memorable when a character recognizes you, reacts to what you're wearing, or strikes up a conversation.
And when I asked Laughlin what this convergence of robotics, AI, and Audio-Animatronics could mean for Disney's characters over the next decade, he pointed to the growing range of possibilities, from robots and Audio-Animatronics to puppets and roaming characters.
"We now have more tools in the toolkit to bring these characters to life in all kinds of new ways," he said. "And so, my hope is over the next 10 years you're going to continue to see an incredible pace of scale and delivering these experiences worldwide."

articles.title: GTA VI runs at 1440p on PS5 and Xbox Series X, but just 720p with upscaling on Series S — Rockstar details upscaling technologies ahead of launch
articles.text:
GTA VI runs at 1440p on PS5 and Xbox Series X, but just 720p with upscaling on Series S — Rockstar details upscaling technologies for launch
No support for native 4K.
The most highly anticipated video game of the decade is here. GTA VI arrives almost 13 years after GTA V, with reports suggesting that it has already generated around $1.54 billion in revenue from 16 million preorders. Ahead of its release, Rockstar Games has finally shared some technical details, including rendering resolutions and upscaling technologies being used across all consoles.
In a statement shared with Wccftech, the technical team at Rockstar has confirmed that GTA VI uses different upscaling solutions across all consoles in order to achieve a balance between visual quality and performance with a target of 30FPS. The PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X use Rockstar's own temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) solution, while the PlayStation 5 Pro relies on Sony's second-generation PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR2). The Xbox Series S, meanwhile, relies on AMD's FSR 4 upscaling technology.
As for rendered resolutions, the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and PlayStation 5 Pro all start with a native base resolution of 1440p, which is then upscaled to 4K. The Xbox Series S is the least powerful console; thus, the game runs at a lower base resolution of 720p, which is upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4. The final image on all consoles is then composited with a 4K user interface before being presented.
Rockstar has also developed a physically-based material library for GTA VI and a cinematic imaging pipeline to deliver realistic lighting, reflections, and material details within the game. The team says it has worked to maintain a consistent lighting solution across all consoles, including the Xbox Series S, while adjusting ray-traced global illumination (RTGI) features depending on each platform's hardware capabilities.
The PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S launched all the way back in 2020, and while the consoles have capable hardware, their architectures are finally beginning to show their age. The fact that Rockstar is targeting just 30FPS across all consoles, while relying on different upscaling technologies and rendering resolutions, highlights how much performance is potentially being left on the table in order to maintain visual fidelity. That being said, a PC release of GTA VI continues to be a big question mark. Rockstar is yet to announce a release date or even provide a launch window, meaning that PC gamers can only rely on Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream the game on their systems.

articles.title: Molecular discovery speeds up at Texas A&M supercomputing - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI and supercomputing merge as universities build GPU clusters at cloud-provider scale
Universities racing to build AI infrastructure are learning that raw compute changes the pace of science itself, from molecular discovery to materials engineering.
AI and high-performance computing are converging, and campus technology leaders are now building like cloud operators. The Texas A&M University System is standing up two major clusters for researchers across its 12 universities and eight state agencies, according to Vince Kellen (pictured), chief information officer of The Texas A&M University System.
“A lot of it is going to be related to molecules, molecular discovery, and the size of these computers lets researchers go through their research program in a fraction of the time. What would normally take five months now gets done in a week,” Kellen said. “That’s a big deal for the scientists. It lets them do more exploration more frequently.”
Kellen spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how the system’s supercomputing clusters are speeding up molecular discovery, the security and operational demands of running them, and the convergence of AI and supercomputing. (* Disclosure below.)
Molecular discovery at supercomputer speed
The system’s VISION supercomputer, an Nvidia Corp. DGX H200 SuperPOD, ranked No. 66 on the June 2026 Top500 list, making it the most powerful university supercomputer in the U.S. — with a second cluster on the way, according to Kellen. The Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station selected Dell Technologies Inc. to build IGNITE, a platform running Advanced Micro Devices Inc. GPUs in an Equinix Inc. data center in Dallas. With some research tied to highly secure federal contracts, protection tops the policy agenda.
“On the policy side, our main concern is security. Are we doing this in a secure way?” Kellen said. “Are we vetting the employees who are coming into the platform to make sure that they’re properly credentialed to come in?”
Texas A&M is working through those access questions as it brings more computing power to researchers across the system, but faster molecular discovery is only the first payoff. Materials engineering, fluid dynamics and other engineering disciplines are next in line, and the system has no plans to slow its buildout, according to Kellen.
“We already know that AI and supercomputing are one and the same,” he said. “That trajectory is going to continue in Texas for some time.”
