articles.title: GTA 6 : test, notes et avis, ce que disent les premiers tests du jeu
articles.text:
L’attente a duré treize ans, et le verdict de la presse est tombé quelques heures avant la sortie du jeu en France, prévue cette nuit à minuit. À l’heure de ces lignes, Grand Theft Auto VI affiche une moyenne de 99 sur 100 sur Metacritic, sur la base de 141 tests, ce qui le place au niveau des jeux les mieux notés de l’histoire. En France, Gamekult lui attribue même un 10/10, une première pour le site, qui explique avoir longuement débattu avant de « faire sauter un verrou ». Jeuxvideo.com lui donne 19/20, le Journal du Geek 9/10. À l’étranger, Eurogamer lui accorde la note maximale de cinq étoiles, IGN lui donne 10/10 et parle du « jeu vidéo le plus impressionnant » que son testeur ait jamais pratiqué, et Jason Schreier, journaliste de Bloomberg et l’un des meilleurs connaisseurs de l’industrie, n’hésite pas à qualifier le jeu de « chef-d’œuvre ».
Un monde ouvert qui met tout le monde d’accord
S’il y a un point sur lequel tous les tests s’accordent, c’est la richesse du monde ouvert. « Peu de jeux vidéo ont des villes aussi vastes, aussi denses, aussi pleines de secrets et de systèmes qui s’imbriquent », écrit Jason Schreier, qui raconte avoir été incapable de terminer l’histoire à temps, sans cesse distrait par les rencontres improbables de Vice City. Jeuxvideo.com parle du « plus bel open world urbain jamais conçu », Gamekult du « monde ouvert le plus vivant et palpable » qu’il ait connu. Tous citent les personnages non-joueurs, qui réagissent de manière crédible à vos actes, du conducteur qui sort de sa voiture pour en découdre après un coup de klaxon au mendiant qui sort une arme quand on ne lui donne que dix dollars.
L’ambiance sonore fait elle aussi l’unanimité, avec une sélection de radios jugée quasi parfaite et une bande originale signée notamment par le duo français Justice. La conduite est également saluée, IGN la jugeant la meilleure de la série. Plusieurs tests soulignent au passage l’intérêt des gâchettes adaptatives de la manette DualSense sur PS5, qui permettent de mieux doser l’accélération.
L’histoire et le réalisme divisent davantage
Les avis sont plus partagés sur le scénario et Jeuxvideo.com, IGN ou encore Gamekult saluent un duo Jason-Lucia attachant et une écriture qui a gagné en maturité, à la manière de Red Dead Redemption 2. Le Journal du Geek se montre beaucoup plus critique, dénonçant une narration « décousue » et un côté satirique en retrait, qu’il attribue au départ de Dan Houser, cofondateur et scénariste historique de Rockstar. Jason Schreier se situe entre les deux et estime que l’histoire est meilleure que celle de GTA V, mais n’atteint pas les sommets émotionnels de Red Dead Redemption 2.
Le virage vers le réalisme ne convainc pas non plus tout le monde. Il faut désormais nourrir ses personnages, les faire dormir et aller à la salle de sport, faire le plein d’essence ou laisser ses armes dans le coffre de sa voiture. Le Journal du Geek y voit une « charge mentale » inutile, quand Gamekult, d’abord sceptique, a fini par se prendre au jeu de ce qu’il appelle « le Tamagotchi le plus cher de l’histoire » du jeu vidéo. GTA 6 introduit aussi un profil moral, de « Professionnel » à « Irrécupérable » selon Jeuxvideo.com, qui évolue selon votre façon de jouer et influence la réaction de la police, mais aussi la fin de l’histoire, qui en compte plusieurs. Ceux qui espéraient un défouloir sans conséquence risquent d’être déçus, prévient le site spécialisé. Quelques reproches reviennent enfin, comme une interface parfois confuse, des repaires de gangs peu inspirés ou un premier chapitre très lent.
30 images par seconde, mais une claque technique
Côté technique, le jeu tourne à 30 images par seconde sur toutes les consoles, y compris sur PS5 Pro, et les testeurs disent pour la plupart s’en être accommodés. L’analyse la plus poussée vient de Digital Foundry, référence en la matière, titre sur « une réussite marquante qui redéfinit une génération de consoles ». Sur PS5 comme sur PS5 Pro, le jeu est calculé en 1440p. La PS5 Pro s’appuie ensuite sur son upscaler PSSR pour obtenir une image proche de la 4K, là où la PS5 classique affiche une image plus douce. La PS5 Pro tient ses 30 images par seconde sans faiblir, tandis que la PS5 standard peut descendre autour de 25 images par seconde lors des scènes les plus chargées en explosions. Le Journal du Geek et Jeuxvideo.com disent pourtant avoir constaté quelques chutes, même sur PS5 Pro, lors de grosses fusillades.
Digital Foundry salue surtout l’usage massif du ray tracing, pour l’éclairage global et les reflets sur toutes les consoles, et pour les ombres sur la PS5 Pro, qu’il juge peut-être « la meilleure implémentation du ray tracing » vue à ce jour. Selon lui, la densité de la simulation, jusqu’aux cheveux de chaque passant animés mèche par mèche, explique pourquoi un mode 60 images par seconde n’était pas envisageable sur les consoles actuelles. Gamekult précise enfin que Rockstar a déjà publié deux correctifs durant sa période de test.

articles.title: Leaked Ohio bill could allow AI data center companies to seize private land for their buildouts using eminent domain law — proposed law would expand list of beneficiaries
articles.text:
Leaked Ohio bill could allow AI data center companies to seize private land for their buildouts using eminent domain law — proposed law would expand list of beneficiaries
It's not the first time eminent domain fears have been raised around AI data centers
While Ohioans have rejected the building of new data centers at every turn, they might not have much choice in the future. That's if a newly leaked bill that could allow data centers to be classified as public utilities is allowed to progress. The move would see the list of who can qualify for eminent domain law expanded, moving beyond entities owned or operated by municipal corporations, electric cooperatives, and agencies holding a certificate of public convenience and necessity granted by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. The bill, leaked to WCPO Cincinnati, would add "and an agency holding a certificate of environmental compatibility and public need from the power siting board for constructing an electric transmission line and associated facilities or gas pipeline and its associated facilities."
Legal experts have warned that the change could mean a transmission developer, like a power company, would be able to seize land to be used for a data center or a facility that would power one. The writing has been on the wall for a while, too, after it was discovered in June that the Ohio Business Roundtable trade group recommended that lawmakers change eminent domain law to "extend possession authority to energy infrastructure projects once public use and necessity have been established.”
This follows a July 2026 report that the government was able to seize private land for new transmission lines needed to power new data centers. The law gives the government the power to take private land without the need for the owner's consent, so long as it is for public use and the owner receives appropriate compensation. The government can also delegate the same land-grabbing power to “private entities or common carriers,” which includes utility companies.
This is already happening, too. Earlier this year, the largest utility company in Georgia required the removal of 30 residential properties in order to upgrade its grid. Residents claimed that the expansion was to power AI data centers, a fact given more weight by the fact that one such data center was located just a few miles away.
Despite this, eminent domain law can still be used for good. Nashville set out to use the same law to block the building of a 69,220-square-foot single-story data center next to a zoo. Nashville Metro Council approved the use of eminent domain as a way to buy the land from a local developer who planned the $700 million data center buildout.

articles.title: Paytm public-market investors earn 1.7x returns in five years as shares hit record high
articles.text:
Paytm public-market investors earn 1.7x returns in five years as shares hit record high
An analysis of the company's shareholder base shows that public investors have collectively acquired around 41.5 crore shares at a weighted average price of Rs 1,092 apiece.
Public shareholders in One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm, have earned returns of approximately 1.7 times their investment over the past five years, as the fintech company's shares climbed to a new high, reflecting a significant expansion in public ownership and institutional participation since its stock market debut.
An analysis of the company's shareholder base shows that public investors have collectively acquired around 41.5 crore shares at a weighted average price of Rs 1,092 apiece. Based on the National Stock Exchange's closing price of Rs 1,903 on November 17, 2026, this translates into an annualised return of approximately 17%.
The stock closed at Rs 1,888.30 on Wednesday.
The calculation includes both investors who subscribed to Paytm's initial public offering (IPO) in November 2021 and those who subsequently purchased shares from pre-IPO shareholders in the secondary market.
However, investors who received shares in the IPO at Rs 2,150 apiece are still trading at approximately 0.9 times their initial investment, underscoring the difference between returns for the original IPO allotment cohort and those for public-market investors who entered at lower prices.
The analysis, based on NSE and BSE block deals, bulk deals and disclosed open-market transactions, also shows that pre-IPO shareholders have sold approximately 34.6 crore shares since listing at a weighted average price of Rs 832 apiece.
At the November 17 closing price, these shares are valued at around 2.3 times their average selling price, translating into an annualised return of approximately 40.4% for investors who acquired them at the reported average price.
Paytm's shareholder composition has undergone a significant shift since its market debut, with the company's free float increasing from around 15% at listing in 2021 to approximately 68%.
Domestic institutional ownership has also risen substantially, increasing from 1.3% in September 2022 to 29.5% in September 2026.
Mutual funds now hold around 21.2% of the company's equity, while insurance companies account for another 6.2%, indicating a larger institutional presence in its shareholder base.
The increase in institutional participation comes as Paytm has worked through regulatory and business challenges while focusing on its core payments operations, merchant ecosystem and financial services distribution.
Under founder and Chief Executive Vijay Shekhar Sharma, the company has continued to invest in technology, expand its merchant network and strengthen its financial services offerings, alongside efforts to improve operational efficiency and build a more sustainable business model.
Paytm's operating performance has also improved, with the company reporting six consecutive quarters of profitability.
For the second quarter of FY27, the company reported revenue of Rs 2,648 crore, up 28% year-on-year, while EBITDA increased 90% to Rs 270 crore. Its EBITDA margin reached 10% for the first time, while profit after tax stood at Rs 225 crore.
The improvement in financial performance reflects higher operating leverage and the company's continued focus on profitable growth, as it seeks to strengthen its position in India's digital payments and financial services market.
The expansion in domestic institutional ownership and the rise in public shareholding mark a significant change in Paytm's investor profile since its listing.

articles.title: Amazon lanzó un nuevo Kindle Colorsoft por 299,99 euros, pero este otro cuesta la mitad y es la compra inteligente este Black Friday
articles.text:
Dentro de apenas una semana tendrá lugar, como cada año, el Black Friday, en la que se espera que sea la mayor campaña de rebajas de todo 2026. Pero muchas tiendas ya han comenzado sus Black Friday anticipados y no hace falta esperar al viernes 27 de noviembre para aprovechar toda clase de chollos.
Kindle Colorsoft de Amazon 16 GB
Amazon es una de ellas. Porque aunque no será hasta esta medianoche cuando dará su pistoletazo de salida al Black Friday 2026, ya tiene rebajados algunos dispositivos propios como los lectores Kindle. Y entre ellos, el modelo Colorsoft de la pasada generación tiene ahora su mejor precio hasta la fecha: 164 euros.
Con pantalla a color y 16 GB de capacidad
Decimos "de la pasada generación" porque recientemente Amazon renovó parte de su catálogo de lectores Kindle, entre los que se encuentra una revisión del Colorsoft: algo más fino pero prácticamente idéntico en especificaciones al anterior Colorsoft. Black November: Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro para poliatletas tem mega desconto
Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro tem corpo de titânio e suporta mais de 100 atividades esportivas; smartwatch atinge o 2.º menor preço de 2026 em oferta da Amazon no Pix
O Watch GT 6 Pro está saindo por apenas R$ 1.330 no Pix na Amazon. O smartwatch da Huawei, com corpo de titânio e suporte a mais de 100 atividades físicas, atinge o 2.º menor preço de 2026, com desconto de 47% sobre o original de R$ 2.499 durante a Black November.
O Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro é bem parecido com o novo GT 7 Pro, com diferenças incrementais. O modelo de 2026 possui uma pulseira mais confortável e um melhor acabamento no bisel com cerâmica, em comparação ao seu antecessor.
O GT 6 Pro suporta mais de 100 modalidades diferentes contra mais de 110 do GT 7 Pro, que inclui novos esportes como golfe e esqui. De resto, os sensores de ambos suportam funções de qualidade de vida, como eletrocardiograma (ECG), monitores do sono e da oxigenação no sangue (SpO2).
Este wearable também pode ser essencial em momentos críticos. Ele inicia uma contagem caso detecte uma emergência médica e, se o usuário não se recuperar sozinho, pode ligar para números de emergência como 190 (polícia) e 192 (ambulância), mas precisa estar pareado a um celular.
A tela AMOLED de 1,47″ do Watch GT 6 Pro possui brilho de até 3.000 nits, reproduzindo imagens com cores excelentes e visibilidade garantida. O vidro Cristal de Safira protege o display contra pancadas e arranhões.
Seu corpo em liga de titânio de 46 mm recebe certificação IP69 e 5 ATM, que o permite ser usado em esportes aquáticos. A bateria de 867 mAh resiste a até 21 dias de uso moderado e 12 dias no modo normal, segundo a Huawei, e suporta carregamento sem fio de 10 W.
O Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro (apenas R$ 1.330 no Pix) possui conectividade Bluetooth 6.0 e GPS multibanda, que determina a posição exata do usuário em tempo real.

articles.title: I spoke with our GTA 6 reviewer about the game’s “unbelievable” immersive audio, and these are the soundbars I’d recommend for getting the very best out of your escapades in Vice City on PS5 or XBox
articles.text:
‘You want to be immersed in it as you would be in an IMAX movie’: a soundbar can totally bring the sprawling soundscape of GTA 6 to life, and these are the models I’d recommend — with options for every budget from JBL, Sony, and more
Turn up that radio
Grand Theft Auto 6 is here, and it’s accomplished the extremely daunting task of meeting our steep expectations after an epic 13-year-long wait, earning a perfect five-star review from us here at TechRadar Gaming.
Now that its release date has finally arrived, millions of people are finally getting started with the game, but I spoke with someone who’s already had the chance to sink countless hours into Rockstar’s smash hit. TechRadar Gaming’s Managing Editor, Rob Dwiar, penned our GTA 6 review, and we sat down to discuss everything from the game’s technical performance to its standout moments.
But there was one topic that we kept coming back to: its incredible sound design. In a title filled with crazy car chases, bustling urban zones, and rich natural areas, you’d really hope that the audio makes you feel a part of the world, and Rob felt it did just that.
The absorbing audio of GTA 6 seemed to be crucial to his enormously enjoyable experience with the game, something that became apparent as he recounted high-octane car chase segments. “There have been multiple times where things like knowing where sirens and the cops are coming from when travelling at high speeds around the city has been really key when trying to plan an escape to get out of trouble fast”.
But even if you fail in doing so, and find yourself in a spot of bother, Rob told me that weapon noises engage you in the action far more than they did in Grand Theft Auto 5. “There’s a lot of the best of Red Dead Redemption 2’s audio in that respect,” he said. “Car engines, noises, screeches, smash-ups, and the destruction of scenery — they are in the audio itself rather than just a subject of it”.
With Dolby Atmos audio available for Xbox players and Tempest 3D Audio harnessed for the PS5 version, we cannot understate the sheer scale and depth of the sound available in GTA 6. Indeed, Rob told me, “There’s lots going on, which is great, but you want to make sure you hear everything…it’s cinematic, and you want to be immersed in it as you would be in an IMAX movie”.
But how can you make sure that you truly “hear everything”, as is Rob's recommendation, and get the very best out of your time with the game? Well, for me, one of the greatest options available is a soundbar.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
You don’t want to miss out on the spacious sound of GTA 6, and you certainly don’t want tinny audio when bumping tunes on the radio — something that your basic TV speakers will likely subject you to. So, I’ve compiled a list of the best soundbars for GTA 6 by combining Rob's thoughts on the audio and sound design of the game with my own years of testing audio-visual gear, with plenty of amazing options for everyone — no matter your budget. Without further ado, then, let’s get right into my top picks.
The best soundbars for GTA 6: my personal recommendations
1. The budget-friendly bar: Sony HT-SF150
I can’t even count the number of times I’ve recommended this soundbar on both hands — and if I could, I’d have an alarmingly high number of fingers.
The Sony HT-SF150 (known as the Sony HT-S100F in the US) is a budget soundbar done right in every sense. Rather than attempting to cram the fanciest features, like Dolby Atmos support or ultra-powerful bass, into a cheap and compact package, it mainly focuses on the fundamentals — which it gets absolutely spot on.
You’ll never have to second-guess what Lucia or Jason say thanks to this soundbar’s excellent handling of dialogue, and there are plenty of sound modes, including a Night option for playing in the early hours of the morning. And although this unit won’t provide palpable bass, I was impressed with the quality of its low-end output thanks to the built-in bass reflex speaker, which will give a bit more oomph to explosions than your basic TV sound.
One of my favorite things about this model, though, is its use of Sony’s S-Force Front Surround virtual processing, which endeavors to emulate “cinema-style surround sound”. This is great for adding a bit more width to the sound of GTA 6’s vibrant world, and will help the soundbar to map the movement of the on-screen chaos more effectively.
This soundbar is often available for less than $100 / £100, and it’s far better than most of the competition in this price range, so if you want to upgrade your audio setup for GTA 6 without breaking the bank, this is the model to go for.
2. The sonically stellar step-up: Klipsch Flexus Core 100
As much as I love the previous entry, it's admittedly an entry-level option, so why don’t we take things up a notch, eh? And the Klipsch Flexus Core 100 feels like a very natural step-up.
You can often scoop this one up for less than $300 / £300, which is still relatively affordable. But there are a lot of big improvements to be found here, including Dolby Atmos support and considerably stronger bass output.
Yes, when I tested the Klipsch Flexus Core 100, I was wowed by this lil’ soundbar's seismic bass output, with a deep rumble that filled every inch of our testing room. Its powerful bass will be excellent for GTA 6’s firefights, but also for its soundtrack, as Rob explained: “Background music during missions can be quite synthy with prominent beats and bass, and this complements the action really, really nicely — especially when you’re going through, sneaking about or breaking into places”.
Powerful bass never comes at the expense of crystal-clear dialogue, though, and Atmos effects are well-replicated considering the absence of dedicated up-firing drivers. This means that you may not get the almost-tangible height effects that a soundbar with ‘true’ Atmos provides, but the Flexus Core 100 still plates up sound with delicious depth and multi-dimensionality.
3. The premium yet compact option: Sonos Beam Ultra
This next entry currently reigns supreme in our guide to the best soundbars, and for good reason. The Sonos Beam Ultra is, without doubt, one of the greatest soundbars I’ve had the pleasure of testing, offering a brilliant blend of cinematic sound, exquisite design, and wonderful value for money.
Like the previous two entries, this soundbar is still a compact, single-box model, but it provides a huge jump in quality. First of all, the Beam Ultra has dedicated up-firing drivers, meaning you get true Atmos, and the verticality of sound — as well as the width — that this soundbar provides is absolutely sensational. It's perfect for truly immersing yourself in the shenanigans of Vice City.
For such a small soundbar, the bass on offer is astonishing. Whether I was gaming or watching Dolby Atmos movies, I was stunned by the bar’s ability to reach down to the deepest depths with a confident and regimented delivery.
The Beam Ultra can also get seriously loud while still maintaining its composure with movies and music alike, which is ideal for an audio-visual spectacle like GTA 6. Rob spoke to me about a particular montage that's teamed with a famous Dire Straits song, where visual and audio are matched perfectly to the song's beats, and this, he said, is “something you can’t imagine listening to quietly”.
This soundbar is incredibly feature-rich, with a top-class speech enhancement mode, Wi-Fi streaming for high-res music listening, and a companion app for adjusting height effects, EQ, and more. Sure, at $699 / £699 / AU$1,099, it’s by no means cheap, but there aren’t many soundbars in this price category that get close to the Beam Ultra in terms of all-round quality.
4. The multi-box maestro: Samsung HW-Q800F
As amazing as the Sonos Beam Ultra is, it’s still a single-box solution — but what if you want to take things further? Well, the Samsung HW-Q800F could be the perfect pick, as it also delivers sublime sound and Dolby Atmos capabilities, and packs in a separate sub.
With a standalone sub, you’ll feel like you’re playing GTA 6 in a movie theater — forget the living room. The sub packs in almighty low-end power, giving every bass hit, blast, and thump serious venom. Said sub is also paired right out of the box, so you won’t have any confusing set-up processes to sift through.
Beyond its raucous bass, the HW-Q800F is a marvel. It supports both Dolby Atmos and DTS:X and whips up an imposing sense of space, with the noise of gunfire sure to sound as if it's firing into the corners of your room as you play. That’s perfect for the moments where you want to be aware of cops running up on you, or simply want to enjoy the gorgeous sounds of nature in wild areas.
Something else that this 5.1.2 channel model has over the aforementioned entries is HDMI passthrough. This means that you can plug your PS5 or Xbox directly into the soundbar without any trade-offs to picture or audio — a big plus given that you’ll already be taking up a precious HDMI slot to use the soundbar itself.
Mix in some awesome customization options in the SmartThings app, surprisingly strong music playback over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, and the ability to pair compatible surround speakers, and the Samsung HW-Q800F is more than worthy of the five-star score I bestowed upon it. Despite a seemingly high launch price, you can often find it now for less than $600 / £500 — bargain!
5. The ultimate surround sound system: JBL Bar 1300MK2
It's all been building to this: the most luxurious, powerful, three-dimensional, and glorious soundbar on this list: the JBL Bar 1300MK2.
This soundbar is one of the most feature-rich, sonically gifted systems that money can buy, with a main soundbar, sub, and detachable rear speakers which are fully wireless (and can even be used as standalone Bluetooth speakers). It’s the most powerful soundbar I’ve tested by a mile, with a gargantuan maximum power output of almost 2,500W across a total of 29 drivers.
When it comes to surround sound performance, this model is hard to beat, with top-tier Atmos effects and MultiBeam 3.0 technology, which uses beamforming and digital processing to create ultra-immersive audio.
Again, there’s a Night mode, which uses the detachable speakers for late-night gaming sessions; there are loads of connectivity options for playing GTA 6 or listening to music; and there are loads of ways to personalize sound to your specific tastes in the soundbar’s companion software.
This bar supplies rippling bass, word-perfect dialogue, and has a great handling of dynamics for more sudden in-game sounds. It’s also amazing for music, which Rob would undoubtedly appreciate, as he shared that his favorite moments from GTA 6 came from “listening to 80s music while driving around at night under the neon lights”.
As our sit-down came to an end, Rob told me that GTA 6 is “one of the coolest games I’ve ever played, one of the most technically accomplished games I’ve ever played, and one of the best games I’ve ever played”. So, if you want that generational experience to truly blossom, then the JBL Bar 1300MK2 is all you need. I’ve spotted it going for less than $1,200 / £1,200 lately, and for the sheer versatility, might, and talent of this model, it's worth every last penny.
I'm a Senior Reviews Writer here at TechRadar, where I cover a blend of audio-visual gear as well as the latest gaming software and hardware releases.
I've spent years testing soundbars and have reviewed everything from compact budget-friendly models to premium multi-box surround sound systems, meaning I know exactly what makes a standout model.
All of the soundbars in this list have been tested by me personally in our dedicated TV testing space at Future Labs, so they've truly had to impress me to earn a spot on this list.
Rob is the Managing Editor of TechRadar Gaming and Streaming. He joined in 2023 as the Deputy Editor of TechRadar Gaming (TRG), and was a Commissioning Editor and writer at sister-site GamesRadar+ for nearly five years before then, and has multiple years of games media and games writing experience under his belt, with a variety of bylines at games publications, but also in the world of gardens and landscapes.
He has spent around 100 hours playing Grand Theft Auto 6 and wrote our review, awarding it a five-star rating. You'll find his thoughts on the sonic wonders of Rockstar's blockbuster hit scattered throughout this guide.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
Harry is a Senior Reviews Writer for TechRadar. He reviews everything from party speakers to wall chargers and has a particular interest in the worlds of audio and gaming. Harry has a background in business tech journalism, particularly around the telecoms industry.

articles.title: Java4Shell: qué pueden hacer los usuarios para proteger sus cuentas ante la falla que afecta a bancos y grandes empresas
articles.text:
Una vulnerabilidad en Java conocida como Java4Shell obligó a empresas, organismos públicos y proveedores tecnológicos a revisar sus sistemas, pero los usuarios pueden reducir el riesgo de fraudes al actualizar sus aplicaciones, evitar enlaces sospechosos y controlar los movimientos de sus cuentas.
La falla, registrada como CVE-2026-114938, está en una función de OpenJDK que procesa información codificada en Base64, un formato habitual en inicios de sesión, cargas de archivos e intercambios de datos entre servicios. En determinadas condiciones, un atacante podría provocar la exposición de información almacenada en la memoria de una aplicación o ejecutar código de forma remota.
El problema fue divulgado el 17 de noviembre y Oracle publicó parches de seguridad para las versiones afectadas. La vulnerabilidad puede alcanzar sistemas empresariales que usan Java, entre ellos plataformas de gestión, servidores y herramientas de autenticación. Sin embargo, no hay reportes públicos de ataques que ya hayan aprovechado esta falla.
La actualización de Java corresponde a las empresas que administran los sistemas
Para una persona que usa una aplicación bancaria, una billetera digital o un servicio de salud, la corrección técnica no depende de instalar manualmente Java en el celular. El parche debe aplicarlo la organización que opera los servidores y las aplicaciones afectadas.
La vulnerabilidad impacta en ciertas versiones de OpenJDK ejecutadas en equipos con procesadores x86-64 que cuentan con una función específica de aceleración. Los dispositivos con arquitectura ARM64 no estarían alcanzados por esa condición. Además, la posibilidad de un ataque depende de cómo cada aplicación recibe y procesa datos externos.
En consecuencia, la prioridad para bancos, empresas y organismos consiste en identificar sus sistemas expuestos, actualizar el entorno de Java y comprobar que las aplicaciones vuelvan a iniciarse con las versiones corregidas. Las recomendaciones oficiales incluyen revisar también componentes de Java incorporados en contenedores, dispositivos y programas de terceros.
Mantener actualizadas las apps reduce riesgos derivados de una brecha
Aunque Java4Shell se concentra en infraestructura corporativa, los incidentes de seguridad pueden abrir la puerta a campañas de engaño contra clientes. Por eso, una primera medida es instalar las actualizaciones disponibles para el sistema operativo y para las aplicaciones financieras desde las tiendas oficiales o los canales de cada entidad.
Las personas deben evitar archivos de instalación enviados por correo electrónico, mensajes de texto o WhatsApp. Una actualización de un banco o una billetera virtual debe descargarse desde Google Play, App Store o el sitio oficial del proveedor, no desde un enlace recibido de forma inesperada.
También conviene activar las actualizaciones automáticas cuando el dispositivo lo permita. Esa configuración no soluciona una vulnerabilidad en los servidores de una empresa, pero reduce la exposición a fallas presentes en las aplicaciones que se usan a diario.
Los mensajes sobre una “actualización urgente” pueden usarse para robar datos
Los ciberdelincuentes suelen aprovechar noticias sobre fallas conocidas para dar credibilidad a campañas de suplantación de identidad. Un correo o mensaje que mencione Java4Shell, un supuesto bloqueo preventivo o la necesidad de “validar” una cuenta puede buscar que la víctima entregue sus datos de acceso.
Un banco no debe solicitar por mensaje una contraseña, un código de verificación, el número completo de una tarjeta ni la clave de un token. Tampoco corresponde instalar programas de acceso remoto por indicación de una persona que se presenta como representante de una entidad.
Ante una comunicación que parezca urgente, lo más seguro es no responder ni abrir los enlaces incluidos. Para verificar si existe un aviso real, hay que ingresar por cuenta propia a la aplicación oficial, escribir la dirección del banco en el navegador o llamar a los números publicados por la entidad.
Revisar consumos y transferencias permite detectar operaciones ajenas
Activar alertas por compras, transferencias y accesos a la cuenta ayuda a identificar movimientos que el titular no reconoce. También es recomendable revisar con frecuencia los últimos consumos de tarjetas, las transferencias realizadas y los datos de contacto registrados en la cuenta.
Si aparece una operación desconocida, el usuario debe comunicarse de inmediato con el banco o la billetera a través de un canal oficial. Según el caso, podrá pedir el bloqueo de la tarjeta, desconocer el movimiento y cambiar sus credenciales desde la aplicación o el sitio legítimo.
La contraseña debe ser única, extensa y diferente de la utilizada en otros servicios. Cuando esté disponible, es conveniente habilitar la verificación en dos pasos. Esa medida no reemplaza los controles de la entidad, pero añade una barrera si una clave queda expuesta en una filtración o un engaño.
No hay confirmación pública de ataques que exploten Java4Shell
La empresa de ciberseguridad Calif probó escenarios de ejecución remota de código en aplicaciones empresariales como Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak y JFrog Artifactory. No obstante, los investigadores señalaron que no existe una técnica única que funcione contra todos los sistemas: el método depende de la aplicación, su configuración y el hardware donde se ejecuta.
La falla recibió una calificación de 9,2 sobre 10 según el sistema CVSS 4.0 empleado por Calif, mientras que Oracle la evaluó con 8,1 sobre 10 bajo CVSS 3.1. La diferencia responde a las metodologías de medición, aunque ambas valoraciones refuerzan la necesidad de que las organizaciones apliquen el parche.
Para los usuarios, la recomendación central es mantener las aplicaciones al día, no entregar credenciales por mensajes y actuar con rapidez ante cualquier aviso o movimiento inusual. Mientras las compañías revisan sus entornos de Java, esas precauciones pueden limitar los fraudes que suelen acompañar a los incidentes de ciberseguridad.

articles.title: Best Buy sells Blu-rays online and in-store again
articles.text:
Best Buy is selling Blu-rays directly through its website and in physical stores again after exiting Blu-ray and DVD sales in 2023.
The Best Buy website’s movie section currently lists 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) that are “sold & shipped by Best Buy.” New titles available include The Odyssey (2026), Project Hail Mary (2026), Supergirl (2026), Super Mario Galaxy (2026), and Obsession (2025). Best Buy is also selling some older titles on Blu-ray, including It’s a Wonderful Life (1943), Saving Private Ryan (1998), and The Godfather (1972).
Most of the Blu-rays are available for purchase online and can be delivered to an address or picked up at a Best Buy store within a few days. As of this writing, The Odyssey appears to be in stock at Best Buy stores, as it’s currently listed as available for pickup within as little as an hour.
Ars Technica reached out to Best Buy to ask whether customers can expect the store to continue selling Blu-rays moving forward.
In October 2023, Best Buy announced that it would stop selling Blu-rays and DVDs online and in stores starting in 2024.
“To state the obvious, the way we watch movies and TV shows is much different today than it was decades ago. Making this change gives us more space and opportunity to bring customers new and innovative tech for them to explore, discover and enjoy,” a Best Buy spokesperson said in a statement issued at the time.
Last year, the Best Buy website started selling Blu-rays and DVDs from third parties via its online marketplace.
Numerous other companies have reduced or ended their Blu-ray and/or DVD businesses in recent years. Target, for instance, only sells the discs in stores during special occasions (like holidays or for big releases) now. Disney outsourced its DVD and Blu-ray business to Sony, which subsequently stopped selling recordable Blu-rays to people, and DVD rental company Redbox went out of business.

articles.title: WhatsApp veut vous faire oublier Google Drive, mais son offre gratuite risque de vous laisser sur votre faim
articles.text:
WhatsApp va bientôt proposer son propre espace de sauvegarde en ligne, avec 2 Go seulement à la clé.
Les développeurs de WhatsApp ne manquent pas d’inspiration pour améliorer leur produit. Récemment, ils ont créé un accès express aux médias récents, qui n’a pas reçu l’accueil escompté. Ils ont également testé un outil de retouche IA sur iPhone et lancé un réglage pour permettre aux utilisateurs d’avoir un meilleur contrôle sur la visibilité de leur numéro de téléphone. Un nouveau projet, déjà évoqué en avril dernier, prend enfin forme sur Android.
WhatsApp tourne le dos à Google Drive
WABetaInfo a repéré dans la version bêta 2.26.46.4 de WhatsApp une petite nouveauté qui devrait faire grand bruit : il est désormais possible de sauvegarder son historique d’échanges directement dans les serveurs de l’application. Pour l'instant seule une poignée de testeurs a accès à cette nouvelle fonctionnalité. Elle devrait être proposée plus largement dans les prochaines semaines. Aucune date précise n’a toutefois été dévoilée.
La nouvelle option se cache sur l’écran de sauvegarde des discussions : elle donne à l’utilisateur le choix d’utiliser Google Drive ou le stockage de WhatsApp. Ce dernier peut changer d’avis à tout moment.
WhatsApp mise plus que jamais sur la sécurité. Le chiffrement de bout en bout doit être activé dès la première copie et il est impossible de le désactiver. Le dispositif s’appuie sur une clé d’accès, mais on peut aussi passer par une clé de 64 chiffres, si cette solution ne nous convient pas. En procédant ainsi, ni WhatsApp ni Meta ne peuvent consulter le contenu de ces archives. On ne va pas s’en plaindre.
Une capacité de stockage un peu légère
Côté capacité de stockage, WhatsApp se montre un peu radin : l’application fournit seulement 2 Go aux utilisateurs gratuits. C’est bien loin des 15 Go proposés par un compte Google, même s'ils sont partagés entre Drive, Gmail et Google Photos. Les abonnés payants sont mieux lotis : ceux qui possèdent un abonnement WhatsApp Plus bénéficient de 100 Go d’espace disponible et les formules Meta One vont jusqu’à 4 To.
- Chiffrement de bout en bout.
- Appels audio et vidéo gratuits.
- Compatibilité multiplateforme.
Une autre information qui a son importance : ceux qui souhaitent renoncer à leur forfait payant auront 4 mois pour récupérer leurs sauvegardes. Quand ce délai sera passé, les archives disparaîtront définitivement si aucun renouvellement n’est intervenu entre-temps.
Derrière ce pied de nez à Google, on devine que Meta recherche surtout une nouvelle stratégie de monétisation pour sa messagerie instantanée. Les utilisateurs mordront-ils à l’hameçon ? L’avenir nous le dira.

articles.title: Epic Games Store regala un simulador de maquinaria pesada para PC: cómo descargarlo gratis
articles.text:
Epic Games Store permite descargar gratis para PC Contractor: The Clean Up Part II, un simulador de maquinaria pesada que normalmente cuesta 4,49 euros. La promoción estará activa hasta el miércoles 2 de diciembre a las 11:00, hora peninsular española, y el juego quedará asociado de forma permanente a la cuenta que lo reclame dentro de ese plazo.
Cuál es el nuevo juego gratuito en Epic Games Store
Contractor: The Clean Up Part II es un juego de simulación para una persona centrado en el manejo de maquinaria pesada. Sus tareas se desarrollan en antiguas fábricas, instalaciones industriales y obras con estructuras derrumbadas, donde cada encargo exige retirar residuos y recuperar el aspecto del entorno.
La experiencia se apoya en la física de los materiales y en el control de los vehículos. El objetivo no consiste en superar rivales ni en cumplir una misión bajo presión de tiempo. Cada zona puede limpiarse con calma, a través de una sucesión de trabajos que transforman poco a poco el espacio.
El planteamiento responde a un tipo de videojuego que convierte oficios y actividades cotidianas en una rutina interactiva. La limpieza de una obra o el movimiento de restos de construcción pueden resultar agotadores fuera de la pantalla, pero dentro de un simulador se convierten en una tarea organizada por objetivos y progresos visibles.
La oferta puede servir para descubrir una producción independiente que tendría menos visibilidad entre estrenos de mayor presupuesto. Hace dos semanas, la tienda distribuyó otros 10 juegos mediante una iniciativa similar. Ahora suma esta promoción puntual al catálogo de juegos sin coste.
La promoción estará disponible hasta el 2 de diciembre
El juego puede reclamarse hasta el miércoles 2 de diciembre a las 11:00 en España peninsular. No es necesario instalarlo de inmediato ni tener espacio libre en el computador durante el canje.
La condición principal es completar la adquisición dentro de la fecha anunciada. Una vez que el pedido gratuito se confirma, el título permanece vinculado a la biblioteca personal y podrá descargarse cuando el usuario lo considere oportuno.
Esta fórmula permite conservar el juego aunque se desinstale después o no se ejecute durante meses. Como ocurre con las compras digitales, el acceso corresponde a una licencia asociada a la cuenta de la plataforma, no a una copia física que pueda revenderse.
La promoción no obliga a elegir entre Contractor: The Clean Up Part II y el otro juego gratuito de estrategia disponible durante la semana. Ambos pueden añadirse a la misma biblioteca si se cumplen los plazos de cada oferta.
Cómo descargar gratis el simulador en Epic Games Store
Para reclamar el título es necesario disponer de una cuenta en Epic Games Store. El procedimiento se puede realizar desde la página web de la tienda o desde su cliente para PC.
Los pasos son los siguientes:
- Entrar en Epic Games Store e iniciar sesión.
- Buscar Contractor: The Clean Up Part II o localizarlo en la sección de ofertas.
- Abrir la ficha del juego y comprobar que aparece con un descuento del 100%.
- Pulsar el botón “Obtener”.
- Completar la confirmación del pedido gratuito.
- Revisar que el título quede guardado en la biblioteca.
Si el precio figura como cero, el proceso no requiere introducir un método de pago. Tras la confirmación, el juego estará disponible para su descarga e instalación desde el cliente de Epic Games Store.
Las ofertas gratuitas refuerzan el catálogo de PC
Las tiendas digitales han convertido las promociones temporales en una vía para ampliar bibliotecas sin compras inmediatas. En el caso del PC, este modelo coincide con un mercado que ofrece configuraciones de hardware ajustables y tecnologías como DLSS de Nvidia y FSR de AMD, orientadas a adaptar el rendimiento y la resolución a cada equipo.
También influye la llegada de juegos antes exclusivos de consola. Microsoft y PlayStation han llevado parte de sus lanzamientos a computadoras, lo que amplía las opciones del público que prefiere jugar en PC.
En ese contexto, Contractor: The Clean Up Part II añade una propuesta de simulación a la colección de Epic Games Store. El canje estará disponible hasta el 2 de diciembre; después de esa hora, volverá a aplicarse su precio habitual de 4,49 euros.

articles.title: La NASA va a estrenar el telescopio Roman por todo lo alto y te ofrece que adoptes uno de los píxeles de sus primeras imágenes
articles.text:
El pasado 30 de agosto, la NASA lanzó con éxito el Nancy Grace Roman, el telescopio que pretende convertirse en el detective de la materia oscura. Desde entonces, todo ha sido una sucesión de buenas noticias. Cada maniobra fue mucho más precisa que en el mejor de los escenarios previstos, por lo que ahorró combustible para 12 años adicionales. Las primeras imágenes de prueba que se enviaron a medida que calibraba sus instrumentos tuvieron un rendimiento muy bueno, a pesar de no haber alineado aún todos sus espejos.
En general, el Roman, como se le conoce coloquialmente, ha superado todas las expectativas que había sobre él. Por eso, la NASA espera con emoción sus primeras imágenes oficiales. Tal es la emoción que se ha propuesto compartirlas con el mundo entero e incluso ofrecer a quien lo desee adoptar uno de sus píxeles. No es broma, quédate con esta información.
7 de diciembre. Esa es la fecha en la que la NASA presentará las primeras imágenes públicas del telescopio Roman. Será durante la reunión anual de la Unión Geofísica Americana (AGU), en San Francisco, pero el anuncio podrá verse en directo tanto en las plataformas online de la NASA como en los canales de la AGU. Será a las 15:30 del este de Estados Unidos (21:30, hora peninsular española). Una vez finalizado el anuncio, las imágenes se publicarán de forma permanente en la web de la NASA. Un día después, la NASA hará una presentación para medios de comunicación, en la que dará más información sobre las imágenes.
Mano a mano con el Hubble. El Nancy Grace Roman tiene un campo de visión mucho más amplio que el del Hubble. Eso le permite cartografiar una región de cielo mucho mayor de un solo vistazo, por lo que le será mucho más fácil encontrar puntos interesantes de estudio. No obstante, esto no deja obsoleto al Hubble, sino todo lo contrario. El veterano telescopio espacial, con su campo más pequeño, puede apuntar a una zona concreta y observarla en otras longitudes de onda, como el ultravioleta, que el Roman no cubre. Por eso, si el Roman encuentra, por ejemplo, una lente gravitacional de interés, los científicos podrán recurrir al Hubble (o a otros telescopios como el James Webb) para analizar esas coordenadas con más detalle.
Organiza tu propio evento. La NASA anima a la comunidad internacional a organizar eventos para emitir el anuncio de las primeras imágenes del Roman. Puedes verlas en la comodidad de tu sofá, pero quizás un planetario o museo de ciencias de tu ciudad decida organizar una actividad para que muchas personas puedan verlo y asombrarse juntas.
Adopta tu píxel. En otro intento más de hacer partícipe a la sociedad de este gran hito, la NASA ha puesto en marcha una iniciativa para adoptar píxeles de la primera imagen que se emita del Nancy Grace Roman. Si quieres el tuyo, solo tienes que entrar a este enlace y dar tu nombre, apellidos y correo electrónico. Inmediatamente recibirás un certificado de la adopción. Además, el correo que proporciones se usará para recuperar tu píxel más adelante. Solo se asignará un píxel por email. Yo ya tengo el mío. El número 894.760.
Lógicamente, un píxel de las imágenes es un puntito de la inmensidad del Universo. No se ve nada. Sin embargo, de forma simbólica, puedes decir que posees una mínima parte de la luz captada por el telescopio más esperado de los últimos años. Es emocionante, aunque la imagen completa lo será muchísimo más. No te olvides de conectarte el 7 de diciembre para no perderte el anuncio.

articles.title: Travail et IA : ces métiers où les offres d'emploi se sont effondrées
articles.text:
Derrière les fantasmes de remplacement par des robots, la réalité autour de l’intelligence artificielle et du marché du travail s’avère plus subtile, mais bien réelle. Deux études récentes, menées par France Travail auprès de 16 000 établissements et par le cabinet Coface, révèlent les vraies tendances du marché. Si les patrons privilégient pour l’instant le gain de productivité plutôt que les suppressions de postes, les embauches reculent déjà dans les professions tertiaires.
Des secteurs plus touchés que d’autres par l’IA
Selon France Travail, seuls 6 % des dirigeants prévoient une automatisation importante où l’IA exécuterait la majorité des tâches humaines d’ici cinq ans. En revanche, 35 % des patrons considèrent cette technologie comme un assistant de travail, capable de libérer du temps sur la rédaction, la recherche ou l’analyse. Parmi les métiers les plus touchés, on compte ceux du numérique et des services intellectuels, avec 94 % des ingénieurs informatiques, 83 % des comptables et 75 % des bancassureurs concernés. À l’inverse, le BTP (80 % sans effet), les services aux particuliers (85 %) et la restauration (76 %) ne sont que très peu touchés.
D’après l’étude, cette transition vers l’IA se concentre fortement dans les grandes agglomérations comme l’Île-de-France, le Rhône, la Loire-Atlantique ou la Haute-Garonne. Dans ces bassins d’emploi tertiaires, l’IA générative prend par exemple en charge les tâches administratives répétitives et la saisie de texte ou de données. Les salariés concernés par ces changements réorientent ainsi leur temps vers la prise de décision, la gestion de projets et la relation client.
La baisse notable des offres d’emploi
L’étude mesure également l’impact de l’intelligence artificielle et de ses usages sur l’embauche. Elle indique en effet que pour chaque tranche de 10 % d’exposition d’un métier à l’IA, les annonces sur France Travail chutent de 12,4 % au troisième trimestre. Cela représente 25 000 offres d’emploi en moins sur la période, un chiffre similaire à l’Allemagne (-10,2 %) et la Suède (-10,8 %). La chute la plus spectaculaire est à aller chercher du côté des ressources humaines et du secrétariat, avec des annonces en baisse de respectivement -42,8 % et -40 % depuis 2022.
À lire : Microsoft propose un plan de départ volontaire à 60 000 salariés pour faire des économies
Ce gel des embauches touche les jeunes diplômés, mais ils sont loin d’être les seuls concernés. Les baisses atteignent ainsi 14 % pour les débutants, 19,4 % pour les profils ayant un à deux ans d’expérience et 16 % au-delà de quatre ans. Les entreprises adoptent ainsi plus ou moins rapidement l’IA dans leur processus de travail, sans pour autant supprimer énormément de postes. Ces chiffres étant directement dépendants de l’activité économique des entreprises, les économistes préviennent qu’en cas de récession, cette stagnation pourrait accélérer l’autonomisation de certaines tâches, ce qui aurait un impact important sur l’emploi.

articles.title: Bengaluru leads India in AI startup funding: Innovation Report 2026
articles.text:
Bengaluru leads India in AI startup funding: Innovation Report 2026
$85 billion raised, a growing AI ecosystem and a strong deep-tech pipeline. The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 maps the city's startup growth as Karnataka looks to spread its tech ambitions beyond the capital.
Bengaluru's position as India's technology hub is increasingly being shaped by artificial intelligence and deep tech. The city accounts for 36.3% of the country's native AI startup funding and is home to 71% of India's AI and deep tech unicorns created since 2023.
These findings feature in the Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026, released by Karnataka IT and BT Minister Priyank M. Kharge on November 18 at the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, held at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC).
Prepared by the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) with 3one4 Capital and data from Tracxn, the report examines Bengaluru's startup ecosystem across capital, talent, unicorns, policy and six frontier technology sectors.
AI and deep tech lead the way
Bengaluru has seen 1,556 deep tech startups founded since 2010, of which 1,319 remain active and funded. Together, these companies have raised US$3.77 billion.
The city also has 799 native AI startups, with 764 active and funded. Its share of India's native AI funding is higher than that of any other city.
Bengaluru's overall startup ecosystem has raised approximately US$85 billion since 2010, accounting for 47% of all venture funding raised by Indian startups. The city has 3,810 active, funded startups founded since 2010, compared with 1,982 in Mumbai.
Its 57 unicorns are valued at US$211 billion, representing 44% of India's unicorn count and 55.3% of their combined valuation. Bengaluru is also home to 212 soonicorns, accounting for 36% of India's total.
Capital and exits strengthen ecosystem
The report points to growing participation from domestic investors. Around 52% of capital raised by Category I and II alternative investment funds (AIFs) now comes from domestic investors.
Bengaluru has 75 Category I AIFs, representing 21% of India's total, and around 300 venture capital firms operate in Karnataka.
The city has also recorded 16 Bengaluru-linked company listings since November 2024, together valued at approximately US$42 billion at listing. Startups in the ecosystem take an average of 8.2 years from founding to exit, compared with the global average of 11.1 years.
Women entrepreneurs are another part of the ecosystem. Nearly 30% of India's active, funded women-led startups in deep tech and native AI were founded in Bengaluru. These companies have collectively raised US$323.65 million.
Karnataka looks beyond Bengaluru
The report also examines the State's efforts to expand its technology ecosystem beyond the capital.
Since 2017, the ELEVATE grant-in-aid programme has supported 1,479 startups with Rs 393.58 crore, with 38.6% of the beneficiaries based beyond Bengaluru. Karnataka has also established a Rs 75 crore Beyond Bengaluru Cluster Seed Fund and is developing Global Technology Centres in Mysuru, Hubballi and Belagavi.
The Rs 1,000 crore Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP) aims to generate five lakh jobs over five years.
Releasing the report, Kharge said Karnataka's next priority was to extend its technology strengths to other parts of the State.
"The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 shows how far Karnataka's founders have come and how much more they can build from here. Our next task is to make sure a world-class AI, quantum or semiconductor company can grow just as well in Kalaburagi, Hubballi or Mangaluru," he said.
He added that deep tech requires patient investment and that Karnataka would continue supporting the sector.
Shri Sharath Bachegowda, Chairman of KEONICS, said the findings reaffirm Karnataka's leadership in AI and deep tech while pointing to opportunities to expand innovation across the State.
Dr Manjula N, Secretary of the Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T, said the focus was now on helping startups move from early support to scale through government procurement, patient capital and stronger research commercialisation.
BV Naidu, Chairman of KDEM, said the report offers investors, global capability centres (GCCs) and founders a data-backed view of Karnataka's technology ecosystem.
The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 is available on the KDEM website.

articles.title: Starburst adds context support to give AI agents consistent access to business data definitions - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Starburst adds context support to give AI agents consistent access to business data definitions
Starburst Data Inc. is expanding its data federation platform into business context management with the introduction of Context Studio, a new capability designed to help artificial intelligence agents produce more accurate and trustworthy answers from information distributed across enterprise systems.
Context Studio collects business definitions from existing data catalogs, business intelligence tools, metric stores and documents, making them available alongside data when AI agents respond to prompts. The system is intended to eliminate conflicting definitions that can cause AI agents to produce incorrect results.
The new capability addresses a problem the company encountered as customers began deploying its Aida natural-language data assistant in production environments, said Starburst co-founder and Chief Executive Justin Borgman.
“We’ve found that as you get into production, the biggest issue is context because you need to trust the answers the agent gives back,” he said.
The challenge is particularly acute in large organizations where different departments may use different definitions of common business metrics, such as revenue or active customers. Without a consistent understanding of those terms, AI models can produce plausible but inaccurate answers.
“When those definitions conflict, the [large language model] doesn’t know any better; it’s just going to guess,” Borgman said. “That’s what leads to bad answers and an erosion of trust.”
Data products
Context Studio builds on Starburst’s existing data products architecture, which allows organizations to create curated views spanning multiple data sources. Those products incorporate business definitions, metadata and access controls that can be applied consistently when agents retrieve information.
Unlike conventional semantic layers that require organizations to consolidate definitions within a single platform, Context Studio federates existing definitions without requiring customers to move or rebuild their underlying data.
Built-in approval workflows resolve conflicting definitions, and a feedback mechanism is provided through which agents can propose improvements. Human reviewers approve changes before regression testing checks their impact on other queries.
Borgman characterized the expansion as an evolution of Starburst’s longstanding strategy of querying distributed data without centralizing it.
“We think context is going to live everywhere, just like we think data will live in multiple places,” he said. “Our approach treats [context] as a first-class principle in our design.”
Starburst hasn’t yet disclosed quantitative evidence of Context Studio’s impact on AI accuracy or productivity. The company said it is collecting benchmark data from private preview customers.
The company is also emphasizing traceability to increase confidence in AI-generated answers. Context Studio records which data sources agents access, the SQL queries they generate and the information used to produce responses. Access controls remain attached to underlying data products.
“Context is going to increase the probability of a good answer, but there’s also a need to trace how it got to that answer,” Borgman said.
An agent can interview domain experts to capture business knowledge and convert it into draft data products. Starburst is also extending its Aida data assistant to answer questions across multiple data products and introducing an agent that automatically generates dashboards.
Other platform enhancements include Mission Control for monitoring usage and costs, automated Apache Iceberg maintenance, a bring-your-own-cloud deployment option and graphics processing unit-accelerated querying. Starburst claims its recently introduced Torin query engine delivers up to sevenfold performance improvements in company benchmarks.
Context Studio is available in private preview for Starburst Galaxy and Starburst Enterprise. A public preview is planned for January, with general availability expected in the first quarter of 2027. Pricing hasn’t been finalized.

articles.title: Waymo pulls driverless cars from highways nationwide after California ban
articles.text:
What just happened? Waymo has taken its driverless cars off all limited-access highways in the United States after California regulators ruled that the company's freeway operations posed a danger to the public. The California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the suspension after three Waymo vehicles entered a closed construction zone on Highway 101 and another attempted to pass California Highway Patrol vehicles that were deliberately slowing traffic on Interstate 280. The pullback temporarily ends Waymo's highway operations, nearly a year after the company began offering freeway rides to passengers in the San Francisco Bay Area.
The DMV directive requires Waymo to stop both operating and testing its driverless vehicles on all California freeways, citing "an imminent hazard to public safety." The order will remain in effect until the company takes "effective corrective actions," the agency said. It did not provide a timeline.
Waymo went beyond what the order required. Company spokesman Chris Pappas said the company pulled its vehicles off freeways nationwide that same day. He said the Highway 101 incident "did not involve any injuries or collisions" and that Waymo would review its vehicles' performance while they remain off the highways.
The two incidents highlight areas where the system struggles. On Highway 101, three separate vehicles entered a lane that had been closed for construction. On Interstate 280, a video posted on social media showed a Waymo car attempting to pass two California Highway Patrol vehicles that were deliberately slowing traffic. In both cases, the software had to recognize a temporary change in road conditions, whether construction cones and lane closures or police directing traffic, and respond appropriately while traveling at freeway speeds.
Construction zones have caused problems for Waymo before. In June, the company recalled 4,000 robotaxis for a software update after vehicles in Phoenix and San Francisco drove into work zones. Earlier in the year, it also had to update software in thousands of its vehicles after some drove into flooded roads. In each case, the solution involved a software update to the fleet. California's order now requires Waymo to submit its next fix for regulatory review before its vehicles can return to freeways.
Matthew Wansley, a law professor at Yeshiva University's Cardozo School of Law who studies the regulation of self-driving technology, said that, in principle, freeways are "actually a simpler driving environment than local roads." There are no pedestrians, cyclists or cross traffic to track. Robotaxis have also encountered construction zones and police activity on city streets, he told The New York Times, but the consequences of such incidents are generally less severe.
"When you are doing it at highway speeds, the margin for error is a lot lower," Wansley said. "It's very hard to kill someone at 25 miles per hour. It's very easy to kill someone at 65 miles per hour."
Philip Koopman, a professor emeritus at Carnegie Mellon University who studies autonomous vehicle safety, said the state's response was more forceful than regulators have typically been in dealing with the industry.
"Pulling them back from freeways is more of a firm hand than we've seen before, which is a good thing because these are concerning incidents," Koopman said. Wansley and Koopman both said the restriction should help prevent further accidents and give Waymo time to improve its technology.
The ban also threatens Waymo's growth plans, with airport trips likely to take the biggest hit. Freeways provide the most direct routes to major airports, and Koopman said losing access to them cuts into one of the company's most valuable markets.
"Highways are an issue because they really need to get to airports, and if you can't go on highways, that's a real problem for the airport business," he said. "That's a huge fraction of the value they can unlock."
Riders can still reach the airport using surface streets, although the trip may be less convenient. "You can get to San Francisco airport on surface streets, but it's not a lot of fun," Koopman said.
Waymo has not said when it expects to return its vehicles to freeways, nor has it explained what changes it plans to propose to convince the DMV that its vehicles can safely handle closed lanes and police-directed traffic slowdowns at speeds of 65 miles per hour.

articles.title: Nvidia says it’s ‘absurd’ to assume that company predicted the agentic moment during Vera’s development – ‘product intuition’ helped drive CPU design, superior memory bandwidth will play critical role in future AI agents, CPU head claims
articles.text:
Nvidia says it’s ‘absurd’ to assume it predicted the agentic moment during Vera’s development – ‘product intuition’ helped drive CPU design, superior memory bandwidth will play critical role in future AI agents, CPU boss claims
It turns out Nvidia doesn’t have a crystal ball, either.
One criticism that has emerged of Nvidia’s Vera CPU, driven by AMD, is that Nvidia – and, to a lesser degree, Arm with its AGI CPU – couldn’t have developed an “agentic CPU,” as the chip is often characterized in Nvidia’s marketing materials. Ian Finder, the head of Nvidia’s data center CPU business, pushed back on that criticism in a recent conversation with Tom’s Hardware Premium at SC26, calling the notion that Nvidia somehow knew about the agentic wave four years ago when Vera development began "absurd."
“There's a conviction around the design philosophy of the part, right? Am I going to sit here and tell you that we have this magic crystal ball around the agentic moment? That would be absurd, right?” Finder said. “But what we do have as a company, and I think this has been proven out in our track record, is [that] we have design intuition.”
Instead of specifically designing Vera for agentic workloads, which would be impossible without a way to see several years into the future, Finder characterized the part by its codesign with Nvidia’s accelerators, something that the team has continued to work on since its first Grace data center CPU. Coming from the assumption that data centers and AI workloads are accelerated (and they largely are), Finder says the co-design approach on the CPU can start in a “conceptually simple space, like what kind of CPU do we need to keep the accelerator fed and happy?”
Although conceptually simple, Finder continually looped back to a particular word to describe aspects of Vera and, to a lesser extent, Grace. “Opinionated” is the word he used, which in the broader context of Vera’s design, shows up in two places. Grace, Finder says, introduced an opinionated memory system with Nvidia’s Scalable Coherency Fabric, while Vera extends that memory system while adding an opinionated microarchitecture, Nvidia’s Olympus core.
The picture Finder paints is one of Nvidia starting from scratch in this space, contrasting it with the “legacy constraints” of, presumably, Intel and AMD in particular, who have large pools of customers with specific needs. As we described in our original breakdown of the Olympus architecture in Vera, Nvidia’s goal doesn’t seem to be to steal market share from AMD and Intel, but rather to grab market share in a CPU space that’s vastly accelerating on the back of AI agents.
This “clean sheet of paper” approach, and Nvidia’s codesign, led to some natural assumptions about what the CPU should do. “If we have silicon that needs really, really great single-thread performance, [and] we also need concurrency, then we need to get there with IPC instead of frequency. We need to make sure we have good loaded memory latency. We need to make sure we have a lot of bandwidth, and you start to design something on a clean sheet of paper that's not encumbered by dollar-per-core economics.”
Although Finder was clear that Vera’s design didn’t explicitly center around the agents we see today, there were early indications of the workload. “To say that four years ago, when we started putting pen to paper on Vera, [that] we absolutely saw the agentic moment, would [not] be... something I would claim, but we were starting to see the beginnings of tool calling and things like that. We certainly knew what we needed from a head node, and we knew the overall shape of this problem.”
As you can see in our Vera CPU benchmarking, the chip doesn’t excel at every workload. And, from the data you can see in our recent AMD EPYC Venice benchmarking, the AMD camp has reclaimed some top spots in several benchmarks. Finder suggests that the superior memory bandwidth of Vera will play a much bigger role in the agentic future as these systems evolve to take better advantage of the compute available.
Taking full advantage of the CPU
We need to rewind for just a moment. When the agentic wave hit earlier this year, some characterized the demand as a shift away from GPUs and toward CPUs. That is incorrect. Rather, as is becoming increasingly clear as these agentic workloads progress, these loops can’t take full advantage of the GPUs in a GPU-centric environment, with GPUs often oversubscribed on host nodes. The solution isn’t to get rid of GPUs, of course, nor is it to stop buying them. Rather, it’s to also buy enough CPUs to properly leverage that compute.
A portion of the AI industry is focused on tackling the problem of fully utilizing the GPU, Nvidia included. GPUs shouldn’t sit idle for very long (if at all) with the demand today, and they don’t. The challenge today is spinning up these agent sandboxes quickly, within milliseconds, so that the CPU isn’t sitting idle, either.
Finder provided an example of using a coding agent. If you’ve used a coding agent before, you’re probably familiar with this process. After prompting, the model will make several small tool calls to read and locate files, passing back to the model in between. These are tiny calls, almost negligible, and the vast majority of the time is spent in the model on the GPU. Then, it may start compiling and testing the project, which is much more bound by the CPU. The GPU, Finder says, isn't sitting idle during that time. It’s being leveraged for another purpose. Finder suggests “that very same thing is going to happen on the CPU.”
“The idea that we're just going to say, ‘OK, the CPU can just chill out here, and we're just going to wait,’ that's not going to happen,” Finder said. “What's going to happen is we're going to pack multiple environments together, and we're going to subscribe the socket.”
This “very interesting computer science problem,” as Finder described it, is being investigated by AI startups such as Daytona and E2B to spin up and close down agentic sandboxes in milliseconds. And serving more agents will naturally put pressure on the memory system, which is an area where Vera has an edge. “We built a product that does really, really well without such optimizations, but as a design point that really will lean into them when the industry starts to catch up to this,” Finder said.
Vera is a fascinating chip, regardless of what you think of it and how it’s presented in marketing materials (from Nvidia itself or elsewhere). Although Grace was the starting point internally, Vera has ridden the wave of agentic to become a much bigger player in the world of CPUs, and Nvidia has already announced that it will follow up with its Rosa CPU featuring the new Rigel microarchitecture. Vera is an opinionated CPU indeed, and time will tell if that opinion is correct.
Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

articles.title: ‘Playing Grand Theft Auto can wait until the weekend’: As GTA 6 launch nears, schools are offering pupils prizes to attend as they battle ‘GTA flu’
articles.text:
School offers students prizes to avoid 'GTA flu' outbreak — Xbox and PlayStation gift card draw aims to avoid attendance drops
Low attendance is expected
- GTA 6 arrives tomorrow in the biggest game launch of the year
- Schools are bracing for low attendance numbers as students play the game
- Some schools are offering prizes to encourage pupils to show up
Grand Theft Auto 6 is launching tomorrow, and you can bet people across the globe will be skipping work to enjoy the game as soon as it becomes available. Some schools are worried that pupils will take a similar approach, and they’re taking some pretty unusual steps to ensure attendance, even as GTA 6 threatens to pull excited students away.
According to BBC News, Belfast Boys’ Model school in Northern Ireland is offering students prizes to attend lessons on November 19, with students who turn up on both Thursday and Friday being entered into a draw to win one of two gift cards each worth £70 (about $91) for either Xbox or PlayStation consoles. Entries for the draw will mark International Men’s Health Day and raise money for the charity.
The school sent a letter to parents saying that “activities such as playing Grand Theft Auto can wait until the weekend” and reminding “all parents and carers of the importance of ensuring that students attend school on Thursday 19th November.”
The date is important because it coincides with GCSE math exams for 15- and 16-year-olds, with the school’s letter arguing that “Good attendance is one of the strongest indicators of academic success.” The school evidently wants to avoid a repeat of the so-called “GTA flu” that saw pupils flunk out of school on the day GTA 5 launched in 2013.
Mary Montgomery, principal of Belfast Boys’ Model school, stated that the voucher idea was a “pupil-led incentive.” Students had initially suggested offering GTA 6 itself as a prize, Montgomery said, but this proposal was turned down because the game is 18-rated. Instead, a gift card for two of the best consoles on the market was suggested as an alternative.
And Belfast Boys’ Model school pupil Michael, aged 17, told BBC News that gaming can help young people to “switch off and manage some of the stress around exams, which is important with GCSE modules this week.”
How to pre-load GTA 6
Any students tempted to flunk out for a day or two are hardly alone. Research from Zety claims that one in ten workers plans to take time off to play GTA 6 and breathless headlines proclaim the release could “paralyze the working world” — although not everyone is feeling so credulous.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There’s no need to stay home to download GTA 6 to your console — it can be pre-loaded ahead of time so that it’s ready to play as soon as it unlocks on November 19. As long as you’ve pre-ordered the game and enabled your console’s automatic update and download settings, you’ll be able to enter your activation code and start downloading the game automatically. But at a huge 212GB in size, it’ll take a while to finish, so make sure you give it plenty of time.
Of course, that doesn’t give you a full day of playing the game instead of working or studying, but it at least means that GTA 6 will be ready and waiting for you when you get back home.
With some schools offering incentives to put the controller down for a few hours, we’ll have to see if it’s enough to avoid another outbreak of the dreaded “GTA flu.”

articles.title: 'GTA VI' es monumental y ya hay quien dice que es el mejor juego de la historia. Un juego de 1998 acaba de levantar la ceja
articles.text:
A las horas de escribir estas líneas, ya han salido los análisis de 'GTA VI', y la crítica lo tiene claro: 153 reivews publicadas para una media de 99. Es la más alta de la historia en cuanto a media teniendo en cuenta la cantidad de análisis de los medios que puntúan en Metacritic y si lees los análisis de los principales medios, no tarda en aparecer la reflexión que no sólo es el juego más ambicioso de la historia: es el mejor.
Y, si sólo nos fijamos en la media, así es, pero hay algo que hay que tener en cuenta: 'GTA VI' no es 'The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time'. Sígueme en esto porque te prometo que tiene sentido.
El reflejo de Metacritic
La media es apabullante porque, a estas alturas, 'GTA VI' no es sólo un videojuego: es un evento. Tengo colegas que se pillaron la PS5 de salida pensando en jugar al nuevo 'GTA' (y viendo cómo han subido los precios, creo que les ha valido la pena esperar seis años desde el lanzamiento de PS5 y Xbox Series X).
A nivel publicitario, el título de Rockstar no tiene parangón, y en esos análisis sale a la palestra el hecho de que esos 13 años se sienten reflejados en el título. Puede que no te guste el 'GTA' por los motivos que sean y es perfecto, pero la salida de este juego es un acontecimiento. Mis compas de 3DJuegos se han explayado en su análisis, pero para mí hay otros dos hechos notables:
- Digital Foundry, medio especializado en el apartado visual de los juegos, lo llama "El juego de la generación", alabando un apartado técnico excepcional.
- HobbyConsolas le ha cascado el primer 100 de su historia.
Y mira, puedes estar de acuerdo con los análisis o no, ya que al final son algo subjetivo, pero ocurre lo mismo que con el propio 'GTA VI': es innegable que ha revuelto algo.
Como digo, esta media de 99 ya está haciendo que se hable del mejor juego de la historia y se da por hecho que va a arrasar en unos The Game Awards en los que parte con ocho nominaciones y donde el público ya puede votar por él... sin haberlo jugado.
Pero pese a todo, pese a que un 99 de 153 análisis sea más que un 99 de 22 análisis como el de 'Ocarina of Time' de 1998, ocurre una cosa: 'GTA VI no es 'Ocarina of Time'.
El problema de Metacritic
A nivel de ambición, técnico (algo con fecha de caducidad), magnitud, situación de la industria y casi todos los parámetros que quieras, sí: 'GTA VI' es mastodóntico. Rockstar ha construido inmunerables pisos sobre las bases tan sólidas y ambiciosas que ya tenían en casa como 'GTA V' y, sobre todo, 'Red Dead Redemption 2'.
Es un "más, más, más" y, además, mejor, una expansión 3D como pocas se han visto en este medio, pero una expansión, en definitiva, partiendo de una base que ya estaba ahí. Afirmar que es "el mejor juego de la historia" basándonos sólo en las notas pues sí, no es una mentira, pero ahí es donde vuelvo a mencionar el 'Oracina of Time' de 1998.
En un año en el que la industria seguía peleando con el 3D y el paso a tecnologías extremadamente nuevas, Nintendo parió algo que se convirtió en el estándar de... bueno, de los videojuegos. Había cosas que no tenían referente y que no construían sobre unos cimientos, sino que fueron inventando sobre la marcha y resolviendo problemas que aparecían por el camino.
El modo de seleccionar un enemigo para orbitar a su alrededor en los combates es un ejemplo, pero también el botón contextual que cambia en función de la acción y la situación, la escalada y salto contextuales, el ciclo de día y noche y los eventos asociados a cada etapa, el montar a caballo en un mundo 3D, una guía por el mundo para no depender del minimapa o la vibración del Rumble Pak.
Hubo cosas que pulió de ideas anteriores, claro, pero también mucho que, como digo, fue inventando para resolver los problemas que encontraron a medida que el desarrollo avanzaba. Hay un poco de 'Ocarina of Time' en casi cualquier juego 3D y, rejugando el excepcional remake, me he dado cuenta de todo lo que bebe 'Dark Souls' del juego de Nintendo.
Al final, 'GTA VI' es construir sobre lo que ya existía y llevarlo a una escala monumental, pero 'Ocarina of Time' tuvo una influencia en los videojuegos que es imposible encapsular en una nota. Y lo bueno es que no tenemos que pelear por absurdeces, y este fin de año podemos disfrutar casi a la vez del mejor juego de la historia por nota y del remake del juego que hizo historia.
