articles.title: Han pesado la Vía Láctea con una precisión nunca vista: 1,19 billones de veces la masa del Sol
articles.text:
Pesar la Vía Láctea no es sencillo. Se pueden hacer estimaciones analizando el brillo de las estrellas que la componen. Están bastante bien cartografiadas, así que sería algo alcanzable. Sin embargo, la mayor parte de la masa de nuestra galaxia está compuesta por la enigmática materia oscura, de modo que toda esa masa se quedaría fuera. La alternativa es analizar el movimiento de las estrellas del halo galáctico, ya que este está perturbado por la influencia gravitatoria del conjunto total de la galaxia. Hasta ahora, se habían hecho algunas estimaciones al respecto, pero contaban con un porcentaje de error bastante alto. Sin embargo, una nueva medición, llevada a cabo con datos de DESI y Gaia, ha aportado una cifra muchísimo más precisa.
El equipo perfecto. DESI (Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument) es una colaboración internacional que se encarga principalmente de cartografiar el Universo en 3D para estudiar la energía oscura. Entre sus instrumentos destacan los espectrógrafos, capaces de descomponer la luz proveniente de las estrellas y analizar tanto su composición como parte de su movimiento. Según el efecto Doppler, si la estrella se aleja de nosotros su espectro se desplaza hacia el rojo, mientras que si se acerca lo hace hacia el azul. Por su parte, Gaia es un telescopio europeo que mide con precisión las posiciones de las estrellas a lo largo de los años.
Al poner en común los datos de ambos proyectos se puede analizar el movimiento de las estrellas de una forma muy precisa. Con Gaia analizamos su desplazamiento por el cielo y con DESI se ve si se alejan o se acercan. Todo esto, en conjunto, es lo que ha servido a estos científicos para pesar la Vía Láctea.
Más preciso que nunca. Los autores del preprint que se acaba de publicar analizaron más de 10.000 estrellas distantes observadas por DESI durante sus tres primeros años. Estas se encontraban a distintas distancias, entre unos 30.000 y 310.000 años luz del centro galáctico. Después, combinaron estos datos con los movimientos en el cielo medidos por Gaia de las mismas estrellas.Las estrellas eran de dos tipos: estrellas de la rama horizontal azul (BHB) y estrellas RR Lyrae (RRL). Ambas son estrellas viejas, típicas del halo galáctico, que se encuentran en una fase tardía de su vida, y son muy útiles porque su brillo intrínseco es conocido o muy predecible. Si sabes cuánta luz emite realmente una estrella y mides cuánta luz te llega, la diferencia te dice a qué distancia está.
Con toda esta información sobre las posiciones y velocidades de las estrellas, utilizaron cuatro modelos, previamente calibrados con galaxias simuladas desde cuatro puntos de vista. Esto permitió extrapolar el movimiento de las estrellas a la masa total de la galaxia de una forma bastante precisa.
Los datos. Se calculó que la masa de la Vía Láctea sería de 1,19 billones de masas solares, con una incertidumbre de en torno al 11%. Esto incluye tanto materia oscura como ordinaria. Además, para la materia situada a menos de unos 260.000 años luz del centro, la incertidumbre baja al 8%.
No tan redonda. Los cuatro métodos que se usaron para analizar los datos de las estrellas de la Vía Láctea tienen en cuenta una conformación esférica de la galaxia, ya que eso simplifica mucho los cálculos. Sin embargo, las seis galaxias con las que se calibró eran realistas y, por lo tanto, no esféricas. Dado que las galaxias se habían simulado para la ocasión, los científicos sabían cuál es su masa. Al pasarlas por los modelos, no obtuvieron esa masa, ya que contemplaban una galaxia redonda, por lo que obtuvieron un error. Esa calibración permitió establecer el error que se debe eliminar para obtener los datos realistas cuando se analice la Vía Láctea.
Eso es lo que les ha permitido analizarla con más precisión que nunca; pero, además, les ha dado información útil para futuras investigaciones. De aquí en adelante, nuestra propia galaxia debería contemplarse en los modelos de una forma más realista y, por lo tanto, menos esférica.
En el futuro. Estos científicos esperan afinar la masa del halo exterior con estrellas aún más lejanas y más datos de Gaia. Además, el segundo conjunto de datos de DESI, a partir del que se ha hecho este estudio, será de dominio público pronto, así que cualquier astrónomo podrá contribuir a los cálculos. Quizás en un futuro tengamos mediciones aún mejores. De momento, la que han obtenido ahora es mucho mejor que cualquiera que se haya obtenido jamás.
Imagen |PHILIPPE SERRAND

articles.title: « Je vois tout » : le système testé par l'armée de Terre prédit les déplacements ennemis
articles.text:
Le 152e régiment d'infanterie fabrique désormais ses propres drones et s'est doté d'une section dédiée. Mise à l’épreuve fin juin au camp de Mourmelon, elle illustre la mue de l’armée de Terre face aux nouvelles menaces.
Dans le dernier numéro d'Esprit défense, un magazine du ministère des Armées paru le 16 novembre 2026, une partie est consacrée au fameux 152e régiment d'infanterie, qui dispose désormais de sa propre section drone. Le ministère revient sur ses débuts au camp de Mourmelon, cette année. Le magazine des Armées revient sur un camp d'expérimentation mené en juin et juillet derniers, destiné à valider la transformation engagée par le régiment trois ans plus tôt. Des drones, radars, missiles et industriels étaient réunis, avec l'ambition de mettre l'innovation au service de la victoire.
Ce régiment de l’armée de Terre fabrique désormais ses propres drones
Alors que certains pays « s'engagent sur la voie de la domination », selon les mots du magazine, les unités opérationnelles musclent leur outil de défense, et le 152e RI ne fait pas exception Sa vedette est la Section drone régimentaire (SDR), inaugurée quelques jours avant la manœuvre du 25 juin. Chez les Diables rouges, surnom du 152e RI, elle assure la reconnaissance et la frappe à longue portée. Et tout est allé vite, au régiment comme dans le reste de l'armée de Terre. « Le régiment a acquis son premier drone en 2019. Aujourd'hui, il en fabrique », résume le lieutenant-colonel Benoît, son chef opérations. Le reportage montre aussi des drones FPV, pilotés en immersion totale grâce à une caméra haute définition couplée aux lunettes de l'opérateur, utiles pour la reconnaissance avancée mais aussi pour neutraliser un objectif.
Ce jeudi-là, la compagnie d'appui a une mission. Elle doit arrêter une progression ennemie, à deux kilomètres seulement de la ligne adverse. Le drone du soldat de première classe Landry décolle, et en quelques secondes, un blindé est neutralisé. L'explosif est fictif, exercice oblige, mais le système qui l'emporte a bien été conçu par les dronistes du régiment, une trouvaille maison encouragée par la cellule dédiée à l'innovation. « Notre métier évolue avec son temps », savoure le soldat, qui trouve « exaltant » de participer à ce changement.
Mais il n'est pas question pour autant de tout miser sur la machine. « Le drone seul ne suffit pas pour vaincre », prévient le lieutenant-colonel Benoît. Selon lui, l'engin s'inscrit dans un système de combat global qu'il reste à définir et à ériger en doctrine. Et le matériel ne fait pas le soldat. « L'intégration technologique ne se limite pas à une question d'équipement », insiste l'officier. Il faut former, entraîner, sans sacrifier les savoir-faire fondamentaux du fantassin.
Guerre électronique : quand le radar voit venir l'ennemi
Avant de frapper, vous serez d'accord avec nous pour dire qu'il faut voir. Pour la section de reconnaissance et de guerre électronique (SRGE), l'exercice est lui aussi celui des premières fois. Elle teste le radar à impulsion Murin, doté d'une fonction d'aide au tir, qui détecte une compagnie adverse sur engins blindés à trois kilomètres. Elle teste aussi Vénus, l'interface de pilotage du radar, qui affiche et transmet les informations en temps réel. « Je vois tout », s'exclame le sergent Aymeric, chef de groupe. D'après lui, l'outil estime le type, l'allure et le nombre d'engins, et il « prédit leur déplacement ».
Il faut encore confirmer. Alors, le chef de section fait appel au système Esus, encore en expérimentation, situé à 500 mètres du groupe, qui détecte et sectorise les ondes militaires. Le renseignement est validé, l'ordre de frappe part vers la SDR, c'est la frappe de Landry. Son équipe a tout juste le temps de se replier qu'Esus signale une nouvelle menace, un véhicule de combat d'infanterie armé d'un canon. Un drone Parrot Anafi s'élance d'un abri pour le reconnaître, puis un binôme met en place un missile moyenne portée (MMP). Le missile antichar fait mouche, sous l'œil de tireurs d'élite quasi invisibles, prêts à riposter.
Rien de tout cela ne s'est fait en vase clos. La SRGE a été formée par le 54e régiment de transmissions et la 785e compagnie de guerre électronique, deux spécialistes de la guerre des ondes. Le régiment travaille avec des industriels, notamment Thales, Airbus et Procomm. Certains étaient présents sur le camp pour former les fantassins et récolter leurs retours en temps réel, afin d'ajuster si besoin les équipements. Le général Maxime Do Tran, qui commande la 7e brigade blindée, estime que les armes des premières phases de la guerre moderne, comme les drones, seront sans doute les plus technologiques, et celles des dernières phases relèveront du combat rapproché. Comme il le dit si bien, « la guerre allie innovation et rusticité. »

articles.title: The Downfall of Jensen Huang — a timeline of allegations and scandals that brought down the king of AI infrastructure
articles.text:
The Downfall of Jensen Huang — a timeline of allegations and scandals that brought down the king of AI infrastructure
Affairs, geopolitics, and the global AI race. Plus a whole lot of money.
Nvidia rose from a niche gaming hardware company with an unofficial motto of "Our company is thirty days from going out of business” to becoming the world’s most valuable company by market capitalization in 2024, and co-founder and chief executive Jensen Huang was the man behind its meteoric rise.
He planned and founded the company in 1993 alongside Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem while sitting inside a Denny’s diner in the Silicon Valley area. After more than 30 years, Nvidia had thousands of employees, a global footprint, and a name that people equated to AI chips.
All this came crumbling down for the billionaire founder in a matter of weeks, but the cracks started long before the first accusation. Let’s go back and see how it all began. This is an ongoing saga, so we have listed stories related to the scandal below, which we will update as events unfold.
The end of an era
Jensen resigned from Nvidia on November 12, after two weeks of news reports accusing him of multiple affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and another with his own subordinate. This is significant for Nvidia, which has had a single CEO since its inception. Huang was the face of the company, and many of its employees, shareholders, partners, and fans still support him despite the circumstances of his departure. He steered Nvidia into the giant that it is today by having the vision to develop CUDA nearly 20 years before ChatGPT made AI accessible to the average user and buying companies that helped it scale deployments to hundreds of thousands of AI GPUs.
Jensanity
By 2022, ChatGPT’s arrival and subsequent boom set the AI race in motion, with tech giants and AI startups buying up as many GPUs as they could get their hands on. The increased demand for Nvidia’s products caused it to break the trillion-dollar mark in less than a year after the release of OpenAI’s LLM. As the largest individual shareholders of the company, Huang and his wife, Lori, became some of the wealthiest people in the world.
The billionaire founder hasn't always gloated about his position. He once said in a podcast that if he could turn back time, he wouldn’t have founded Nvidia at all, and also cringed at the praises that the Caltech Board of Trustees chairperson heaped on him before he gave the 2024 keynote speech at the institute’s commencement exercises. He has frequently cited his history working as a “Dishwasher, Busboy, Waiter” at Denny’s, noting it under his experience on his LinkedIn page. More than that, people have seen Jensen go where other celebrity CEOs are rarely seen — enjoying street food in Vietnam, dining at a local fried chicken joint in Korea, and even dragging along 35 of Taiwan’s semiconductor CEOs to a restaurant in Taipei.
But even as he’s building his “Man of the People” persona, his position as the head of arguably the most important chipmaker in the AI industry meant that he was also gaining influence in business and governance. Industry leaders noticed the power that Nvidia held over those who want GPUs to train their AI models, with some of his fellow billionaires begging him over dinner to sell them GPUs. Just weeks into President Donald Trump’s second term, Jensen Huang was meeting with him at the White House, discussing AI policy and hardware export controls — something the Biden administration started in 2022 in an attempt to hold back China’s ambition'sin AI.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The China problem
The rivalry between the U.S. and China has been simmering for years, with Chinese companies like Huawei getting blacklisted because of their work with the People’s Liberation Army. In August 2022, about three months before ChatGPT made AI a household term, Washington expanded its trade bans on Beijing and imposed export controls on Nvidia’s H100 and A100 GPUs. The company responded to this by building a new data center GPU that conformed to U.S. standards specifically for the Chinese market, called the A800, by November of that year. Despite delivering only 70% of the performance of the A100 it was based on, the GPU reportedly still saw great demand from Chinese customers.
However, the A800 only had a relatively short run as the Biden administration once again increased the performance threshold in October 2023, which resulted in the export prohibition of A800 and H800 GPUs to China. This move forced the company to iterate once again, creating new models that it could sell to Chinese companies, like the Nvidia H20. These chips arrived on the market in early 2024, but before the Biden administration ended in January 2025, it proposed even stricter rules called the AI Diffusion Policy. This sorted nations into different tiers based on trust and risk levels — countries in tier 1, which includes the U.S. and its closest allies, have minimal restrictions, while those in tier 3 are effectively barred from receiving advanced AI GPUs containing U.S. technology.
This is problematic for Nvidia, as China is the second-largest computer market in the world t and represented between 20% and 25% of Nvidia's data center sales. The company lobbied the U.S. government to ease AI GPU export restrictions, with Trump reportedly suspending the proposed Nvidia H20 ban after Jensen spent $1 million to have dinner with the president in early April 2025. The White House went ahead anyway and banned the sale of the AI GPU less than a week after that, resulting in a $5.5 billion write-off for the company.
Jensen Huang himself had harsh comments about Washington’s trade ban, saying that “export control was a failure,” and that it had caused the company’s AI GPU market share in China to go from 95% to zero. He even argued that “conceding an entire market the size of China probably does not make a lot of strategic sense, so I think that has already largely backfired.”
But even as Huang was fighting to have the trade ban on the Nvidia H20 chip lifted, he continued praising Trump’s tariff plan, calling it “utterly visionary.” The president eventually reversed the ban three months later, and by December 2025, he had approved Nvidia H200 exports to China, but only if Nvidia pays a 25% fee. The newer Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips remain out of reach for Chinese companies, though — at least on paper.
“There’s no evidence of any AI chip diversion”
Allegations that Chinese companies have been breaking Washington’s trade ban and smuggling Nvidia AI GPUs into China have been circulating since June 2023, after Reuters revealed that vendors in Shenzhen could secure A100 chips when asked discreetly. They reportedly bought these chips from the excess stocks sold in the open market or through intermediaries in India, Taiwan, and Singapore. Another story published in January 2024 asserted that the Chinese military and related institutions, state-run data centers, and even universities continue buying banned A100 and H100 chips. Six months after that, accounts of underground networks dedicated to smuggling AI GPUs — even entire servers — through other countries started emerging.
In 2025, an investigative report showed that at least a billion dollars’ worth of Nvidia AI chips were allegedly funneled into China. Some sellers likened the illicit AI GPU trade to a seafood market, with brokers and retailers openly advertising the most advanced Nvidia AI chips online, from RTX 5090 GPUs to complete B200 servers.
Even with all these reports, Huang continued denying that Nvidia’s chips were being smuggled into China. “There’s no evidence of any AI chip diversion,” the then-CEO told reporters at Computex 2025. He also added, “The Grace Blackwell system is nearly two tons, and so you’re not going to be shipping — you’re not going to be putting that in your pocket or your backpack anytime soon. And so, these systems are fairly easy to keep track of... but the important thing is that the countries and the companies that we sell to recognize that diversion is not allowed, and everybody would like to continue to buy Nvidia technology, and so they very well monitor themselves very carefully and they’re quite careful about that.”
In the midst of all these AI chip smuggling rumors, the Bureau of Industry and Security, the agency in charge of enforcing U.S. trade sanctions, was found to be “inadequate” and underfunded, and it has been relying on outdated manual processes to enforce restrictions on Chinese tech companies. Despite that, companies and individuals across the world are being investigated and arrested for bypassing Washington’s export controls.
Singaporean authorities broke up a smuggling ring in early 2025 that smuggled Nvidia GPUs for Chinese AI lab DeepSeek, resulting in a raid of 22 different locations and the arrest of nine people. In October of the same year, a Singapore company called Megaspeed, which was led by Alice Huang, allegedly diverted $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips. Four Americans were then arrested the following month for shipping 400 Nvidia A100s and attempting to send 50 more Nvidia H200 GPUs to China.
An even bigger smuggling scandal unfolded some four months after the arrests, after three Super Micro employees were arrested for smuggling $2.5 billion of Nvidia hardware into China. The suspects included company co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw, although Super Micro itself was not implicated. The Super Micro case spanned the globe, with Taiwanese authorities raiding 12 locations related to the case in May 2026, with another nine sites and six people investigated in June. Jensen Huang urged the company to fix its export control compliance after the arrests and raids, telling the media, “We insist our partners are compliant. We hope that they will enhance and improve their regulatory compliance and prevent that from happening in the future.”
But just five months after he made this statement, one stunning accusation unraveled it all.
Scandal erupts
On October 29, 2026, The New York Times published a report that Jensen Huang may have been the target of a Chinese spy plot through the executive of a firm who was “close” to him — that executive is Alice Huang. Nvidia denied the accusation. “Megaspeed has been no different than many other regional cloud customers. Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO's job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” a company spokesperson told Tom's Hardware. “Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security."
But a little over a week later, U.S. intelligence sources claimed that the former Nvidia chief had an affair with the Megaspeed executive. This is the same Megaspeed that has been accused of smuggling Nvidia chips to the tune of $2 billion. By the evening of Sunday, November 8, Jensen admitted to the affair, although he did not name the third party in his statement.
Many government officials would usually turn a blind eye towards a tech executive’s personal life, but the fact that he is the leader of the U.S.’s premier AI chip maker and that he is also close to the president has caught the attention of authorities. This has led to the U.S. Congress asking him to a closed-door meeting to discuss Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” and the FBI investigating his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy.
The admission and allegations led to people digging deeper into Alice Huang. An investigation by The Information revealed that she was connected to a “labyrinth” of companies spanning Singapore, China, and the British Virgin Islands, and that she allegedly helped move around $7.5 billion worth of AI GPU imports. $2 billion was routed from Megaspeed to Speedmatrix, its Malaysia subsidiary, while another $4.6 billion moved directly from the Singaporean company into Shanghai Century Litong, a China-based cloud services company. It has also reportedly bought Nvidia GPUs from other sources, resulting in the estimated total value of its imports.
People close to her also said that she would leverage her relationship with Jensen to customers, often posting pictures with him on her WeChat account, showing potential clients unpublished photos with the Nvidia chief, and even boasting that he would take her to dinner and give her gifts on her birthday. It also seems that Alice Huang was not acting alone. 
Multiple sources say that Kang Wei, Alice Huang’s husband, was central to the operation to acquire AI GPUs. He even seemingly acknowledged her relationship with Jensen Huang and has jokingly said that she was a personal assistant to the billionaire.
However, it seems that the straw that broke the camel’s back was another allegation that Jensen had an affair with another woman — this time, with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of health care who directly reported to him. Hours after this revelation, the company board announced that Jensen had resigned from all his leadership positions at Nvidia, with employees saying he looked “broken and shattered” as he left the company he spent over three decades building in disgrace. 
Nvidia is looking for internal and external CEO candidates. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim chief executive.
Huang resurfaces
It may be the end of an era, but this does not necessarily spell the end for Jensen Huang. Despite his sudden downfall and quick removal from Nvidia, his status as the king of AI infrastructure remains valuable to the AI industry. Elon Musk even said on X that it “would be an honor” to hire him, and this could ring true for any business that wants to break into the semiconductor space. But does he even want to return?
Huang's first public statement after his resignation came on X on Nov. 17, in which the former CEO said he has "outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO," and that if asked by the company's board, he would be "honored" to take the job."
Over 190,000 shareholders, partners, current and former employees, and fans, including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, have signed an online petition to bring him back as the leader of the company. President Donald Trump called for his reinstatement as Nvidia CEO.
The board, however, may not see things the same way. Multiple reports suggest that the board isn't considering bringing Huang back, and instead is focusing on a new candidate, the ongoing investigation into Huang, and preparing for national security investigations.

articles.title: 5 Life-changing lessons from It's Okay by Jaya Kishori
articles.text:
5 Life-changing lessons from It's Okay by Jaya Kishori
Discover 5 meaningful lessons from It's Okay by Jaya Kishori on accepting emotions, overcoming self-doubt, letting go and finding inner peace.
Life rarely unfolds exactly as we imagine. Sometimes, despite our best efforts, things fall apart. Relationships change, plans fail, people disappoint us, and situations arise that leave us questioning ourselves.
In such moments, we often feel pressured to stay strong, hide our emotions and pretend that everything is fine. But what if we allowed ourselves to admit that things are not okay?
In It's Okay: A Book of Inspirational and Mystic Thoughts, Jaya Kishori offers a comforting perspective on dealing with life's challenges. Rather than encouraging readers to ignore their struggles, the book reminds them that problems, emotional setbacks and difficult experiences are natural parts of being human. It encourages readers to acknowledge their circumstances, develop a healthier perspective and find ways to move forward.
Drawing on personal experiences, spiritual teachings and stories passed down through generations, Jaya Kishori explores how people can approach life's uncertainties with greater understanding and emotional strength.
5 Life lessons from It's Okay by Jaya Kishori
1. Accepting your reality is the first step towards healing
One of the most important things we struggle with is accepting situations that do not go according to our expectations. We spend days questioning why something happened, wishing things had turned out differently or comparing our present circumstances with the life we once imagined.
However, constantly resisting reality does not change what has happened. It only makes it harder to find peace. The book encourages readers to understand that accepting a situation does not mean being happy about it or agreeing with everything that happened. It simply means acknowledging the truth instead of exhausting yourself by fighting something that is already beyond your control.
For instance, if you experience failure, lose an opportunity or go through a difficult phase in a relationship, accepting the situation allows you to understand what happened and decide what to do next.
The takeaway: You cannot always control what happens in life, but you can choose how you respond to it. Accepting reality gives you the clarity to stop dwelling on the past and start working towards a better future.
2. It is okay to acknowledge your emotions
Many people believe that being strong means never crying, feeling disappointed or expressing vulnerability. They hide their sadness behind smiles, tell everyone that they are fine and avoid discussing what is actually troubling them.
But ignoring emotions does not make them disappear. An important lesson to take from the book is that experiencing difficult emotions is a natural part of life. You do not have to feel happy every day, and you do not need to pretend that nothing affects you. Whether you are feeling lonely, anxious, disappointed or overwhelmed, acknowledging those emotions is an important step towards understanding yourself.
Instead of judging yourself for feeling a certain way, give yourself the space to understand what is causing those feelings. Sometimes, talking to someone you trust, taking a break or simply allowing yourself to process an experience can make a difference.
There is also a difference between acknowledging your emotions and allowing them to control your decisions. You can accept that you are hurt without letting that hurt define your entire life.
The takeaway: Emotional strength does not mean suppressing your feelings. It means understanding them, accepting them and learning how to deal with them more healthily.
3. Stop allowing other people's opinions to define you
We live in a world where people constantly have something to say about our choices, appearance, careers, relationships and personal lives. Sometimes, even a small comment from someone can make us question our abilities or feel inadequate.
Over time, we may start making decisions based on what others expect from us rather than what genuinely matters to us. This creates unnecessary pressure and takes away our ability to appreciate our own journey. The lesson here is to understand that everyone sees life through their own experiences, beliefs and expectations. What works for someone else may not necessarily work for you. Similarly, someone else's opinion about your life does not automatically make it the truth.
It is important to listen to constructive feedback, but there is no need to carry every criticism or allow every comment to affect your self-worth. You deserve to make decisions that align with your values and aspirations, even when everyone does not understand them.
The takeaway: Your worth should not depend on how others perceive you. Learn to value your own decisions, recognise your strengths and stop seeking approval from everyone around you.
4. Let go of what you cannot change
One of the biggest reasons people struggle to find peace is their attachment to things that are no longer within their control.
We revisit old conversations, regret decisions, think about missed opportunities and wonder what would have happened if we had chosen differently. While reflecting on the past can help us learn, constantly living in it prevents us from appreciating the present.
Letting go is not always easy, especially when something or someone has been an important part of your life. It takes time to accept certain endings, forgive yourself for past mistakes and make peace with experiences that did not turn out as expected.
However, holding on to every disappointment does not bring back what you have lost. Sometimes, moving forward requires accepting that certain chapters have ended.
This does not mean forgetting your experiences. It means taking the lessons from them without allowing them to become a permanent source of pain.
The takeaway: You cannot rewrite yesterday, but you can decide how you want to live tomorrow. Let go of unnecessary emotional baggage and give yourself the opportunity to experience life beyond your past.
5. Choose faith and a positive perspective during difficult times
Life can be unpredictable. There will be moments when you work hard but do not see results, when your plans fall apart or when you cannot understand why certain things are happening.
During such phases, it is easy to lose hope and believe that things will never improve. The book brings attention to the importance of spiritual understanding, faith and maintaining a positive outlook when dealing with life's challenges. Having faith does not mean expecting everything to happen exactly as you wish. Instead, it means developing the strength to face uncertainty without losing hope.
A positive perspective also does not require you to ignore your problems. It encourages you to look for possibilities, learn from difficult experiences and believe that your present circumstances do not have to determine your entire future.
For readers who find comfort in spirituality, prayer, reflection and faith can also become meaningful ways to navigate emotionally challenging periods.
The takeaway: Not every difficult experience will make sense immediately. Have faith, keep making sincere efforts and remind yourself that one challenging phase does not define your whole life.
Final thoughts
It's Okay by Jaya Kishori offers a reassuring reminder that life does not have to be perfect for us to find happiness and peace. We all experience difficult days, unexpected disappointments and moments when we feel lost. What matters is how we understand these experiences and allow ourselves to grow through them.
The five lessons from the book encourage us to accept reality, acknowledge our emotions, value ourselves, let go of the past and maintain faith during uncertain times.
Perhaps the most meaningful message is that saying "It's okay" should not become an excuse to ignore problems or tolerate situations that hurt us. Instead, it should give us the courage to acknowledge what is happening, face it honestly and take steps towards finding a solution.
Because sometimes, the first step towards changing your life is accepting that you do not have to have everything figured out right now.

articles.title: Las Wachowski quieren recuperar los derechos de 'The Matrix': ¿Problemas para Skydance?
articles.text:
Skydance, el imperio que controla David Ellison, podía sufrir su primer gran bofetón. Según un reporte de Puck, las cineastas Lana y Lily Wachowski pretenden recuperar el control sobre los derechos de la saga The Matrix, una de las propiedades intelectuales icónicas de Warner Bros.
De acuerdo con el citado medio, las Wachowski habrían notificado al estudio que pretenden ejercer su derecho de rescindir el acuerdo de licencia que existe por The Matrix. Si su reclamo funciona, las hermanas podrían recuperar el control sobre la IP a partir de febrero de 2029.
Claro que la historia podría no resolverse con tanta facilidad. Siendo The Matrix una de las franquicias más prolíficas de Warner Bros (a pesar del fiasco de la cuarta película), tiene sentido pensar que la compañía no la soltará con tanta facilidad. A esto hay que sumarle que existe una quinta entrega en marcha de la mano de Drew Goddard, el guionista de Cloverfield, Guerra Mundial Z, The Martian y Proyecto Salvación.
Tanto las Wachowski como Warner Bros tendrían argumentos para tratar de torcer la resolución a favor. Por el lado de la dupla de directoras, pueden esgrimir que escribieron los guiones de The Matrix antes de que el estudio les ofreciera un contrato por múltiples largometrajes, allá por los años noventa.
Por el lado de Skydance, podrían aseverar que The Matrix fue, en realidad, un trabajo por encargo. Si la compañía tiene evidencias para probarlo, la creación de la saga recaería sobre Warner Bros y no sobre las Wachowski. Por ende, la dupla de cineastas no podría reclamar el control sobre la propiedad intelectual.
Las Wachowski aspiran a recuperar el control sobre The Matrix
Si Skydance y las Wachowski no se ponen de acuerdo por el futuro de The Matrix, no se descarta una extensa (y costosa) batalla legal para definirlo. En todo caso, se especula con que el pedido de las directoras no busque quitar la saga del catálogo de Warner Bros, sino forzar a David Ellison a negociar un nuevo acuerdo para licenciar la IP bajo condiciones económicas más suculentas.
Sea como sea, el reclamo de las Wachowski podría complicar el desarrollo de The Matrix 5. La nueva película tiene a Goddard como guionista y director, pero su idea es tener la bendición de las responsables de las entregas previas para seguir adelante. En septiembre pasado, Lily Wachowski reconoció que no quería volver a involucrarse en la saga: "Warner Bros quiere hacer otra. Siempre van a querer hacer otra. En lo personal, ya no quiero seguir con eso. Ya tuve suficiente".
Recordemos que The Matrix Resurrections, la cuarta película de la franquicia que debutó en 2021, fue dirigida por Lana Wachowski en solitario. La cinta fue apaleada por la crítica y los fanáticos, y protagonizó una batalla legal entre Warner Bros y Village Roadshow por su estreno en simultáneo en cines y HBO Max.
Con este panorama, la concreción de The Matrix 5 es incierta. Tampoco se sabe qué idea tendrían las Wachowski si obtuviesen el control sobre la franquicia que las lanzó al estrellato mundial.

articles.title: AI data centers delays push inference chips into existing sites - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Stalled data center buildouts send inference chips hunting for space in telco and colo sites
Demand for inference is outrunning the construction of new AI data centers, as power, capital and permitting delays push fresh capacity further out. That gap is sending chipmakers to hunt for room in existing facilities.
Many older telco and colocation sites have the space and power. But most can’t take today’s dense, liquid-cooled GPU racks without costly retrofits, which opens the door for air-cooled inference systems, according to Anton McGonnell (pictured), vice president of core product at SambaNova Systems Inc.
“We as an industry are just encumbered by the velocity of data center buildouts, and that’s been slowed down by just the physics of how long this takes, by the access to capital, and more and more by legislative hurdles — particularly in the U.S.,” McGonnell said.
McGonnell spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI data centers and the demand for air-cooled inference racks. (* Disclosure below.)
Reviving brownfield capacity for AI data centers
SambaNova’s fifth-generation chip, the SN50, targets the decode phase of inference, where output tokens are generated and data movement becomes the bottleneck. Its racks stay air-cooled and light enough to fit existing facilities, McGonnell explained. Newer GPU racks, by contrast, can demand reinforced flooring and 120 to 250 kilowatts of power per rack, he noted.
“On all of this stuff — the power and the cooling gear — there’s 18- to 24-month lead times to get this equipment into the data centers. Never mind all of the construction costs,” McGonnell said.
SambaNova, which investors valued at $11 billion in July, pairs its decode chips with partners that handle prefill, the compute-heavy first phase of inference. At SC26, it is demonstrating Intel’s D-Series GPUs for prefill alongside its SambaRack SN50 for decode in an air-cooled heterogeneous setup.
“They have developed a chip that has much, much better cost performance for the prefill phase of inference,” McGonnell said. “They’ve sacrificed HBM, which isn’t needed for prefill because it’s a compute-bound problem.”

articles.title: The "shameful" measles data that lost the US its elimination status
articles.text:
International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.
After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases. There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.
But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.
Lost status
The US measles elimination status is a designation granted by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), which is a regional division of the World Health Organization. Last week a committee of experts assembled by the PAHO, called the RVC, met to review measles data for countries across the region, including the US. (RVC is short for the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission.)
For their review of the US data, the RVC heard from an independent committee of experts from the US, called the NSC, which presented measles data collected from January 2025 onward. (The NSC is short for the US National Sustainability Committee for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome.)
According to the PAHO, an elimination status is lost when epidemiological and laboratory data shows that a single viral lineage has spread continuously for at least 12 months within a country. At this point, the virus is considered to be reestablished or endemic. So, to withdraw the US elimination status, the RVC needed to see evidence that a single introduction of a measles virus led to a 12-month-long chain of cases, which requires a lot of data.
The full set of data the NSC presented to the RVC is private for now. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention needs to review and approve such data for public release, which can be a lengthy process that has not yet occurred.
The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the CDC, did not respond to a question from Ars Technica regarding when the data may be released.
Private data
But Ars Technica spoke with the chair of the NSC, Noel Brewer, who tried to talk through the pieces of data in the NSC report to the PAHO that he could discuss—these are pieces that have already been made public at some point by others, such as by state health officials or researchers. Brewer said the NSC presented the PAHO with genetic data spanning January 2025 to January 2026, and also epidemiological data that extended to June 2026.
In a press briefing Tuesday, officials for the PAHO made clear that only some of the data presented by NSC factored into its assessment of the US elimination status. The RVC only looked at the reporting period between January 2025 and January 2026, which doesn’t include the massive outbreak ongoing in Pennsylvania, which began in April. “The number of cases in Pennsylvania did not actually contribute to the decision that was made by the Reverification Commission,” Rhonda Sealey-Thomas, PAHO’s assistant director, explicitly told reporters Tuesday. For 2025, the US reported 2,289 cases nationally.
Still, there was no ambiguity about the US losing its status; “multiple lines of data show clearly that the US has sustained transmission of measles,” Brewer told Ars.
Brewer, who is also the Gillings Distinguished Professor in Public Health at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, confirmed that the beginning of the end of US elimination was January 20, 2025, in Texas—that date was included in the letter PAHO sent to the US informing it of the loss of elimination status. That Texas outbreak was declared over on August 18, 2025, after 762 cases were confirmed in the state. But the virus carried on elsewhere and is still simmering.
“Since January 20, 2025, the US, Canada, and Mexico have been passing measles cases back and forth across borders,” Brewer said, and the national data shows multiple, “genetically distinct” measles introductions into the US. “However, there is one genomic lineage that predominates across the cases and ties many of them, the majority of them, together,” he said.
Key question
For people closely tracking the US measles status, a key question has been whether the big outbreaks that followed the initial one in Texas were clearly linked. If they were, it would be immediately obvious that the US had lost the elimination status; but if not, and the outbreaks were driven by different virus introductions, the US could have kept its measles-free status based on the technicality of how the status is defined.
Data that might hold the answer to this question has been elusive. The measles strain in Texas, D8-9171, appeared similar to the viruses seen subsequently in big outbreaks in Arizona and Utah. But the strain was also similar to those from Mexico and Canada. Generally, there can be relatively small genetic changes among measles viruses, and genetic data alone is not used by PAHO to evaluate elimination. In June, ProPublica tried to get at the answer itself, conducting its own genetic analysis of measles strains in the US. It concluded that “the measles virus still spreading in Utah as of this May is very closely related to the one that sickened Texans over a year ago.” But the outlet acknowledged this wasn’t a “smoking gun.”
To date, the question lingers. Brewer cannot yet explicitly disclose what the NSC reported to the PAHO about possible links between the Texas outbreak and any of the subsequent large outbreaks in 2025. That includes the one in nearby Utah or one in South Carolina, which began in October 2025 and ultimately tallied 997 cases by the time it was declared over in April 2026.
For its part, the PAHO did not respond to multiple requests for comment from Ars Technica on linkages between the outbreaks.
But in a twist, Brewer noted that the answer to the question might be moot; the lineage that started in Texas on January 20 might not be the only one that has been sustained and could have lost the country its status. There are “one or two that have gone on for more than 12 months,” he said.
Bleak outlook
With the designation now formally lost, health and medical experts are coming to grips with the reality that measles is once again endemic in the US. Details of how the US should move forward are up for debate; the US is now required to submit a “corrective action plan” to the PAHO, outlining how the country intends to regain its elimination status. But the fundamental solution is obvious and straightforward: The US needs to increase vaccination rates.
While the virus has been raging in religious communities with low vaccination rates, the entire US has seen slipping vaccination coverage. That makes it easier for the virus to gain a foothold virtually anywhere.
A protective vaccination rate is considered to be 95 percent; according to the latest data, only 92.4 percent of kindergartners were vaccinated with the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine in the 2025–2026 school year. Only 10 states have MMR vaccination rates at or above the 95 percent threshold. Meanwhile, non-medical exemptions from school vaccination requirements have never been higher, at 4 percent. Currently, 24 states have exemption rates at or above 5 percent, meaning that even if they are able to vaccinate every single non-exempt child, they would still not meet the 95 percent target. And this is just the data for young children. The vaccination coverage for adults is another concern, and the data there is scarce. In Pennsylvania’s massive outbreak, 1,055 of the 1,561 cases this year have been in adults ages 18 and older (less than 1 percent of the cases were fully vaccinated).
While some health officials have noted optimistically that 92.4 percent in children is just a few percentage points from the target, the reality of bringing up vaccination rates is more onerous.
PAHO Director Jarbas Barbosa stressed the point in the press briefing Tuesday: It’s “not the national average or the average in the state or even the average in a big city, you need to guarantee that in every community, village, you have this vaccination coverage up to 95 percent. This is very important,” Barbosa said.
The point has been demonstrated in the US. In 2019, the US came very close to losing its measles elimination status. Unlike now—when the virus is on a nationwide rampage, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases—in 2019, the US nearly lost its status from a single, large outbreak that spread in New York. Though it didn’t explode on a national level, it took 11 months to stamp out in those undervaccinated communities. In that year, the US reported 1,274 measles cases total.
The situation in the US has only gotten worse, and the outlook is bleak, Brewer warns. “The measles outbreaks in Canada and Mexico are winding down,” he noted. “However, in the US, our measles problem continues to accelerate. There is no end in sight.”
Beth is Ars Technica’s Senior Health Reporter. Beth has a Ph.D. in microbiology from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and attended the Science Communication program at the University of California, Santa Cruz. She specializes in covering infectious diseases, public health, and microbes.

articles.title: Chief AI Officers are now a common sight in businesses — but new study finds they often don't really have any power
articles.text:
Chief AI Officers are now a common sight in businesses — but new study finds they often don't really have any power
CAIOs don't actually have much independent responsibility
- IBM study finds CAIOs have become 3x more common in UK businesses in just one year
- Only 16% say they have full control over AI investments
- Successful CAIOs are using business outcomes to identify key investment areas
Chief AI Officers (CAIOs) have become far more common in recent months, with over three-quarters (78%) of UK businesses now having one appointed - compared with a tiny 26% in 2025, according to IBM's latest 2026 CEO Study.
But even though they're given C-suite titles, that doesn't always mean anything, as despite how commonplace the CAIO role has become, only 16% say they have full control over AI investment decisions, with even fewer (11%) having full control over their AI-related workforce strategies, implying other C-suite execs are still holding the reins.
IBM found CAIOs are generally unsatisfied with their business' overall AI readiness too, slating slow action and limited access to resources.
CAIO roles are commonplace, but responsibilities still lie elsewhere
AI policies were also slated in the report – four in five (79%) say their organization has finally defined situations in which human oversight is non-negotiable, but enforcement is lacking with just three in five (58%) saying these are consistently applied.
"Giving AI leaders greater influence over investment, workforce and operating decisions will be critical to turning ambition into action," IBM Consulting UK&I Managing Partner Rhodri Arrowsmith said, stressing the importance of clear and enforced governance.
IBM's report is also one of a long list reporting that AI ambitions could be outpacing actual readiness, with 29% of UK CAIOs worried their organizations have not yet made the changes needed to prepare for widespread transformations. Three in four (73%), as a result, worry that their company could fall behind competitors.
The study also found that the most successful CAIOs were able to reinvest productivity gains back into their wider transformation strategy while also using business outcomes to determine which AI initiatives should receive additional investment in the first place.

Looking ahead, IBM wants to see CAIOs gain more responsibility and independence from their senior colleagues, and for them to start off by implanting a clearly defined strategy with effective governance to identify the key areas of investment.

articles.title: GTA VI ya está disponible para Nueva Zelanda, Fiyi y Australia: América Latina espera el 19 de noviembre
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI ya se puede jugar de forma escalonada en algunos mercados de Oceanía, por la diferencia horaria que separa a esos territorios de América Latina. La salida oficial del videojuego está fijada para el jueves 19 de noviembre de 2026, pero los jugadores de países como Nueva Zelanda y Fiyi acceden antes de jugadores de países como Colombia, Argentina o México donde aún transcurre el miércoles 18.
La empresa Rockstar Games confirmó que el nuevo título de su franquicia llegará a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S el 19 de noviembre. La fecha representa el cierre de una espera prolongada para uno de los videojuegos más anticipados de la última década, después de que su calendario inicial fuera aplazado en más de una ocasión.
El videojuego traslada la acción al estado ficticio de Leonida y a una versión contemporánea de Vice City. La historia gira en torno a Lucia y Jason, dos personajes presentados por Rockstar en los avances oficiales. La empresa ha mostrado imágenes de playas, zonas urbanas, carreteras, redes sociales ficticias y actividades criminales dentro de un mapa inspirado en Florida.
La salida internacional no implica, por tanto, que el juego esté disponible de inmediato en todos los países al mismo tiempo. La disponibiidad del juego avanza a medida que cada región alcanza la fecha de lanzamiento en su propio huso horario.
Oceanía y Asia reciben el juego antes que América Latina
Después de Nueva Zelanda y Fiyi, el acceso es para Australia, con ciudades como Sídney y Melbourne. Dos horas más tarde se sumaría Asia Oriental, incluida Japón y Corea del Sur.
La información oficial de Rockstar Games confirma la fecha global, aunque los horarios concretos de desbloqueo pueden variar entre servicios y territorios. Por eso, las personas que esperan jugar desde Latinoamérica deben comprobar la hora que indique PlayStation Store o Microsoft Store en sus respectivas consolas.
En qué consolas de videojuegos está disponible GTA VI
GTA VI está disponible inicialmente en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar no ha anunciado una fecha de estreno para computadores personales, una ausencia que mantiene la atención sobre posibles planes posteriores de la compañía.
La llegada del título ocurre bajo una expectativa comercial considerable. La franquicia Grand Theft Auto es una de las más exitosas de la industria y su entrega anterior, GTA V, se mantuvo durante años entre los videojuegos con mayores ventas y presencia en plataformas digitales.
Cómo descargar GTA 6 en diferentes consolas de videojuegos
La predescarga está disponible desde el 10 de noviembre para quienes reservaron la edición digital. El juego requiere hasta 212 GB de espacio libre en la unidad SSD, una capacidad que puede demorar el inicio si la instalación se realiza cuando se active el lanzamiento.
En PlayStation 5, la descarga se inicia desde la biblioteca de juegos o la PlayStation Store. En Xbox Series X|S, queda habilitada desde la Xbox Store después de completar la reserva.
Las copias físicas tampoco incluirán un disco: la caja contendrá un código de descarga. Por ese motivo, los compradores necesitarán conexión a internet y espacio de almacenamiento suficiente en la consola de videojuegos incluso si eligen esa edición.
Asimismo, la campaña principal podría durar cerca de 50 horas. Esa versión calcula unas 100 misiones distribuidas en cinco capítulos centrados en Jason y Lucia, protagonistas de esta versión de la entrega.
Completar el 100% del título podría demandar hasta 200 horas. Entre las misiones figuran identificar y fotografiar más de 170 especies animales en Leonida, sumado a cumplir logros vinculados con elementos aleatorios que impedirían seguir una ruta fija. Cada jugador deberá probar la dinámica del juego y apartar tiempo para pasar cada reto que supone.

articles.title: US closes the AI chip loophole that let China rent Nvidia hardware abroad
articles.text:
Why it matters: US export controls on advanced AI chips have mostly focused on where the hardware ends up. Now, a new Commerce Department rule dictates who gets to use it. Under the rule, companies must get a license to ship chips from Nvidia and other US suppliers to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil, a move meant to stop Chinese customers from tapping data-center capacity in those countries over the network.
The gap the rule addresses is simple. A Chinese company that can't legally buy a cutting-edge Nvidia processor can still rent time on one, as long as the chip sits in a server rack outside China. The silicon never crosses the Chinese border, but the computing power does.
Firms such as Megaspeed International have built a business on that arrangement. They used billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips to build data centers across Southeast Asia, then sold the computing capacity to Chinese tech giants trying to catch up in artificial intelligence. Shutting down that channel is the main goal of the new rule.
"The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security said in a release.
The rule reaches beyond the five named countries, making it harder for data-center operators anywhere in the world to give Chinese companies remote access to AI chips. It also tightens a separate point in the supply chain by making it more difficult for Chinese chip designers to work with TSMC.
US tech companies could get exceptions to the licensing requirement. The rule took effect immediately, and companies have 60 days to submit comments.
Megaspeed's role has put the rule at the center of a scandal involving Nvidia's top ranks. Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Megaspeed and a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, was having an affair with Jensen Huang, who has stepped down as Nvidia's chief executive. Before he left, Jensen Huang had lobbied President Trump to let Nvidia ship some chips directly to China and to keep export controls loose. His argument was that US companies competing abroad would help push back against Chinese rivals.
How the rule was written has drawn nearly as much attention as what it says. Normally, the Bureau of Industry and Security drafts chip-export rules and then sends them to the State and Treasury departments and the National Security Council for feedback. This time, the order was reversed. The release said the rule was "written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council."
Export-control analysts called that an unusual step. Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations who previously worked on tech and security issues at the State Department, said it signaled a fight inside the administration.
"It is unprecedented for a Commerce Department rule to be written by the National Security Council and the Treasury Department," McGuire told The Wall Street Journal. "The fact that the Commerce Department press release says this shows that Commerce resisted publishing this rule to the bitter end, and was forced to do so by the White House."
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other officials had accused Commerce of moving too slowly to close export-control loopholes. Bessent said last week that Treasury and other agencies had pushed for months for action on Megaspeed and chip exports, and that Commerce stood in the way. National security adviser Marco Rubio, who is also secretary of state, has joined Bessent in pushing for tighter controls.
Both men were among the officials frustrated when Megaspeed and other companies suspected of chip diversion were considered for the Entity List, a trade blacklist, and Commerce didn't move forward. Administration officials have said the agency is wary of upsetting China during trade talks. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has taken much of the blame inside the administration. The Commerce Department didn't respond to a request for comment on the dynamics between agencies.
Trump defended Lutnick this week. He said the commerce secretary has done a good job and that delaying action on Megaspeed made sense, even though hawkish advisers objected.
"He was doing it because if you didn't delay it, you could have a blowup with China," Trump said. "We're having a very good relationship with China right now."

articles.title: GTA 6 va voler des millions d’heures aux autres jeux, à Netflix… et même à votre travail
articles.text:
Plus que quelques heures avant de rejoindre Vice City. GTA VI sort ce jeudi 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series, et ses précommandes ont déjà pulvérisé tous les records. D’après le suivi des ventes tenu par Sensor Tower, le jeu de Rockstar totalisait le 17 novembre 15,88 millions de copies numériques précommandées, remboursements déduits, pour 1,54 milliard de dollars de recettes. La PS5 représente à elle seule 75 % des ventes. Ces estimations ne comptent ni les boîtes vendues en magasin, ni la commission prélevée par les boutiques en ligne, mais elles suffisent à situer l’ampleur du phénomène. Dans un rapport publié à la veille de la sortie, le cabinet s’est surtout penché sur une autre question : où les joueurs vont-ils trouver le temps d’y jouer ?
Fortnite et les grands jeux solo en première ligne
Chaque grosse sortie prend des joueurs quelque part et Sensor Tower a mesuré la fréquentation du reste du catalogue PlayStation dans le mois suivant cinq lancements majeurs récents. Après Monster Hunter Wilds, le nombre de joueurs quotidiens sur les autres jeux a reculé de 7,6 %, et la baisse a atteint 6 % après Oblivion Remastered ou encore 4,7 % après Resident Evil Requiem. Pour GTA VI, le cabinet prévoit une chute de plus de 10 % sur l’ensemble des jeux « qui ne s’appellent pas GTA VI », ce qui en ferait l’impact le plus important jamais mesuré.
Fortnite et les grands jeux solo seraient les plus exposés. L’étude relève que 42 % des joueurs ayant GTA V installé sur PlayStation ont aussi Fortnite, contre 22 % de l’ensemble des joueurs PlayStation. Roblox, en revanche, devrait mieux résister : sa fréquentation a progressé après plusieurs des lancements étudiés, son public étant moins attiré par les grandes productions solo. Le cabinet s’attend aussi à ce que GTA VI retienne ses joueurs pendant des mois, à la manière de Baldur’s Gate 3 ou d’Elden Ring.
Le rapport confirme au passage l’efficacité du marketing de Rockstar. Les précommandes, qui rapportaient entre 2,4 et 3,8 millions de dollars par jour en août, ont bondi à 16,3 millions de dollars le lendemain de la diffusion de « An Extended Look » sur Netflix, soit six fois plus.
Le smartphone ne quittera pas la main des joueurs
GTA VI ne va pas pour autant faire disparaître le smartphone, qui devrait plutôt servir de second écran. Aux États-Unis, Sensor Tower prévoit 60 millions d’heures supplémentaires passées sur les réseaux sociaux le premier mois, pour discuter sur Discord, consulter des guides sur Reddit ou regarder des extraits de parties, ainsi que 100 millions de sessions en plus sur les applications de musique et de podcasts, et 50 millions sur les applications de livraison de repas et de fast-food. Le joueur type serait à 72 % un homme, âgé de 34 ans en moyenne, et nettement plus adepte de Discord, de TikTok et de Twitch que la moyenne des mobinautes.
Ce temps sera forcément pris ailleurs, comme l’explique le cabinet. Ce dernier anticipe 20 millions d’heures de moins sur les jeux mobiles et 6 millions d’heures de moins sur les applications de streaming vidéo. Plus inattendu, les applications professionnelles pourraient perdre 180 millions de sessions durant le mois de lancement, en raison des congés posés pour l’occasion, de la distraction en journée et des « GTA sick days », ces arrêts maladie pris pour jouer. Ces prévisions portent uniquement sur les smartphones Android aux États-Unis, et le profil des joueurs est modélisé à partir des joueurs de consoles et des jeux GTA sur mobile, mais elles donnent une idée de l’onde de choc attendue.

articles.title: Road trip, week-end, shopping : Google Maps planifie maintenant vos sorties avec Ask Maps
articles.text:
Google Maps sait désormais bâtir des itinéraires complets via son assistant Ask Maps : sortie shopping, week-end ou road trip de plusieurs jours, avec étapes numérotées sur la carte. La France fait partie des pays où la fonction est désormais disponible, sous le nom « Demander à Maps ».
Avec Ask Maps, Google Maps ne se contente plus de vous guider d’un point A à un point B : l’application compose le programme à votre place. La fonction arrive à l’approche des fêtes, avec plusieurs nouveautés plus ou moins accessibles selon votre pays.
Un itinéraire jour par jour, retouchable en conversation
D’après 9to5Google, Ask Maps peut produire des plans allant d’une simple virée shopping à un road trip de plusieurs jours. Pour un voyage long, l’assistant génère un programme jour par jour, avec des conseils et des épingles numérotées pour visualiser chaque étape. Google cite l’exemple d’un trajet de trois jours mêlant randonnées côtières et dîners face à la mer.
Le plan se partage avec vos proches et s’exporte vers Google Docs, mais seulement depuis un ordinateur. Une fois sur la route, l’itinéraire s’ouvre depuis Ask Maps ou via un badge « itinerary » dans l’historique de discussion. Il affiche alors le trafic en direct, l’ouverture des lieux et même « l’ambiance » de la prochaine étape, selon la formule de Google.
On peut aussi demander d’ajouter un point de vue ou une pause déjeuner en cours de route, puis lancer le guidage vers l’étape suivante. C’est là que l’outil se distingue d’un simple générateur de listes : le plan reste vivant, ajustable à la volée.
Rendez-vous et listes : les nouveautés qui n’arriveront pas toutes en Europe
Ask Maps gagne aussi des capacités « agentiques ». Il peut chercher des rendez-vous en ligne (beauté, soins pour animaux, auto, réparations à domicile) et appeler les commerces pour vous. Une requête comme « Trouve-moi un rendez-vous manucure à 16 h près de chez moi » renvoie une liste de créneaux libres. Autre ajout : la recherche dans vos listes de lieux enregistrés, par exemple pour repérer ceux qui ont de la place pour cinq personnes dans les 30 prochaines minutes.
Mais attention au calendrier : les itinéraires et la recherche dans les listes sont disponibles partout où Ask Maps existe, soit plus de 200 pays et territoires, en revanche, les conseils « Know Before You Go » et la prise de rendez-vous démarrent d’abord aux États-Unis, sans date précise pour le reste du monde.
Ask Maps débarque dans 30 pays européens de plus
Le déploiement concerne Android et iOS, et l’extension européenne inclut l’Espagne, l’Allemagne et le Royaume-Uni. Google présente Ask Maps comme la plus grosse mise à jour de Maps en plus de dix ans, propulsée par Gemini et alimentée par des informations sur plus de 300 millions de lieux et des avis de plus de 500 millions de contributeurs.
En France, on peut déjà demander à Maps de préparer un week-end étape par étape ou de retrouver une bonne adresse parmi ses lieux enregistrés. Pour laisser Google appeler un commerce à sa place afin de trouver un créneau, il faudra encore patienter : la fonction démarre aux États-Unis et Google n’a donné aucune date pour la France. Si vous vous intéressez aux ajustements récents de l’application, on avait aussi vu Google Maps corriger un défaut sur iPhone.
Reste à voir si l’IA saura bâtir un week-end qui ne ressemble pas au top 10 des lieux les plus avis-és du coin.

articles.title: Luminar à l’automne 2026 : la retouche sans abonnement, et un éditeur RAW qui tourne dans le navigateur
articles.text:
Luminar à l’automne 2026 : la retouche sans abonnement, et un éditeur RAW qui tourne dans le navigateur
Skylum a passé l’année à remanier Luminar, son éditeur d’images, et quelques changements méritent bien l’attention de tous les utilisateurs potentiels : déjà, une mise à jour d’automne permet de retravailler les outils les plus utilisés du logiciel. En parallèle, une nouvelle version web s’avère désormais capable d’ouvrir des fichiers RAW dans un simple navigateur, y compris sous Linux. Bien entendu, ces ajouts ne changent pas le fond de l’affaire : Luminar conserve toujours son modèle à licence perpétuelle.
D’abord, il y a un changement esthétique, et pour mieux s’y retrouver : le nom Neo-Luminar a disparu. Certes, c’est un détail, mais il a malgré tout son importance pour ceux qui suivent le logiciel depuis un temps. Ainsi, depuis la version 1.28, livrée cet été, Luminar Neo s’appelle simplement Luminar. La mise à jour accompagnait une refonte de l’interface, et la nomenclature redevient lisible après plusieurs années de déclinaisons.
La mise à jour d’automne et ses cinq chantiers
Abordons maintenant les cinq chantiers majeurs entrepris par les développeurs de Luminar pour le rendre le plus simple d’accès et aisé à employer que possible.
Déjà, il y a Enhance, qui est de loin l’outil le plus utilisé du logiciel. Ainsi, désormais, au lieu d’appliquer la même recette à toutes les images, il évalue d’abord la photo et adapte le traitement selon une huitaine de situations types, selon l’exposition, une dominante de couleur, l’état du ciel ou le risque de halo. Des passes de protection interviennent ensuite là où une image casse habituellement. De fait, les hautes lumières sont préservées au lieu d’être poussées, les tons les plus clairs s’atténuent progressivement plutôt que d’être écrêtés, et l’équilibre des couleurs est protégé quand la correction risquerait d’exagérer l’une d’entre elles, un peu trop dominante.
De son côté, Atmosphere passe d’un placage de textures à du vrai brouillard volumétrique en 3D, ce qui a le don d’offrir à la brume une position et une forme dans la scène choisie, qui peut aussi réagir à la lumière et aux ombres. Par ailleurs, plutôt que d’être systématiquement blanche, Atmosphère préserve désormais la couleur de la brume, sans l’altérer.
Par ailleurs, Smart Compositions s’attaque au recadrage. Plutôt qu’un modèle unique capable de produire une seule proposition, l’outil peut désormais analyser la scène, identifier le sujet principal et la direction des regards, puis générer plusieurs cadrages qu’il note selon les règles de composition classiques avant de vous en proposer une poignée. Donc si vous ne savez pas trop par où commencer pour améliorer votre photo, vous avez une solution toute trouvée ici.
Parce qu’on est en 2026, il semble tout à fait logique qu’un outil de ce genre tire parti de l’IA. Ainsi, Luminar offre un assistant IA (accessible dans l’abonnement Prie détaillé plus bas) qui peut accepter des consignes en langage courant pour modifier une image sans vous pousser à le faire manuellement. Par exemple, une demande précise du type “réchauffe l’image” ou “enlève les fils électriques” renvoie un réglage appliqué par-dessus vos retouches existantes. En parallèle, si vous avez une demande un peu plus vague, l’outil vous propose trois solutions adaptées à la scène, que vous pouvez ensuite choisir.
Enfin, l’impression est désormais intégrée au logiciel. Autrement dit, vous imprimez une photo terminée sur votre propre matériel, ou choisissez de commander un tirage en laboratoire professionnel livré chez vous.
Luminar Web : du RAW dans le navigateur
Luminar Web fonctionne dans un navigateur récent, sans rien installer, et accepte maintenant les fichiers RAW, ce qui reste extrêmement rare sur ce type d’outil. Et puisque vous pouvez utiliser Luminar dans sa version Web, vous pouvez aussi en profiter sur Linux, que la version de bureau ne prend pas en charge jusqu’ici.
Luminar Web offre donc une interface divisée en sept sections : outils de recadrage, préréglages, ciels, filtres, effacements et restauration. On y retrouve aussi les curseurs de développement, la profondeur de lumière et les modules portrait, du bokeh au traitement du visage et de la peau. Notez cependant une chose : cette version est moins complète que celle de bureau et demande une connexion stable. Mais elle n’a rien d’un éditeur au rabais, et c’est une porte d’entrée crédible pour qui débute avec un premier appareil.
Trois formules sont proposées aux utilisateurs de Luminar : la version web gratuite donne accès aux outils de base avec la prise en charge du RAW, 100 Mo de stockage en ligne et une exportation limitée à 1 280 pixels de large. Le palier à 69 €, en licence perpétuelle (un seul achat, pour faire clair), ajoute l’application mobile, les préréglages, l’effacement, la profondeur de lumière et les retouches par IA sans limite. La formule à 139 €, également perpétuelle, couvre le bureau, le mobile et le web.
Le vrai argument : pas d’abonnement, pas de crédits
C’est là que Luminar permet de se distinguer de la concurrence directe. Vous en avez marre de payer des dizaines d’abonnements par mois en tous genres ? Parce que la majorité des éditeurs concurrents fonctionnent, eux, par abonnement mensuel. Pire, certains facturent aussi certaines fonctions d’IA par crédits. Or Luminar conserve son système de licence perpétuelle qui implique que vous n’avez qu’un paiement à effectuer.
En parallèle, Luminar Prime se superpose à cette licence. C’est un abonnement complémentaire et facultatif, qui apporte trois choses bien concrètes. Les outils d’IA, d’abord : Restoration, GenErase, GenSwap, GenExpand et l’AI Assistant évoqué plus haut. Une bibliothèque de ressources, ensuite, avec plus de 2 150 préréglages, 500 LUT, 400 superpositions, 550 ciels et plus de 50 cours. Les nouvelles fonctionnalités de chaque année, enfin, sans avoir à les acheter séparément au fil des versions.
Reste une subtilité qui concerne précisément les trois outils refondus cet automne. Enhance, Atmosphere et Smart Compositions sont accessibles aux détenteurs des formules lancées depuis le 5 août, soit Desktop, All Platforms et Max, aux abonnés, aux membres Prime, ainsi qu’aux acheteurs d’une licence Cross-device ou Max postérieure au 1er juin 2026. Si votre licence est antérieure, il faut passer par Prime pour y accéder, avec une contrepartie qui mérite d’être connue, car elle distingue ces trois outils du reste de l’offre : une fois débloqués, Enhance, Atmosphere et Smart Compositions vous restent acquis de façon permanente, même si vous mettez fin à l’abonnement.
Ce qui arrive encore
Skylum annonce pour novembre une refonte du masquage, présentée comme l’évolution la plus importante des capacités de retouche du logiciel. Nous la jugerons sur pièces, mais c’est la brique qui manque à l’édifice pour qui travaille ses images en profondeur.
