articles.title: Sarvam’s move to host Chinese AI models triggers debate
articles.text:
Sarvam’s move to host Chinese AI models triggers debate
Sarvam’s decision to host Chinese AI models on Indian infrastructure has ignited a debate over AI sovereignty, public funding and India's ambitions to develop homegrown frontier technology.
Sarvam AI’s decision to host Chinese-developed artificial intelligence models on its India-based infrastructure has reopened questions about what it means to build sovereign AI.
With its newly-launched Token Factory offering access to models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Z.ai, alongside its own models and Google’s Gemma, the Bengaluru-based company is positioning itself as an AI developer and an inference provider.
The move has attracted criticism from those who believe a company backed by public resources should prioritise original Indian research, as well as support from those who see a commercial opportunity in hosting international models locally.
Announcing the service, Sarvam said, “We host our own models, and the full range of best-in-class open-weight models, in India.” It added that enterprises would have more models to choose from and “an AI stack they can own without lock-ins”.
Token Factory is an inference platform, which provides the computing infrastructure required to run trained AI models and generate responses. Instead of purchasing expensive hardware and managing individual models themselves, developers can access several models through a single application programming interface.
Sarvam said its customised software and infrastructure allow it to compete on speed, reliability and cost.
The debate
The criticism centres on the distinction between hosting AI and developing it. Sanchit Monga, chief executive of Runanywhere AI, a Y Combinator-backed AI infrastructure company, questioned whether the launch reflected the ambitions associated with Sarvam’s selection under the government’s IndiaAI Mission. He wrote, “I wanted Sarvam to be the lab that ships frontier research out of India. After that much capital and subsidized compute, this is not it.”
Similar concerns were expressed by technology commentator Shakthi, who argued that hosting predominantly Chinese models was not what the country’s sovereign AI ambitions should amount to.
The debate became particularly interesting after Sarvam co-founder Vivek Raghavan’s remarks at the Bengaluru Tech Summit on November 17.
Warning against India’s dependence on foreign AI systems, he said, “A lot of people are proud to say that India is the largest user of ChatGPT. But that is not a good thing. We are exporting data and importing intelligence.”
Although he was not directly addressing Token Factory, his comments underline the strategic concerns surrounding dependence on foreign-developed models.
There are, however, strong commercial arguments for Sarvam’s approach. Hemant Mohapatra, a partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the launch, pointing out that international inference providers are already making money by hosting foreign models in India. He argued that there was considerable demand for such services, particularly as computing capacity becomes increasingly difficult to secure in some markets.
Technology entrepreneur Nikhil Pahwa also defended the company’s need to develop a sustainable business. “They’re a business, and they have to work in shareholder interest. Nationalism is a pitch that got them the GPUs. They’re not expected to deliver anything beyond their contract,” he wrote.
Nischal Jain, co-founder of Egma AI, offered a more nuanced assessment. While acknowledging that companies must generate revenue, he argued that Sarvam had acquired a particular significance in India’s technology ecosystem. “Sarvam was supposed to be India’s answer to the US & China. When we don’t see their frontier labs do these kinda things, it looks demotivating in an already tough situation. Everyone's gotta make money and I empathise with both ends of arguments,” he wrote.
Questions have also emerged around the platform’s competitiveness. Atharva Ingle, an AI engineer at competing inference provider JarvisLabs, said his company had compared the performance of three models across the two platforms. “We’re on par with or faster than Sarvam across speed and latency metrics, while offering lower pricing,” he claimed.
Reduce AI dependence
The wider context is India’s attempt to reduce dependence on overseas AI technology.
The IndiaAI Mission, approved in March 2024 with an outlay of approximately Rs 10,372 crore, is intended to strengthen domestic computing infrastructure, research and foundational model development.
Sarvam was selected in 2025 for indigenous model development and received subsidised access to 4,096 Nvidia H100 GPUs. The reported subsidy was Rs 98.68 crore. The company also raised over $300 million at a reported valuation of $1.5 billion.
Ultimately, hosting foreign models on Indian infrastructure and developing indigenous models are different achievements, although they need not be mutually exclusive. Local hosting can improve data residency, access and computing efficiency, while a successful inference business could generate revenue to support further research.
The more important test will be whether Sarvam can translate its public support and commercial expansion into original technology and competitive Indian models.

articles.title: José Andrés, chef, 57 años: “Yo volvería a crear el servicio militar y, en paralelo, otro social, para que la gente joven tuviera la oportunidad, con un salario, de hacer este tipo de servicio a su país”
articles.text:
El servicio militar le enseñó a trabajar con diferentes tipos de gente de diferentes orígenes sociales. Así cuenta José Andrés su experiencia en el servicio militar. “Yo volvería a crear el servicio militar y, en paralelo, otro social, para que la gente joven tuviera la oportunidad, con un salario, de hacer este tipo de servicio a su país”.
El cocinero asturiano (57) conecta así con su pasado. “Sí, yo soy quien soy gracias al servicio militar”. Le pregunta el periodista Andrés Galisteo por una de las experiencias que él mismo ha destacado en otras ocasiones. Así es como justifica su apoyo a estos programas.
“A mí el servicio militar me enseñó el respeto por mi país, por el prójimo, a trabajar en equipo; conocí muchísima gente de diferentes niveles sociales compartiendo la misma misión… Me abrió al mundo, me hizo ser quien soy. Mi año y medio en la marina me marcó mucho”.
Servicio social remunerado, paralelo al militar
Con salario para los jóvenes. Con un servicio social paralelo. Para promover la convivencia, que se sientan parte de una comunidad. “No me lo pensaría dos veces, crearía unidad y conciencia”.
Por otra parte, José Andrés también ha desarrollado esta faceta en su trabajo dentro de World Central Kitchen. Se trata de una ONG que creó tras el terremoto de Haití en 2010. Proporcionan alimentos a las personas afectadas por desastres y conflictos. Operan en Ucrania y en Gaza (donde varios miembros de su equipo han perdido la vida en su labor humanitaria).
En Europa, el debate sobre el servicio militar se produce en un contexto de fortalecimiento de la propia defensa (con amenazas de seguridad y la guerra de Ucrania). Por ejemplo, en Alemania han aprobado en 2025 un proyecto de fortalecimiento de sus tropas y reservas (mediante el reclutamiento voluntario). Esta declaración de José Andrés es anterior a dicho proyecto y a la invasión rusa de Ucrania en 2022.
También en España hay otros que han defendido el servicio militar. El humorista Miki Nadal ha destacado que permite conocer a personas de otras regiones. Aunque también confiesa que tiene dudas sobre si debería ser obligatorio para todos/as. Por otro lado, la periodista Ana Iris Simón se ha declarado partidaria porque puede ayudar a la cohesión nacional. Además, permite que los jóvenes de diferentes entornos sociales puedan relacionarse.

articles.title: Ya es oficial: el servicio universal de internet será diez veces más rápido en 2027 y beneficiará a mucha más gente
articles.text:
Ya es oficial. El Consejo de Ministros ha aprobado el Real Decreto que aprueba el Reglamento del Servicio Universal de telecomunicaciones. Se han incluido todos los cambios que conocimos en el Proyecto de Orden que publicó el Gobierno hace unas semanas y que entrarán en vigor el próximo 1 de enero.
En primer lugar, el nuevo reglamento libera a Telefónica de la obligación exclusiva de garantizar este servicio y la hace extensible al resto de operadores. También multiplica por diez la velocidad mínima de la banda ancha fija, que pasa de 10 a 100 Mbps.
Y además, permite a muchos más usuarios beneficiarse de tarifas asequibles de telefonía fija e internet. Entre ellos, todos los perceptores del Ingreso Mínimo Vital, las pymes o las ONGs.
Qué es el Servicio Universal de telecomunicaciones. Dicho en pocas palabras, es la obligación por ley de garantizar los servicios básicos de telefonía fija y acceso fijo a internet con una calidad determinada y a un precio asequible para cualquier ciudadano español, independientemente de su ubicación geográfica o su situación económica.
Las prestaciones de este servicio universal han ido evolucionando con el paso de los años y, del mismo modo que en su día se eliminaron las cabinas y las guías de teléfonos, también se empezó a considerar como servicio básico la conexión fija a internet con una velocidad mínima. Actualmente, son 10 Mbps, pero con la nueva normativa, que entrará en vigor el 1 de enero de 2027, se incrementa la velocidad mínima a 100 Mbps. Diez veces más.
Tarifas baratas para más gente. Otra novedad importante del Real Decreto es que podrán acceder a las tarifas asequibles todas aquellas unidades de convivencia perceptoras del Ingreso Mínimo Vital (unos 800.000 hogares). Si un operador no dispone de las tarifas asequibles que establece la CNMC, deberá ofrecer un 25% de descuento a los beneficiarios del Ingreso Mínimo Vital respecto al precio medio de mercado.
Además, el Real Decreto amplía el "tipo" de usuarios que pueden beneficiarse del Servicio Universal. A partir del 1 de enero, no sólo podrán solicitarlo los consumidores, sino también las microempresas, las pymes o las organizaciones sin ánimo de lucro (ONGs).
Buenas noticias para Telefónica. Ante la falta de interés del resto de operadores, la CNMC lleva casi 30 años designando a Telefónica como única compañía encargada de garantizar ese servicio. Pero eso también va a cambiar. La última adjudicación finaliza el próximo 31 de diciembre, de manera que, a partir del 1 de enero, todos los operadores atenderán solicitudes en las zonas donde ofrezcan cobertura.
De lo que no se librará Telefónica es de seguir ofreciendo las ofertas vigentes del actual Abono Social, que aplican una bonificación para jubilados y pensionistas a la hora de contratar una línea de telefonía fija o una línea fija con conexión a internet.

articles.title: Pas fan de GTA ? Le prix de Battlefield 6 s’effondre sur PS5
articles.text:
Battlefield 6 est actuellement proposé à 25,31 € sur PS5, alors qu’on le trouve habituellement autour de 35 €. Plusieurs enseignes s’alignent sur ce prix.
- Battlefield 6 à 25,31 € chez Amazon
- Battlefield 6 à 25,31 € chez Leclerc, avec le retrait gratuit en magasin
- Battlefield 6 à 25,31 € chez Cdiscount
Tout ce qui tient debout peut tomber
Battlefield 6, c’est le retour de la série à ce qui a fait sa réputation. Des batailles à grande échelle, des chars, des hélicoptères, et des décors que l’on peut réduire en miettes. Un immeuble gêne la progression de votre escouade ? Quelques roquettes bien placées suffisent à changer la carte, et la partie avec. Rien n’est scripté, ce sont les joueurs qui créent le chaos, si bien qu’aucune partie ne ressemble à la précédente.
Les sensations suivent. L’arsenal est très fourni, chaque arme se personnalise en profondeur et les tirs ont un vrai impact. Les combats sont nerveux sans tomber dans la frénésie, et les quatre classes emblématiques (Assaut, Ingénieur, Soutien, Éclaireur) gardent tout leur intérêt pour qui joue en équipe. Les véhicules ont aussi trouvé leur place, avec des hélicoptères qui rappellent les meilleurs souvenirs de Battlefield 4. Les nostalgiques retrouveront même une version modernisée d’Opération Tempête de feu, l’une des cartes cultes de Battlefield 3.
Ce retour aux sources a visiblement parlé aux joueurs. Battlefield 6 s’est écoulé à plus de 7 millions d’exemplaires en trois jours, ce qui en fait le plus gros lancement de l’histoire de la série selon Electronic Arts.
Les saisons se sont enchaînées avec leur lot de nouvelles cartes et de nouvelles armes, et un battle royale gratuit, Battlefield REDSEC, est venu s’ajouter fin octobre 2025. Le mode Portal permet aussi de créer ses propres parties, et même ses propres cartes. De quoi largement rentabiliser l’achat.
Le bon moment pour monter au front ?
Le jeu était sorti à 79,99 € en octobre 2025, et il se vendait encore 64,99 € chez Amazon et Leclerc au moment de notre test. À 25,31 €, il coûte environ trois fois moins cher qu’à son lancement. Seule la Fnac reste un peu au-dessus, à 29,99 €.
Avec un 8/10, notre test le considère comme une proposition très solide. On aurait simplement aimé, au moment du test, un peu plus de variété entre les modes de jeu, qui reposent souvent sur le même principe de capture de zones, et quelques cartes plus marquantes. Depuis, les saisons successives sont venues étoffer l’offre.
Pensez aussi que le multijoueur en ligne demande un abonnement PlayStation Plus, comme pour la plupart des jeux sur PS5. Mais pour retrouver le grand spectacle qui a fait la réputation de la série, à ce prix-là, il y a peu de raisons d’hésiter.
Chez Leclerc, l’offre est disponible jusqu’au 6 décembre 2026. Le jeu se retire gratuitement en Click & Collect ,

articles.title: Sony wins $2.6 billion PlayStation Store pricing lawsuit, but digital game prices could still rise
articles.text:
What just happened? The long-running billion-dollar lawsuit Sony has been fighting in the UK over allegations it used its "monopoly position" to inflate the price of digital games has gone Sony's way, though an appeal is still possible. London's Competition Appeal Tribunal dismissed the claim in its entirety on Tuesday, finding that the claimants had failed to prove Sony violated competition law.
Consumer rights campaigner Alex Neill filed the lawsuit way back in August 2022 on behalf of an estimated nine million UK PlayStation users. At the time, the claim was worth up to £5 billion, or around $5.9 billion. Sony tried to have the case thrown out, calling it "flawed from start to finish," but the tribunal allowed it to proceed in November 2023, when the figure being reported was $7.9 billion.
By the time the two sides went to trial in March, the number of players covered had grown to around 12.2 million, while the amount Neill was seeking had fallen. The final claim was for a still enormous £1.49 billion in damages, rising to £1.97 billion ($2.6 billion) with interest.
Neill's argument will sound familiar to anyone who's ever found a boxed PlayStation game going cheap while the digital version was still full price. Retailers can undercut each other on discs, but if you want to download a game or buy DLC, Sony sets the price on the PlayStation Store. Neill argued that Sony's 30% cut pushed up prices and that players would have paid around 20% less if rival stores had been allowed onto the console.
The tribunal disagreed that buying a PlayStation effectively locked players into paying whatever Sony wanted. It added that someone weighing up a PlayStation against an Xbox or a Nintendo console could take the price of games into account before buying the hardware. And for anyone with a disc drive, that cheaper boxed copy was itself a reason for Sony to keep its digital prices competitive.
There was also the question of how much Sony actually makes from a PlayStation. The company sells consoles at thin margins or even at a loss, counting on game sales to make that money back. Looking at the business as a whole, the tribunal found no evidence that Sony's profits were excessive.
Neill says she's considering whether to appeal. The tribunal will hear any application for permission to do so during the week of December 14.
Sony will stop releasing new PlayStation games on disc in January 2028, though publishers can still reorder discs for existing titles. The tribunal said the change fell outside the period covered by the lawsuit, but it also noted that losing competition from retailers selling boxed copies could give Sony room to raise digital prices.
A July price comparison gives PlayStation owners an idea of what they stand to lose. Dutch site Tweakers tracked 16 PS5 games and found that Final Fantasy VII Rebirth was cheaper on disc than on the Dutch PlayStation Store around 90% of the time. Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart, meanwhile, still cost €80 on Sony's store five years after launch. A new boxed copy was going for around €40

articles.title: Microsoft says Bing serves 1B people. Its next search engine isn't for them.
articles.text:
Microsoft says Bing serves 1B people. Its next search engine isn’t for them.
Microsoft says its Bing search engine now has one billion monthly users. The company says those are humans — not AI agents — looking up information on the web. What most people may not realize, though, is that Microsoft also uses the same Bing index to serve agents through Web IQ.
Web IQ is Microsoft’s agentic search service, competing with upstarts like Exa, Firecrawl, and Tavily. DeepSeek opened its own search API to developers in October.
At Microsoft’s Ignite conference this week in San Francisco, The New Stack sat down with Jordi Ribas, Microsoft’s president of Search & AI. Ribas joined the search team in 2008, back when Bing was still called Live Search. Today, his team runs both Bing and Web IQ, which Microsoft introduced at Build in June and opened broadly to Azure customers on Tuesday.
How agents search differently
“Bing is a search engine for humans,” Ribas says. “This is really [a] search engine where the queries come from the AI, and so you do need to design it differently because agents search differently.”
“Bing is a search engine for humans.”
It’s not just that human and agent search queries look different (and Ribas noted that agent searches often look a bit “robotic”), but that they also have different expectations for the results.
On Bing, Ribas says, the order of the results matters because people have to decide which link to click. “An agent doesn’t really need that,” he says, “because an agent will read everything.”
At their core, Bing and Web IQ share the part of the search engine that finds the relevant documents, Ribas says. For agents, Web IQ picks out the passages it deems most relevant and sends them back.
For example, an agent comparing corporate earnings results might need only one row in a table on page 12. Sending the whole report would give the agent more context than it needs, and because the model would have to wade through far more text, the search would become far more expensive.
As Ribas puts it, “the agent will spend money basically by reading all the documents.” “So it’s very important that you extract exactly what you need, and no more.”
Microsoft builds that shared index, always follows the instructions in a site’s robots.txt file, and identifies itself as a crawler, Ribas stressed multiple times. “Not everybody does that in the space.”
How much of the search should the agent do?
Typically, the agent’s orchestrator decides when to call Web IQ as a tool and what queries to send, Ribas notes. “Sometimes the orchestrator is not that smart about knowing what queries to do,” he says, “and it may do multiple iterations.”
At Ignite, Microsoft is addressing this by making Auto the default search mode in Web IQ, which Ribas describes as “kind of like a mini orchestrator that happens within Web IQ.”
With this change, an agent sends Web IQ only one question. Microsoft then tries a few variations of the query in parallel and sends back passages with citations.
Auto Advanced takes this a step further and checks whether the first round turned up enough information. If it finds a gap, it revises the query and searches again. “And we do have a model that says, ‘OK, is that evidence enough to provide a good chat response?'” Ribas says. “And if it’s yes, great, we’re done.”
Unlike some Web IQ competitors that try to create full answers and research reports themselves, Microsoft leaves the agents and models that power them to create the actual answers.
“You can use pretty much any model on top of it,” Ribas says, though he adds that Microsoft is thinking about packaging Web IQ with a model at some point.
What Web IQ costs
On Web IQ, one thousand standard web searches cost $7, compared with $8 for Auto and $9 for Auto Advanced. (The $1 starting price Microsoft advertises is for Browse, where you already have the URL.) If you know exactly what you’re looking for, the standard search may be all you need. But if your agent routinely reads the results, rewrites the query and tries again, a single Auto call could cost less overall.
“If you want to be fast but you want higher quality, maybe Auto is the way to go.”
“If all you care is about being super fast, then you would just use maybe the primitives directly,” Ribas says, referring to the individual search APIs. “If you want to be fast but you want higher quality, maybe Auto is the way to go.”
A crowded agent search market
“People are predicting that in a couple of years there will be 1,000 times more queries done by agents than by humans,” Ribas says. “That’s why there are so many competitors in [the] space.”
Some of those competitors optimize for quality, Ribas says, but “bring a lot of tokens to come up with a comprehensive answer,” which drives up both cost and latency. Others, he says, are very fast, but the quality isn’t there.
“We are able to optimize across three dimensions: quality, latency, and token efficiency,” he says, “and that’s really hard to do.”
Genspark co-founder Ray Zhong says in Microsoft’s announcement that switching to Web IQ cut its voice assistant’s response time from six seconds to 0.6 seconds. “Six seconds in a voice turn is audible dead air.”

articles.title: Sul-coreano confessa ter usado IA para colar em prova de concurso • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Sul-coreano confessa ter usado IA para colar em prova de concurso
Han Won-seok, de 34 anos, quase gabaritou uma prova para certificação de contador tributário na Coreia do Sul ao usar uma minicâmera e inteligência artificial para colar.
Han Won-seok, de 34 anos, quase gabaritou um dos exames profissionais mais importantes da Coreia do Sul. Ele errou apenas uma das 160 questões aplicadas, obtendo 397,5 pontos de um total de 400. Teria sido um desempenho notável se não fosse por um detalhe: o candidato usou uma minicâmera e IA para “colar” na prova.
O exame em questão consiste em um disputado concurso para obtenção de certificado de contador tributário. Trata-se de uma prova tão complicada que os 397,5 pontos registrados por Han Won-seok, que o colocaram na primeira colocação da lista de aprovados, logo fizeram outros candidatos e profissionais que já atuam no segmento tributário suspeitarem de fraude.
Inicialmente, Won-seok negou as indagações. Mas, sentindo-se pressionado e sugerindo estar arrependido, o homem admitiu ter fraudado a prova. A confissão foi feita por meio de um vídeo publicado no canal de seu advogado, Lee Don-Ho, no YouTube.
No vídeo, Won-seok explica que recorreu a uma câmera em miniatura para fotografar as questões, que eram enviadas automaticamente ao seu smartphone. Ele programou o celular para enviar as imagens a uma ferramenta de IA generativa, que gerou as respostas.
As respostas, por sua vez, eram consultadas por meio de uma tela auxiliar ligada ao smartphone. Inicialmente, havia a suspeita de que ele usasse fones de ouvido para obter as respostas da IA, mas não foi o caso.
O esquema deu tão certo que Won-seok o repetiu na segunda etapa do exame, realizado três meses depois, quando então ele obteve 663 de 800 pontos, novamente terminando em primeiro lugar.
É possível que a trapaça tivesse sido impedida se os candidatos houvessem sido proibidos de entrar no local da prova portando o celular. No entanto, eles foram apenas orientados a desligar e guardar o aparelho. Havia dois fiscais na sala onde a prova foi aplicada, nas duas ocasiões, mas nenhum deles notou comportamentos suspeitos por parte de Han Won-seok.
Além de ter confessado a fraude em um vídeo, Han Won-seok afirma ter se entregado à Polícia Metropolitana de Seul, que segue investigando o caso. Ainda não está claro quais punições serão aplicadas ao homem, mas, muito provavelmente, ele perderá a certificação e poderá ficar impedido de prestar um novo exame por cinco anos.
Como o caso foi parar na esfera criminal, existe também chances de Han Won-seok receber uma pena de prisão, embora as investigações sigam com ele em liberdade.
Independentemente do desfecho desta história, o episódio deve servir de base para que as autoridades da Coreia do Sul revisem normas e procedimentos para aplicação de exames públicos. Isso porque casos de fraude em provas envolvendo inteligência artificial não são inéditos no país. Quatro exemplos recentes envolveram o uso de óculos com IA em exames escolares.

articles.title: It shouldn’t be this easy to pedal 25 mph: Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo
articles.text:
I’ve had only one experience of pedaling an e-bike after it ran out of juice, but it was enough to make checking the battery display an anxiety-driven habit: “Can I afford to use the highest assist level up this hill? Should I switch to eco mode to preserve power and make sure I have enough to get home with the bike lights on?”
These aren’t fun questions to have rattling around in your head while riding home in the dark.
But those intrusive thoughts never crossed my mind while I was testing Specialized’s Turbo Vado 3 Evo. I didn’t experience range anxiety, even while blowing through city streets at 25-plus mph (40.2 kph). The bike has so much juice (840 watt-hours) and power (810 watts of peak power and 105 newton-meters of torque) from Specialized’s 3.1 motor system that I could ride as far and as fast as I wanted without worrying about having enough battery to get back home.
Given my preference for biking over driving, I need a bike that can get me across town at a decent clip without draining an entire charge. That’s exactly what the Evo delivered on my longest rides.
What sold me on the bike was a 24-mile round trip that took 83 minutes and used just 56 percent of the battery. According to Specialized’s app, which connects to the bike over Bluetooth, I averaged 235 W of assist power while moving an average of 17 mph, though I was generally closer to 20 mph on stretches where I didn’t have to slow down. I also hit a max speed of 27.3 mph with little effort.
Power and comfort
The bike is a beast, weighing around 70 pounds for the large-size frame I tested. Despite being the heaviest e-bike I’ve ridden, the Evo makes pedaling easier than ever. The bike lacks a throttle, so it takes a few rotations to get moving, but once the assist kicks in, it’s remarkable how easily you can reach the 18–20 mph range.

articles.title: One UI 9.5 ya está aquí: principales novedades y primeros móviles compatibles
articles.text:
Después de una larga espera, Samsung por fin está abriendo el acceso a One UI 9.5, la próxima versión de la capa de personalización que ejecuta sobre Android. El fabricante coreano ha puesto en marcha la beta del nuevo software, que desde hoy se encuentra disponible en sus móviles más importantes y que llega con características bastante interesantes.
Como no podía ser de otra manera, la beta de One UI 9.5 llega primero a los Galaxy S26, S26+ y S26 Ultra. Los usuarios interesados en sumarse al programa tienen que apuntarse a través de la aplicación Samsung Members. La actualización estará disponible inicialmente en un puñado de países, aunque se espera que su alcance se expanda con el correr de las semanas.
Respecto de novedades, One UI 9.5 trae adiciones para destacar en el inicio de la beta. Lo primero para mencionar es que el software incorpora un nuevo modo Pro tanto para la captura de fotos como para la grabación de vídeos. Este llega para ofrecer un control más granular sobre los ajustes de la cámara, algo que tanto entusiastas como creadores de contenido llevaban tiempo reclamando.
Otra característica importante que llega primero a los Galaxy S26 de la mano de One UI 9.5 es el bloqueo de apps con un PIN o datos biométricos. Si bien esta función dice presente en móviles Android de otras marcas, Samsung todavía no la había implementado de forma nativa en su capa de personalización. Esto significa que en adelante será posible blindar el acceso a una aplicación instalada a través de la huella dactilar o un código.
One UI 9.5 inicia su beta en los Samsung Galaxy S26
La beta de One UI 9.5 también introduce cambios en las funciones de salud a través de Samsung Health. Dicha app ahora incluye un apartado dedicado a medicamentos, con recordatorios y un registro para las tomas diarias. Asimismo, introduce una suerte de diario personal enfocado en el bienestar emocional.
El apartado de accesibilidad también se ve mejorado con One UI 9.5. La beta permite, por ejemplo, acceder a los controles para audífonos desde el panel de notificaciones. El software de la firma coreana también implementa los nuevos atajos flotantes, destinados a brindar acceso rápido y con un solo toque a controles de uso esencial.
Todavía no se sabe cuándo se expandirá la versión de pruebas de One UI 9.5 a otros dispositivos que no sean los Galaxy S26. No obstante, Samsung suele ser bastante ágil para abrir su software a un mayor número de modelos cuando la beta ya está en marcha. Los primeros países en recibir el software son Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, Polonia, Alemania, India y Corea del Sur, pero se expandirá a otros mercados con el paso de los días.

articles.title: Spend management platform Payhawk announces $280M raise, 2B valuation | TechCrunch
articles.text:
U.K.-based fintech Payhawk announced a $280 million Series C funding round Wednesday, led by Goldman Sachs’ growth equity arm, making it one of Europe’s largest Series C rounds this year, as noted by Sifted. The round values the company at $2 billion, bringing its total funding to more than $500 million to date.
Founded in 2018, Payhawk is an enterprise financial management platform that helps companies track and manage expenses and procurement using AI agents. Speaking to FinTech magazine, Payhawk’s co-founder and CEO, Hristo Borisov, said the company saw “an incredible growth opportunity and room to bring finance teams AI-native products that combine agents, payment infrastructure, and enterprise controls.”
Payhawk competes with spend management companies Pleo, Moss, and Spendesk, and says it operates in 33 countries. Notably, the company said it still has 70% of the $100 million it raised in 2022, a round that valued the company at $1 billion. This fresh capital will support its global expansion. Other investors in the round include Greenoaks, Lightspeed, and QED.

articles.title: We’ve played GTA 6 at home, and these are the 6 gaming TVs to buy this Black Friday to really immerse yourself in this ‘cinematic blockbuster of a game’, including models from LG, Sony, TCL and Hisense — all reviewed by our experts
articles.text:
‘A world that demands your attention’: Now we’ve played GTA 6 in-depth, I’ve picked 6 gaming TVs I reviewed to make the most of the ‘incredibly lifelike’ Vice City
Get the best out of GTA 6
After a 13-year wait, GTA 6 launches at midnight on Thursday, November 19: less than two full days! Hopefully, you’ve got your PS5 or Xbox Series X ready in time for the launch, but as TechRadar’s TV reviewer, I thought I’d pick some of the best gaming TVs I’ve tested this year that will hopefully do justice to the latest installment in Rockstar’s legendary franchise.
Thankfully, I don’t have to guess how GTA 6 looks, as I’ve been speaking to Rob Dwiar, TechRadar Gaming's Managing Editor, who’s been playing the game ahead of launch for review, and he’s told me all about how the game looks and performs after playing on an Acer Predator X32QFS monitor. So I’ve based my TV picks based on Rob’s impressions and my top gaming TVs.
LG C6
The LG C6 ticks every box you need for gaming. It’s fully kitted out with four HDMI 2.1 ports that support 4K 165Hz, full VRR, ALLM, and Dolby Vision gaming. While some were sad about the news that GTA 6 will only run at 30fps, Rob assures me that the world is so densely detailed and smooth that he’d "long forgotten he was playing at 30fps".
This means you’ll need a TV that can handle the densely packed world of Vice City without sacrificing performance and detail, and the C6 is more capable based on my time using it with other games.
The C6 excels at delivering excellent picture quality. One of Rob’s favorite images is when you see "neon lights piercing a black sky" when driving around at night, and as the C6 delivers rich, vibrant colors and inky blacks, thanks to its OLED panel, it will do justice to these moments.
Xbox Series X gamers will also benefit from Dolby Vision, and as the C6 supports it, you can expect a gorgeous, high-contrast, detailed picture with Dolby Vision’s benefits. But fear not if you’re a PS5 owner: the C6’s HDR picture is also incredible.
The C6 is available in a range of sizes, from 42-inch for bedrooms and smaller rooms, to 83-inch for those who want the full experience. The C6 is arguably the best bang-for-your-buck TV on the market, and that’s why it’s my top recommendation. A 48-inch C6 is available for $999 at Best Buy in the US, while you can pick up a 48-inch C6 for £908.03 at Amazon UK in the UK.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
TCL QM7L/C7L
If you want a gaming TV that still delivers premium performance but is a little more affordable, especially if you’re looking for a bigger screen, the TCL QM7L (known as the TCL C7L in the UK) is easily one of the best picks.
Using TCL’s new SQD (super quantum dot) mini-LED panel, the QM7L/C7L offers powerful contrast and bold colors, and does a great job at reducing backlight blooming, something that can affect mini-LED TVs.
This is going to be vital as Rob tells me that "every image, scene, and locale is dense and detailed", so you’ll want a TV that can deliver a balanced but strong picture. Having used the C7L for gaming myself, I know it's capable of delivering superb picture quality and performance, even with chaotic 120fps games like Battlefield V.
The QM7L/C7L also supports Dolby Vision, so Xbox gamers will benefit from this, as both the Xbox Series X and GTA 6 support Dolby Vision.
The QM7L/C7L’s real selling point is its price. In the US, you can pick up a 65-inch QM7L for $849.99 at Best Buy, which is a steal for a TV of this calibre. In the UK, the 55-inch C7L is available for £749 at Argos
LG B6
OLED doesn’t have to be expensive, and when it comes to great value OLED TVs, the LG B6 is one of the best. Crucially, it’ll still deliver the picture quality and features I’d recommend for GTA 6, but at a lower price than other OLEDs.
While it doesn’t deliver the same brightness as step-up OLEDs (just over 800 nits), HDR highlights and contrast are still fantastic, which will work great for nighttime drives through the neon-clad streets of downtown Vice City.
OLED TVs also deliver realistic details and textures, and Rob told me during his playtime so far that you’ll want to "devour every detail" of Vice City, from people’s faces and hair to the clothes they’re wearing and cars they drive. Even details like "rust on an RV wheel arch" warrant appreciation, and the B6’s picture is good enough for that.
Where the B6 is at its best is its price. A 48-inch B6 costs $599 at Best Buy in the US, perfect for those who’ll be playing in their bedroom. Similarly, you can pick up a 48-inch B6 for £774 at Amazon UK, as well as a host of other retailers in the UK.
Sony Bravia 7 II
The Sony Bravia 7 II is Sony’s entry-level RGB mini-LED TV, but as I found during my testing, it really shows the potential of the new panel tech.
Not only does it deliver deep black levels and strong contrast that some standard mini-LED TVs can’t, but it also has rich, bold colors that really pop on screen. It also delivers true-to-life textures, and as Rob explains, outside of downtown Vice City, there are "breathtaking vistas on the ocean" and "natural landscapes in the north that feel very Red Dead 2-esque". The Bravia 7 II is going to do a great job with these landscapes.
The Bravia 7 II is also an excellent option for PS5 gamers, as it’s equipped with ‘Perfect for PS5’ features, including Auto HDR Tone Mapping, which makes contrast and textures even sharper. Again, this is perfect for the detail-packed graphics.
The Bravia 7 II isn’t cheap for a ‘mid-range’ TV, but you can pick up a 55-inch Bravia 7 II for $1,499.99 at Best Buy in the US and a 55-inch Bravia 7 II for £1,299 at Richer Sounds in the UK. While this puts it in the same bracket as OLED TVs, I’d argue that the Bravia 7 II delivers OLED-like performance.
Hisense U7
If you’re looking for a big screen for cheap in the US, the Hisense U7 is a brilliant option. Again, it comes with the bells and whistles we look for in gaming TVs — 4K 165Hz, FreeSync Premium Pro and Dolby Vision gaming — with great performance to match.
When playing games on it, reviewer James Holland found that ‘action was smooth and clear regardless of the game’. That’s going to be important for the lifelike Vice City, which, as we’ve discovered from Rob, is densely packed with detail.
Rob points out that in some cases the game "can be quite bright," pointing to clear sky days where reflections off objects, realistic lighting, and the sun beating down can all add to an overall light and bright image. As the U7 boasts brightness over 2,800 nits in most of its picture modes, it’ll easily be able to handle these bright scenes. This is something entry-level LED TVs just won’t be able to do.
Hisense’s TVs are often fantastic value, and that’s no different for the U7. You can pick up the 75-inch U7 for $999 at Best Buy, which is a great price for a TV at that size with this performance. In the UK, the U7 Pro 65-inch costs £999 at Currys.
LG G6
If you’re looking for the ultimate gaming TV, the LG G6 is a flagship OLED that delivers excellent brightness, lifelike detail and textures, and balanced contrast and vivid colors that are perfect for gaming. Plus, it has every feature you could need, including four HDMI 2.1 ports that support 4K 165Hz, full VRR and Dolby Vision gaming.
Speaking to Rob, he describes GTA 6 as a "cinematic blockbuster of a game", and the LG G6 has served as my reference TV for all things movie and gaming this year, so what better TV to get the most out of GTA 6, a world that Rob says "demands your attention".
From the detailed, natural landscapes to the downtown nighttime driving in Vice City, the G6 will more than handle this densely packed world. And with super smooth performance, it should easily render the hustle and bustle of "the most complete open world experience you’ll ever play".
The G6 is a premium TV and, as such, carries a premium price. Still, you can pick up a 55-inch G6 for $1,899 at Best Buy in the US, and the 55-inch G6 for £1,619.10 at Smart Home Sounds in the UK. A high price, but this TV more than delivers on it.
I'm the Senior TV Writer here at TechRadar, where I test all things TV, AV and 4K Blu-ray. Before joining TechRadar, I worked in a specialist AV retailer, helping plan cinema room installations and demoing the latest TVs and Hi-Fi.
I've seen and tested every kind of TV on the market since starting my journey in the AV world, from budget 32-inch screens, to elite OLED and cinema-sized 116-inch TVs, so I know what makes for a good TV.
I've personally tested nearly every TV on this list, so to earn a spot, they've had to impress me with their features, performance and value for money. I know all these TVs will do GTA 6 justice.
Rob is the Managing Editor of TechRadar Gaming and Streaming. He's been on TechRadar in one form or another since joining TechRadar Gaming (TRG) as Deputy Editor after being a Commissioning Editor and writer at sister-site GamesRadar+ for nearly five years, and a Gaming Editor at another publication. He has nearly a decade's worth of experience writing about games and tech, with a number of bylines at games publications, but also in the world of landscapes and horticulture.
He has played GTA 6 for around 100 hours for our review, and gave it the highest score we offer: a full five stars. You'll find his thoughts on the visual delights and offerings of Rockstar's blockbuster behemoth throughout this guide.
Follow TechRadar on Google News and add us as a preferred source to get our expert news, reviews, and opinion in your feeds.
James is the TV Hardware Staff Writer at TechRadar. Before joining the team, he worked at a major UK based AV retailer selling TV and audio equipment, where he was either telling customers the difference between OLED and QLED or being wowed by watching a PS5 run on the LG 65G2. When not writing about the latest TV tech, James can be found gaming, reading, watching rugby or coming up with another idea for a novel.

articles.title: Exclusive: Wherobots AI agents automate complex spatial data engineering - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Wherobots AI agents automate complex spatial data engineering
Cloud-native spatial analytics and artificial intelligence startup Wherobots Inc. today introduced an artificial intelligence agent that enables users to build and deploy spatial data pipelines using natural-language instructions, reducing the need for specialized programming expertise.
Called Waldo, the agent can discover data sources, generate queries, perform analysis, visualize results and schedule recurring operations. It’s designed for applications involving location-based information such as satellite imagery, road networks, GPS tracking data and geographic features.
Spatial data presents unusual processing challenges because it combines multiple data types, including geographic coordinates, imagery and geometric shapes. Analyzing this information at scale often requires specialized tools and scarce technical expertise.
A recent survey by Global Marketing Insights Inc. concluded that the global geospatial workforce is 10 to 15 years behind in building the skill levels employers need.
Wherobots, which was founded in 2022 by the creators of the open-source Apache Sedona spatial analytics engine, said Waldo can compress development projects that traditionally take weeks into days.
“Waldo is our new agentic interface,” said Damian Wylie, Wherobots’ head of product. Unlike general-purpose AI coding assistants, he said, Waldo can invoke specialized computational engines that can process enormous geographic datasets.
“We’re not deploying some net-new [large language model] under the hood,” Wylie said. “We’re connecting existing LLMs to our product and also giving it the context it needs to speed up that spatial data workflow.”
The agent orchestrates several components of Wherobots’ platform. Its Havasu spatial data and knowledge catalog discovers and prepares public geographic datasets alongside customers’ private information. RasterFlow, Wherobots’ serverless Earth intelligence and inference engine, processes satellite and aerial imagery using computer vision models to identify features such as buildings, roads and land-use changes.
WherobotsDB executes the resulting analysis using more than 300 spatial functions, while Wherobots Maps visualizes the results. Completed pipelines can be scheduled to refresh automatically as new data arrives.
The distributed processing platform uses existing cloud storage and enterprise data catalogs, including Amazon Web Services Inc.’s Glue and Databricks Unity Catalog, eliminating the need for customers to migrate their data, Wylie said.
In a demonstration, he showed how Waldo could identify the drainage area surrounding Montana’s West Boulder River using geographic and elevation data. The agent located relevant datasets, constructed a geographic representation of the watershed and displayed the results on a map.
The resulting geometry could support subsequent analysis of snowfall, water runoff or changing environmental conditions, Wylie said. Waldo can also process satellite imagery using specialized machine learning models, including Meta Platforms Inc.’s Segment Anything Model 3.
Potential commercial applications include identifying delivery vehicles that deviate from planned routes, assessing weather-related transportation disruptions and analyzing advertising impressions based on billboard locations and mobility patterns.
Wherobots said customer Action Engine Inc. is using the technology to build recurring fleet analytics pipelines and reports that it can deliver new spatial analyses two to three times faster that was possible with manual processes. Another customer used the platform’s distributed computing architecture to reduce a large-scale data-joining operation from approximately a week to less than an hour, said Benjamin Pruden, Wherobots’ go-to-market executive.
Waldo isn’t intended to eliminate human oversight, executives said. Users can inspect generated queries, review geographic visualizations and create Jupyter notebooks to examine individual processing steps. Wylie acknowledged that the technology can’t guarantee accurate results from every prompt.
“That’s an area we’ll invest,” Wylie said. “We’re not at the stage where we’re going to say every prompt is the best quality you’ll ever get.”
Waldo is available in public preview, with agent tokens currently included at no additional charge in Wherobots Professional Edition. Customers pay primarily for the computational resources they consume, with controls to select processing capacity and monitor costs.

articles.title: Wüstensand als Gedächtnis fremder Welten – wie Dünen die Windstärken auf dem Mars verraten
articles.text:
Fremde Welten: Wie Sanddünen auf der Erde die Windgeschwindigkeiten auf dem Mars verraten
Wissenschaftler der Stanford University im US-Bundesstaat Kalifornien haben nachgewiesen, dass die mittlere Korngröße des Sandes in Dünen auf der Erde und dem Mars Rückschlüsse auf die Geschwindigkeit jener Winde zulässt, welche die Formationen aufgebaut haben. Wie aus einer in der Fachzeitschrift „Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences“ veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, können Forscher:innen den Sand dadurch wie einen Geschwindigkeitsmesser für heutige und vor Milliarden Jahren versteinerte Dünen im Sonnensystem nutzen.
In den vergangenen Jahrzehnten hatten Raumsonden und Teleskope vom Wind geformte Dünen und Rippelmarken auf der Venus, dem Mars, dem Saturnmond Titan sowie auf einem Kometen entdeckt. Anhand der äußeren Form und Ausrichtung dieser Strukturen konnten Planetenforscher:innen zwar die Richtung und die Beständigkeit der Winde bestimmen, nicht jedoch deren konkrete Geschwindigkeit am Boden.
Stanford University: Wie Korngröße und Windgeschwindigkeit in Sanddünen zusammenhängen
Der Erstautor Colin Marvin und der Seniorautor Mathieu Lapôtre von der Fakultät für Erd- und Planetenwissenschaften der Stanford University belegen in ihrer Untersuchung, dass Dünen auf der Erde und dem Mars überwiegend von Winden geformt werden, die gerade stark genug sind, um die Sandkörner am Boden in Bewegung zu setzen. Da größere und schwerere Körner einen stärkeren Luftstrom benötigen, um über diese physikalische Transportschwelle gehoben zu werden, gibt der mittlere Durchmesser der Sandkörner einer Düne Auskunft über die vorherrschende Windstärke.
In der Geologie wird dieser Vorgang, bei dem Wind einzelne Körner vom Boden abhebt und in kurzen Sprüngen vorwärtstreibt, als Saltation bezeichnet. Zwar bewegen seltene Stürme kurzfristig große Mengen an Material, doch über lange Zeiträume hinweg leisten die deutlich häufigeren Winde knapp oberhalb der kritischen Bewegungsschwelle den größten Beitrag zum Aufbau einer Düne.
Laut einer Mitteilung der Stanford University bezeichnet Colin Marvin, der inzwischen als Postdoktorand an der US-amerikanischen Brown University forscht, Dünen daher als einen „großartigen Datenspeicher für das, was auf der Oberfläche eines Planeten geschieht, und insbesondere für die Wechselwirkungen zwischen den Vorgängen in der Atmosphäre eines Planeten und den Prozessen an der Oberfläche“. Dass sich Dünenfelder auf ein solches Gleichgewicht nahe der Transportschwelle einpendeln, hatten zwei Wissenschaftler der US-amerikanischen University of Pennsylvania bereits im Jahr 2010 anhand weniger Stichproben als Hypothese formuliert.
Da diese Annahme seither nicht systematisch an einer größeren Zahl von Wüsten oder auf anderen Himmelskörpern überprüft worden war, werteten Marvin und Lapôtre nun Wetterdaten aus einem Zeitraum von 30 Jahren sowie Messungen der Korngrößen aus 24 weltweit verteilten Dünenfeldern mit unterschiedlichen Formen und Ausmaßen aus. Die Berechnung, welche Windgeschwindigkeiten im Laufe der Zeit am meisten Sand bewegten, bestätigte vom Coral Pink Sand Dunes State Park im US-Bundesstaat Utah bis hin zur Namib-Wüste im afrikanischen Namibia durchgehend das vermutete Verhältnis zwischen Korndurchmesser und Windstärke.
Vom Mars bis zur frühen Erde: Klimamodelle mit versteinerten Sanddünen prüfen
Anschließend übertrugen die beiden Wissenschaftler ihre Berechnungsmethode auf die Messdaten eines Dünenfelds auf dem Mars, obwohl sich der Planet bei Atmosphärendruck, Schwerkraft und der Dichte des Sediments deutlich von der Erde unterscheidet. Da sich auch dort dieselbe statistische Korrelation zeigte, gehen die Autoren davon aus, dass Winddünen auf allen Himmelskörpern nach demselben Prinzip entstehen, sofern ausreichend loses Sediment vorhanden ist und starke Stürme seltener auftreten als schwächere Winde.
Weil sich historische Dünen über geologische Zeiträume zu Sandstein verfestigen und die Korngrößen darin erhalten bleiben, ergänzt die Methode eine frühere Untersuchung desselben Forschungsteams im Fachmagazin „Geology“ und erlaubt auch Berechnungen für die frühe Erdgeschichte, wie Mathieu Lapôtre erläutert: „Das funktioniert bei heutigen Dünen ebenso wie bei Sandsteinen, die bis zu drei Milliarden Jahre alt sind.“ Mit diesen aus versteinerten Dünen gewonnenen Werten wollen Forscher:innen künftig Computermodelle zur atmosphärischen Zirkulation auf der frühen Erde und dem Mars überprüfen.
Grenzen der Methode für die Planetenforschung auf Mars und Titan
In der praktischen Anwendung unterliegt das Verfahren der durch die US-amerikanische Forschungsstiftung National Science Foundation geförderten Studie allerdings deutlichen Einschränkungen. Um aus der Korngröße eines Dünenfelds auf einem anderen Himmelskörper die Windgeschwindigkeit abzuleiten, müssen zunächst Daten über den mittleren Durchmesser und die Materialdichte der dortigen Sandkörner vorliegen.
Während Kameras auf Raumsonden im Orbit zwar die großflächigen Formen von Dünen auf dem Mars, der Venus oder dem Saturnmond Titan erfassen, lassen sich millimetergroße Partikel aus der Umlaufbahn nur indirekt und mit Unsicherheiten über thermische Messungen abschätzen. Verlässliche Berechnungen setzen daher im Regelfall Messungen durch Lander oder Rover direkt vor Ort voraus und liefern selbst dann nur Durchschnittswerte der häufigsten Winde, während seltene Extremwetterereignisse im Sand kaum dauerhafte Spuren hinterlassen.

articles.title: Nvidia board faction angling for Jensen Huang return as CEO, report claims — company defiant at earnings calls, says no possibility of reinstatement
articles.text:
Nvidia board faction angling for Jensen Huang return as CEO, report claims — company defiant at earnings calls, says no possibility of reinstatement
Huang has already said he'd be willing to return, but whether he will get the chance is still very much up in the air.
Even though Nvidia says that it does not plan to bring its former CEO Jensen Huang back to the company, that hasn't stopped some of its board members from continuing to lobby for his return. Following the news that some of Huang's allies have formed a "war room" to drive his reinstatement just days after his resignation, one Nvidia employee went so far as to warn that the company faces the possibility of an exodus of "irreplaceable talent" if Huang isn't reinstated. We've even seen U.S. President Trump argue for giving Huang his old job back, but the company said during its November 17 earnings call that wasn't in the cards. Now, Semafor reports that some Nvidia board members aren't taking "no" for an answer.
Huang, for his part, has already said that he would be "honored" to return to the company that he resigned from in disgrace just a few days ago. At the time, he admitted to having an affair with a woman who worked for Megaspeed, a controversial Nvidia customer linked to the smuggling of export-controlled AI hardware into China. That woman has also been accused of being a Chinese spy, further complicating an already troublesome matter for Nvidia and Huang. Huang and Nvidia's top lawyer will make an appearance before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees in early December and are likely to face some difficult questions.
But despite all of this, Huang is said to have spoken with at least one Nvidia board member about the possibility of making a return to Nvidia. That meeting took place hours before Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that Huang wasn't coming back. The board voted unanimously to accept his resignation, and won't be backtracking. It's reported that three board members don't agree with that stance, while others have already turned their attention to who will replace Huang long-term. Interim CEO Colette Kress is not being considered as a full-time replacement for Huang.
Instead, Arm CEO Rene Haas has appeared as a frontrunner for the top job, with the Nvidia board believed to have already made an approach. Marvell CEO Matt Murphy is also another name under consideration, but the ongoing calls for Huang to be brought back into the fold are thought to have put him off. Rene Haas has reportedly been considere
It isn't just some of Nvidia's board members who have rallied around Huang. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have also chimed in, while a Taiwanese skyscraper was used to send messages of support to a man who has proven hugely popular in the country.

articles.title: Microsoft amplia linha própria de IA com sete novos modelos • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Microsoft amplia linha própria de IA com sete novos modelos
Nova geração inclui IAs para código, cibersegurança, imagem e voz. Modelos devem ser integrados ao GitHub.
A Microsoft apresentou uma nova geração de modelos proprietários de IA chamados MAI. Os sistemas são especializados em tarefas como programação, cibersegurança e edição de imagens, e devem ser usados para reduzir o custo de tarefas sem recorrer aos modelos mais avançados do mercado.
O anúncio foi feito nessa terça-feira (17/11), durante a conferência Ignite e, segundo o CEO da Microsoft AI, Mustafa Suleyman, eles devem ser integrados ao GitHub. Ainda assim, a Microsoft não informou quando o uso do GitHub Copilot pretende migrar para a tecnologia própria.
Na ocasião, a empresa também anunciou o MAI Licensed Weights, para empresas que queiram adaptar os modelos da Microsoft dentro do Azure.
O MAI Code 2 é a principal aposta da nova geração para programação. O modelo foi treinado para tarefas comuns dentro do GitHub Copilot, como escrever código e fazer manutenção de sistemas. Ele, segundo a Microsoft, alcança 98% do desempenho do GPT-6.1 Sol por 40% do preço. Em comparação com o Claude Opus 5.5, da Anthropic, a empresa diz entregar 96% da performance por apenas 5% do custo.
Há ainda o MAI Code 2 Flash, versão mais leve para tarefas que exigem menos tempo de raciocínio. Segundo a companhia, ele alcança desempenho equivalente ao GPT-6 Luna por 65% do preço e ao Claude Haiku 5.5 por 20% do custo.
Além do lançamento voltado à criação e edição de código, a Microsoft também apresentou soluções para outras tarefas. Para criação visual, ela traz o MAI Image 2.7, que, segundo a companhia, assumiu o primeiro lugar no ranking de edição de imagens da Artificial Analysis.
Aproveitando o cenário de tensão em relação às IAs e a segurança digital, a companhia também lançou o MAI Cyber 2 Flash, voltado à defesa de sistemas. Segundo a companhia, o modelo pode executar verificações repetidamente e em segundo plano e teria igualado resultados do GPT-6 Astra no benchmark CyberGymE2E.
Ao todo, Suleyman apresentou sete novos modelos ou sistemas:
A aposta da Microsoft parte da ideia de que nem toda solicitação precisa ser enviada a um modelo de propósito geral que resolveria problemas muito mais complexos. Na avaliação de Suleyman, sistemas de fronteira carregam conhecimentos muito avançados que continuam presentes mesmo quando o usuário pede algo simples, aumentando o custo de processamento.
A proposta dos modelos especializados é concentrar capacidade em um conjunto mais restrito de tarefas. “Isso basicamente significa que você coloca mais tokens, conhecimento e especialização na mesma quantidade de parâmetros”, afirmou Suleyman ao Axios.
Outras companhias também têm investido mais nessa integração entre modelos de maior e menor capacidade de raciocínio. O Google, por exemplo, desenvolveu uma ferramenta para o Google Antigravity — chatbot de programação da empresa — para que o usuário possa atribuir tarefas mais ou menos pesadas entre seu modelo mais avançado, o Gemini 4 Carbon, e outros modelos mais básicos como a versão Hydrogen, lançada em seguida.

articles.title: Google's AI feature in Search gets its own incognito mode | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google’s search engine has long offered an incognito mode for all those search queries you don’t want logged or associated with your account. Now, Google’s AI Mode in Search is getting a similar feature. In a blog post, the company announced a new feature that brings “temporary threads” to AI Mode, where the conversations you have won’t be resurfaced later in areas like your search history or recommendations.
Many leading AI chatbots already offer the option for temporary chats, Google Gemini included. However, there was not yet an option to have a temporary chat when you’re searching Google and are dropped into its conversational interface, known as AI Mode.
Google says that users won’t have to adjust their settings to take advantage of the new option. Instead, they’ll be able to click a temporary threads icon in the upper right corner of AI Mode to engage in a temporary chat. This essentially works the same as a temporary chat would in the stand-alone Gemini chatbot.
The option could be convenient to use at those times when you start digging deeper into a particular topic via AI Mode and realize that you don’t want the discussion to become a part of your search history because of its personal nature.
Once the temporary thread is started, the session becomes detached from your account, Google says. This means that the responses the AI provides won’t be informed by past preferences, nor will they impact future personalization. That could also be useful for those times when you want to learn about something as more of a one-off, but don’t want Google to start to think of the topic as one of your main interests.
When you close out of the thread, you will return to searching as usual.
The company says the option to engage in temporary chats in AI Mode is rolling out globally on desktop and mobile across all supported languages.

articles.title: Zink-Luft-Akku statt Lithium: Warum ausgerechnet Vitamin B12 ein altes Ladeproblem löst
articles.text:
Vitamin B12 im Stromspeicher: Forscher:innen machen Zink-Luft-Batterien wiederaufladbar
Ein Team aus Forscher:innen der spanischen Universität Córdoba hat einen wiederaufladbaren Zink-Luft-Akku entwickelt, der mithilfe von Vitamin B12 arbeitet. Wie in einer im britischen Fachmagazin „Journal of Materials Chemistry A“ veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, überstand der Prototyp im Labor bis zu 250 Lade- und Entladezyklen.
Entgegen manchen Schlagzeilen liefert der auch als Cobalamin bekannte Nährstoff dabei nicht selbst die Energie, sondern wirkt an der Luftelektrode als Katalysator, der die chemischen Prozesse beschleunigt. „Vitamin B12 hat bewiesen, dass es die notwendigen Voraussetzungen erfüllt, um als guter Katalysator zu fungieren: Beim Entladen katalysiert es die Reduktion von Sauerstoff zu Wasser, und beim Wiederaufladen fördert es die Bildung von Sauerstoff“, erklärt der beteiligte Studienleiter Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero, wie Scitechdaily unter Berufung auf die Hochschule berichtet.
Warum Zink-Luft-Batterien bisher meist Einwegprodukte sind
Zink-Luft-Batterien erzeugen elektrischen Strom, indem metallisches Zink im Inneren mit Sauerstoff reagiert, der direkt aus der Umgebungsluft in die Zelle strömt. Weil dieser Sauerstoff nicht im Gehäuse gespeichert werden muss, sind solche Batterien deutlich leichter als herkömmliche Akkus und erreichen rechnerisch eine Energiedichte von 1.218 Wattstunden pro Kilogramm.
Zudem ist Zink reichlich verfügbar, lässt sich recyceln und kommt in der Zelle mit einer Batterieflüssigkeit auf Wasserbasis aus, die weder brennen noch explodieren kann. Im Alltag stecken Zink-Luft-Zellen bisher trotzdem überwiegend als Einweg-Knopfzellen in Hörgeräten, weil sich der chemische Prozess beim Aufladen ohne passende Hilfsstoffe nur sehr träge umkehren lässt.
Die Arbeitsgruppe an der Universität Córdoba hatte für diese Aufgabe in früheren Versuchen bereits natürliche Stoffe wie den roten Blutfarbstoff Hämoglobin und das Enzym Katalase getestet, konnte diese Batterien wegen des darin enthaltenen Eisens jedoch nicht wieder aufladen. Vitamin B12 besitzt in seiner Mitte hingegen ein Kobalt-Atom, das die Reaktion in beide Richtungen antreibt, also sowohl die Aufnahme von Sauerstoff beim Entladen als auch dessen Freisetzung beim Aufladen.
Kohlenstoffnanoröhrchen verhindern das Auflösen von Vitamin B12
Bei der Konstruktion der Elektrode mussten die Wissenschaftler:innen zunächst ein praktisches Problem lösen, denn Vitamin B12 löst sich leicht in Wasser auf und würde in der Batterieflüssigkeit nach kurzer Zeit weggespült. Um den Nährstoff dauerhaft an seinem Platz zu halten, heftete das Team die Vitaminmoleküle an mikroskopisch dünne Röhrchen aus Kohlenstoff.
Diese Kohlenstoffnanoröhrchen leiten nicht nur den elektrischen Strom, sondern gehen mit dem Vitamin eine feste chemische Verbindung nach demselben Prinzip ein, das in der Natur auch die Bausteine von Proteinen zusammenhält. Während herkömmliche Kobalt-Katalysatoren bei der Herstellung oft auf 700 bis 1.000 Grad Celsius erhitzt werden müssen, läuft diese Verknüpfung bei Raumtemperatur ab, bevor das Material bei 40 Grad Celsius trocknet.
In der Lauge im Inneren der Batterie klappt das gebundene Vitaminmolekül teilweise auf, sodass der einströmende Luftsauerstoff direkt an das Kobalt-Atom im Zentrum gelangt. Dadurch funktioniert der Ladungsaustausch ohne störende Zwischenschritte, bei denen in früheren Versuchen mit nur lose aufgetragenem Vitamin B12 noch unerwünschte Nebenprodukte die Reaktion bremsten.
Leistung im Labor und die Schattenseiten der Zink-Luft-Technik
„Wir haben uns die Eigenschaften angesehen, die wir in natürlich vorkommenden Materialien finden können, um sie in neuen Batterien einzusetzen“, sagt der Mitautor Manuel Cano Luna zur Motivation hinter dem Experiment. Im Labortest hielt die rund einen Quadratzentimeter große Testzelle mit einem leitfähigen Gel im Inneren bis zu 250 Ladezyklen durch, während eine baugleiche Zelle ohne Vitamin B12 schon beim zweiten Aufladen ausfiel.
Trotz dieser Ausdauer zeigen die Messdaten der Studie, dass bis zu einem alltagstauglichen Stromspeicher noch deutliche Hürden bestehen. Die von den Forscher:innen berechnete Kapazität von 199,4 Amperestunden pro Gramm bezieht sich nämlich allein auf die hauchdünne Vitaminschicht und schrumpft auf 4,13 Amperestunden pro Gramm, sobald das Gewicht der gesamten Elektrode mitgezählt wird.
Hinzu kommt, dass auch ein biologischer Stoff wie Vitamin B12 im Kern nicht ohne das Schwermetall Kobalt auskommt, wenngleich hier nur kleinste Mengen nötig sind. Nach rund 250 Ladezyklen verliert der Akku zudem an Leistung, weil gelöste Zinkteilchen vom Gegenpol und Salze aus der Batterieflüssigkeit eine Kruste über dem Vitamin bilden und die Luftzufuhr verstopfen.

articles.title: Google Keep prépare une nouveauté très attendue pour enfin retrouver vos notes en un clic
articles.text:
Si vous utilisez Google Keep régulièrement, vous savez qu’il n’est pas toujours simple de retrouver une note en utilisant simplement la barre de recherche ou le système d’étiquettes manuelles. Google semble conscient du problème si l’on en croit nos confrères d’Android Authority qui ont trouvé une nouveauté très intéressante dans le code de la version 5.26.461.01.90 de l’application qui intègre désormais des filtres sous forme d’onglets.
Des onglets pour trier vos notes Google Keep
Placés juste en dessous de la barre de recherche principale, ces nouveaux filtres ont évidemment pour but de faciliter la navigation. La vue par défaut, intitulée « Tous », conserve l’affichage classique en plaçant les notes épinglées en haut de liste, suivies immédiatement par les notes les plus récentes. En sélectionnant l’option « Cette semaine », l’application isole uniquement les notes rédigées au cours des sept derniers jours, ce qui évite d’avoir à trop faire défiler l’écran.
Source : Android Authority
Le filtre « À faire » rassemble quant à lui l’ensemble des notes associées à des tâches et des rappels. De son côté, l’onglet « Listes » filtre uniquement les notes au format à puces. L’onglet « Partagés » permet également de retrouver en un clic les documents partagés avec d’autres utilisateurs. Pas mal de filtres supplémentaires, donc, qui devraient aider à la navigation sur Google Keep.
Quelques changements d’interface au passage
En plus de ces nouveaux outils de tri, cette version v5.26.461.01.90 de Google Keep cache quelques changements visuels sur la page d’accueil. Les notes épinglées n’apparaissent ainsi plus sous une section dédiée, mais affichent désormais une icône d’épingle discrète dans leur coin supérieur droit.
Source : Android Authority
À lire : Google Keep ne plaisante plus avec ces deux nouveautés
Enfin, le texte qui se trouve dans chaque carte sur l’écran d’accueil profite désormais d’un effet de fondu progressif vers le bas. Toutes ces nouveautés étaient fonctionnelles en manipulant le fichier APK, mais ne sont pas encore déployées sur la version stable de l’application. Reste maintenant à savoir quand Google se décidera à les déployer.

articles.title: Paso a paso para invertir en criptomonedas y cuál es su valor este miércoles 18 de noviembre
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 64.674,74 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -0,338% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de -0,633% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 1.811,43 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de -0,01%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 592,72 dólares, con un cambio de 0,34%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 44.68 dólares, tras una variación de 0.5470506.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,06 dólares tras presentar un cambio de 1,41% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Criptomonedas en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Circular economy company Recove Ventures raises Rs 56.25 Cr
articles.text:
Circular economy company Recove Ventures raises Rs 56.25 Cr
The company said that it will use the capital to build circular economy infrastructure in Maharashtra and expand Recove’s footprint in Karnataka.
B2B circular economy startup Recove Ventures has raised Rs 56.25 crore in a funding round comprising Rs 36.25 crore in equity and Rs 20 crore in debt.
The round saw participation from Samara Capital Founder and CEO Sumeet Narang, Capri Global and Amit Prakash Sharma Family Trust (Sunrise Foods). Existing backers, including the family office of Chaitanya Kejriwal of Parksons Packaging and 5F World Chairman Ganesh Natarajan, also invested.
Recove will deploy the funding towards expanding its operations across India, with a focus on setting up circular economy infrastructure in Maharashtra and strengthening its presence in Karnataka, it said in a statement.
The investment will also go towards increasing industrial processing capacity, adding to its network of pre-processing facilities and developing technology to track materials and ensure quality.
The company has entered into 10-year MoUs with the governments of Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Uttar Pradesh. The agreements envisage investments exceeding Rs 500 crore in each state.
Including its existing commitments in Karnataka, Recove expects its planned investments across these markets to cross Rs 2,000 crore over the next decade.
The company is also exploring its next expansion opportunity in Uttar Pradesh.
“India's plastic recycling industry has a quality problem, not a recycling problem. The quality of recycled plastic is decided at the very start of the chain, at segregation, and cannot be recovered downstream. That is why Recove started at segregation and is building upwards from there to deliver consistent, industrial-grade recycled material at scale," said Viral Chhajer, Co-founder, Recove Ventures.
“Recove’s focus on segregation, processing and traceability addresses the practical challenges that manufacturers face when sourcing recycled plastic. Its network combines local sourcing with processing at scale—a strong foundation for serving customers reliably and building a commercially durable business," said Sumeet Narang, Founder & CEO, Samara Capital.
Recove uses digital tracking to monitor its materials. The company said this allows it to maintain traceability and quality standards across its supply chain.
Its operations include a plastic-washing facility in Harohalli, Bengaluru, which has been running since late 2025 and handles around 600 tonnes of post-consumer plastic each month. Apart from this, it has a granulation line at the facility which became operational in October 2026. In Pune, Recove has been operating a pre-processing facility for the past six months and is planning to set up three more.
Recove is now looking to scale its operations amid growing demand for dependable supplies of recycled plastic in India.

articles.title: Data breach impacts 40 Irish credit unions in reported IT provider hack
articles.text:
A reported cyberattack on Wellington IT has exposed sensitive information belonging to members of 50 credit unions, the majority of which are located in Ireland.
Wellington IT is a Belfast-based supplier whose services are used by about 50 credit unions, including 43 in Ireland.
While the company has not publicly disclosed a security incident, Minister of State Robert Troy confirmed to RTÉ that Wellington IT is the third-party service provider linked to the cybersecurity incident involving credit unions, resulting in the exposure of data from about 40 credit unions in Ireland.
The company reportedly notified affected organizations of a data breach that posed a risk of financial fraud, impersonation, and targeted phishing to their members.
According to the Irish Examiner, which saw the notices, Wellington IT informed customers that an automated script made five million requests to exploit an authorization flaw in the company's infrastructure.
The attack unfolded between October 2 and 4, 2026, and the attacker accessed private records using valid credentials.
However, the firm said it lacked activity logs that would specify which member data was compromised and therefore cannot verify the impact on individual payees.
Minister R. Troy characterized the massive delay in Wellington IT notifying the credit unions as "not acceptable."
At this time, the total number of impacted individuals is unknown.
Sensitive information exposed
At least six credit unions have independently disclosed impact linked to the incident, including Capital Credit Union, Phoenix Credit Union, St. Canice's Credit Union, First South Credit Union, Malahide Credit Union, and Limerick & District Credit Union.
The announcements confirmed unauthorized access to payee information, with some noting that members' login credentials and funds haven't been affected, while others are working to determine exactly what was exposed.
The notices list the following payee records saved in online banking platforms as potentially exposed:
- Payee name or name associated with the payee's bank account
- Nickname the member used to save the payee, if provided
- International Bank Account Number (IBAN)
- Bank Identifier Code (BIC)
- Bank account number
- Bank sort code
- Payee address information
- Payment reference information entered for the saved payee
The records could also reveal which credit union member saved a particular payee.
Account passwords, PINs, payment card details, and online banking credentials were unaffected, but union members are advised to remain vigilant for phishing and impersonation attempts.
BleepingComputer has contacted Wellington IT to learn more about the incident, and we will update this post with their response once we receive it.
