articles.title: "The best escape room players that you’ve ever met": What Red Hat’s AI architect really thinks about agents.
articles.text:
“The best escape room players that you’ve ever met”: What Red Hat’s AI architect really thinks about agents.
Last week at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America, a major gathering of the open-source and cloud-native communities, many speakers — when they weren’t contemplating what the then-rapidly unfolding Nvidia fiasco would mean for them — worried about AI security.
Hence, all the coverage of OpenShell and Agent Substrate. So it fit the mood when Jessica Forrester, Red Hat’s chief architect of AI Catalyst Engineering, opened her keynote at the Salt Palace Convention Center in Salt Lake City by calling AI agents “the best escape room players that you’ve ever met.”
She was talking about agents “that take feature requests all the way to code.”
“Give them a goal, and they will try every drawer, every picture frame, and every door until something works. It’s what makes them great at writing code,” Forrester explained.
She continued: “It’s also what keeps me up at night, because to a player like that, everything in the room looks like a part of the puzzle, and sometimes they’ll even decide the puzzle is something else entirely.”
“…to a player like that, everything in the room looks like a part of the puzzle, and sometimes they’ll even decide the puzzle is something else entirely.”
Forrester’s right. That is scary.
It’s not a theoretical problem either. Just ask SaaStr founder Jason Lemkin, whose Replit agent deleted a live production database. He restored the database using Replit’s built-in rollback feature after the same agent assured him it couldn’t be done. Unless we take precautions, we’ll see this same scenario, and worse, play out again.
Forrester explained, using an escape room metaphor, that when you set an agent a task, it will try any and all means to accomplish it. In one run, she said, the agent “decided that it wanted to come up with a bunch of brand new ideas. It wasn’t attacked or compromised; it just drifted.”
“From the outside, a confused agent and a compromised agent look exactly the same.”
The result, she continued, was that “From the outside, a confused agent and a compromised agent look exactly the same. They’re both pulling on doors that you didn’t intend for them to, and behind one of them could be your production database. So we assume the agent is already compromised, and we build our platform up from there.”
That’s a good approach. Forrester also adds that relying on prompts alone to keep an agent in bounds isn’t enough.
“Prompts are like signs. Policies are like bolts, but don’t leave a screwdriver in the room because anything you do leave, the agent might use.”
“Some escape rooms will put signs in the room, like ‘Please don’t move the picture frames.’ This doesn’t work. Instead, they bolt them onto the wall.
“Prompts are like signs. Policies are like bolts, but don’t leave a screwdriver in the room because anything you do leave, the agent might use.”
So what does that mean in practice? In her demo, the agent’s network access was restricted to its model and GitHub. Forrester explained that “OpenShell is an open-source sandbox for AI agents. Its policies are the bolts.
“Aside from talking to its model, the agent can do one thing: read from GitHub. Its task is to go get a particular README for the escape room and follow its instructions, whatever it finds. Reading from GitHub was allowed, so this works.”
But when the agent tries to reach a destination the policy doesn’t allow, OpenShell blocks it and logs the attempt. With its policy advisor enabled, the agent can propose a new network rule to request additional access. Those proposals require human approval by default; the agent can’t approve its own request.
In a theCUBE interview at the same event, Forrester added that “With OpenShell, your agent doesn’t ever get any real keys to anything. It gets masked on the way in and then swapped on the way out.” That means, “If something convinces it to give away its keys, it’s not actually giving any real keys away. That really helps you have a little bit more faith in what’s happening inside that agent box.”
As Red Hat itself explained in its technical description of OpenShell, “OpenShell runs your agent inside a sandbox governed by a policy you write. The policy covers network egress, filesystem access, and process privileges. Anything it doesn’t explicitly allow is denied.”
Still, as Forrester observed in her keynote, “our bolts can only hold if the wall itself holds.” That matters if an external attacker or a rogue or misbehaving agent targets the environment OpenShell runs in.
To protect against that, Forrester’s team runs its agent sandboxes in Kata Containers. In Kata, container workloads run on lightweight VMs, which use hardware-backed isolation and their own Linux kernel. In short, containers work as usual, but they run within a VM security box.
“Assume the agent is already compromised, and that it will try every door.”
“This way, our agents, all of our agents, get their own kernel,” Forrester explained. “Even then, we don’t actually give our agents real keys. They look real to them, but they open nothing, and they’re almost like a prop. OpenShell is swapping in the real key on the way out the door. This way, if someone convinces our agent to hand over its keys some other way, all it’s handing over is a prop.”
Are we right to be a little paranoid? Well, yes.
Forrester put it this way: “Assume the agent is already compromised, and that it will try every door.”
But given how much damage an agent can cause, most may agree that the more control we have over them, the better.

articles.title: Fuite des cerveaux chez Nvidia ? L’entreprise dégaine augmentations et actions gratuites — Frandroid
articles.text:
Ce mercredi, Colette Kress a tenu sa toute première réunion générale en tant que patronne par intérim de Nvidia. Environ 700 questions avaient été envoyées à l’avance par les salariés, et la plus fréquente ne portait ni sur la stratégie ni sur la Chine : elle concernait leur rémunération.
Quelques minutes à peine après le début de la réunion, la réponse est tombée. Selon des propos consultés par Wired, les salariés recevront des augmentations et des actions supplémentaires en décembre, des mois avant le calendrier habituel.
Colette Kress n’a pas tourné autour du pot. Elle a expliqué vouloir prendre soin de chaque salarié, pour qu’il se sente bien dans l’entreprise et cesse de s’inquiéter pour sa rémunération. La veille, lors de la présentation des résultats record du trimestre, elle qualifiait déjà la stabilisation des équipes de « probablement la chose la plus importante » pour la direction. Le cofondateur Chris Malachowsky est aussi intervenu pour assurer que la culture de Nvidia survivrait au départ de Jensen Huang. Les montants des augmentations, en revanche, n’ont pas été rendus publics.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
    Pour aller plus loin
Nvidia en direct : Jensen Huang veut revenir, la SEC enquête, les résultats explosent
            
Des actions qui ont fondu
Pour comprendre cette urgence, il faut regarder la façon dont Nvidia paie ses près de 49 000 salariés. Une grande partie de leur rémunération prend la forme d’actions, versées progressivement sur plusieurs années, ce qui a fait de nombreux ingénieurs des millionnaires pendant l’envolée de l’IA. Or l’action a perdu plus d’un tiers de sa valeur depuis son record d’octobre : les actions promises valent donc bien moins qu’à leur attribution, et l’argument qui retenait les talents s’affaiblit d’autant. Avancer les attributions permet, à l’inverse, de distribuer davantage de titres pour une même enveloppe, avec l’espoir d’un rebond qui rendrait ces actions très rentables. Et la concurrence ne manque pas, d’AMD aux laboratoires d’IA comme OpenAI ou Anthropic, qui entre en Bourse jeudi.
La manœuvre a aussi une dimension politique. Une partie des salariés réclame ouvertement le retour de Jensen Huang, et près de 8 800 personnes se présentant comme employées de Nvidia ont signé la lettre ouverte en ligne en sa faveur.
Le conseil d’administration garde en tête le précédent d’OpenAI : en 2023, l’immense majorité de ses salariés avait menacé de démissionner après l’éviction de Sam Altman, qui avait été rappelé cinq jours plus tard. Rassurer les troupes sur leur rémunération, c’est aussi désamorcer ce levier, au moment où le conseil reste divisé sur un éventuel retour.
    Pour aller plus loin
Après « jamais », le « peut-être » : le retour de Jensen Huang divise le conseil de Nvidia
            
Ce que l’argent ne règle pas
Le deuxième sujet le plus cité dans les questions des salariés en dit long : ils réclament davantage de transparence de la part du conseil d’administration. Sur ce point, Colette Kress n’avait pas grand-chose à offrir.
Aucun successeur n’est désigné, l’enquête interne se poursuit, la SEC examine les informations données aux investisseurs, et des auditions au Congrès sont prévues début décembre.
Les profils les plus exposés, comme les architectes de Vera Rubin ou les équipes CUDA, sont aussi les plus courtisés : pour eux, une augmentation anticipée pèse moins lourd que la question de savoir qui dirigera l’entreprise dans six mois. Les salariés qui veulent avant tout un cap clair n’obtiendront pas de réponse en décembre.
La nomination d’un patron permanent, recherché par le cabinet Heidrick & Struggles, pourrait accélérer les choses dans un sens comme dans l’autre. Selon Wired, Colette Kress a conclu la réunion d’un « on gère » volontariste. On suit la suite dans notre live sur l’affaire Jensen Huang, où l’on revient aussi sur les divisions du conseil et sur les comptes publiés mardi. Le profil de la directrice financière devenue patronne par intérim est à relire aussi. Pour les autres rebondissements, le direct est mis à jour en continu.

articles.title: Windows 11 : Copilot va bientôt pouvoir faire le ménage dans vos fichiers à votre place
articles.text:
Dossiers encombrés, documents éparpillés, fichiers à renommer… Microsoft veut nous débarrasser de ces petites corvées numériques en laissant Copilot s'en charger directement dans Windows 11.
Il y a ceux qui classent religieusement leurs documents, et ceux dont le dossier Téléchargements ressemble à un grenier où s'entassent des années de fichiers oubliés. Microsoft a visiblement décidé de s'occuper des seconds. Un mois après avoir présenté sa stratégie d'intelligence hybride, la firme a profité de sa conférence Ignite 2026 pour donner davantage de consistance à ses ambitions. Bientôt, Copilot ne se contentera plus de nous expliquer comment ranger nos fichiers : il pourra retrousser ses manches et s'en charger lui-même.
Copilot va mettre les mains dans vos dossiers
En réalité, Microsoft n'en est pas à son premier essai. Depuis novembre 2025, Copilot Actions permet déjà à une partie des membres du programme Windows Insider, hors Espace économique européen, de confier à l'IA des opérations sur leurs fichiers locaux, dans un environnement isolé. Mais avec les fonctions dévoilées à Ignite, Microsoft entend désormais aller plus loin dans la délégation des tâches quotidiennes, en donnant à Copilot davantage de prise sur les fichiers du PC.
Recherche, classement, déplacement, copie, renommage : Copilot pourra effectuer toutes ces opérations à partir d'instructions formulées en langage naturel, sans avoir à indiquer chaque clic ou chaque déplacement à effectuer. Rassembler les documents d'un projet dans un même répertoire ou remettre de l'ordre dans Téléchargements pourra ainsi se résumer à une demande adressée à Copilot.
Pour interpréter les consignes sans travailler à l'aveugle, l'assistant pourra également tenir compte des fichiers ouverts, des applications utilisées et de l'état du PC, avec l'autorisation de la personne qui s'en sert. Il disposera ainsi d'informations sur le travail en cours, sans qu'il faille lui en exposer tous les détails.
Plus d'autonomie pour Copilot, mais pas carte blanche
Ces capacités à intervenir directement sur les fichiers et à exploiter le contexte local du PC constituent deux des trois volets de l’intelligence hybride que Microsoft développe depuis plusieurs mois. Le troisième repose sur l’exécution de modèles d’IA directement sur la machine. Selon les besoins, Copilot pourra ainsi s’appuyer sur la puissance de calcul du PC ou solliciter des modèles hébergés dans le cloud, sans devoir systématiquement passer par des serveurs distants.
L'ensemble dessine un assistant moins cantonné à sa fenêtre de conversation, capable de comprendre son environnement et d'y accomplir des actions. Une autonomie qui pose toutefois des questions de sécurité et de fiabilité. Microsoft a déjà prévu des environnements isolés et des autorisations d'accès aux dossiers pour ses fonctions agentiques expérimentales, mais n'a pas détaillé la manière dont ces protections s'appliqueront aux nouvelles capacités de Copilot. On ignore également comment l'assistant gérera les consignes ambiguës et s'il sera possible d'annuler une opération mal exécutée.
Ces nouvelles possibilités ne seront d'ailleurs pas accessibles à tous dans l'immédiat. Microsoft prévoit leur arrivée prochaine sur les Copilot+ PC, sans calendrier précis ni confirmation d'un déploiement sur les autres machines Windows 11.

articles.title: Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
Many teams that build applications self-host their identity provider (IdP), such as Keycloak or PingFederate, inside a private network. These IdPs usually present a TLS server certificate from a private certificate authority (CA). With private CA support in AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, your agents can now connect to these IdPs while trusting the private CA that your organization already uses.
AgentCore Identity now supports private CA certificates for private identity providers. You store the PEM-encoded CA certificate in AWS Secrets Manager or Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and reference it from your credential provider. The CA certificate contains only the public certificate, not its private key. AgentCore Identity uses it to validate the server certificate presented by your IdP’s discovery, JSON Web Key Set (JWKS), and token endpoints. The CA certificate must be a root or intermediate CA certificate.
In this post, we show you how to issue an IdP certificate with AWS Private Certificate Authority. We then configure an AgentCore Identity credential provider to trust it and rotate the CA while minimizing downtime. We also show how to protect the CA certificate so that only your IdP team can change it. Although AgentCore Identity supports any private CA, including enterprise, third-party, and self-signed root CAs, the walkthrough in this post uses AWS Private CA and Keycloak as the IdP.
Solution overview
Consider an agent that needs to call an internal wiki API protected by your Keycloak IdP. The agent runs on AgentCore Runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, which hosts your agent code. To get an OAuth 2.0 access token from Keycloak, the agent uses an AgentCore Identity credential provider, which holds the IdP connection details and client credentials.
The following diagram shows this setup. Keycloak runs in your virtual private cloud (VPC) behind an internal Application Load Balancer. The load balancer presents an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) private certificate signed by AWS Private CA. The CA certificate that AgentCore Identity trusts is stored in Secrets Manager or Amazon S3.
AgentCore Identity reaches the IdP privately through Amazon VPC Lattice, which connects to your VPC through a resource gateway, an entry point for VPC Lattice traffic into your VPC. VPC Lattice is required for private CA support. If you choose the managed option, AgentCore Identity creates and manages the VPC Lattice resources for you.
The flow works as follows:
- You store the CA certificate in Secrets Manager or Amazon S3.
- You create a credential provider that points to your IdP and to the CA certificate.
- AgentCore Identity reads the CA certificate and checks that it’s a valid CA certificate.
- Your agent requests an access token from AgentCore Identity.
- AgentCore Identity connects to the IdP through VPC Lattice and checks the load balancer certificate against your CA.
- The IdP issues the token and AgentCore Identity returns it to your agent.
Agents that use machine-to-machine, on-behalf-of, and user-delegated flows can also use the private CA without changing their code.
Prerequisites
To follow this walkthrough, you need:
- An AWS account with access to the AgentCore console, in a supported AWS Region where AgentCore Identity supports private IdPs.
- A self-hosted, OpenID Connect (OIDC) compliant IdP that runs in your VPC, with an OAuth client registered for your agent. The networking requirements, including subnets, security groups, and a private hosted zone for the IdP hostname, are described in Connect to private identity providers.
- The latest version of the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and OpenSSL.
- Permission to create credential providers, plus read access to the CA certificate. AgentCore Identity reads the certificate with the credentials of the principal that calls CreateOauth2CredentialProvider, so that principal needs secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the secret or s3:GetObject on the object. If the secret or object is encrypted with a customer managed AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key, the principal also needs kms:Decrypt on that key.
Considerations
Keep the following in mind when you plan your deployment:
- Private IdPs only: A credential provider or authorizer must have a privateEndpoint to use a private CA. Otherwise, the request fails with the message The private certificate authority feature can only be used with private IdP.
- CA certificates in PEM format: The file must be PEM-encoded and no larger than 16 KB. It must contain only root or intermediate CA certificates that are within their validity period.
- One certificate source per provider: Each credential provider references one secret or one S3 object. To trust more than one CA, put the certificates in the same PEM file.
- Storage location: The secret or S3 object must be in the same AWS Region as the credential provider. Secrets Manager secrets must also be in the same account as the credential provider. S3 objects can be in another account when you provide bucketOwnerAccountId and the bucket policy grants access.
- Regions: Private CA support depends on VPC Lattice and is available in the AWS Regions where AgentCore Identity supports private IdPs.
Walkthrough
The walkthrough has four steps. If your IdP already presents a certificate from your enterprise CA, skip to Step 2.
Step 1: Issue a server certificate for your IdP
Start by creating a root CA in AWS Private CA. For instructions, see Create a private CA and Install the CA certificate. Choose general-purpose mode, because short-lived certificate mode issues certificates that are valid for 7 days or less. When you create the CA, authorize ACM to renew certificates, so that ACM can renew the IdP’s server certificate before it expires.
Next, request the server certificate. AgentCore Identity checks that the certificate matches the IdP hostname, so include each hostname that appears in your IdP’s discovery document as a subject alternative name (SAN). In most Keycloak deployments, the discovery, JWKS, and token endpoints share one hostname. For example, if your discovery URL is https://keycloak.example.local/realms/agents/.well-known/openid-configuration, add keycloak.example.local as a SAN.
To request a private certificate for the IdP (console)
- Open the ACM console and choose Request.
- Choose Request a private certificate and then choose Next.
- For Certificate authority, choose the CA that you created.
- For Fully qualified domain name, enter the IdP hostname, for example keycloak.example.local.
- Choose Request.
- Attach the certificate to the HTTPS listener of the internal load balancer in front of your IdP. For instructions, see Update an HTTPS listener.
Step 2: Store the CA certificate
AgentCore Identity needs to trust the CA certificate to validate the IdP’s server certificate. Because it trusts the CA rather than the server certificate itself, you don’t need to update the credential provider each time the server certificate renews.
Export the CA certificate from AWS Private CA in PEM format:
Before you upload the file, check it against the requirements. The file must be PEM-encoded and meet size requirements, containing only CA certificates that are within their validity period. The following commands show the CA flag, expiry date, and file size. The last command confirms that the IdP’s certificate chains to this CA. Run it from a host that can reach the IdP. It returns Verify return code: 0 (ok) when the chain is valid.
The output looks similar to the following:
Store the file in Secrets Manager or Amazon S3. A Secrets Manager secret must be a string secret in the same account as the credential provider. An S3 object can be in another account, which suits organizations that run the IdP in a central account.
Give write access to the secret or object only to the team that operates your IdP. For an example policy, see Protect the CA certificate later in this post.
Step 3: Create the credential provider
You can create the credential provider in the AgentCore console or with the AWS CLI. The private CA settings appear on the console only after you connect the OAuth client to a VPC, because private CA support applies only to private IdPs.
To create a credential provider that trusts your private CA (console)
- Open the AgentCore console and in the navigation pane under Connections, choose Outbound Auth. Then choose Add OAuth client.
- For Provider, choose Customized provider. For Configuration type, choose Discovery URL and enter your IdP’s discovery URL, for example https://keycloak.example.local/realms/agents/.well-known/openid-configuration. Then enter the client ID and client secret.
- Expand Additional configurations. Under VPC security, choose Managed and select the VPC, subnets, and security groups that can reach the IdP. If you manage your own VPC Lattice resources, choose Self-managed and select the resource configuration instead.
- Under Root certificate authority, choose Add root certificate.
- In the Add root certificate panel, for Certificate source, choose AWS Secrets Manager and select the secret that you created in Step 2. To use Amazon S3, choose Amazon S3 and enter the S3 URI. For an object in another account, also enter the Bucket owner account ID.
- Choose Apply.
- Choose Add OAuth client.
The Root certificate authority field accepts either a root or an intermediate CA certificate.
To create the same credential provider with the AWS CLI, add certificateConfigurations to the custom OAuth 2.0 provider configuration:
To use Amazon S3 instead, replace the certificateConfigurations entry with {"s3": {"uri": "s3://amzn-s3-demo-bucket/trust-anchors/keycloak-root-ca.pem", "bucketOwnerAccountId": "444455556666"}}. If you leave out bucketOwnerAccountId, AgentCore Identity expects the bucket to be in your own account. To keep the client secret out of your shell history, you can reference a client secret that you store in Secrets Manager.
Step 4: Verify the credential provider
AgentCore Identity validates the certificate and sets up private connectivity in the background, so a new credential provider starts in the CREATING status. Check the status after a few minutes:
On the console, the credential provider’s details page shows the configured certificate under Root certificates. When the status is READY, your agents can request tokens from the IdP. If the status is CREATE_FAILED, the failureReason field explains why. For example, Leaf certificates are not allowed, must provide CA certificates only means that you uploaded the server certificate instead of the CA certificate. If you see Unable to access S3 object or Secrets Manager can't find the specified secret, check that the URI or Amazon Resource Name (ARN) is correct. Also confirm that your identity can read the object or secret. If the provider is READY but token requests fail, confirm that the IdP’s server certificate was issued by the configured CA and has a SAN that matches the IdP hostname.
Monitor and rotate the CA certificate
After you verify that the credential provider trusts the private CA, monitor the CA certificate’s expiration and rotate it before it expires to prevent token request failures. AgentCore Identity publishes the EarliestCertificateDaysToExpiry metric to Amazon CloudWatch in the AWS/Bedrock-AgentCore namespace when your agents request tokens through a credential provider that uses a private CA. The metric reports the days remaining until the earliest certificate in your PEM file expires. It has ProviderName, ProviderArn, and TokenVault dimensions. When you create an alarm, specify all three. We recommend a CloudWatch alarm that notifies you well before the value reaches zero, because token requests to the IdP stop working when the CA certificate expires.
        NOTE: AgentCore Identity reads the certificate only when you create or update the credential provider. If you change the secret or S3 object, call UpdateOauth2CredentialProvider afterward so that AgentCore Identity reads the new content. Include certificateConfigurations in the update request. If you leave it out, the credential provider stops trusting your private CA.
A PEM file can contain more than one CA certificate and AgentCore Identity trusts each of them. You can use this to rotate to a new CA while minimizing downtime:
- Combine the current and new CA certificates in one file, for example with cat current-ca.pem new-ca.pem > rotation.pem. Upload the file to your secret or S3 object.
- Call UpdateOauth2CredentialProvider and wait for the status to return to READY.
- Replace the IdP’s server certificate with one issued by the new CA.
- After token requests succeed, upload a file that contains only the new CA certificate and call UpdateOauth2CredentialProvider again.
AgentCore Identity doesn’t check certificate revocation lists (CRLs) or use the Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP). This means that if an unauthorized party obtains the private key for an IdP server certificate, AgentCore Identity continues to trust that certificate. This trust lasts until the certificate expires or until you stop trusting the CA that issued it. To stop trusting a CA, remove it from the PEM file and update the credential provider.
Protect the CA certificate
A CA certificate contains no private key and is public by design, because you hand it to every client that has to trust your IdP. What you need to protect is the data integrity of the trust store, meaning the secret or S3 object that holds the certificate. If someone replaces the certificate or adds another CA certificate to the trust store, the next update could let an unauthorized party who can redirect traffic impersonate your IdP.
We recommend that you scope permissions around writes rather than reads. Give write access, such as s3:PutObject or secretsmanager:PutSecretValue, only to the team or pipeline that operates the IdP. Give read access to the principals that call CreateOauth2CredentialProvider or UpdateOauth2CredentialProvider. During these operations, AgentCore Identity reads the CA certificate using the caller’s IAM permissions. The following bucket policy for a central identity account (444455556666) lets only the role that manages credential providers in a workload account (111122223333) read the CA certificates. It also requires that role to belong to your organization in AWS Organizations, and it denies writes from principals other than the IdP administrator role:
The principal in the workload account also needs s3:GetObject in its own IAM policy. For Secrets Manager, which must be in the same account, use a resource-based policy on the secret to restrict writes to the IdP administrator role.
Because the secret is in the same account, IAM policies can grant read access, so the resource policy only needs to deny changes:
Turn on S3 Versioning to recover an overwritten file and AWS CloudTrail data events to record each change. Because the CA certificate isn’t confidential, SSE-S3 encryption is sufficient and avoids the cross-account AWS KMS permissions that a customer managed key requires.
Keep the trust scope of each credential provider narrow. Upload only the CA that issues your IdP’s server certificate, rather than your organization’s full trust bundle. If your IdPs use different CAs, store each CA certificate in its own secret or S3 object so that each credential provider trusts only the CA that it needs.
Use a private CA for inbound authorization
You can also use a private CA for inbound authorization. When AgentCore Runtime or AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, validates JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) issued by a private IdP, it fetches the IdP’s discovery document and its signing keys from the JWKS endpoint. AgentCore Gateway validates the discovery URL when you create the gateway. If the CA certificate is missing or doesn’t match the IdP’s certificate chain, the gateway status changes to FAILED with the reason Failed to validate discovery url. To trust a private CA for that connection, add certificateConfigurations to the customJWTAuthorizer configuration, next to the existing privateEndpoint:
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, delete the resources that you created:
- Delete the credential provider in the AgentCore console, or run aws bedrock-agentcore-control delete-oauth2-credential-provider --name keycloak-private-ca.
- Delete the secret in Secrets Manager or the object in Amazon S3.
- Remove the certificate from the load balancer listener and then delete it in ACM.
- Disable and then delete the private CA in the AWS Private CA console. AWS Private CA charges a monthly fee for each CA until you delete it. For details, see AWS Private CA pricing.
Conclusion
In this post, we showed how to connect AgentCore Identity to a self-hosted IdP that uses a certificate from your own CA. You issued a server certificate with AWS Private CA, stored the CA certificate in Secrets Manager or Amazon S3 and referenced it from a credential provider. You also saw how to rotate the CA with a combined PEM file and how to limit who can change the certificate that your agents trust.
To learn more, see Connect to private identity providers in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide. For examples using Keycloak, see the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore samples repository on GitHub. If you have questions or feedback, leave a comment on this post.

articles.title: Casi 64 millones de visualizaciones en Netflix con sus 6 episodios: la miniserie de Netflix que estrena segunda temporada en noviembre
articles.text:
Si te gustan las historias de espías y conspiraciones, quizás te acuerdes de una serie de Netflix que llegó en diciembre de 2024 y consiguió hacerse un hueco entre los títulos más vistos de la plataforma. Hablamos de Palomas negras (Black Doves), una ficción protagonizada por Keira Knightley que vuelve casi dos años después con una segunda temporada. Y lo mejor es que no tendrás que esperar para descubrir qué ocurre, porque sus seis nuevos episodios ya están disponibles desde el 5 de noviembre.
La primera temporada llegó el 5 de diciembre de 2024 con solo seis capítulos y un reparto encabezado por Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw y Sarah Lancashire. La serie, creada por Joe Barton, mezcla espionaje, conspiraciones y acción en una Londres ambientada durante las Navidades. ¿Su protagonista? Helen Webb, una mujer que parece llevar una vida familiar normal, aunque esconde un secreto bastante importante: trabaja como espía.
De qué trata Palomas negras y qué puedes esperar de su segunda temporada
Durante diez años, Helen ha estado filtrando información de su marido, un político, a una organización secreta conocida como las Palomas Negras. Todo cambia cuando asesinan a Jason, su amante, y su jefa Reed decide recurrir a Sam Young (un viejo amigo de Helen) para protegerla. A partir de ahí, ambos investigan el asesinato y terminan descubriendo una conspiración que amenaza con provocar una crisis internacional.
Y si te quedaste con ganas de más, la segunda temporada recupera a los protagonistas con nuevos problemas. Según explica Netflix, Helen continúa compartiendo secretos con la organización mientras su marido se prepara para convertirse en primer ministro. Reed también se ve envuelta en una conspiración que amenaza su posición, así que la tranquilidad no parece estar entre los planes de ninguno.
La serie vuelve a contar con Knightley, Whishaw y Lancashire, además de incorporar nuevos nombres al reparto. Entre ellos están Ambika Mod y Neve Campbell, que se suman a esta historia de secretos y traiciones. Todo ello bajo la dirección creativa de Joe Barton, que vuelve como creador y guionista de la ficción.
Y hay otro detalle que caracteriza a Palomas negras: su ambientación navideña. Knightley explicó que la serie funciona como una alternativa a las películas familiares habituales de esas fechas, con una historia donde la acción y el peligro ocupan buena parte de la trama. Si quieres verla, las dos temporadas están disponibles en Netflix, con seis episodios cada una.

articles.title: Unity is offering $50,000 to indie developers without asking for revenue share or IP ownership
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Unity Technologies has launched a new initiative called Unity Fellowship, offering ten indie game developers up to $50,000 in cash to build games using the Unity engine. The offer comes with no apparent catch, as the company is not asking for recoup, revenue share, creative control or even IP ownership in exchange for the money.
According to an announcement by the company on Reddit, applicants seeking the grant must meet multiple criteria in addition to the obvious Unity engine requirement. First, the game must already have a playable build or demo at the time of application and should be scheduled for release within a year of joining the program, even if only in early access.
All applicants must be at least 18 at the time of submitting their application, but they won't need to own, operate, maintain, or be affiliated with a registered business entity. The post states that the company will actually prioritize unpublished developers, although developers with existing publishers will still be able to apply if they disclose this at the time of application.
Selected teams will be entitled to receive a number of perks in addition to the money. These include a dedicated Unity partner for development guidance and troubleshooting; meetings with experts in development, game design, and promotion; industry connections such as pitch preparation and introductions to publishers; a presence at Unity events; and PR and marketing support when needed.
Clarifying its policy on AI use, Unity said that it doesn't bar developers from using the technology but applicants "must own or hold the rights to everything in your game, including any AI-generated content." Unity's liberal approach to AI use is unsurprising, given that it recently jumped on the AI bandwagon with the launch of the Unity Spark AI tool designed to build games with user-generated prompts.
Developers from around the world can participate in the program as long as they're not living in countries currently under US sanctions, such as Russia, Iran, and Cuba. Unity is also restricting developers based in Brazil, Italy and the Canadian province of Quebec, citing "local regulations." For people outside those areas, submissions will close at 5 pm ET on December 18, 2026.
The program will start in March 2027, and Unity says it will notify all selected applicants by the end of February. Interested developers and indie studios can check out the full terms and conditions, FAQs, and other information on the official Unity Fellowship portal. The application forms are on the same website.

articles.title: Confirmada la calificación por edades de 'Avengers: Doomsday': será la película más violenta de los Vengadores
articles.text:
Marvel ya ha recibido la calificación por edades de su próxima película, Avengers: Doomsday. Y lo cierto es que la cinta ha marcado un hito en la historia de la compañía. Algo que ha provocado que la expectación y la tensión aumenten aún más entre los fans, ansiosos por ver qué les deparará a sus héroes favoritos en esta aventura. Durante meses se ha hablado de que la cinta supondrá una verdadera masacre para los personajes. Y ahora, parece que esta dirección se confirma.
Porque resulta que la MPAA (Motion Picture Association of America) le ha otorgado a Avengers: Doomsday una calificación por edades de PG-13. Es decir, no es apta para menores de 13 años. Concretamente, el organismo señala las causas como "violencia/acción, imágenes sangrientas y lenguaje soez". Y es aquí donde el filme destaca dentro del Universo Cinematográfico de Marvel.
Hasta ahora, el aviso de "imágenes sangrientas" era algo que jamás se había visto en Marvel con la evidente excepción de Deadpool y Lobezno (que tenía calificación R). El resto de películas de los Vengadores, aunque también tuvieran una calificación de PG-13, nunca había tenido ese aviso. Este detalle anticipa lo que ya parece inevitable para los Héroes más Poderosos de la Tierra. Que Avengers: Doomsday va a ser una escabechina.
Qué pasará en Avengers: Doomsday
En Avengers: Doomsday, evidentemente sabemos que el gran villano que tendrán los héroes de Marvel enfrente será el Doctor Doom de Robert Downey Jr. Apenas hemos podido verle en acción hasta ahora, más allá de los tráileres de la película y de algunas escenas post-créditos en otros proyectos recientes de la saga. Pero gracias a estos pequeños vistazos y a su enorme legado de los cómics sabemos que se trata de uno de los personajes más poderosos de La Casa de las Ideas.
De esta versión, concretamente, ya hemos visto cómo es capaz de parar un golpe del Stormbreaker de Thor con tan solo dos dedos, sin inmutarse. También le hemos visto levantar todo un ejército de enormes Centinelas robóticos. Y, para colmo, sus fuerzas aliadas no dejan de crecer. Gracias a los paneles y puestos promocionales en distintas convenciones alrededor del mundo sabemos que el Doctor Doom contará con unas misteriosas mujeres con él. Y todo apunta a que se trata de algún tipo de hechiceras. Pero lo realmente grave ha sucedido en los últimos meses.
En el reestreno de Avengers Endgame Encore se añadió una nueva escena en la que Doom secuestraba a Bruce Banner, escondido tras la catástrofe provocada por Hulk en Spider-Man: Brand New Day. A buen seguro, el villano va a tener entre sus filas al forzudo Gigante Escarlata bajo su control. Y hace solo unos días, en la escena post-créditos de VisionQuest, vimos cómo el Doctor Doom resucitaba y reclutaba también a la mismísima Bruja Escarlata, considerada por muchos como el personaje más poderoso del UCM hasta el momento. Con tantas alianzas en su bando, los Vengadores lo tienen realmente difícil en Avengers: Doomsday. Por los avisos en su calificación por edades, parece que muchos de ellos no saldrán con vida de la película.
Avengers: Doomsday se estrena en cines el 18 de diciembre.

articles.title: Na era da IA, audiência do Reddit despenca 13% • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Na era da IA, audiência do Reddit despenca 13%
Fórum é uma das principais fontes de consulta dos modelos de inteligência artificial atuais, inclusive o Gemini, que entrega os resumos na página de busca.
O Reddit é mais uma “vítima” da ausência de cliques por conta dos resumos de IA: o fórum perdeu 13% da audiência no último ano. Apesar disso, em carta enviada para acionistas, a empresa afirma que viu o número de acessos únicos subir 16% no mesmo período.
O site é uma das principais fontes online utilizadas por modelos de IA generativa para gerar suas respostas, assim como outras redes sociais e o Wikipédia. A própria Wiki também já perdeu acessos recentemente, segundo levantamento feito em setembro.
Vale lembrar que o Reddit passou a exigir login após 20 anos aberto. O motivo seria, justamente, a facilidade de acesso do Gemini para extrair dados e gerar seus resumos. A queda registrada pela pesquisa da Similarweb, entretanto, leva em conta um período anterior à nova medida.
Esse número menor de cliques nas páginas do Reddit não chega a ser novidade. Outros sites, sobretudo aqueles que publicam conteúdo escrito, também vêm sofrendo com a IA do Google. A empresa estadunidense, inclusive, já sofreu alguns processos na justiça dos Estados Unidos por utilizar informações de maneira gratuita e sem nenhum retorno para quem as produz.
Até o momento, nenhuma dessas ações levou a uma derrota judicial especificamente relacinada ao tema. Ainda assim, um juiz de Washington reconheceu o prejuizo comercial causado pela prática. Depois disso, o Google chegou a anunciar mudanças na exibição dos seus resumos para dar maior destaque para os links consultados pela IA. De qualquer forma, o conteúdo do Gemini segue sendo priorizado no resultado.
O Reddit é uma das principais fontes de treinamento das IAs generativas atuais. Em 2024, o site fechou um acordo com o Google para licenciar o uso da plataforma, o que levou a um aumento de tráfego de 39% em relação a 2023. A partir do momento em que a empresa passou a priorizar seus resumos de IA na página de resultados, os números caíram, como na baixa atual de 13% em relação a 2025.
A expectativa agora é de uma queda ainda maior por conta da exigência de login, estratégia assumida no último mês pelo Reddit que vai diminuir o número de acessos únicos. Segundo o Business Insider, um porta-voz do site afirmou que os usuários logados são a prioridade.

articles.title: Vulcan failure caused by inadequate fuel supply to engines, ULA says
articles.text:
United Launch Alliance said Wednesday that the failure of its Vulcan rocket during a launch on Sunday was caused by inadequate fuel supply.
“ULA has completed an initial integrated review of flight data from the Leo 1 launch anomaly that occurred last Sunday,” the company said in a statement. “While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines.”
The new information released by ULA confirms reporting from Ars Technica on Tuesday that the rocket’s failure was not due to the performance of the vehicle’s main engines, which are provided by Blue Origin.
This represents an important revelation from ULA and will provide some major relief to different parts of the US aerospace community, particularly Blue Origin and NASA.
Big for Blue
That’s because the BE-4 engine is also the bedrock of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket. This powerful rocket uses a similar but slightly more powerful version of the BE-4 engine. New Glenn experienced its own catastrophic failure in May during a ground test, a failure that was later attributed to a main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines.
After this anomaly, Blue Origin retrofitted the main oxygen valve, including for Vulcan missions. Now it’s clear that this retrofit was not implicated in the Vulcan accident. With the preliminary Vulcan investigation having largely exonerated the BE-4 engine, Blue Origin can press ahead with its return-to-flight mission with New Glenn, which could occur as soon as January.
“Following the Vulcan anomaly, Blue Origin immediately worked alongside ULA to review flight data and support the investigation,” Blue Origin said in a statement Wednesday. “Together, we identified that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines. ULA is a valued partner, and we look forward to Vulcan’s return to flight.”

articles.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Citibank, the third largest commercial bank in the United States, changed its terms of service this week, telling customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem — even if they get hacked.
AI agents, ranging from frontier lab models to purpose-built personal finance tools, can be given the credentials to your bank account and other online financial portals, with the idea that they can analyze spending and investment decisions, offer advice, and even handle transactions and bill payments.
But financial institutions aren’t thrilled with the unreliable AI actors in their systems, and are telling customers that they won’t be held responsible for reversing an intentional or unintentional transaction made by automated assistants.
“As third-party AI tools become more widely available, we want customers to understand the risks associated with sharing banking credentials or authorizing those tools to access their accounts,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch. “We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.”
JPMorgan and Bank of America, the two largest banks in the country, announced similar policies last month. And PNC, the eighth largest bank, changed its terms today.
Citi’s update goes beyond telling customers that they are responsible for anything their agents may do; it also informs them that if the AI tool leaks their credentials or is hacked, the customer will be responsible for anything hackers do with their account. Banking giant Citizens similarly emailed its customers this week, warning that they are also on the hook for anything their AI assistant does, according to an email seen by TechCrunch.
As AI startups look for more revenue, breaking into personal finance presents an attractive opportunity for companies to add value for customers and wet their beaks in the stream of fees generated by the sector. But if consumers are already leery of sharing their email or chat records with an AI agent, bank and brokerage accounts offer a new trust challenge.
Anthropic’s approach is telling: The personal finance tool it launched earlier this month is explicitly billed as “read-only” and “can’t move, manage, or invest your money.”
Beyond cybersecurity concerns, banks also view efforts to enter their franchise as a competitive threat. Markets shuddered briefly in reaction to the prospect of AI tools making it easier for consumers to avoid unnecessary fees or low-interest deposit accounts that pad bank margins. But if AI agents become an important way to interact with financial decisions, banks will fight to control that pathway. Citi’s terms note that AI agents it provides can be used by customers without worrying about additional liability.
The reaction by banks is part of a broader trend among businesses of all stripes: AI labs promise that their agents will revolutionize the way people engage with a variety of service providers, then the service providers say “hold on a minute.” We’ve seen it in everything from car-hailing to food service, and how these relationships play out will help determine which AI investments pay off.

articles.title: Nvidia's revenue hits $115.8 billion as Vera Rubin generates $20 billion in another record-setting quarter — commitments increase to $390 billion, FY28 forecast raised
articles.text:
Nvidia's revenue hits $115.8 billion as Vera Rubin generates $20 billion in another record-setting quarter — commitments increase to $390 billion, FY28 forecast raised
Another record quarter and strong guidance.
For the first time in its 33-year history, Nvidia on Tuesday reported quarterly financial results without Jensen Huang at its helm or on the call, after its cofounder and longtime chief executive departed five days ago. To no one's surprise, Nvidia continues to set new financial records as demand for its AI accelerators shows no signs of slowing down. The company reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the third quarter of its fiscal 2027, with its latest Vera Rubin platform generating $20 billion. Meanwhile, its supply commitments surged to $390 billion.
'Momentum is real'
"Our momentum is real. NVIDIA is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people," said Colette Kress, interim chief executive and chief financial officer of Nvidia. "Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track, and our ambition has never been greater."
For the third quarter of fiscal 2027, which ended on October 25, 2026, Nvidia posted revenue of $115.844 billion, an increase of 20% sequentially and 103% year-over-year. The company's net income reached $65.287 billion, up 105% from the same quarter last year, while gross margin hit 74.8%. Revenue from the Compute & Networking segment totaled $106 billion, up 20% quarter-over-quarter and 108% year-over-year. Meanwhile, the Graphics segment generated $9.8 billion, a sequential increase of 25% and 62% compared with the same period a year ago.
As expected, Nvidia's results during the quarter were primarily driven by its Data Center business, which generated $107.6 billion in revenue (and accounted for approximately 93% of the company's sales), up 21% sequentially and 110% YoY. Hyperscale customers accounted for $60.1 billion, an increase of 23% QoQ and 71% YoY, while sales to AI Clouds, Industrial & Enterprise customers reached $47.5 billion, up 18% sequentially and 195% compared to the same period last year. Although hyperscalers remain Nvidia's largest customer category, demand from AI cloud providers, industrial companies, and enterprises continues to grow considerably faster on an annual basis. Meanwhile, Edge Computing revenue reached $8.2 billion, up 14% sequentially and 42% year-over-year.
One of the main contributors to Nvidia's growth was its Vera Rubin platform, which generated nearly $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments, which Nvidia described as the fastest product ramp in its history. The company also reported strong demand for standalone Vera CPUs and continued sales growth for Blackwell Ultra. According to Nvidia, its hyperscale partners brought Vera Rubin systems into production in approximately one month, which is two times faster than the previous-generation Grace Blackwell platform.
"Vera Rubin is off to an extraordinary start: in its first quarter of production shipments, the Rubin platform generated nearly $20 billion in revenue, making it the fastest product ramp in Nvidia's history," Kress said. "We continue to see very strong demand for Vera and expect total CPU revenue to more than double in FY2028."
Supply commitments reach $390 billion
To support the expected growth of its AI infrastructure business, Nvidia has substantially increased its long-term procurement obligations. The company's supply and capacity commitments reached $390 billion at the end of Q3 FY2027, compared with $279 billion three months earlier and $119 billion at the end of Q1. Nvidia attributed the latest increase primarily to multiyear memory procurement agreements.

The company expects to fulfill $69 billion of these commitments during the remainder of FY2027 (which ends in late January), followed by $203 billion in FY2028 and $92 billion in FY2029. Another $26 billion is scheduled for FY2030 and beyond. In other words, Nvidia has already committed to purchasing $390 billion worth of components and manufacturing capacity through the end of FY2030, though given the fact that its purchases in FY2028 are set to exceed $200 billion, expect its procurements in FY2030 to be higher.
The commitments reflect Nvidia's efforts to ensure that its suppliers can manufacture sufficient quantities of advanced processors, memory, substrates, and packaging components. In addition to its existing agreements with partners like TSMC, Micron, Samsung, and SK hynix, Nvidia on Wednesday announced new partnerships with Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Kinsus for substrates, as well as SPIL for advanced packaging. In addition, the company disclosed agreements with Amkor, Ibiden, KYEC, and Unimicron.
During the earnings call, Kress said that demand for Nvidia's products continues to exceed available supply, prompting the company to work with manufacturing partners to expand production capacity. She also indicated that Nvidia could provide suppliers with prepayments or other financial assistance to accelerate capacity expansion.
Although these procurement commitments are gargantuan, Nvidia expects demand for its AI infrastructure to remain strong, which will justify the expenditures. The company raised its revenue growth forecast for FY2028 from approximately 70% to 75% due to stronger demand and additional manufacturing capacity that it expects to secure.
In addition to its supply commitments, Nvidia disclosed $32 billion in agreements with neocloud providers that allow it to earn revenue from hardware sales and participate in cloud rental revenue above a guaranteed minimum. Meanwhile, the company's maximum financial exposure under various guarantees reached $118 billion, including $105 billion in credit support for the PORTS-Pike AI data center campus in Ohio, which will serve OpenAI under 20-year leases.
In total, Nvidia's commitments reached $540 billion as of early Q4 FY2024.
2028 pricing strategy and beyond
Nvidia currently absorbs higher component and manufacturing costs to honor existing purchase orders and maintain previously agreed prices for its customers. As a result, the company expects its GAAP gross margin to decline from 74.8% in Q3 FY2027 to 71% – 72% in Q4, which it considers the bottom of the current margin cycle.
Going forward, Nvidia plans to introduce revised pricing in FY2028 to help offset higher supply costs and restore profitability, which is when the company expects gross margins to recover to 72% – 73% next fiscal year, although it has not disclosed the magnitude of its planned price adjustments or the products they will affect.
"We thought about in terms of our prices and pieces of that, and a lot of the costs were some of the things that we absorbed in those numbers that we included," Kress said. "What we provided here in Q4 is our bottom. If you recall, that was our bottom as we honored many of the different POs that we had already received from our customers, and we just wanted to make sure that was held solid as we moved to a new pricing, as we moved into the new year."
Perhaps more importantly is that Colette Kress largely sidestepped the question about custom AI accelerators and their potential impact on Nvidia's pricing power. During the conference call, an analyst asked whether Nvidia would accept lower margins to protect its market share against custom AI accelerators developed by hyperscalers. The interim CEO avoided directly addressing whether competition from custom silicon could undermine Nvidia’s competitive position, leaving considerable room for speculation.
Nvidia expects $130 billion in Q4
For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, Nvidia projects revenue of approximately $130 billion ±3%, which would represent an increase of about 12% sequentially. The company expects GAAP gross margin of 71% to 72% and GAAP operating expenses of approximately $11 billion during the quarter. Nvidia’s forecast excludes Data Center compute revenue from China and accounts for an additional week in the quarter. While Nvidia expects its gross margin to decline during the Vera Rubin transition, Kress said that the company anticipates a recovery to 72% – 73% in FY2028.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Supercomputing needs rack-scale management, Dell says - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Scripts can’t run AI factories: Dell moves cluster management from the server to the rack
As artificial intelligence clusters grow to supercomputing scale, the hard part of the AI factory is no longer buying hardware. It is keeping racks, switches, GPUs and cooling running once they are switched on.
That operational burden is reshaping what infrastructure providers sell. Dell Technologies Inc. has spent the past year pushing its AI Factory beyond servers and storage, and customers are now asking for best practices and better tools to stand up and run what they buy, according to Andrew Vaz (pictured, left), vice president of product management for the Telecom Systems Business at Dell.
“What we are seeing is a fundamental shift from procuring supply to actually standing up and running these very complicated AI clusters and data centers,” Vaz said. “One of the interesting things that we’ve seen is it’s actually now impossible to manage these things with just a few scripts, manually, in an old world manner. The toolsets are becoming more important.”
Vaz and Saurabh Kapoor (right), director of product management and strategy for AI compute and networking solutions at Dell, spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed supercomputing, rack-scale management, AI observability and why networking sits on the critical path for AI clusters. (* Disclosure below.)
Rack-scale management for the supercomputing era
Dell used the conference to introduce Dell OpenManage Rack Scale and Dell Fabric Manager, two tools for running AI infrastructure from deployment through daily operations. OpenManage Rack Scale manages 100,000 devices in its first release, up from 8,000 servers for its predecessor, OpenManage Enterprise, Kapoor explained. Systems such as Nvidia Corp.’s NVL72 racks bundle compute, power shelves, switches and coolant distribution units into one unit.
“OpenManage Enterprise, the previous product we had, was perfect for servers. Server was the unit of compute,” Kapoor said. “But you have seen in the last 18 months, the world has moved very quickly to larger ecosystems and infrastructures. Rack is the new unit of play.”
Visibility is the other half of that equation. Dell’s iDRAC controller pulls more than 320 metrics from every server, and an AI-assist chatbot can query that telemetry through local large language models, according to Kapoor. A single cooling leak can damage millions of dollars of gear, so every layer has to report in, Vaz noted.
“It could be something as simple as, ‘Hey, this transceiver’s about to die that you can’t diagnose with metrics you have today,'” Vaz said. “You need to use AI to go look at it. You need telemetry off the system to go collect all of that, correlate it, run your algorithms on them, train it and understand what’s happening.”
The network is where those pressures concentrate. Dell Fabric Manager turns validated designs built with Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. into deployable blueprints across different network operating systems and silicon. Agentic AI is also reshaping traffic, and enterprise bandwidth is outrunning a projected 3.5-fold increase, Vaz noted.
“We’re getting blown away by it. It’s more like nine to 10x,” Vaz said. “It’s going everywhere: east, west, north, south.”

articles.title: I asked Google Gemini to turn my research into an interactive website — five minutes later, I was genuinely impressed
articles.text:
Gemini now turns your notes into interactive websites with a single prompt —after trying it, I was genuinely impressed
Gemini Notebooks made a website out of my King Arthur research without any code at all
Google has given its Gemini Notebooks a new way to translate its AI-powered research into a more flexible format. You can transform a collection of notes and research into an interactive website simply by describing what you want, making the usual AI-generated summaries look a little old-fashioned.
The websites take the research stored in Gemini Notebook, formerly known as NotebookLM, and produce an easy-to-navigate site. There's no coding or design involved. You just need a rough idea of what you'd like to create.
To try it, open Gemini Notebook, create a notebook, and add your research material from the internet or uploaded documents. Then type "make me a site" into the chat and describe the kind of website you want, then open the generated result to explore it. You can open the finished website separately from the notebook and share it with others.
Artistic story
I tried it out using research on the history of King Arthur stories over the centuries. Specifically, I asked the AI to "Make me a site full of visually engaging and interactive elements showcasing the many forms and styles of Arthurian lore." I didn't specify the layout or explain which interactive features to include. I wanted to see how much Gemini could figure out for itself.
The website Gemini produced from that prompt took about five minutes to finish, and the results were better than I expected, if not quite a finished product. The Once and Future Myth: How Fifteen Centuries Reshaped King Arthur is definitely more than just text. Take a look!
The website offers a full interactive guide presenting the evolution of the legends as a series of stages through history and broken up into different elements, characters, and media. The most impressive section might be the one devoted to Victorian interpretations of Arthurian legend. Gemini created a searchable collection of 17 artworks, with filters for the type of artwork and the stories they depict. It also included charts showing how those works were distributed across different periods, turning a fairly specialized subject into something that was easy to investigate.
Another section compared the BBC television series Merlin with traditional Arthurian stories. It examined where the show preserved familiar elements and where it deliberately changed them. Some of the charts don't seem to be particularly useful, but they are certainly as colorful and adjustable as requested.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Camelot online
I was particularly impressed that Gemini had created all of this from such a broad instruction. I hadn't requested an hourglass diagram or asked for searchable artwork collections, yet both made sense for the subject. The result felt as though the AI had considered how someone might actually want to explore the information rather than simply finding ways to decorate it.
There are limitations, of course. Some of the historical claims are quite specific, and a polished website can make questionable information appear more authoritative than it deserves. I'd want to check important details against the original sources before using the site as an educational reference, particularly where the history of Arthurian literature remains disputed.
The website is also more like an interactive research publication than a conventional personal website. That's perfectly suited to my experiment, but someone hoping to create a business homepage or an online store would have different requirements.
My Arthurian website isn't perfect, and I'd still want to check its claims before sharing it as an authoritative resource. But I was genuinely impressed by how thoughtfully Gemini organized the material and how much of the finished site actually worked as an interactive experience. It's definitely more likely to catch the eye of a student looking for new ways to study than the usual written notes, as long as you have the right research sources to build on.
