articles.title: Youtube krempelt die View-Zählung um: Co-Views werden ab sofort mitgezählt
articles.text:
Youtube zählt ab jetzt Co-Views: So verändert sich die View-Zählung
Die Videoplattform Youtube hat ein großes Update für die View-Zählung in petto – schon wieder. Erst im Sommer wurde eine Metrikanpassung für die View-Zählung vorgestellt. Seit dem 24. August genügt auf Youtube schon der Start eines Videos, damit ein View gezählt wird. Jetzt kommt eine Neuerung für die Integration von Co-Views im öffentlichen View-Count hinzu.
Was Co-Views auf Youtube sind und wie die Plattform sie einordnet
In einem Video für den Creators Insider Channel erklärt Rene Ritchie von der Youtube-Liaison, was es mit den Co-Views auf sich hat. Dabei handelt es sich um einen geschätzten Wert für die Anzahl der Personen, die auf TV-Geräten zusammen Youtube-Inhalte schauen. Diesen Wert generiert Youtube nicht durch die Überwachung der User, betont Ritchie darauf, sondern auf Basis von Statistiken, demografischen Daten und Sehzeiten in Kombination mit Daten aus Panels. Er führt aus:
Youtube doesn’t use devices, cameras, microphones or anything like that. Co-views are estimated using a privacy safe statistical mode, developed by Google research scientists, based on factors like demographic patterns and viewing times, calibrated against ground-truth data sources like industry panels
Die errechneten Co-Views sollen künftig direkt in den öffentlichen View-Count einfließen. Sie werden bei allen Inhalten angezeigt, Shorts, Longform-Videos und Live Content. Historische View-Counts bleiben davon aber unberührt. Das gilt aber nur für die TV-Rezeption, Desktop und Mobile sind davon nicht betroffen. Hierfür kann Youtube keine Schätzwerte zur Co-Rezeption ermitteln, wenngleich sie ebenso bei diesen Geräten möglich ist. Da aber Youtube-User schon mehr als eine Milliarde Stunden Content auf Youtube pro Tag auf TV-Geräten anschauen, möchte die Plattform die Co-Views als Metrik mehr in den Fokus stellen. Bisher gab es nur eine Private Views (Co-Viewed)-Metrik im Youtube-Studio. Diese wird im Mai 2027 eingestellt.
Bei der Analyse von Co-Views wird Youtube als Zusatzmetrik eine Co-View Rate einführen. Diese offenbart, wie viele Views es ohne Co-View für Inhalte gab. In der Aufteilung nach Gerätetypen im Youtube-Studio können die Creator diese Rate mit den Views gegenchecken. Für Views via Mobile und Desktop wird die Co-View-Rate immer 1,0 sein, da dort keine Co-Views gemessen werden können.
Für die Creator dürfte zudem noch von besonderem Interesse sein, dass die Co-Views die Werbeeinkünfte und die Hürden für das YouTube-Partnerprogramm nicht beeinflussen. Einkünfte, Auszahlungen und die Qualifizierung für das Programm bleiben an qualifizierte Views und gesehene Stunden geknüpft.
And while co-views also don’t impact metrics like Thumbnail Impressions, Click Through Rate, and Average View Duration – Watch Time will be consistent with the updated public view counts to reflect the co-view audience watching together,
schließt Rene Ritchie. Du kannst dir seine Ausführungen im X‑Post im Wortlaut durchlesen.
Der Artikel stammt von Niklas Lewanczik aus der OnlineMarketing.de-Redaktion und wird im Rahmen einer Content-Kooperation auf t3n veröffentlicht.

articles.title: Cómo crear láminas para colorear de Las Guerreras K-pop en WhatsApp en segundos
articles.text:
Desde WhatsApp es posible crear láminas para colorear inspiradas en Las Guerreras K-pop de Netflix a partir de una imagen de referencia y una instrucción escrita.
La función se realiza mediante Meta AI, la inteligencia artificial (IA) integrada en la aplicación de mensajería, sin necesidad de instalar programas de edición peligrosos.
El procedimiento permite transformar una foto promocional o una ilustración de los personajes, incluidos los Saja Boys, en un dibujo de líneas para imprimir o compartir. Puede hacerse desde un celular y desde WhatsApp Web o la aplicación de escritorio en un computador.
Dónde encontrar imágenes de Las Guerreras K-pop o los Saja Boys
El primer paso consiste en buscar una imagen clara de Las Guerreras K-pop o de los Saja Boys. Puede tratarse de una captura de una escena, un póster, una imagen promocional o una ilustración publicada en canales oficiales de Netflix y sus redes sociales.
Conviene elegir archivos con los personajes en primer plano, fondos simples y buena iluminación. Las imágenes con muchos elementos, sombras o textos suelen dificultar que la inteligencia artificial identifique las figuras y las convierta en un dibujo apto para colorear.
Qué hacer luego de descargar las imágenes
Tras guardar la imagen en el dispositivo, hay que abrir WhatsApp y localizar el acceso a Meta AI. En muchos teléfonos aparece como un ícono circular multicolor en la pestaña de chats; en otras versiones, se puede encontrar desde la barra de búsqueda o al iniciar una conversación nueva.
Al tocar el ícono, se abrirá el chat con Meta AI, el asistente de Meta. Si es la primera vez que se utiliza, la plataforma puede solicitar la aceptación de sus condiciones de uso.
Dentro del chat con Meta AI, hay que pulsar el botón para adjuntar archivos, que suele tener el símbolo de una cámara, un clip o un signo más. Luego se debe seleccionar de la galería la imagen de Las Guerreras K-pop o de los Saja Boys que se descargó previamente.
La imagen quedará adjunta en el mensaje, pero todavía no habrá sido procesada. Antes de enviarla, es necesario escribir una instrucción que explique qué transformación se busca. Meta AI permite editar fotos e imágenes que los usuarios cargan de forma voluntaria en la conversación.
Cuál prompt escribir para obtener una lámina para colorear de Las Guerreras K-pop
El prompt debe ser directo y describir el resultado esperado. Una opción es escribir: “Convierte esta imagen en una lámina para colorear infantil, en blanco y negro, con contornos negros definidos, sin sombras, sin colores y con fondo blanco”. Después, hay que enviar el mensaje junto con la foto.
Se pueden sumar detalles para ajustar el diseño. Por ejemplo, se puede pedir “líneas gruesas”, “rostros reconocibles”, “estilo de dibujo para imprimir” o “sin letras ni logotipos”.
Si el resultado se aleja mucho de la referencia, se puede responder en el mismo chat con una nueva orden para corregir el fondo, simplificar los trazos o eliminar detalles.
Cómo revisar y descargar el dibujo final en el dispositivo
Meta AI mostrará en la conversación la imagen generada. Antes de guardarla, se debe revisar que los personajes mantengan rasgos reconocibles y que las líneas sean suficientemente claras para colorear con lápices, fibras o pinturas. Si aparecen manchas, áreas oscuras o elementos incompletos, se puede solicitar otra versión.
Asimismo, cuando la lámina esté lista, se debe mantener pulsada la imagen y elegir la opción “Guardar” o “Guardar foto”, según el sistema operativo. El archivo quedará en la galería del celular y podrá imprimirse o enviarse por WhatsApp.
En el computador, el proceso es similar: se abre la conversación con Meta AI, se adjunta la imagen, se escribe la indicación y se descarga el resultado desde la versión web o de escritorio.

articles.title: Why Tobi Oyewole took a pay cut to build a software career
articles.text:
In 2020, Tobi Oyewole had a company car, an official apartment, and two sponsored trips to China behind him. Then he left for a new job that paid less.
“I wasn’t really satisfied with the kind of work I was doing,” he says.
For Oyewole, a petroleum engineering graduate turned software engineer, taking the pay cut was a first in another sense. Until then, someone else had made most of his career decisions for him.
As a boy, he daydreamed about playing football professionally and even won a prize in secondary school. He also wanted to become a pilot. But his father had other plans, teaching his son maths himself in the hope that he would pursue engineering.
“I’m just going to do what they wanted. I am going to be a good child,” Oyewole remembers thinking.
He initially applied to the University of Lagos (UNILAG) in south-west Nigeria to study electrical engineering, but eventually settled on petroleum engineering, another course his father approved of.
“Oil and gas is not that bad either,” he says. He enrolled in 2011.
Yet the oil and gas job he had trained for never materialised. Despite sending out applications, he heard nothing back.
“Trying to get an oil and gas job was not very easy,” he says. “I still think about it now. Maybe I didn’t try hard enough.”
Oyewole’s interest in technology and coding began in his second year at UNILAG, when he started building websites in Adobe Dreamweaver and teaching himself HTML and CSS along the way.
“I’d just be learning a few things, just to see what’s happening in this tech thing,” he says. “At the time, I wasn’t even into tech, and it wasn’t tech the way we see tech now. We just had some guys who came to teach about building stuff on the Internet.”
His growing interest in programming soon began to affect his academic performance.
“My 200-level GPA [grade point average] was the worst I ever had, because I was really inquisitive about programming and I was concentrating on it badly,” he says. By his third year, however, he had set aside his coding interest to focus on his petroleum engineering degree.
He would eventually return to programming, a decision he says he has never regretted. Today, he is also helping secondary school students discover opportunities in technology, giving others an introduction to a path he once found for himself.
Dumping oil and gas
After graduating from UNILAG in 2016, Oyewole said he had hoped to work in the oil and gas industry. However, he joined MOJEC, an electrical company, instead. The company, which builds smart electricity metres gave him his first real shot at paid employment after tertiary studies.
“I didn’t really have much experience. It was just time to put the body to work. Anything they threw at me, I was ready to do it,” he says.
He spent much of his time programming meters at the factory, supporting the information technology (IT) team, and fixing the office Internet. MOJEC also gave him room to explore other areas of the business. He describes it as “a canvas you can paint your life however you want,” where employees could take on projects with few restrictions. One such project involved renewable energy and took him to China twice on company-sponsored trips, he says.
“It was a place where you could give yourself out, and they were ready to pour back into you,” he says.
His experience gradually drew him towards the technology side of the business, prompting him to consider what he could build rather than simply fixing existing problems. He enrolled at New Horizons, an information and communication technology (ICT) training institute that offers professional certification programmes, to develop his skills, studying programming languages C# and .NET.
Although he still had his sights on oil and gas, seeing colleagues receive technology job offers and leave MOJEC about three years into his employment made him reconsider.
“I knew that I had to take this tech seriously,” he says. “I don’t think I can be putting my eyes out on oil and gas stuff anymore. This is the time for me to get fully focused on building a career in software engineering.”
In 2020, he left MOJEC and decided to spend time strengthening his programming skills through YouTube tutorials and other learning resources.
Building software
After spending time at home developing his coding skills, Oyewole joined Reliance Infosystems, an IT consulting firm and Microsoft partner, in November 2020.
Placed on the company’s customer relationship management (CRM) team, he worked with Microsoft Dynamics 365. Although his role involved learning to use and administer the platform, he was far more interested in understanding how to build software himself.
“The thing with Dynamics 365 and the likes is that these are apps that have already been built. You have to know how to use them well. But I was much more interested in building those apps myself,” he says.
He likened this curiosity to using Microsoft Excel while wanting to understand how the spreadsheet was built.
“It’s one thing to know how to use Excel well, but there are also people who built Excel from scratch,” Oyewole said.
That curiosity led him to build applications that integrated with Dynamics 365. When a client needed a custom application that no one else on the team could develop, Oyewole says he took on the project and built it from scratch.
“That was one project that really boosted my skills,” he says.
He left Reliance Infosystems in October 2021 and joined Softcom, a technology company building digital solutions, in 2022. There, he worked on Kwiksell, a product that helped merchants sell online, manage inventory, and track sales.
Working with experienced engineers introduced him to more structured development practices, including daily stand-ups, sprints, and customer validation sessions. He also began to understand how engineering decisions connected to customer needs and business goals.
“At Softcom, I started seeing systems that scale and engineers offering really smart solutions to problems,” he says.
The job also gave him the opportunity to move beyond tutorials and personal projects, deploying software to real customers, observing how they used it and learning what it took to build and maintain production software.
He also learnt to balance his interests as an engineer with the needs of the product and to work at a faster pace.
But his time at Softcom was short-lived. Financial difficulties eventually led to layoffs.
“It was my first experience of being laid off,” he says.
The experience was particularly difficult because he struggled to tell his parents, who had been sceptical about his decision to pursue software engineering.
“My layoff from Softcom was not funny at all. It was so bad I could not even tell my parents,” he says. “I was scared because my parents weren’t really okay with me venturing into software. It wasn’t something they saw potential in.”
It was one of the lowest points in his career. He began questioning his decision to pursue software engineering but knew he had to keep applying for jobs and find another opportunity.
Working with a global engineering team
In 2023, Oyewole persisted and eventually joined Andela, a Nigerian-founded talent marketplace that became a unicorn startup in 2021 after raising $20 million at a $1.5 billion valuation.
“I applied to Andela like four times before I finally got in,” he says. “After getting into Andela, I went for a couple of client interviews.”
One led to an engagement with Science Corporation, a US-based biotech startup, marking his first international role. Working with colleagues in Egypt, Pakistan and the United States, he gained experience collaborating across time zones and adapting to a more demanding engineering culture.
“It was an awesome experience because at Science, it was much more core engineering, being able to think critically about what you write,” he says.
According to Oyewole, the company’s head of engineering often reminded the team that “the best kind of code you write is no code,” encouraging engineers to keep solutions simple and think carefully before making changes.
This also pushed Oyewole to expand his skills beyond frontend specialisation; it allowed him to learn how to fix issues on the company’s Ruby on Rails server and make design decisions in the absence of a dedicated designer, he told TechCabal.
“But it was an eye-opener into global standards for technology. Being able to write code the right way, not just writing code as usual, but writing it to work,” he says.
Science was developing software to help scientists digitise experiments and track their findings. As the company grew, it shifted towards having engineers work alongside scientists in person to better understand their challenges. The change ultimately led to Oyewole’s layoff.
“We got laid off from Science because they were moving to a model where they needed engineers to be physically at the company,” he says. “They needed people who could interface with those scientists themselves to understand the pain points that the scientists were facing.”
His second international role was with Mars, best known for its chocolate brands. He joined the company’s Petcare brand as a frontend engineer on the Kinship team. The experience introduced him to a market with a very different attitude towards pets from what he was used to in Nigeria.
“When I joined Kinship US, I was the only Nigerian on my team. There was lots of culture shock, talking to different people, especially about pets,” he says. “Coming from Nigeria, where people don’t really care about pets as much as they do out there, joining the company meant you literally had to care for pets.”
His team built digital products for pet owners, including platforms connecting them with veterinarians and animal shelters, as well as tools for purchasing pet food and publishing pet-care content.
Kinship also gave Oyewole room to expand beyond frontend development. During regular check-ins, his manager encouraged him to discuss his career ambitions, and he expressed an interest in understanding the full software development lifecycle, from frontend and backend development to deployment.
“I might not be an expert at everything, but I wanted enough knowledge as an engineer to know how this works,” he says.
His manager responded by assigning him backend tasks, giving him opportunities to build features, review code, and work alongside backend engineers.
He also took on his first team leadership role, managing engineers across time zones and leading projects from start to finish.
“At that point, it was not just about writing code, but also being able to manage people,” he says. “It’s one thing to build for yourself. It’s another to manage people and scale quickly while you’re also building.”
He left the company in June 2026.
Beyond writing code
Over the years, Oyewole has come to see technology less as an end in itself and more as a tool for solving problems, a perspective shaped by his experience working across industries.
“I see technology as an enabler. I think of technology as something that could help your process,” he says. “It’s nice if you are building something cool, but what’s best is something that makes money for you.”
He believes engineers must look beyond the technical appeal of what they build to consider the value it delivers to businesses and their customers. That perspective also shapes the projects he explores outside his regular work.
Towards the end of 2025, as interest in artificial intelligence grew, Oyewole began experimenting with Model Context Protocol (MCP), a way of connecting AI applications to external tools and information. He built a tool that allowed AI assistants to search Nigerian e-commerce platforms and compare product prices, according to him. Inspired by his own experience of trying to find the most affordable options online, he built it to work with existing AI chatbots, such as ChatGPT, rather than as a standalone application.
He also explored how MCPs could improve his work as a frontend engineer, experimenting with connecting Figma, a design tool, to his team’s codebase to reduce the manual work involved in translating designs into code.
His interest in the wider tech community led him to open-source. While reading the MCP documentation, he came across an issue involving the addition of agent skills and joined the team working on it. This allowed him to contribute to the technology’s development while collaborating with engineers from companies including Amazon and Google, according to him.
He hopes to continue contributing to open-source projects and speaking at technology events, particularly those aimed at helping younger developers. He is also planning talks at secondary schools around Lagos to introduce students to technology careers, explain how the websites and applications they use are built, and highlight the opportunities available in the industry.
Beyond these interests, Oyewole’s next career goal is to take on greater responsibility for how software products are built and managed. Having spent most of his career as an individual contributor, he is increasingly interested in the decisions that go beyond writing code: choosing which features to build, balancing business priorities with technical constraints, and ensuring products solve customers’ problems.
“Over the past six years, I’ve come to realise that building great software goes beyond writing code,” he says. “There’s also the people, planning, decision-making and coordination required to turn an idea into a product.”
He hopes to take on more leadership responsibilities, from mentoring engineers and leading technical discussions to participating in product planning.
“I’d love to be remembered as someone who was always about solving problems in any industry,” he says. “I believe impact goes beyond the software we write.”

articles.title: Luis Tosar, actor, 54 años: “Me produce mucha tristeza que ahora haya niños por ahí hablando de Franco, reivindicando su figura”
articles.text:
La infancia de Luis Tosar fue un poco de descampados y de fábricas abandonadas. Cuando habla de sus hijos, le preocupa el mundo en el que están creciendo. En su charla con Ana Trasobares se lamentaba del panorama actual. “A mí me produce mucha tristeza que ahora haya niños por ahí hablando de Franco, reivindicando su figura”.
“Niños, cuyos padres ni siquiera han vivido el franquismo y, aun así, están en ese discurso”. En un contexto de polarización de redes, Tosar lamentaba que hubiera jóvenes reivindicando al dictador.
“No se dan cuenta de que este señor se alzó en armas el 18 de julio y acabó con un gobierno legítimo. Es increíble”. Se refería al día que se produjo la sublevación militar de los militares contra la Segunda República (que derivaría en la Guerra Civil).
De los descampados de Lugo a la crianza de sus hijos
Por otro lado, la conversación tocaba también el tema de la infancia de Tosar. Cómo era su entorno. Vivió en un ambiente rural, pero luego su padre empezó a trabajar en Lugo y entonces se mudaron a esta ciudad. Vivían en un barrio del extrarradio. “Era un mundo urbano, pero a medias”.
En este periodo recuerda haber tenido una infancia “superdivertida”. Él era un niño “gamberro, pero no más que los demás”. Jugaban a piratas y a Indiana Jones. También descubrió el breakdance. “Recuerdo que nos íbamos a bailar a las fábricas abandonadas y nos creíamos que estábamos en Nueva York porque aquello parecía el Bronx”.
La paternidad de Tosar también le ha cambiado. Aunque admite que a veces es sobreprotector, intenta que sus hijos se relacionen con el campo. Además, viven fuera de Madrid. Por eso pueden “descubrir” todo lo que les rodea. “Me gusta que investiguen las texturas de las plantas, de las tierras, de los metales”.
La conversación partía de “Golpes” (de Rafael Cobos), la historia de dos hermanos divididos por las circunstancias y con un difícil reencuentro.
El actor cree que España no está totalmente reconstruida desde la Guerra Civil. Todavía quedan algunas heridas por curar. Sin embargo, tiene cierta confianza en el resto. “Me parece que la especie humana, a estas alturas, ya debería estar extinta por las cosas que hacemos. Sin embargo, aún hay gente capaz de arrancarnos del abismo. Es de agradecer”. Resumiendo: “Menos mal que existe toda esa gente buena, porque si no este mundo ya habría desaparecido”.

articles.title: Optimizely hack made Zoom, CNN, BBC, and 175 other sites serve crypto-stealing malware
articles.text:
What we know so far: Most big websites load a handful of scripts they didn't write themselves, from analytics tags to A/B testing tools. On Monday, one of those tools was turned against them. Attackers slipped malicious code into Optimizely's experimentation platform. For most of the day, it pushed a crypto stealer and card skimmer to visitors of Zoom, CNN, the BBC, and roughly 175 other organizations.
Optimizely is best known for letting companies A/B test their web pages on real visitors. Customers embed a small snippet that pulls each project's code straight from Optimizely's servers. So whoever controls that code effectively decides what runs in every visitor's browser.
That's exactly the kind of power the attacker grabbed. To see how far it reached, Report URI's Scott Helme and his team checked 1,611 Optimizely snippets. The malicious code turned up in 188 of them. Those belonged to 178 organizations, including Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM and even hardware wallet maker Ledger. Embarrassingly, Optimizely's own websites were serving it too.
As for how it happened, Optimizely told Gizmodo that someone exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow. The attacker then wrote code into each customer's "Project JavaScript" field. That setting runs on every page, so Optimizely's servers delivered the malware just like any legitimate experiment.
Strangely, the company hasn't explained how a signup bug let an outsider edit other companies' live projects. Even so, Optimizely says it has blocked the vulnerable path, deployed a fix, and notified affected customers.
Once loaded, the payload hunted for crypto wallet addresses across eight blockchains and replaced them with the attacker's own. It even rewrote addresses copied to the clipboard, so anyone pasting a wallet address from an infected page could end up paying a stranger. A card skimmer joined in partway through the day, lifting card numbers, expiry dates and CVVs from checkout forms.
On iOS 18.6 and earlier, the code also quietly loaded the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits – the same leaked tools criminals have used to raid iPhones this year.
By that evening, Helme estimated the attacker's wallets had pulled in about $7,040. But in its own analysis, StepSecurity says that figure undersells the damage. Stolen cards and hacked iPhones simply don't show up on the blockchain.
For visitors, Helme recommends updating iPhones to at least iOS 18.7.3 or iOS 26.3. Any card entered on an affected site on November 16 should be treated as exposed, too.
Optimizely's customers aren't the first to get burned this way, either. Just this July, Adform's tracking script was rigged to swap crypto addresses in much the same way. Two years earlier, the Polyfill.io takeover pushed malicious code to more than 100,000 websites.

articles.title: Vercel Releases UI SDK for Agents to Compose UI from Reusable Behaviors
articles.text:
Vercel has released UI SDK, an open-source TypeScript library that treats keyboard navigation, focus, selection, popups, and drag and drop as reusable behaviors rather than details buried inside finished components. Vercel UI SDK is published on GitHub as vercel-labs/ui and is currently in beta.
The behaviors live in @ui-sdk/core. Vercel says it built more than 50 of them, including createPopup, createSelection, createTypeahead, createRovingFocus, createReorder, createResize, createViewport, createListbox, createChange, createFocusRecovery, and createVirtualizer. A developer, or more often an agent, combines those helpers inside definePrimitive, which declares a component's state, API, and slots once. Framework adapters then render the same primitive through createParts in React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, or as Web Components. The parts are unstyled and expose attributes and CSS variables. The same behaviors also back a starter library of more than 50 unstyled components, from Color Picker, Token Input, and Command to Calendar, Tree, and OTP Input, with the same part names in all five adapters.
UI SDK is meant to be used by agents, not only written by them. The ui-sdk skill, installed with npx skills add vercel-labs/ui --skill ui-sdk, points an agent at the Markdown docs shipped in the installed packages. At runtime, createAgent, imported from the matching framework package such as @ui-sdk/react/agent, exposes snapshot, act, and query so an agent can read component state and call actions through the component API, without screenshots. Apps can approve or refuse those steps, and change callbacks receive a source of "agent" and may cancel a change. registerTools can expose the same methods to a browser's built-in agent through WebMCP, when the browser provides document.modelContext.
Developers already have several headless libraries at this layer, including Radix UI, Base UI, React Aria, Ark UI and its Zag.js state machines, and Headless UI. shadcn/ui sits one level above those primitives as a copy-into-your-repo component kit. UI SDK aims lower, at composable behaviors shared across frameworks, and adds a first-class agent bridge. The changelog thanks the teams behind Radix, Base UI, React Aria, shadcn/ui, Nuxt UI, and Geist. Vercel has not said whether shadcn/ui will be rebuilt on UI SDK.
Rahim, a product engineer at Mux who built Vidstack, wrote after reading the source:
This is so genuinely cool. I love how it's been packaged up. So elegant @shadcn and @shuding! I'll be studying this for a while. 1. createAgent is an "agent bridge" which gives a snapshot, act, and query tool. It allows agents to interact with the actual UI components directly 2. Change callbacks know when the agent made the change (details.source === "agent"), and the app can refuse it with cancel (I love this)
A developer identified as Stefan looked at the repository and asked how the idea compares with existing headless libraries:
I tried looking at the repo a bit but I’m not sure I quite understand the value prop of this versus something like Base UI. Is the thought process that we should be thinking about UIs/components as combinations of behaviours?
UI SDK is in beta as 0.1.0-beta.1, licensed under the Apache License 2.0, and subject to Vercel's public beta terms; the APIs, documentation, and behavior may change before general availability. Install @ui-sdk/core plus the adapter for your framework, for example npm install @ui-sdk/react @ui-sdk/core, which requires React 19 or later. The Vue, Svelte, and Solid adapters document peer ranges of Vue 3.5, Svelte 5.33, and Solid 2 from 2.0.0-rc.14. Setup details are in the documentation.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.text:
Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
- Date:
- November 17, 2026
- Source:
- University of Jyväskylä - Jyväskylän yliopisto
- Summary:
- A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.
- Share:
An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.
The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.
The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers. A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to poorer academic performance, while regular exercise is known to support brain function, particularly in adults. However, scientists still have much to learn about how physical activity, sitting, and screen use during childhood influence thinking abilities later in adolescence.
These questions are especially important because childhood and adolescence are critical periods of brain development. Changes in attention, memory, and learning during these years can have lasting consequences, potentially influencing educational opportunities and career paths well into adulthood.
To investigate these relationships, Finnish researchers examined how screen time, physical activity, and sedentary behavior from childhood through adolescence were associated with cognitive performance in teenagers. They also explored whether the connections differed between boys and girls and whether the intensity of physical activity made a difference.
More Screen Time Linked to Better Thinking Skills
One of the study's most unexpected findings was that greater screen time throughout childhood was associated with better cognitive processing in adolescence.
Cognitive processing refers to the mental abilities people use to take in information, pay attention, remember details, learn new things, and solve problems. These abilities play an important role in school performance and everyday decision-making.
The findings challenge the idea that all screen time should be viewed as harmful. However, the researchers caution that the relationship may depend on what children are actually doing while using digital devices. Watching videos, playing games that require strategic thinking, and engaging in educational activities may involve very different levels of mental effort.
"The findings suggest that screen time can support children's and adolescents' cognitive processing. Presumably, the essential point here is what kind of things they do in their screen time. Teachers and parents should encourage children to use devices and screens in such ways that promote active thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and learning," states Doctoral Researcher Petri Jalanko from the University of Jyväskylä.
"We should not regard screen time solely as harmful but seek balance between physical activity and screen time that promotes active thinking," Jalanko summarizes.
Exercise Affects Boys' and Girls' Brains Differently
The researchers also uncovered a more complicated picture of how physical activity relates to thinking and memory.
Among girls, spending more time engaged in light-intensity physical activity since childhood was associated with better working memory during adolescence. For boys, greater participation in guided physical activity over the same period was linked to stronger working memory.
Working memory is the brain's ability to temporarily hold and use information. It allows someone to remember instructions while completing a task, keep track of numbers during mental calculations, or follow a conversation while processing new information.
Light-intensity physical activity generally includes relatively gentle movements that do not substantially increase breathing or heart rate. Guided physical activity refers to exercise carried out with some form of instruction or supervision, such as organized sports or structured exercise sessions.
The differences between boys and girls suggest that the relationship between exercise and brain health may depend on more than simply how much a person moves. The type of activity, how it is organized, and the individual's sex could all play a role.
Another Surprising Finding About Physical Activity
The study produced another counterintuitive result. Teenagers who reported spending less time in unsupervised physical activity tended to perform better on measures of cognitive processing.
Yet when researchers used wearable sensors to objectively measure movement and heart rate, they found no association between overall physical activity or sedentary time and cognitive performance.
One possible explanation is that wearable devices measure movement without revealing what a person is actually doing. For example, a sensor may record periods of sitting or physical activity, but it cannot determine whether someone is solving a difficult problem, studying, participating in an organized activity, or simply resting.
This distinction could help explain why questionnaire responses revealed relationships that were not apparent in the sensor measurements.
"Our study indicates that the connections of physical activity and sedentary behavior to cognitive processing are complex and depend on the sex, the type and assessment method of physical activity and sedentary time. Moreover, boys and girls may benefit from different types of physical activity in view of brain health," Jalanko adds.
"However, we need more intervention studies to find out causal relations and sex differences in this respect. Moreover, it is important to examine more specifically the effects of the intensity of physical activity on changes taking place in cognitive processing."
What the Eight-Year Study Revealed
The findings come from an eight-year follow-up conducted as part of the PANIC study, a long-running Finnish research project investigating children's physical activity and nutrition.
The current analysis included 260 participants, consisting of 124 girls and 136 boys. Their average age at the adolescent assessment was 15.8 years.
Researchers collected information about physical activity and sedentary behavior using both questionnaires and wearable devices that combined heart rate monitoring with movement measurements. This approach allowed them to compare participants' reported activities with data collected by sensors.
To evaluate cognitive abilities, the researchers used the CogState test battery, a collection of computerized assessments designed to measure aspects of mental performance. The tests examined learning, attention, and working memory.
Importantly, the findings show associations rather than cause and effect. They do not establish that increasing screen time will improve a child's thinking abilities or that reducing certain types of exercise will produce cognitive benefits. Intervention studies, in which researchers deliberately change participants' activities and measure the results, are needed to determine whether these relationships are causal.
Nevertheless, the results offer an important perspective on the continuing debate over children's screen use. Rather than treating all time spent with digital devices as equally harmful, the researchers suggest paying closer attention to whether those activities encourage active thinking and learning.
The research also highlights the importance of considering different forms of physical activity rather than focusing exclusively on the total amount of exercise children receive.
Together, the findings suggest that supporting healthy brain development may require a more nuanced approach, one that combines physical activity with opportunities for learning, creativity, and mental engagement, including those that take place on screens.
The study was published in the scientific journal Pediatric Exercise Science.

articles.title: Sony's updated turntable is an easy entry into the world of vinyl | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Record players and other retro tech are making a strong comeback, and I’ve recently rejoined the world of vinyl collecting. Lately, I’ve noticed myself turning to Spotify less frequently, so it felt like the perfect time to start using a record player again.
Choosing a turntable can be quite overwhelming, especially for beginners. That’s where Sony’s new PS-LX3BT turntable comes in.
Since 2019, Sony’s PS-LX310BT has been a go-to choice for vinyl newbies. Now that it has been discontinued, the PS-LX3BT emerges as its successor, keeping the same beginner-friendly approach while adding a few modern upgrades.
Currently priced at $399.99, the PS-LX3BT is designed for people who want to enjoy vinyl without getting too caught up in the technical side of things. It’s also a good option for those looking to upgrade from their first inexpensive turntable without having to learn how to set up or customize a more complicated audio system.
One of its biggest selling points is how easy it is to use. The PS-LX3BT features automatic playback, so you simply press start and the tonearm lifts, moves into position, and drops onto the first track for you. There’s no need to manually position the needle or worry about getting everything just right. It’s a small convenience, but one that makes the experience much less intimidating for newcomers.
Sony has also made a few welcome changes compared with its predecessor. The PS-LX3BT now uses USB-C for power and supports Qualcomm’s aptX Adaptive Bluetooth codec, allowing it to transmit audio at up to 24-bit/96kHz. It also has a traditional phono output alongside Bluetooth, so you can choose between a wired speaker setup and listening wirelessly.
One slightly strange design decision, however, is the repositioning of the start, stop, and tonearm buttons. On the older model, these were placed outside the dust cover. Now they’re underneath it, meaning you’ll have to lift the cover just to press start. It’s not a huge inconvenience, but still kind of annoying.
The turntable also offers USB connectivity for digitizing your vinyl collection. Connect it to a computer, and you can convert your records into digital audio files, which is useful if you want to preserve older records or listen to your collection on the go.
My biggest disappointment is the lack of a built-in speaker. It would have been nice to have everything included for someone just getting started. You’ll need to buy speakers (and possibly an amplifier) or compatible Bluetooth headphones separately, so keep that added cost in mind.
If you’re searching for a more affordable and beginner-friendly automatic record player, there are cheaper options, such as this $179 option from Audio-Technica. But overall, Sony’s PS-LX3BT is a solid choice for anyone ready to dive into the world of vinyl for the first time.

articles.title: GTA 6 sort à minuit : mettez votre PS5 à jour dès maintenant
articles.text:
Même si vous avez déjà téléchargé GTA 6, il vous reste un tour dans les paramètres de votre PS5. Sony a rendu une mise à jour de la console obligatoire pour lancer le jeu, qui se débloquera dans la nuit du mercredi 18 au jeudi 19 novembre en France métropolitaine.
GTA VI sort dans quelques heures, et après 13 ans d’attente, les joueurs sont prêts à se perdre des heures durant dans les rues de Vice City. Vous avez fait le tri sur votre SSD, récupéré le jeu et prévu de veiller un peu plus tard que d’habitude ? Un conseil : allumez votre PS5 avant ce soir. L’assistance américaine de PlayStation a en effet prévenu les joueurs à quelques heures de la sortie : la console doit avoir installé une mise à jour du logiciel système pour pouvoir lancer Grand Theft Auto VI.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Même si GTA 6 est déjà installé, vérifiez votre PS5 pour installer la dernière mise à jour obligatoire
Le préchargement est ouvert depuis le 10 novembre sur PS5. Si vous avez déjà fait de la place et récupéré les fichiers du jeu, ils sont prêts pour le lancement. La mise à jour dont parle Sony concerne le système de la console. Le constructeur ne précise pas pourquoi elle est nécessaire à GTA 6, mais elle est visiblement obligatoire pour accéder au jeu.
Si vous avez configuré les mises à jour automatiques de votre PS5, normalement tout est bon. De notre côté, la nouvelle version a été installée durant la nuit, en plus d’une mise à jour de GTA VI livrée juste à temps par Rockstar Games avant la sortie du titre.
Si ce n’est pas le cas, nous vous conseillons vivement de faire un tour dans les réglages de votre console et de télécharger le paquet rapidement, pour ne pas perdre une seconde avant le lancement. Et si vous n’avez pas encore lancé le préchargement (mais qu'attendiez-vous ?), Sony demande de prévoir 212 Go d’espace libre sur la console.
Où trouver la mise à jour sur votre PS5 ?
Depuis l’écran d’accueil, ouvrez Paramètres > Système > Logiciel système > Paramètres et mise à jour du logiciel système. Si la mention Mise à jour disponible apparaît, choisissez Mettre à jour le logiciel système et attendez la fin de l’installation.
Voilà, vous êtes fin prêts à vous rendre à Vice City, et vous ne serez pas seuls. Selon les derniers chiffres en date, GTA VI se serait déjà écoulé à plus de 15 millions d’exemplaires avant même sa sortie, et on peut parier que des millions de joueurs, emportés par la hype, devraient les rejoindre dans les prochains jours. L'événement d'une génération qu'on vous dit.

articles.title: Si vous voulez un robot cuiseur avant les repas de fêtes, Lidl fait baisser son Monsieur Cuisine Smart
articles.text:
Velouté de potimarron, pâte à brioche, risotto qui se remue tout seul : le Monsieur Cuisine est le robot cuiseur que Lidl vend sous sa marque maison Silvercrest. On le cite souvent comme l’alternative au Thermomix de Vorwerk. Sa version Smart Black Edition, connectée au Wi-Fi, baisse de prix.
Pour le Black Friday, Lidl affiche son robot cuiseur à 399 € au lieu de 549 €, soit 150 € de moins.
C’est quoi, ce Monsieur Cuisine Smart Black Edition ?
Un robot cuiseur chauffe et mixe dans un même bol. Celui-ci est en inox, avec une contenance de 4,5 litres dont 3 litres utiles. La puissance maximale atteint 1 200 W, avec 1 050 W pour la chauffe et 1 000 W pour le moteur. La température se règle de 37 à 130 °C. Les lames tournent entre 125 et 5 500 tours par minute, sur 10 vitesses avec une fonction turbo. La rotation à droite hache les ingrédients. La rotation à gauche remue un ragoût ou un risotto sans réduire les aliments en purée. Une balance intégrée pèse jusqu’à 5 kg directement dans le bol.
16 fonctions et programmes automatiques sont présents, parmi lesquels le pétrissage, la cuisson vapeur, les smoothies, la fermentation, la cuisson lente et la cuisson sous vide. Cette dernière cuit à basse température un aliment emballé hermétiquement. L’accessoire vapeur fourni empile les niveaux de cuisson : un poisson au-dessus, les légumes en dessous, et le repas se prépare en une fois. Vous trouverez aussi un fouet, un panier de cuisson et une spatule. Tous les accessoires passent au lave-vaisselle.
La partie « Smart » repose sur un écran tactile de 8 pouces et une connexion Wi-Fi. Le robot embarque plus de 1 000 recettes guidées pas à pas, dont certaines en vidéo, et ajuste le nombre de portions sur une sélection d’entre elles. Google Assistant permet de le commander à la voix, à condition que le Wi-Fi soit actif. L’application ajoute un planificateur de menus hebdomadaire et une liste de courses.
À ce prix, le Monsieur Cuisine Smart est-il une bonne affaire ?
Avec 150 € de remise, le robot perd un peu plus d’un quart de son prix et passe sous la barre des 400 €. C’est un très bon prix pour un appareil qui remplace à la fois le blender, la balance de cuisine et le cuiseur vapeur. Le Thermomix de Vorwerk, qui reste la référence du secteur, coûte nettement plus cher pour un principe similaire.
Deux réserves avant de vous décider. Avec environ 45,7 x 37 x 29 cm, le robot prend de la place sur un plan de travail. Ses fonctions les plus avancées dépendent aussi de l’écosystème de recettes de Lidl et d’une connexion Wi-Fi. Si vous cuisinez souvent maison, les 150 € économisés couvriront largement les premières courses pour les gros repas de fin d’année.

articles.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
articles.text:
Apache has released security updates to address a critical Roller flaw that threat actors are exploiting to gain code execution on vulnerable servers.
Apache Roller is an open-source, Java-based group-blogging server with a much smaller market share than modern content management systems and blogging platforms.
However, while this is a niche product, Apache has flagged the flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-129448) as actively exploited in the wild.
Apache has not yet provided details about these ongoing attacks, including who is responsible and how many servers have already been compromised.
"Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester," Apache explained in a Tuesday security advisory.
"This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited."
To block ongoing attacks, Roller users should immediately upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects malicious XML-RPC requests after turning off the XML-RPC feature.
Admins who can't immediately upgrade can also temporarily mitigate CVE-2026-129448 by setting "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, removing the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restarting Roller.
According to Apache, disabling XML-RPC in the administration user interface is not enough to block attacks because older versions deserialize the request before checking whether that setting is toggled on.
In April, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) also flagged a 13-year-old Apache ActiveMQ vulnerability (CVE-2026-34197) as exploited in attacks and ordered federal agencies to secure their systems within two weeks.
More recently, earlier this month, Apache fixed a critical vulnerability in the HTTP/2 module of Apache HTTP Server that an unauthenticated attacker could exploit to gain remote code execution on unpatched servers.
Since November 2021, CISA has added 41 Apache flaws to its catalog of vulnerabilities exploited in the wild, eight of them also abused by ransomware gangs.

articles.title: XPRIZE launches $6m competition to tackle foundational learning crisis in Africa, India - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Global non-profit XPRIZE has launched XPRIZE Accelerate Learning, a two-year, US$6 million competition seeking tech-driven solutions that help first graders in Sub-Saharan Africa and India master foundational reading and maths.
XPRIZE is an established global leader in designing, launching, and executing large-scale competitions to solve humanity’s greatest challenges.
The competition, which takes place in Rwanda, aims to cut the time it takes children to learn reading and maths skills from four years to one, at a cost as low as US$10 per child, and to reach nearly one million students in target communities. In Sub-Saharan Africa, nine in 10 children cannot read and understand a simple sentence by age 10.
Startups, non-profits, universities, corporates, government agencies and individuals can enter one or both of two tracks. The Core Track, worth US$5 million, seeks end-to-end solutions that improve mastery by at least 25 percentage points at under US$10 per child per year. Up to eight finalists will deploy at school district scale, with the winner taking home US$2.5 million.
The Last Mile Moonshot track, with separate US$400,000 purses for Sub-Saharan Africa and India targets a 50 percentage point improvement at under US$40 per child. Finalists will test their solutions in a six-month randomised controlled trial.
Teams will be paired with local schools or districts to co-design and test their solutions, so that governments can adopt them long term.
“Rwanda’s Vision 2050 depends on a skilled and productive workforce, and that journey begins with children who can read, understand and apply what they learn,” said Joseph Nsengimana, Rwanda’s Minister of Education. “We welcome XPRIZE as a partner in accelerating solutions and invite Rwanda’s innovators, educators and researchers to help transform learning outcomes for every child.”
Partners include the Republic of Rwanda, the African Union Development Agency-NEPAD, Equity Group Foundation, ShikshaNext and IDinsight. Qualified teams will be announced in 2027, and winners in 2029.

articles.title: Windows 11 : pourquoi certaines de vos applications risquent bientôt de refuser de démarrer
articles.text:
La sécurité dans Windows 11 est sur le point de subir une évolution majeure. Microsoft vient en effet d’introduire sa nouvelle Windows Baseline Protection, un nouveau système de protection qui laissera chaque application installée sur votre PC décider si votre configuration est suffisamment sécurisée pour qu’il puisse s’exécuter.
Un nouveau bilan de sécurité unique pour Windows
Concrètement, cette Windows Baseline Protection consiste à regrouper huit fonctionnalités de sécurité matérielle et logicielle du système sous la forme d’une simple vérification binaire. Contrairement au passé, où la sécurité d’un PC consistait à un assemblage d’options séparées qui devaient être vérifiées individuellement, ce nouvel outil, va regrouper huit modules de protection du système au sein d’un bilan de sécurité unique qui fournira un résultat simple.
Windows contrôlera alors votre puce TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, la sécurité basée sur la virtualisation (VBS), l’intégrité de la mémoire, la signature des pilotes (pour empêcher le chargement des pilotes de périphériques non identifiés), les pilotes certifiés Windows, la protection contre le débogage du noyau, et enfin le blocage des pilotes vulnérables.
Au démarrage de votre PC, tous ces éléments de sécurité seront ainsi vérifiés par Windows qui indiquera si « oui » ou « non » votre machine est correctement protégée.
Ce signal unique sera ensuite annoncé aux applications installées sur votre ordinateur qui pourront alors décider des mesures à prendre en fonction du niveau d’exigence respecté par votre PC.
Un manque de sécurité pourra bloquer certaines applis
Avec ce nouveau système de protection intégré à Windows 11, Microsoft veut laisser aux éditeurs d’applications le choix de la réaction à adopter en cas de manquement côté sécurité.
Vos applications pourront ainsi afficher un simple message d’avertissement à l’écran. Elles pourront aussi choisir de restreindre l’accès à certaines de leurs fonctionnalités, avec dans les cas les plus extrêmes, de bloquer complètement leur lancement si la sécurité requise n’est pas atteinte.
Plusieurs grands éditeurs sont d’ores et déjà en train de tester ce système, à commencer par Adobe. L’éditeur de Photoshop aurait ainsi une nouvelle solution pour lutter contre le piratage et les logiciels contrefaits ou modifiés. Battle.net (Blizzard) testerait également ce système de protection pour renforcer la lutte contre la triche dans les jeux vidéo. D’autres éditeurs, comme Schoolyear (pour vérifier la sécurité du PC d’un étudiant avant d’autoriser le début d’un examen en ligne), 1PassWord et Raycast (pour garantir la protection des mots de passe et des interactions avec l’IA) testeraient également cette technologie.
Comment vérifier si votre PC est correctement protégé ?
Pour savoir si votre machine est conforme aux critères de sécurité de Microsoft, vous pouvez vous rendre dans les Paramètres de Windows 11, puis dans la section Sécurité, entrer dans le module de Protection de base.
Un indicateur visuel indiquera l’état de votre PC. Un bouclier vert sera ainsi affiché lorsque « Tout est protégé », tandis qu’un bouclier jaune sera affiché si « une attention est requise » de votre part. Dans le cas où une option de sécurité manquerait à l’appel, Microsoft affichera un bouton pour réactiver celle-ci et redémarrer votre PC.
Et si toutefois l’un des paramètres du BIOS/UEFI devait être modifié, Microsoft affichera un QR Code à scanner avec votre smartphone pour accéder à un guide d’utilisateur décrivant la marche à suivre pas à pas.
Ce nouveau système de sécurité est pour l’heure en cours de test auprès des Insiders. Microsoft n’a pour l’instant donné aucune date de déploiement dans la version stable de Windows 11.

articles.title: Botsync raises $11M to expand industrial automation
articles.text:
Botsync raises $11M to expand industrial automation
Botsync has raised $11 million led by IvyCap Ventures to advance its AI-powered industrial automation platform, improve robotics capabilities and expand its presence in India and global markets.
Singapore-headquartered Botsync has raised $11 million in a round led by IvyCap Ventures, a homegrown venture capital firm.
Other participants include Capital 2B, a deeptech investor; Taiwan-based accelerator and venture investor AppWorks; South-East Asian early-stage investor Iterative; Singapore angel network AngelCentral; Genesis Alternative Ventures; and angel investor Nalin Advani.
The round follows a January 2026 Series A extension led by SGInnovate, taking total funding above $20 million.
Founded in 2019, Botsync builds autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), or driverless material movers, and software that coordinates factory and distribution-centre operations. Its SyncOS platform connects robots, robotic arms, conveyors, machines and enterprise software, managing tasks and traffic through one interface. Its MAG robots move loads of up to 1.5 tonnes.
“As India’s manufacturing ecosystem evolves, solutions combining robotics, AI, and intelligent automation will play a critical role in driving efficiency and scale. We believe Botsync is well positioned to address this growing opportunity and expand its footprint across global markets,” said Vikram Gupta, Founder and Managing Partner of IvyCap Ventures.
Funds will add SyncOS tools for throughput optimisation, predictive maintenance and operational analytics, helping factories move goods more efficiently, spot faults early and use operating data to improve performance. Botsync will also improve MAG reliability, add Indian engineering and project-delivery staff, deepen local automation partnerships, and expand in Australia and the US.
India is both a market and capability centre, with a Bengaluru office and experience centre serving automotive and fast-moving consumer goods manufacturers. Chief executive Rahul Nambiar said the opportunity lies in “connecting robots, machines and software systems” so facilities operate more efficiently.
Botsync claims more than 70 projects across six countries, over two million production tasks and 99% uptime. Its customers include Caterpillar, Ford, Nestlé, Honda, Coca-Cola and Kimberly-Clark. The asserts some customers recover their investment within 24 months through reduced forklift use and manual handling.
The raise comes as robotics investment in India gathers pace, although from a small base. Tracxn data put startup funding at $63.2 million across 15 rounds by July 2026, compared with $26.7 million across 24 rounds in the same period of 2025. Recent deals included Unbox Robotics’ $28 million round in January, Armatrix’s $2.1 million in February and Anscer Robotics’ Rs 45 crore Series A in May.
Meanwhile, policy support is also building. In August 2026, four SAMARTH centres had reached more than 2,700 industries and trained about 33,000 people in Industry 4.0 technologies. The National Manufacturing Mission announced in 2025 prioritises technology access and workforce readiness, while NITI Aayog’s roadmap names robotics, artificial intelligence and digital twins as manufacturing enablers.

articles.title: Black Friday : la Ninja CREAMi Scoop & Swirl à 249,99 €, le glacier à la maison
articles.text:
Black Friday : la Ninja CREAMi Scoop & Swirl à 249,99 €, le glacier à la maison
C'est la machine à glaces dont tout le monde parle depuis l'été. La Ninja Creami Scoop & Swirl, star de TikTok et des réseaux sociaux, passe de 329,99 € à 249,99 € pour le Black Friday, soit 80 € d'économie. Et avec le code NUMSN10, vous gagnez 5 % de réduction supplémentaires sur ce prix déjà cassé. Une occasion rare de s'offrir le glacier à la maison.
Ninja a bâti sa réputation sur les airfryers, puis sur les machines à café. Avec la Creami Scoop & Swirl, la marque s'attaque à un terrain plus ludique : celui des desserts glacés. Et elle ne fait pas les choses à moitié. Là où les machines classiques se contentent de produire des boules de glace, celle-ci pousse le concept jusqu'au service à l'italienne, avec un levier et une buse qui déposent la glace en tourbillon directement dans le cornet . Un geste qui rappelle les glaciers et les parcs d'attractions, transposé dans une cuisine.
La glace à l'italienne comme chez le glacier
C'est la signature de cette machine, et ce qui explique son succès. Une fois la base congelée puis transformée par la technologie Creamify, il suffit de basculer le pot du côté distribution, de placer un cornet sous la buse et d'actionner le levier. La glace sort en spirale, avec une texture onctueuse, légère et aérienne, fidèle à celle des soft serve professionnels . Trois vitesses permettent d'ajuster le débit, et le tour est joué.
Les retours d'expérience confirment la promesse : la texture est bluffante, le goût parfaitement maîtrisé, et l'effet visuel fonctionne à chaque fois . De quoi transformer un simple dessert en animation familiale, les enfants participant volontiers à la préparation comme à la dégustation.
Treize programmes pour toutes les envies
La Scoop & Swirl ne se limite pas au soft serve. Elle embarque treize programmes à touche unique : six modes classiques pour les boules de glace, les sorbets, les gelatos, les yaourts glacés et les milkshakes, six modes dédiés à la glace à l'italienne, et un mode Mix-In pour incorporer pépites, biscuits ou fruits secs . Le mode CreamiFit, lui, est pensé pour les préparations protéinées à moins de 150 kcal, dans la lignée des recettes virales qui ont fait le succès de la marque .
Deux pots de 480 ml sont fournis, de quoi préparer deux parfums différents et les conserver au congélateur. Toutes les pièces amovibles passent au lave-vaisselle, ce qui simplifie l'entretien après une session de créations .
Un prix Black Friday difficile à battre
À 249,99 €, la Creami Scoop & Swirl se place parmi les machines à glaces les plus complètes du marché. Le Black Friday est le moment d'en profiter : ajoutez le code NUMSN10 au moment de la commande pour faire descendre la facture un peu plus bas, et offrez-vous le glacier à domicile pour les fêtes et les week-ends gourmands.

articles.title: Detectaron una falla tecnológica que podría afectar a las compañías más grandes del mundo
articles.text:
Una falla de seguridad detectada en Java, una tecnología que permite que funcionen desde aplicaciones empresariales hasta servicios de bancos, hospitales y organismos públicos, puso en alerta a compañías de todo el mundo. Oracle publicó el martes 17 de noviembre una actualización para corregir el problema, identificado como Java4Shell.
Java es un lenguaje de programación muy utilizado para crear programas y plataformas. También es la base sobre la que corren muchas aplicaciones ya instaladas en servidores de empresas e instituciones. The New York Times informó que se usa en alrededor del 90 % de las compañías que integran la lista Fortune 500.
La firma de ciberseguridad Calif halló la vulnerabilidad con apoyo de GPT-6 Cyber, un modelo de OpenAI orientado a la búsqueda de fallas. El defecto recibió una puntuación de 9,2 sobre 10 en la escala que mide la gravedad de este tipo de riesgos.
La falla podría abrir la puerta a accesos no autorizados
El problema está en una función de Java que ayuda a procesar información enviada en forma de texto, una tarea habitual en inicios de sesión, cargas de archivos e intercambios de datos entre sistemas. En ciertos equipos, esa función puede cometer un error al recibir información preparada de manera maliciosa.
Si se dan las condiciones necesarias, un atacante remoto podría leer datos reservados o tomar control de un sistema sin contar con usuario y contraseña. Calif aclaró que no existe una forma única de aprovechar la falla en todos los casos, por lo que el riesgo cambia según la aplicación y la configuración de cada organización.
La empresa probó el problema en herramientas utilizadas por compañías, entre ellas Keycloak, Jira y Confluence de Atlassian, JFrog Artifactory y Jenkins. También detectó posibles escenarios de riesgo en otros programas que requieren que el atacante ya haya iniciado sesión. La lista no incluye todos los servicios que podrían verse alcanzados.
El alcance depende de la versión de Java y del equipo utilizado
Java4Shell afecta a determinadas versiones de OpenJDK, la implementación más extendida de Java, y a distribuciones basadas en ella. Entre estas figuran Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Red Hat OpenJDK, Oracle Java SE y Oracle GraalVM for JDK.
La falla no impacta en todos los dispositivos que usan Java. Calif indicó que se presenta en servidores con procesadores específicos, habituales en algunos centros de datos, mientras que los equipos con procesadores ARM64 no están afectados. Por eso, las organizaciones deben revisar tanto la versión de Java instalada como el tipo de hardware que usan.
La investigación fue coordinada con agencias de Estados Unidos, Canadá, Australia, Nueva Zelanda y Reino Unido, que integran la alianza Five Eyes, además de empresas como Google y Microsoft. El objetivo fue dar tiempo a los proveedores y usuarios para aplicar medidas de protección antes de divulgar los detalles del caso.
Oracle recomienda instalar la actualización de seguridad
La principal recomendación es actualizar Java con el parche distribuido por Oracle y comprobar qué versiones funcionan en los servidores de cada organización. Calif también mencionó alternativas temporales para desactivar una función de aceleración en algunos equipos, aunque señaló que esa medida debe aplicarse con cuidado y no reemplaza la actualización.
El caso vuelve a mostrar cómo la inteligencia artificial puede acelerar la búsqueda de errores informáticos. Calif sostuvo que el investigador Quang Luong detectó la falla en cerca de una hora y desarrolló una primera prueba en dos horas más. La rapidez de ese proceso eleva la importancia de mantener los programas actualizados, en especial cuando sostienen servicios esenciales.
Una recomendación para los usuarios
Para quienes usan computadoras personales o aplicaciones bancarias, la recomendación es mantener actualizado el sistema operativo y descargar las actualizaciones de las apps apenas estén disponibles desde tiendas oficiales. Esta falla afecta sobre todo a los sistemas que operan las empresas, por lo que los usuarios no suelen tener que instalar un parche de Java por su cuenta. De todos modos, conviene evitar enlaces recibidos por mensajes o correos, no instalar aplicaciones fuera de los canales oficiales y comunicarse con el banco ante cualquier movimiento o aviso inusual.

articles.title: TechCabal expands SA coverage with launch of TC Mzansi
articles.text:
TechCabal is launching TC Mzansi, a weekly newsletter dedicated to South Africa’s technology and innovation economy, as the pan-African technology publication deepens its editorial presence in one of the continent’s largest technology markets.
Tomiwa Aladekomo, CEO of Big Cabal Media, TechCabal’s parent company, announced the newsletter at Africa Tech Festival in Cape Town on Wednesday. The first edition is scheduled to reach subscribers’ inboxes on November 23, extending the publication’s coverage of South Africa and the wider Southern African Development Community (SADC) region.
The launch reflects TechCabal’s push to build a stronger regional newsroom presence and give South Africa’s technology industry more dedicated coverage. While the publication has reported on African technology for 13 years, starting in Lagos, Nigeria, it has expanded its operations in South Africa with a Johannesburg-based editorial team.
“We have hired an A-team here, and next week we’re launching a new newsletter focused on South Africa. It’s TC Mzansi,” Aladekomo said during a fireside chat moderated by Jessica Hope, founder and chief executive officer of public relations firm Wimbart.
He said the newsletter would focus on telling stories about innovation in South Africa, including the journey from university research and technological development to commercial products, as well as connecting the country’s technology ecosystem with the rest of the continent.
TC Mzansi will cover developments across South Africa’s startup and technology industries, including funding, acquisitions, telecommunications, digital payments, artificial intelligence and policy. Its coverage will also extend to SADC markets, particularly developments with implications for South African businesses and investors.
The newsletter is designed to go beyond a roundup of headlines. Its editorial format will combine important regional developments with deeper reporting and analysis of the businesses, investments, people and policy decisions shaping the technology economy.
Each edition will include a selection of major headlines, a closer look at a major development, technology business moves, relevant industry data, and developments readers should watch.
“Super excited about that and about telling the stories of innovation here, the bridge between research and technology in universities and what becomes end products, and connecting South African tech with the rest of the continent,” Aladekomo said.
The launch comes as South Africa’s tech ecosystem navigates a period of significant change. Telecommunications consolidation, the expansion of digital financial services, artificial intelligence adoption and renewed investment in digital infrastructure are reshaping the competitive landscape.
Aladekomo said connecting South African technology with the wider continent was an important part of what made the market exciting for TechCabal.
TC Mzansi joins TechCabal’s existing newsletter portfolio, which includes TC Daily, its weekday briefing on Africa’s technology ecosystem; The Next Wave, which examines innovation and the future of the industry; and Francophone Weekly, which covers technology developments in French-speaking Africa.
The launch is also part of a wider refresh of Big Cabal Media’s newsletter products, including a redesigned TC Daily and the introduction of Crypto by TC, a vertical focused on cryptocurrency developments, deals and regulation across Africa.

articles.title: Juan Manuel Rojas, arquitecto: “Si hoy tuviésemos albañiles como los que hicieron la Plaza de España, yo diseñaría una plaza así”
articles.text:
Para explicar este problema de profesionalidad en las obras de construcción, Juan Manuel Rojas utiliza el ejemplo de la Plaza de España de Sevilla. “Si yo tuviese los albañiles que hicieron la Plaza de España, yo diseñaría la Plaza de España, pero desgraciadamente no tengo esos albañiles”, explica en esta entrevista. Con ello justifica que hay que llevar las viviendas a la fábrica.
El arquitecto fundó en 2002 su propio estudio Hombre de Piedra Arquitectos junto a Laura Domínguez. Además, es profesor en la Escuela Técnica Superior de Arquitectura de Sevilla. Pertenece a Arquitectura Industrializada Colaborativa (AIC), que es el grupo de trabajo de los colegios sevillanos de arquitectos y de arquitectura técnica que están trabajando en la industrialización de la construcción.
Para Rojas, hay que ver cómo era la albañilería de antes. Era un tipo de albañil que tenía un conocimiento muy grande. Recordemos al maestro que hacía el muro sin que el arquitecto le dijera mucho. Tenía un conocimiento que le permitía solucionar casi todo mejor que el arquitecto que proyectaba. Ahora, según él, tenemos un problema de falta de cualificación que pone en riesgo lo que pasa en las obras.
Rojas lo relaciona con el poco valor que se da al trabajo manual. También es un problema de remuneración de esa tarea. Antes se tenía más orgullo en hacer las cosas bien. Había un conocimiento que se pasaba de padres a hijos.
La vivienda que propone fabricar
Es aquí donde entra la construcción industrializada. Es uno de los argumentos que utiliza para justificar que haya que llevar las casas a las fábricas y no dejarlas en manos de la mano de obra de cada obra.
Rojas cree que se puede combinar la artesanía con la industria. Un buen artesano es un artista. Hay que pagarle el precio adecuado por su trabajo.
Sin embargo, no podemos resolver la problemática de la vivienda con artistas. Necesitamos un tipo de producción que nos permita hacer muchas viviendas de manera más económica.
Recuperar a los arquitectos que se marcharon
Juan Manuel quiere que el potencial técnico de los arquitectos españoles se centre en este tipo de producción. También valora el nivel de preparación de los arquitectos españoles. Sin embargo, critica que no hay un equilibrio entre las responsabilidades que tienen y los honorarios que cobran. Eso es otro de los problemas para producir viviendas, tal y como explica en esta entrevista.
Por otro lado, están los que se han visto obligados a emigrar tras la crisis de 2008. Para Rojas, a muchos les ha ido bien fuera. Por desgracia, en otros países están aprovechándose de su formación (que es pagada por la sociedad española). Hay que retener ese talento o recuperarlo. La arquitectura industrializada es una opción de vuelta. “Ese talento es algo que deberíamos retener, incluso recuperar”.
