articles.title: What’s next for Nvidia? Whatever doesn’t rock the mind-bogglingly profitable boat
articles.text:
If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do? That’s how much pure profit Nvidia now makes. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change.
What’s next for Nvidia? Whatever doesn’t rock the mind-bogglingly profitable boat
I want you to understand just how much money this company rakes in.
What’s next for Nvidia? Whatever doesn’t rock the mind-bogglingly profitable boat
I want you to understand just how much money this company rakes in.
It’s easy to look at Nvidia, a company that just lost its visionary founder CEO due to a series of scandals, and think that the company and maybe the entire AI industry are in terrible trouble. Perhaps so?
But I want you to understand: Nvidia isn’t your average semi-successful company that might tempt a new CEO to fix things that are broken. It is a company so staggeringly, mind-bogglingly successful it’ll do everything in its power not to rock the boat. There is so much money at stake.
It’s so much money that when I heard about Jensen Huang’s resignation, my first thought was: I need a way to visualize this jaw-dropping amount of money for you. I want to show you that Nvidia has risen so far, so fast, that rival chipmakers AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm barely qualify as competition now.
If you’re on a desktop OS, you could mouse over each dot in our chart above to see the staggering sums. But we built another way to visualize the rise of Nvidia I like even better. It’s a horizontal bar graph that not only puts Nvidia’s revenue growth in perspective, but shows you its monster profits right alongside them — plus the world events that made Nvidia a star.
TL;DR: The crypto boom and the great GPU shortage have nothing on the AI boom. Those earlier periods saw Nvidia’s profits briefly peak at $1.24 billion and $3 billion a quarter respectively, while the rise of data centers has driven them to $65 billion per quarter with no sign of stopping.
Yes, Jensen may have set a trillion dollars of Nvidia’s market cap on fire — from around $5 trillion at the start of November to “only” $3.6 trillion now — but the smoldering company is raking in $700 million in profit a day on average.
Put another way: Nvidia could give a $1 million bonus to every one of its 42,000 employees, every three months, without running out of cash. Or, you know, Nvidia could end world hunger or provide clean water for everyone, now that it’s making over $200 billion in pure profit a year.
Maybe that’d make people feel differently about data centers?
But even if we stick to self-serving capitalism, you’re probably still a happy investor if you bought Nvidia a decade ago. A $1,000 investment 10 years ago is now worth over $67,000. You’d have over $1 million if you invested $15,000 back then.
And make no mistake, Nvidia is sticking to capitalism. Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress just promised to return as much money to investors as possible on the company’s November 17th earnings call. “Going forward, we intend to return all excess free cash flow net of strategic uses to shareholders,” she announced. “All” is a lot more than the 50 percent baseline that Jensen promised five months ago.
Nvidia isn’t the only company whose fortunes have risen this dramatically. RAMageddon revealed that just three companies — Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron — controlled nearly 90 percent of the entire global DRAM market, and those three have repeatedly signaled that they’d prefer to celebrate record profits instead of ramping up production too fast.
But while their revenues and profits have been skyrocketing even faster over the past year or so, even Big RAM hasn’t caught the AI wave quite the same way as Nvidia. Samsung, of course, doesn’t just make memory — its revenue numbers include phones, tablets, TVs, home appliances, chips, displays, camera sensors, audio, networking equipment, medical equipment, and more.
In the most recent quarter, Micron made $37.7 billion in profit, SK Hynix made $29.8 billion, and Samsung came in at around $55.3 billion, but they’re all shy of Nvidia’s $65.3 billion. Historically, RAM has also been a bit more cyclical: Both Micron and SK Hynix actually lost money in 2023 because they produced too much memory.
On its latest earnings call, the first since cofounder Jensen Huang’s resignation, interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress reinforced the idea that Nvidia expects the good times to keep on rolling.
Asked how things might change under new management, she suggested that they wouldn’t: “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual,” she said. She added that the company has secured the backing of customers and suppliers including TSMC, the all-important firm that actually fabricates Nvidia’s chips.
“Our momentum is real, our demand is accelerating, our supply is growing. Our customers and partners are with us, and employees are committed,” she claimed. “We’ve got this.”
Nvidia claims it’ll rake in even more money next quarter, with projected revenue of $130 billion. Profit may be proportionally smaller since gross margins are estimated to drop to 71–72 percent (compared to nearly 75 percent), but Kress said Nvidia intends to get them up as high as 73 percent next year.
In other words: This astounding gravy train isn’t going anywhere. At least that’s the plan.
Stevie Bonifield contributed to this story.

articles.title: Senkung der Stromsteuer: Die Koalition verschiebt die Probleme nur
articles.text:
Senkung der Stromsteuer: Die Koalition verschiebt die Probleme nur
Na bitte, geht doch, könnte man nach dem Gezerre um die Stromsteuer sagen. Die Koalition hat in einer stundenlangen Sitzung beschlossen, die Stromsteuer auch für Privathaushalte auf das europäische Mindestmaß zu senken. Für Unternehmen gilt eine solche Regelung schon länger.
Dass ein durchschnittlicher Haushalt dadurch lediglich vier bis acht Euro im Monat sparen wird – geschenkt. In diesem Fall ist schon die Geste viel wert. Alles andere wäre nämlich ein Desaster gewesen: für Friedrich Merz persönlich (er hatte die Senkung gefordert), für die Glaubwürdigkeit der Koalition (die Senkung wurde im Koalitionsvertrag versprochen) und für die gesamte Energiewende sowieso (Elektrifizierung ist ein entscheidender Hebel zur Senkung der Emissionen).
Stromsteuer-Senkung ist mehr ein Provisorium als gesichert
Doch die Koalition wäre nicht die Koalition, wenn sie nicht an entscheidender Stelle wieder nur ein halbgares und halbherziges Provisorium angerichtet hätte. Die Steuersenkung ist nämlich nur auf das Jahr 2027 befristet. Alles darüber hinaus steht unter Finanzierungsvorbehalt.
Man darf sich also darauf einstellen, dass das einmal Erreichte bei jeder neuen Haushaltsverhandlung wieder infragegestellt wird. Dabei sehnen sich Unternehmen und Privatpersonen vor allem nach Planungssicherheit. Wer jetzt vor der Entscheidung steht, sich eine Wärmepumpe oder ein E-Auto anzuschaffen, dem ist mit dem aktuellen Kabinettsbeschluss wenig geholfen. Seine Lenkungswirkung dürfte überschaubar bleiben.
Geld für fossile Brennstoffe sitzt lockerer
Dass die Koalition sich auch schnell und geräuschlos einigen kann, hat sie schon mehrfach gezeigt. Leider bei den falschen Dingen. Bei den beiden Tankrabatten in diesem Jahr waren die Milliarden beispielsweise hopplahopp da. Das Geld für fossile Subventionen sitzt offenbar immer etwas lockerer als das für die Unterstützung der Energiewende.
Ein anderes Beispiel ist die Gasspeicherumlage. Bisher wurde sie von den Gaskunden bezahlt. Doch im Herbst 2025 beschloss die Koalition, sie mit Steuergeldern zu begleichen. Das hört sich zwar nach einer Verschiebung von der linken Tasche in die rechte Tasche an, doch das täuscht: Steuern zahlen praktisch alle Bürger und Bürgerinnen, aber nicht jeder verbraucht auch Gas. Die Summe der Steuerzahlenden subventioniert also den Gaskonsum einer Teilgruppe. Ähnliches gilt auch für Stromsteuer und Tankrabatt: Jeder verbraucht Strom, aber nur eine Minderheit fährt Auto.
Senkung der Stromsteuer ließe sich für ein Jahr gegenfinanzieren
Wenn die Koalition also wieder mal verzweifelt nach Milliarden sucht: Geld wäre genug da. Die wirklich knappe Ressource ist politischer Mut, sich an die Subventionen für fossile Brennstoffe zu wagen. Ansgar Heveling, Präsident des Bundesrechnungshofes, beziffert diese auf 17 Milliarden Euro pro Jahr. Zum Vergleich: Die nun beschlossene Senkung der Stromsteuer kostet den Fiskus etwa 5,4 Milliarden Euro. Allein durch den jüngsten Tankrabatt (rund 2,5 Milliarden Euro) und durch die Gasspeicherumlage (3,4 Milliarden Euro) ließe sich die Senkung der Stromsteuer für ein Jahr gegenfinanzieren. Von den steuerlichen Privilegien für Diesel, Kerosin und Dienstwagen ganz zu schweigen.

articles.title: Nvidia is making boatloads of cash and confirms it 'does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO' — while Huang seems to have given up, and the future for gaming GPUs looks shakier than ever
articles.text:
Nvidia is making boatloads of cash and confirms Huang is out for good — and I fear the worst for gaming GPUs now
Even Huang himself appears to have admitted defeat at this point
- Nvidia's financial results for Q3 show it has doubled revenue year-on-year
- The board took the time to clarify that Jensen Huang won't be returning
- Huang himself seems to have admitted defeat based on a change in his X profile, and a reported SEC investigation only complicates matters further
Nvidia just revealed some bumper financial results in the wake of the exit of its CEO, and the board has made it clear that Jensen Huang won't be coming back — with the man himself also giving a notable signal that he's given up any hope of that outcome.
Nvidia's fiscal Q3 results saw revenue hit $115.8 billion, which is just over double the money raked in during the same quarter last year, with data center takings accounting for a towering 93% of those earnings.
Colette Kress, interim CEO and the CFO of Nvidia, commented: "Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people."
Obviously that's a reference to Nvidia being the sum of its massed ranks of staff, and not just one person, with the board also making it crystal clear that Jensen Huang won't be returning (as was previously rumored).
Sky News reports that the chairman of the board, Harvey Jones, said in an earnings call that: "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."
Huang also appears to be giving up hope that he might return as CEO, an ambition that was doubtless driven by the support he has gained from some quarters built around a petition. Huang even posted on X to say he'd be "honored to answer these calls and return as CEO".
However, the fact that he's just changed his X profile to remove the official Nvidia badge (as spotted by Yahoo Finance) suggests that Huang has accepted that he won't be retaking the helm at Team Green.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Perhaps what might have been the final bucket of cold water to douse Huang's fires of hope is bound up in a report from The Wall Street Journal claiming that the SEC (Securities and Exchange Commission) is now investigating Nvidia.
That civil investigation (on top of the FBI looking into this) would further complicate matters, and although the WSJ said the main focus of the probe wasn't clear, it will apparently include the matter of whether Nvidia's disclosures could be judged to have misled investors in the company. This is all theorizing and rumors from anonymous sources, so season liberally.
Analysis: new CEO could heap more woe on PC gamers
We've heard a great deal about the petition and a lot of noise about a possible return for the ex-CEO this week, but what's happened here concludes that particular avenue of speculation – Huang won't be coming back.
Board chairman Jones also commented that Nvidia wants to get a permanent replacement CEO "as quickly as possible", which appears to rule out some kind of internal co-CEO arrangement. (Kress, alongside Ian Buck, who is VP of HPC Computing, has been floated as a possible semi-permanent solution by the rumor mill).
And with the comeback matter effectively at an end, as far as the impact on consumers goes, I think this is bad news for PC gamers. I've argued this point already, and while some have shot back that Huang was hardly in the corner of GeForce GPU buyers anyway — and I fully accept that's a valid point — I still think the alternative is very likely to be worse.
Maybe only slightly worse, granted, but with the RAM crisis set to intensify next year, I'm wary that any new CEO will focus even more on the bottom line — meaning AI and data centers — for the foreseeable future in order to keep the Nvidia ship sailing steadily. And they won't have Huang's fondness for and history with GeForce GPUs, either (which could count for something when it comes to existential discussions about these graphics cards some way down the line, perhaps).
That said, as TechRadar's Editor At Large, Lance Ulanoff, recently pointed out – Huang isn't irreplaceable. And as Colette Kress just made clear, Team Green is the sum of its staff — the 'Nvidians' themselves — not one single leader. But change is coming to Nvidia, and I feel that will inevitably mean a still tighter focus on data center profits at the expense of gaming GPUs (which are already being very much sidelined, as evidenced by some nasty price hikes in recent times).

articles.title: Moins de 500 € pour ce super pack Dyson du Black Friday qui comprend un robot aspirateur et un balai laveur — Frandroid
articles.text:
D’un côté, on a le Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry, un aspirateur robot dévoilé en septembre dernier, lancé à un prix étonnamment bas pour la marque. De l’autre, on a un PencilWash, un balai laveur extra-mince et très maniable. À l’approche du Black Friday, le vendredi 27 novembre, ces deux appareils qui se complètent bien se glissent dans un pack à moins de 500 euros chez Cdiscount.
Que contient ce pack Dyson ?
- Un aspirateur robot avec sa station de vidage
- Un balai laveur mince que l’on manipule avec aisance
- Un combo qui permet de garder les sols propres (presque) sans effort
Respectivement lancés à 549 euros et à 349 euros, les Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry et Dyson PencilWash sont en ce moment inclus dans un pack proposé à 499,99 euros par Cdiscount, au lieu de 898 euros.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Dyson PencilWash. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Du 10 au 30 novembre, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1500 passe à 1 399 € au lieu de 1 899 €, support de lavage offert ! Sans fil, navigation LiDAR 360°, évitement précis des obstacles, tonte des bordures… La tonte sans effort, même pour les jardins les plus complexes.
Le Dyson R1 Nurovi Dry, le robot aspirateur compact bourré de capteurs
Contrairement au R2 Nurovi Wash+Dry, présenté en même temps que lui, le robot R1 Nurovi Dry se contente d’aspirer. Il n’est donc pas doté de serpillières triangulaires, mais seulement d’une brosse capable de démêler cheveux et poils d’animaux, ainsi que d’une brosse latérale anti-emmêlement, qui s’étend de 27 millimètres pour nettoyer les rebords, les coins et les zones difficiles d’accès. Toutefois, comme son grand frère, ce robot aspirateur peut passer facilement sous les meubles grâce à sa hauteur de 96 millimètres et peut franchir des seuils allant jusqu’à 40 millimètres.
Le R1 Nurovi Dry s’appuie également sur un LiDAR haute vitesse et d’autres capteurs pour cartographier le domicile, éviter les obstacles et contourner les zones surélevées. Les cartes générées sont à retrouver sur l’application MyDyson, qui permet aussi de programmer des nettoyages ou de définir des règles spécifiques à chaque zone.
Côté performances, le R1, comme le R2, offre une puissance d’aspiration maximale de 21 000 Pa. Il embarque en prime un capteur piézo, hérité des balais de la marque, qui mesure la poussière aspirée et augmente la puissance quand il en détecte beaucoup. Enfin, la station de recharge qui l’accompagne vide le robot avec huit cyclones dans un bac sans sac de 2,6 litres, qui peut stocker jusqu’à 90 jours de débris secs.
Le Dyson PencilWash, le balai laveur le plus fin de Dyson
Une fois les poussières et saletés aspirées par le R1 Nurovi Dry, le PencilWash peut entrer en jeu. Attention, cet appareil se contente de laver : il n’a aucun système d’aspiration ni de filtre. Avec son manche de 38 millimètres de diamètre et ses 2,1 kilogrammes, il a clairement été conçu pour les petits espaces. Il se range sans peine dans un coin et, surtout, il est très maniable. Le plastique de la tête de nettoyage paraît en revanche assez fin et fait un peu « cheap » : prenez-en soin.
Le PencilWash embarque un rouleau microfibre, humidifié par de l’eau propre via huit points d’hydratation. À l’usage, lors de notre test, il fait un travail correct sur les taches fraîches, mais il montre vite ses limites sur les taches plus incrustées, notamment parce qu’il n’exerce aucune pression mécanique. Retenez qu’il s’agit avant tout d’un nettoyeur de finition. Le balai est par ailleurs auto-propulsé : il tire donc un peu vers l’avant. C’est agréable au début, un peu moins après une vingtaine de minutes. La poignée n’a pas de revêtement gommeux, et la prise en main manque alors de fermeté.
L’eau sale est ensuite stockée dans un réservoir dédié de 360 millilitres. Oui, c’est petit, mais rassurez-vous, il se remplit très lentement, puisqu’il n’y a pas d’aspiration. Le réservoir d’eau propre de 300 millilitres (100 m² selon Dyson) doit quant à lui être rempli à chaque passage. La solution de nettoyage, facultative, se verse directement dans l’eau. Enfin, Dyson annonce 30 minutes d’autonomie en mode Standard. Pour la recharge, vous devrez obligatoirement séparer la tête lavante du tube. Sinon, l’appareil refusera de faire le plein. Pour la praticité, on repassera.
Pour en savoir encore plus sur le balai laveur, n’hésitez pas à lire notre test complet du Dyson PencilWash.

articles.title: Lumo Desktop : l’IA de Proton se connecte à vos fichiers, à vos applications et à un calendrier de tâches
articles.text:
Comme prévu, Proton lance Lumo Desktop, une application pour Windows, macOS et Linux. Son assistant IA peut maintenant se connecter à vos fichiers et à vos outils, exécuter des tâches à heure fixe et retenir vos consignes d’une conversation à l’autre.
Jusqu’ici, Lumo répondait dans une fenêtre de discussion. Avec Lumo Desktop, il peut agir sur l’ordinateur et dans les applications de l’utilisateur, avec des droits que celui-ci fixe lui-même.
Fichiers, tâches planifiées, consignes : Lumo sort de la fenêtre de chat
Les Connectors, accessibles depuis le menu « Customize », relient Lumo à des outils externes. Sur l’ordinateur, il peut parcourir les fichiers, lancer des commandes tapées dans le terminal et lire des pages web dans le navigateur. Il se connecte aussi à Proton Mail via Proton Mail Bridge, à Google Drive, à Jira, à Confluence et à des serveurs MCP, locaux ou distants. Le MCP (Model Context Protocol) est un langage commun qui permet à un assistant IA de dialoguer avec un outil tiers. Pour chaque connecteur, l’utilisateur choisit ce qui s’exécute seul, ce qui demande son accord et ce qui est bloqué. Proton cite une boîte mail où Lumo peut chercher, doit demander avant d’envoyer un message et ne peut rien supprimer.
Avec Schedules, Lumo exécute une tâche à une heure précise ou de façon récurrente, comme un résumé hebdomadaire de la boîte de réception ou un bilan mensuel des dépenses. On la décrit en langage courant, Lumo pose les questions qui manquent, puis prépare la tâche à valider. Chaque tâche a ses propres permissions. Les Skills, eux, enregistrent des instructions, des modèles et des fichiers de référence que Lumo réutilise d’une conversation à l’autre, par exemple pour rédiger ses e-mails dans son style. On peut écrire un Skill, demander à Lumo d’en créer un ou en importer un. Les Custom Lumos existants sont migrés automatiquement vers les Skills.
Fin août nous rapportions déjà que le dépôt GitHub public de Proton Mail laissait penser que Lumo pourrait agir dans la messagerie (libellés, filtres Sieve, mise en veille), avec confirmation avant toute action sensible. Puisque la connexion nécessite le bridge, cela signifie donc qu’elle est réservée aux abonnements payants. Rappelons que le bridge permet de configurer un compte Proton Mail sur un gestionnaire de courrier tiers en créant un serveur en local et, ce, afin de contourner les vulnérabilités liées au protocole IMAP.
Côté confidentialité, Proton affirme que les conversations et les données des applications connectées ne servent ni à entraîner des modèles ni à diffuser de la publicité ciblée. Grâce au chiffrement « zero access », seul l’utilisateur peut lire son historique. Lumo ne garde aucun journal côté serveur. Il est protégé par le droit suisse et hébergé en Europe, hors de portée du CLOUD Act américain. Un premier cluster NVIDIA B300 entre en service en Suisse. Pour rappel, cet été, proton a déplacé les serveurs de Lumo vers l’Allemagne. Dans sa démarche de transparence, Proton a publié le code de Lumo Desktop.

articles.title: British Scattered Spider hacker sentenced to 6 years in prison
articles.text:
A leader of the Scattered Spider cybercrime collective has been sentenced to six years in prison in the United States for stealing millions in cryptocurrency and conspiring to hack a dozen companies.
US prosecutors charged 24-year-old British man Tyler Robert Buchanan and four other suspects in November with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft in relation to a series of phishing attacks between September 2021 and April 2023.
According to court documents, their victims include companies across a wide range of industries, such as telecommunications, technology, business process outsourcing (BPO), entertainment, and information technology (IT) suppliers, as well as virtual currency providers, cloud communications providers, and individuals.
Buchanan and his accomplices sent hundreds of SMS phishing messages to victim companies' employees' phones (while impersonating the companies or a contracted IT or BPO supplier) to trick them into entering sensitive information (including credentials and personally identifiable information) into phishing pages that looked like their employers' legitimate websites.
The stolen information was used to steal over $11.6 million of virtual currency after compromising victims' cryptocurrency accounts and wallets via Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) swaps (also known as SIM swapping attacks).
"Those thefts had severe, life-altering consequences for many victims and underscore both the seriousness and far-reaching impact of this conspiracy," the prosecutors argued in a sentencing memorandum.
"In April 2023, on a digital device found at Buchanan's Scotland residence, he possessed the names and addresses of numerous individual victims, including a text file that contained cryptocurrency seed phrases and login information for one victim's account," the US Justice Department added.
Buchanan was arrested in Palma de Mallorca, Spain, in June 2024, has been in US federal custody since April 2025, and pleaded guilty to crypto theft charges in April.
Three of his accomplices (Evans Onyeaka Osiebo, Ahmed Hossam Eldin Elbadawy, and Joel Martin Evans) were also charged in November 2024 with wire fraud, wire fraud conspiracy, and aggravated identity theft and are now serving multi-year prison sentences after pleading guilty.
Noah Michael Urban (also known online as Sosa and Elijah), a fourth conspirator and another Scattered Spider key member, has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after pleading guilty to wire fraud and conspiracy charges in April 2025.
Scattered Spider hacking collective
The Scattered Spider gang (also tracked as 0ktapus, Scatter Swine, Octo Tempest, Starfraud, UNC3944, and Muddled Libra) is a loose-knit group of young, English-speaking threat actors that orchestrates attacks through Telegram channels, Discord servers, and hacker forums.
Scattered Spider has also partnered with several Russian ransomware operations since early 2023, including BlackCat/AlphV, Qilin, and RansomHub.
This cybercrime group was previously linked to breaches at multiple high-profile companies and organizations, including Caesars, Riot Games, MailChimp, Twilio, DoorDash, and Reddit.
According to the FBI, they're using a wide range of tactics to breach corporate victims' networks, including social engineering, multi-factor authentication (MFA) bombing (targeted MFA fatigue), phishing, and SIM swapping.
Some Scattered Spider members have also previously been linked to "The Com," another hacking collective behind violent incidents and cyberattacks.

articles.title: GTA 6 is here: everything Indian players need to know
articles.text:
GTA 6 is here: Everything Indian players need to know
The biggest game launch in years arrives on 19 November. Here is what it costs in India, what you need to play it, and what is still unclear.
Grand Theft Auto VI goes live on Thursday, 19 November 2026, more than 13 years after GTA V. Store listings in India show a 12:00 am IST start. The game arrives on the PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X and S only. There is no PC version, and none for the PS4 or Xbox One.
The price in rupees
PlayStation India lists the Standard Edition at Rs 5,999 and the Ultimate Edition at Rs 7,499. Both come with the Vintage Vice City Pack and one month of GTA+, Rockstar's subscription service. The Ultimate Edition adds an upgrade pack, and buyers of the Standard Edition can reportedly move up later for Rs 1,500, so there is no need to decide in a hurry.
For anyone who already owns a console, that is the whole bill. For everyone else, the game is the small part of the cost. Amazon India listed the PS5 Slim Digital at Rs 64,990 and the Disc model at Rs 69,985 on 28 October. Add the Standard Edition and a new buyer pays about Rs 70,989 on the digital console. Prices move, so check the final checkout figure before buying.
Do not pay extra for the disc drive
There is one trap for new buyers. The boxed version of GTA 6 reportedly contains only a download code, not a game disc. So the Rs 4,995 extra for the disc-drive PS5 buys you nothing for this game at launch. It may still make sense for other games or for resale, but if GTA 6 is the reason you are buying, the digital console is the cheaper route.
Blinkit will deliver it in minutes
Indian players do not have to wait for a courier. Quick-commerce platform Blinkit announced on its official account that GTA 6 is now available on its app, with delivery in minutes. It is live in select areas of Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, Noida, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Pune, Kolkata and Ahmedabad, and Blinkit says more cities will follow over the next day.
What arrives is a physical box with a download code inside, which matches the disc-free boxes described above. Blinkit pitched the box as a collectible for the shelf. Buyers can redeem the code and start downloading at once, so the game is ready to play when it unlocks on 19 November. Blinkit's post ended with a joke that it expects a suspicious number of people to take sick leave in the next few days.
Get the download done early
Pre-loading opened on 12 November. On the PS5, the game needs at least 212 GB of free space, according to PlayStation's store page. That is a long download on a slow connection and a big bite out of a standard broadband data cap, so it is worth checking both. Players on the Xbox Series S, which has less storage, should clear space first.
The free month that costs money later
Eligible digital pre-orders include one free month of GTA+. PlayStation India says the offer needs a digital pre-order before 20 November and must be claimed by 31 March 2027. After that month, GTA+ becomes a paid plan that renews automatically unless you cancel. Set a reminder if you do not want to keep paying.
What the game is about
The story follows two lead characters, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Rockstar Games describes a criminal conspiracy that spreads across the state of Leonida after a bank job goes wrong. Leonida is a fictional take on Florida, and it includes a modern Vice City, a place longtime fans will know from the series' past. It is the first numbered GTA with a female lead, and the two characters can work together or split up. Reports suggest the map is roughly twice the size of GTA V's, though Rockstar has not given an official figure.
The game is single-player at launch. In the US it carries a Mature 17+ rating from the ESRB, so this is not a game for children, and Indian parents buying it as a gift should keep that in mind.
What is still missing
Rockstar has not announced a PC version. That matters in India, where many serious gamers play on PCs and gaming laptops because consoles are expensive. A gaming laptop will not help on launch day. Rockstar has also not confirmed a date for GTA Online, the multiplayer side of the series.
Reports point to a PC release in the first quarter of 2027, but that is a rumour and Rockstar has not confirmed it. For Indian players with a capable gaming PC, the choice is between playing now on a console and waiting a few months. For those who do not own a console, waiting could save close to Rs 65,000.
Consoles are selling out
Demand for consoles has jumped since Rockstar's extended gameplay look appeared on Netflix. Reports from other countries say resellers have bought up stock and are charging nearly double the usual price for the PS5 Pro and the Xbox Series S, with many listings sold out.
It is not yet clear how far this has reached India, and the figures quoted for Indian listings are not reliable. Still, a buyer who needs a console for launch day should expect tight stock. Buy from authorised sellers, compare the final checkout price, and treat any listing far above the price Sony or Microsoft lists with suspicion.
Why India is watching
The console barrier is the story here. At about Rs 65,000 for the cheapest PS5, the machine costs ten times as much as the game. GTA 6 may push a number of Indian buyers into their first console, but it also shows how far the console market still has to travel in a country where most people play on phones. Whether this launch widens that market, or simply sells to those who already own a console, is the question to watch in the weeks ahead.
Prices and times are as listed by PlayStation India and retailers in early November.

articles.title: Amazon liquida esta casa prefabricada: cocina, baño y dormitorio por 6.250 euros
articles.text:
Las casas prefabricadas y módulos de tipo contenedor llevan tiempo ganando terreno como solución rápida para disponer de un espacio habitable extra, una oficina en el jardín o una vivienda auxiliar sin meterse en obras tradicionales eternas. En Amazon, ahora tienes un módulo prefabricado equipado con dormitorio, cocina y baño, que está disponible ahora por 6.250 euros.
Casa Prefabricada Móvil 37 m2 con Dormitorios, Cocina y Baño
Arquitectura modular tipo contenedor lista para instalar
Este modelo apuesta por un formato modular portátil tipo contenedor, fabricado sobre una estructura metálica galvanizada con paneles aislantes diseñados para resistir la intemperie, el viento y los cambios de temperatura. Su principal atractivo reside en que llega con la distribución interior ya resuelta para funcionar como un pequeño estudio autónomo.
Integra una zona de descanso (dormitorio), un espacio de estar con cocina equipada básica (fregadero, encimera y muebles interiores) y un cuarto de baño independiente con inodoro, lavabo y ducha.
Además, incorpora de fábrica el cableado eléctrico básico, puntos de iluminación LED, tomas de corriente y las preinstalaciones de fontanería listas para conectar las acometidas exteriores. Asimismo, cuenta con ventanas correderas de doble acristalamiento y puerta de acceso con cerradura de seguridad, facilitando tanto el uso como vivienda auxiliar como despacho profesional, casa de invitados o alojamiento turístico en fincas privadas.
Los costes ocultos que debes tener en cuenta antes de comprarla
Ver una casa completa de 6.250 euros en Amazon resulta muy tentador, pero conviene mantener los pies en el suelo: ese importe corresponde únicamente al módulo prefabricado en sí. Para que sea legalmente habitable y funcional en España, tendrás que sumar una serie de gastos adicionales imprescindibles:
- Transporte y descarga con grúa: al tratarse de una estructura pesada y de grandes dimensiones, su envío suele realizarse hasta puerto o punto logístico, por lo que deberás contratar un camión pluma o grúa especializada para trasladarla hasta tu parcela y colocarla en su sitio.
- Cimentación o solera de hormigón: no se puede apoyar directamente sobre tierra blanda o césped; requiere preparar una base nivelada que evite humedades y asentamientos.
- Acometidas de luz, agua y saneamiento: necesitarás conectar el módulo a la red eléctrica, a la toma de agua potable y a la red de alcantarillado (o instalar una fosa séptica homologada si está en suelo rústico).
- Terreno, licencias y normativa urbanística: en España, cualquier construcción destinada a vivienda (aunque sea móvil o prefabricada) exige ubicarse en suelo urbanizable o urbano, contar con proyecto técnico de arquitecto, licencia municipal de obras y cédula de habitabilidad. Si se coloca en suelo rústico sin permisos, te expones a sanciones y órdenes de demolición.

articles.title: GTA 6 : le monde ouvert de Rockstar s'offre la note ultime de 10/10 sur Gamekult
articles.text:
GTA 6 : le monde ouvert de Rockstar s'offre la note ultime de 10/10 sur Gamekult
Grand Theft Auto VI, jeu de tous les miracles, même celui du 10/10 sur Gamekult. Le site de référence, qui partage ses locaux avec ceux des Numériques, a consacré sa première note ultime au nouveau jeu de Rockstar Games.
Faut-il parler du jeu de la génération pour GTA VI ? C'est une discussion tout à fait envisageable pour Gamekult qui a rendu aujourd'hui son test de Grand Theft Auto VI : le dernier bébé de Rockstar marque la rupture avec le passé, non seulement en termes d'ambition technique, mais aussi dans une écriture qui met la satire de côté pour mettre en avant la relation entre son duo de protagonistes. Là où les villes de GTA (Liberty City, San Andreas...) étaient les vrais héros de leurs récits fleuves, GTA 6 veut nous attacher à Jason et Lucia, dont les rapports amoureux ou conflictuels tracent le fil rouge d'une aventure de grand banditisme - sans spoiler, évidemment.
Du western révisonniste de Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar a retenu un rythme beaucoup plus lent que les précédents épisodes de la franchise GTA. Non pas que le sixième épisode manque de grandes scènes d'action, comme le précise Kelmazad, mais l'épopée de Jason et Lucia ne manque pas pour autant de temps morts ; tout autant d'occasion de profiter du travail d'orfèvre réalisé pour donner vie au monde ouvert, émaillé de part et d'autre d'activités annexes (pêche, chasse, mini-golf, courses de drone...) mais aussi des missions secondaires divers et variées. L'autre héritage de la saga Arthur Morgan, c'est ces interactions poussées avec les PNJ qui habitent Leonida ; un accrochage en voiture, une fausse manip et c'est le drame, le facsimilé de Miami grouille de vie.
Nous reviendrons plus longuement sur la technique du jeu dans nos premières impressions sur le jeu à venir ce week-end, mais le test de Gamekult devrait au moins rassurer les sceptiques qui craignaient de voir une PS5 "OG" en souffrance par rapport à sa grande soeur Pro. Cette dernière profite de reflets en ray tracing et d'une qualité d'image sensiblement plus fine ; mais outre des distances de vue réduites et des temps de chargement plus longs, les consoles de Sony de 2020 (!) profitent bien d'une optimisation absolument démente.

articles.title: Amazon Prime : bonne nouvelle, vous pouvez partager votre abonnement avec quelqu'un d'autre
articles.text:
Ce 17 novembre, Amazon lance Amazon Family en France, une fonction réservée jusqu’à maintenant aux États-Unis, au Royaume-Uni, en Italie, au Canada et en Irlande. Elle permet de partager ses avantages Prime avec un autre compte Amazon. Mais attention aux petites lignes : on ne peut pas tout partager et pas à n’importe qui.
Partager ses avantages Prime gratuitement : Amazon Family est là
Si vous êtes abonné à Amazon Prime et que vous allez dans « Gérer votre Famille Amazon », vous pouvez désormais cliquer sur « Partager vos Avantages Prime ». Il permet d’ajouter un compte Amazon d’un adulte et l’inviter à profiter aussi des avantages inclus dans l’abonnement Amazon Prime. De quoi éviter de repayer 69,90 euros par an sur un deuxième compte : une belle économie potentielle.
Dans son communiqué de presse, Amazon annonce que tous les avantages ne sont pas partagés, mais il y a tout de même la livraison Prime gratuite, les offres exclusives sur Amazon, le service de streaming audio Amazon Music Prime, la SVoD avec Prime Video (avec les publicités uniquement) ainsi que le service de cloud gaming Amazon Luna. Manquent donc à l’appel certains avantages assez limités, comme Prime Photos qui permet de stocker des photos dans le cloud ; Prime Reading qui permet de lire via Kindle à des centaines de livres.
L’avantage est que chacun peut garder son compte avec son historique de commandes, ses parties sur Amazon Luna, ses recommandations sur Prime Video, etc. Bien qu’il existe déjà un système de profils sur les services d’Amazon, il faut à chaque fois partager un même compte Amazon. Mais avec Amazon Family, plus besoin de demander le code de la double authentification envoyé par mail.
Le « foyer » : une notion floue pour Amazon, mais qui doit permettre d’éviter les abus
Dans sa communication, Amazon parle d’un foyer au sein duquel un compte abonné à Prime peut partager ses avantages. L’idée derrière cela est d’éviter que certains partagent leur compte à quelqu’un d’autre : un ami, de la famille éloignée, etc. Un foyer pour Amazon, c’est une résidence principale à la même adresse pour deux comptes : « il s’agit de l’adresse que vous considérez comme votre domicile et où vous passez le plus clair de votre temps », peut-on lire sur le site de support.
On imagine qu’un compte pourra être retiré de la famille Amazon s’il n’est pas suffisamment présent à la même adresse que le compte abonné. Pour le moment, Amazon n’indique rien à ce propos sur son support. Par ailleurs, un compte qui quitte une famille Amazon devra attendre 12 mois pour rejoindre une autre famille. Là encore, c’est un moyen d’éviter les fraudes.

articles.title: “Collaboration over competition”: Hugging Face hands model inference traffic to OpenRouter
articles.text:
“Collaboration over competition”: Hugging Face hands model inference traffic to OpenRouter
Hugging Face and OpenRouter have announced a partnership that promises to make AI model inference faster and more reliable for developers.
The collaboration, announced by the two companies on Monday, will see Hugging Face use OpenRouter’s infrastructure to route language-model requests to third-party providers based on pricing, performance and reliability.
Previously, Hugging Face used its own routing system, introduced as part of its Inference Providers service in January 2025, to connect developers with companies running AI models. The service initially launched with four providers: Fal, Replicate, SambaNova and Together AI. The system would select a provider to handle each request, but if that provider encountered a problem, the request failed.
With OpenRouter now in the mix, the request can automatically be passed to another provider, meaning that developers should encounter fewer failed requests.
Hugging Face co-founder and CEO Clément Delangue sees the partnership as an example of how collaboration between AI companies can make open-weight models more accessible to developers, with each company focusing on its own strengths.
“Too many people treat AI as a zero-sum race. Open-source is winning by doing the opposite: collaboration over competition!”
“Too many people treat AI as a zero-sum race,” Delangue writes on LinkedIn. “Open-source is winning by doing the opposite: collaboration over competition!”
“Hugging Face for storage and collaboration. OpenRouter for inference,” he adds.
Stripe, Nvidia and the bigger picture
The announcement comes less than a week after Stripe completed its acquisition of OpenRouter, a deal first announced in August and reportedly worth more than $7 billion.
Hugging Face, for its part, is also in the process of being acquired by AI chip giant Nvidia for nearly $13 billion. Nvidia, however, is currently grappling with a scandal involving its former CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week amid the controversy.
At any rate, the OpenRouter integration is already live, initially covering 160 models from 38 AI labs. For Hugging Face, the arrangement means it can offer developers more dependable access to these models without having to maintain its own routing system.
In real terms, this means that users can continue chatting directly with AI models on Hugging Face’s model pages, while new interface features let them compare providers by price, speed and uptime, and check performance metrics to help them choose a provider.
The integration also works in reverse. OpenRouter users can now send records of their AI model requests to Hugging Face Storage Buckets, where they can examine prompts and responses, build evaluation datasets and prepare models for fine-tuning.
Zooming out, OpenRouter gains a direct route into Hugging Face’s enormous developer community, potentially bringing more inference traffic — and revenue –to its new owner, Stripe.
Looking ahead, Hugging Face says it plans to let developers connect their OpenRouter accounts directly to Hugging Face, while expanding the integration to cover more AI tasks. It hasn’t provided a timeline for either development.
In a blog post announcing the tie-up, OpenRouter’s director of product marketing Sasha Blumenfeld says the partnership builds on the company’s original mission of simplifying access to AI models.
“We built OpenRouter so developers can reach many models and providers through one API, use the best model for each task, and count on it to respond.”
“We built OpenRouter so developers can reach many models and providers through one API, use the best model for each task, and count on it to respond,” Blumenfeld writes. “Starting today, that extends to everyone building on Hugging Face.”
How OpenRouter chooses providers
The integration builds on a recent routing overhaul OpenRouter announced in October, which changed the criteria its infrastructure uses to determine where inference requests are sent.
Rather than relying primarily on advertised prices, the system continuously monitors providers’ actual performance, weighing response times, costs and availability before choosing where to send each request. If a provider becomes overloaded or stops responding, OpenRouter can shift traffic elsewhere and automatically retry failed requests with another provider.
OpenRouter says the changes reduced capacity-related errors by 46%, shortened the wait for the first generated token by 16.9%, and increased token generation speed by 16.3% in one of its tests. There was a cost, however: the average price per request rose by 6%, though these figures relate specifically to OpenRouter’s routing overhaul in October.
Fast-forward to today, and developers using Hugging Face can now choose whether to prioritize lower costs or faster responses, or leave OpenRouter to decide. The interface also shows the companies available to run each model, alongside their respective prices, speeds and recent availability, allowing developers to compare their options before making a request.
Developers can also disable individual providers in their account settings, preventing requests from being sent to those companies. Organizations can apply the same restrictions across all requests billed to them.
There is one notable catch in all of this: developers can no longer use their own third-party provider API keys for language-model requests through Hugging Face. Those requests must now be billed through Hugging Face, although developers can still select particular providers.
Hugging Face says it will continue charging the underlying providers’ prices without adding a markup.
It’s worth noting that the integration currently applies only to language models. Image, video and audio generation continue using Hugging Face’s existing infrastructure.
The rise of open-weights
The backdrop to all this, of course, is the rapid rise of open-weight models as more cost-effective alternatives to those emerging from the trillion-dollar frontier AI labs.
Back in September, The New Stack reported that open-weight models accounted for 60% of OpenRouter’s US token consumption in August, with Chinese-developed models responsible for most of that traffic.
That same month, another milestone emerged: open-weight models had processed a majority of tokens on Vercel’s AI Gateway for the first time, accounting for 56% in August, up from just 7% in December 2025. However, they represented only 14% of estimated spending, while Anthropic alone accounted for 64%.
The trend has very much continued, too. According to OpenRouter’s October analysis, open-weight models accounted for 71.7% of tokens processed by its 50 most-used models at the end of September, up from 26.8% a year earlier. Over that period, weekly token consumption for open-weight models grew more than sixtyfold.
Vercel’s October AI Gateway report painted a similar picture, with open-weight models accounting for 71.5% of tokens in September. Their share of estimated spending also climbed to 23%, although proprietary models continued to account for most of the money flowing through the platform.
“The best open-weight models still trail the best proprietary ones on the hardest benchmarks. For a lot of workloads, that trade-off is worth it.”
In a blog post announcing its partnership with OpenRouter on Monday, Hugging Face argued that developers don’t always need the most capable AI models, particularly when cheaper alternatives can handle their tasks adequately. It noted that open-weight models cost roughly four times less on average than proprietary alternatives.
“The best open-weight models still trail the best proprietary ones on the hardest benchmarks,” the company writes. “For a lot of workloads, that trade-off is worth it.”
For Hugging Face and OpenRouter, the growing appetite for open-weight models creates an opportunity to capture more of that demand, with developers able to choose between competing providers based on cost and performance.

articles.title: From reporting to reasoning: Getting enterprise data ready for AI agents | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
From reporting to reasoning: Getting enterprise data ready for AI agents
AWS Quick User Group DC inaugural meetup recap
Many organizations are asking how to move beyond static reporting dashboards and begin using generative and agentic AI. But before an AI agent can answer questions or help teams act, it requires a trusted data foundation.
On Wednesday, October 7, 2026, data leaders, developers, and practitioners gathered at the AWS Skills Center in Arlington, Virginia, for the AWS Quick User Group DC meetup. The session brought together founders, software engineers, and enterprise leaders, among them a team from Financial Independence Group (FIG). Attendees explored practical strategies for modernizing legacy architectures, preparing structured data for agentic workflows, and automating routine tasks with no-code tools.
        User groups like this provide a forum for peer-to-peer learning and collaborative problem-solving. The event offered attendees an inside look at how organizations are putting AWS Quick to work to drive productivity gains.
What’s new with AWS Quick: Agents, skills, and connectors
For many in the room, this meetup was a first look at what agentic AI looks like in practice with AWS Quick.
The meetup kicked off by exploring the latest product capabilities across AWS Quick, focusing on its evolution into a unified AI assistant for work. Rather than functioning solely as a traditional business intelligence visualization tool, AWS Quick unifies analytics, natural-language interaction, and multi-step task orchestration.
- AWS Quick agents and skills: Turn natural-language questions into multi-step reusable actions that aid in decision making across enterprise data.
- Third-party connectors: AWS Quick includes built-in integrations that connect tools like Salesforce, Slack, Google Drive, and Microsoft 365, breaking down data silos.
- Unified workspace: A cohesive environment that bridges research, automated visual generation, and business artifact creation (presentations, documents, and spreadsheets) directly where users work.
Real-world innovation: Moving to AI analytics and agentic systems
The core of the day highlighted a real-world customer journey showing how one enterprise is rethinking its data architecture so AI agents can work from governed, trusted data.
Financial Independence Group: Innovating at the pace of technology
Vanessa Gonzalez, Vice President of AI at Financial Independence Group (FIG), shared how FIG keeps pushing past what’s possible today. They’re adopting new tools and platforms as technology changes, and building toward AI-powered analytics and agentic systems on top of their data with AWS Quick.
Technology is changing fast, and FIG wants to be at the front of that change. Building on its existing analytics, FIG moved to AWS Quick, a platform that brings AI into its dashboards, reporting, and analytics. AWS Quick is FIG’s “single front door” for enterprise analytics. It brings together structured data such as customer relationship management (CRM) systems, databases, and finance data. It also pulls in unstructured content such as internal knowledge bases, policy documents, and collateral, through a governed data layer. That gives FIG a base for AI-powered insights and agentic workflows built on its own data.
- The AI analytics loop: Moving from reporting on what already happened to a continuous cycle: Ask → Analyze → Automate → Act.
- Centralized discovery: An analytics portal organized by business area (sales, operations, marketing, commissions), with built-in AI chat assistants so teams can talk directly to their documents and datasets.
- Democratized insights: Self-service exploration tools for non-technical business users, plus a learning hub that builds prompt engineering and AI skills across teams while keeping proper governance in place.
Hands-on: Building apps and no-code flows
Attendees worked through two hands-on exercises:
- Build an AWS Quick app in 50 minutes: Every attendee in the room successfully designed and launched a custom application in AWS Quick. This showed how fast non-technical users and developers alike can deploy purpose-built decision tools without writing code.
- AWS Quick Flows workshop: A subset of six participants dove deeper into workflow automation. They built multi-step, event-triggered flows that handle repetitive data tasks, replacing manual reporting handoffs with automated, repeatable pipelines.
One of the key takeaways is how quickly teams can go from an idea to a working solution with AWS Quick. New ideas now take hours or even minutes to build, not weeks or months.
Looking ahead and getting involved
| Figure 6: Attendees during the closing group discussion | The event concluded with an open group discussion where attendees shared practical observations on bridging the gap between legacy infrastructure and generative AI. As organizations move toward agentic architectures, the consensus from the DC user group was clear: successful AI adoption isn’t only about selecting a foundation model. It starts with intentional data design, unified access, and empowering teams to build practical automations. Building fast isn’t only about tools. It also means learning from each other, which is why events like this matter. | 
Next steps
Ready to try it yourself? Start with the AWS Quick product page and the AWS Quick user guide, then connect a data source you already use and ask your first question. From there, try building an app or an AWS Quick Flows automation for a task your team repeats every week.
Join the community
- Connect with peers: Stay up to date on upcoming meetups and presentations by joining the AWS Quick User Group on LinkedIn and participating in the AWS Quick Community.
- Explore upcoming sessions: Keep an eye out for details on our next DC-area meetup, featuring detailed hands-on architectural sessions and customer lightning talks.

articles.title: La CNIL cache le nom d'une entreprise qui stockait des « mots de passe clients en clair », Grok se charge de la balancer
articles.text:
Il suffisait de demander.
Ce 18 novembre 2026, vers 9h30, la CNIL a publié un communiqué intitulé « Conservation des mots de passe clients en clair : la CNIL prononce une sanction de 5 millions d’euros ».
L’organisme expliquait alors avoir choisi de ne pas nommer l’entreprise visée, estimant que son objectif pédagogique ne le rendait pas « utile ».
Moins d’une heure après la publication de l’annonce sur X, un internaute a demandé à Grok de qui il s’agissait. Après une première réponse évasive, l’IA a lâché le nom de Macif Vie, en s’appuyant sur des articles de presse spécialisée parus en octobre.
Des mots de passe lisibles par n’importe quel salarié
Sur le fond, les contrôles de la CNIL ont montré que les mots de passe des espaces clients étaient stockés en clair.
Ils étaient donc lisibles par toute personne ayant accès à la base, alors qu’ils auraient dû être transformés par une fonction de hachage irréversible.
D’après la délibération, près de 1,8 million de mots de passe étaient concernés. Plusieurs salariés partageaient aussi les mêmes identifiants pour accéder aux bases clients, ce qui empêchait de savoir qui consultait quoi.
L’entreprise gardait enfin les messages de son formulaire de contact plus de 10 ans, et ses données de connexion au-delà de la durée d’un an qu’elle s’était elle-même fixée. Aucune fuite n’a été constatée, et la société a corrigé ces manquements en cours de procédure.
Un dossier déjà raconté en octobre
Reste que la CNIL n’était pas tenue de taire le nom de l’entreprise. Sur son site, l’organisme explique choisir de publier ses décisions en nommant ou non l’organisme sanctionné. Elle l’a fait pour Free en 2022 ou pour De Particulier à Particulier en 2024, tous deux sanctionnés pour des mots de passe stockés en clair.
C’est d’ailleurs ce que réclamait son rapporteur dans ce dossier. La CNIL y a finalement renoncé, épargnant ainsi à l’assureur l’atteinte à sa réputation qu’il redoutait.
Sauf que le mal était déjà très largement fait. Le 15 octobre, MLex, agence de presse spécialisée dans l’actualité réglementaire, dévoilait que lors d’une audience à Paris, le rapporteur de la CNIL avait proposé une amende de 7 millions d’euros contre Macif Vie. Il lui reprochait de ne pas avoir sécurisé les mots de passe de ses clients et d’avoir conservé des données personnelles plus longtemps que nécessaire, ce qui correspond aux deux manquements retenus par la CNIL dans son communiqué.
Interrogée par Numerama ce jour, Macif Vie n’a pas démenti être la société visée. L’assureur indique avoir « pris acte de la décision de la CNIL » et assure avoir « mis en place toutes les mesures de sécurité, en conformité avec les exigences en vigueur ». Il tient aussi à « rassurer [ses] clients sur le fait qu’aucune de leurs données n’a été divulguée ».

articles.title: EIT Jumpstarter recognises Europe’s most promising early-stage innovators of 2026 (Sponsored) | EU-Startups
articles.text:
The EIT Jumpstarter 2026 winners have been announced, recognising a new generation of entrepreneurs developing solutions to some of Europe’s most pressing healthcare, food, energy, mobility and industrial challenges.
The winners were revealed during the EIT Jumpstarter 2026 Awards Ceremony, held at Unicorn Factory Lisboa in Lisbon, as an official side event of Web Summit. Selected from a pool of 895 applications, the winning teams developed their ideas through training, mentoring, market validation and pitch development. Their solutions span a wide range of sectors, including nanotechnology, food and AgriTech, energy, shared mobility, geoscience and other innovative technologies addressing real-world challenges.
“The 2026 winners reflect the ambition and diversity of Europe’s emerging innovation talent. They entered EIT Jumpstarter with promising ideas and have worked intensively to understand their markets, validate their solutions and build credible paths towards impact and growth. We look forward to seeing where they take their ventures next,” said Ilaria Tagliavini, Head of Operations, European Institute of Innovation and Technology.
First, second and third-placed teams across six categories received €10,000, €5,000 and €3,000 respectively. Special prizes also recognised outstanding solutions from Ukraine and the Western Balkans, as well as a project aligned with the New European Bauhaus initiative.
EIT Jumpstarter is a pre-acceleration programme of the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT), an EU body and an integral part of Horizon Europe.
Innovation talent from across Europe
These top-ranked teams come from 12 countries, demonstrating the geographical breadth of entrepreneurial talent emerging from Europe’s countries and regions with lower innovation performance.
Spain achieved the strongest overall representation, with three teams placing among the top three: PRECISION-CHEMO, a genomic test that predicts which chemotherapies a tumour will resist before treatment starts, SimOSpine, a digital twins and patient-specific simulation to prevent complications after spinal fusion surgery, and Valumina, spotting hidden supply-chain risks before they become disruptions. Türkiye and Latvia each secured two podium positions, while innovators from Albania, Bulgaria, Czechia, Italy, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Malta and Slovenia were also recognised.
GeoCura, from Albania, received both first place in the Raw Materials category and the Western Balkans Special Prize, underlining the project’s potential to deliver value within its sector while contributing to the growth of the region’s innovation ecosystem. Their innovation turns hazardous mine tailings into high-value construction materials.
Arcmentor, an AI assistant that helps new operators master robotic welding faster, from Ukraine, received the Rebuild Ukraine Special Prize, recognising its contribution to Ukraine’s recovery and long-term innovation capacity.
2026 EIT Jumpstarter winners
| Category | First Place | Second Place | Third Place | 
| Healthcare | Nanoflexion (Czechia) | PRECISION-CHEMO (Spain) | SimOSpine (Spain) | 
| Food & Agritech | VitisIno (Türkiye) | LOOOPS (Italy) | RAUA Systems (Poland) | 
| Energy & Renewables | CENTRA Energy (Slovenia) | Radiant Robotics (Latvia) | CoolAVent (Türkiye) | 
| Smart Cities & Mobility | Coride (Latvia) | Flobe Industries (Bulgaria) | EVDCGrid (Portugal) | 
| Raw Materials | GeoCura (Albania) | Valumia (Spain) | Capture-AI (Romania) | 
| Supporting Maltese Startups and Innovations | Timbria (Synesthesia – Abstract to Music) | BryoWall Moss Hub) | DiGiG8 | 
Special Prizes:
Rebuild Ukraine: Arcmentor (Ukraine)
Western Balkans Special Prize : GeoCura (Albania)
New European Bauhaus: Timbria (Malta)
A pathway from scientific ideas to viable businesses
EIT Jumpstarter helps early-stage innovators transform science and technology-based ideas into viable businesses through structured entrepreneurial education, specialist mentoring and access to the EIT’s pan-European innovation ecosystem. Since its launch, EIT Jumpstarter has trained more than 1,500 innovators, supported the creation of over 150 startups, contributed to more than 2,600 jobs and helped participating companies attract over €150 million in external investment.

articles.title: Miden taps Visa’s network to bring virtual cards to African businesses
articles.text:
Miden, a Y Combinator-backed Nigerian payments infrastructure startup, has partnered with payments giant Visa to help mid- to large-sized African businesses issue virtual cards and manage company spending through a single platform.
The partnership will connect Miden’s card-issuing infrastructure to Visa’s global payments network, allowing eligible businesses to create and distribute virtual Visa cards to employees, teams, suppliers, and projects. The cards will feature programmable spending controls that let companies restrict transactions by merchant, spending category, and location, Miden said.
The deal extends Miden’s efforts to build a card infrastructure for businesses that extends beyond issuing virtual cards. In March, the startup introduced tap-to-pay functionality to its card product, letting customers use their cards through digital wallets such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay.
“By integrating with Visa, we are removing unnecessary intermediaries from the equation,” Dom Okiemute, Miden’s chief executive officer and cofounder, said at the launch event in Lagos. “This gives our partners access to the world’s leading digital payments network alongside the precision card controls required to manage spend securely and at scale.”
Founded in 2022 by Okiemute and Ini Udoh, Miden builds payment infrastructure that allows businesses and fintechs to issue cards and manage collections and payouts through application programming interfaces (APIs). In 2024, the startup joined Y Combinator’s Winter batch. Since then, Miden has expanded beyond card issuance to support disbursements, collections, global payments, and treasury operations.
Under the Visa partnership, Miden provides the card management technology, monitoring, spending controls, and automated reconciliation infrastructure, while Visa provides access to its global card network. Participating financial institutions issue the cards and businesses can configure and distribute them through Miden’s platform or an API.
Miden said it is also rolling out granular spending controls alongside the direct Visa integration. Businesses will be able to restrict transactions to approved merchants, set merchant category code (MCC) limits for expenses such as software, logistics, travel, and procurement, and define geographical boundaries for card usage.
A company could issue its IT department a virtual card specifically for cloud infrastructure expenses. The card could be restricted to an approved provider such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), with a fixed monthly spending limit. Attempts to use it elsewhere would be declined, Miden said.
According to the company, its platform will also provide spending analytics showing where money was spent, by whom, and for what purpose, alongside reporting, transaction categorisation, and accounting integrations. The company said these features will help reduce manual reconciliation and give finance teams better visibility into corporate spending.
Miden says its direct technical integration with Visa removes some intermediary processing layers, allowing transactions to reach Visa’s infrastructure through a shorter route. The company expects this to reduce latency and improve approval rates.
The company operates in a competitive African payments infrastructure market that includes Flutterwave, Interswitch, and Paystack, as well as spend-management platforms such as Sava. While these companies overlap with Miden in merchant payments, card issuing, disbursements, and expense management, Miden says its proposition combines card issuing, banking infrastructure, treasury services, and payment operations in one platform.
It operates a business-to-business (B2B) infrastructure model, earning a share of interchange and per-transaction processing fees on card spending. It also charges API subscription fees from enterprises and fintechs using its financial infrastructure.
The initial rollout of the direct Visa integration covers its operating markets in Nigeria, Kenya, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and South Africa, with plans to extend the infrastructure into additional markets across sub-Saharan Africa.
In 2023, Visa partnered with South Africa’s Direct Transact to expand multi-currency card solutions for banks, fintechs, and businesses across Central Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Visa has also partnered with African fintechs such as Pesapal and MFS Africa to expand digital payments and card access across the continent.
“At Visa, we are committed to powering next-generation financial infrastructure to drive business growth and digital transformation,” Andrew Uaboi, vice president/cluster head, Visa West Africa, said in a statement. “Our collaboration with Miden is an important step forward in expanding access to secure digital issuing rails, and we are excited to see how this collaboration unlocks new efficiencies for African businesses.”

articles.title: Silvia Intxaurrondo, periodista, 46 años: “De Iñaki Gabilondo aprendí que si nos tomamos treinta segundos para pensar lo que estamos contando, podemos afinar la información”
articles.text:
“Si nos tomamos treinta segundos para pensar lo que estamos contando, podemos afinar la información”, explica Silvia Intxaurrondo. “En ese tiempo te da tiempo a reflexionar, a ubicarte y pensar quién lo puede contar mejor”.
Así lo ha explicado durante una entrevista en la promoción de la publicación de su primera novela “Solas en el silencio”. Sobre el aprendizaje de Gabilondo, explica que uno debe pararse a pensar en lo que va a contar. Trabajó con Iñaki Gabilondo en “Hoy por hoy” y luego en el telediario de noche de Cuatro.
Silvia Intxaurrondo (Barakaldo, 1979) ha trabajado en la Cadena SER, CNN+, Cuatro, ETB y Telemadrid. Ahora presenta “La hora de La 1” en Televisión Española. También ha sido en Noticias Cuatro donde ha coincidido durante cuatro años con Gabilondo en la presentación de la edición nocturna.
“Porque a veces en esos treinta segundos, podemos confirmarla, rechazarla o determinar que es un bulo”.
Unos segundos para consultar a quien sabe
Intxaurrondo vinculaba ese margen con el propio oficio: “A veces esos treinta segundos o un minuto son el tiempo diferencial entre un periodista y el que no lo es. Treinta segundos para que pienses y te hagas unas preguntas”.
También es posible que haya que recurrir a otro para resolver alguna duda. Intxaurrondo explica que a veces es necesario pedir ayuda. No siempre tenemos todas las respuestas.
“En ese tiempo te da tiempo a reflexionar, a ubicarte y pensar quién lo puede contar mejor”. Tras recordar el aprendizaje de Gabilondo, ha añadido otro de los aspectos que debe cumplir un buen periodista: “Eso es lo más importante que me enseñó. Y el trabajo duro”.

articles.title: CISO Conversations: Patti Degnan – Part of the Job Is Deciding What Not to Do
articles.text:
Patti Degnan’s journey is unusual. She didn’t have an early plan to become a CISO; but perhaps life events made it inevitable.
Patti Degnan’s first encounter with security shaped her future interest: her identity was stolen in 2006. “That was my first introduction into safeguarding data. It piqued my interest in how to better protect my own information. I wanted to understand what had happened, so I tried to discover what information about me was held by different agencies. The intent was seeing if my personal data was safe – but the effect was learning the concepts of privacy and personal data protection.”
It wasn’t until joining Symantec in 2012 that this underlying interest began to rise to the surface. “I was in internal audit, focusing on the operational and IT perspective, and began to focus on data privacy.” This was pre-Snowden and years before GDPR. She was combining audit knowledge, PCI understanding and privacy knowledge at a time its importance was growing.
Symantec had made several acquisitions. “We probably had close to 60 different backend infrastructure components that were all payment gateways. I worked hard trying to figure out what that complex environment looked like, and how we were deploying controls around it – and that was my first serious foray into security.”
She left Symantec in 2015, having become IT audit and compliance manager, and moved to LendingClub as senior manager in IT compliance and assurance. She was now seriously immersed in security. By 2018 she was senior director, information security GRC at Informatica. She then led security teams at Looker through its acquisition by Google, and by 2023 she was CISO at Notion. In 2025 she became an operating partner with the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz but returned to full-time cybersecurity in 2026 as CISO at Glow, an AI-powered endpoint security company that came out of stealth in July with $180 million in funding.
During this 20-year journey she evolved from a security victim to a security leader. Noticeably, however, it wasn’t a career plan to become a CISO – cybersecurity leadership simply grew from increasing interest and concern over personal privacy.
Leadership is a complex subject. Not everyone can be a leader, but you must be a leader to be a CISO. Where does that ability come from? Are you born with it or without it, or is leadership a quality you can learn?
The most common suggestion is that you learn as you journey. Nobody leaves high school and jumps straight into being a CISO. The journey begins with excelling in a position within a small team, being promoted to lead that team, and progressing to lead a larger team. As time passes, you learn more leadership skills by leading teams. But this still doesn’t explain why some people can be excellent at their job, but don’t seem able to become a leader.
“Philosophically, I don’t think anyone cannot learn to be a leader. But I think you must want it. I think inherently everyone has the capability to become a leader in their own way,” says Degnan. The implication is that everyone is born with the potential to be a leader, but the potential can only be activated through individual desire to do so. If, for whatever reason, you want or need to be a leader, you can learn the skills necessary to be one.
Since Degnan’s early stolen identity, adversarial activity has grown from ‘simple’ identity theft to any credential theft that can be used as an entry point into enterprise networks. The threat is more sophisticated, and the risk is more damaging. It is no longer a simple threat to individuals but a threat to entire businesses. As this threat has widened, so have CISO responsibilities also widened – CISOs must now have increased business understanding to protect the business. Cybersecurity has become a business enabler rather than simply a threat preventer. The modern CISO needs to be a businessperson as well as a technical security expert; and the former is slowly increasing in importance over the latter. So, today, can a CISO be purely a businessperson without a background of technical expertise?
“I think you can,” she says, “although you must at least have some understanding of how technology works. But ultimately, it’s entirely dependent on the business you’re in. If you’re in a tech company, you should understand how technology works because you have to translate across different stakeholder groups. I’ve worked with a guy who has primarily worked in manufacturing, and his landscape of what he would have to secure is entirely different from what I’ve had to secure in my career; so yes, I do think you have to have some level of technical understanding. Do I think you need to be a hands-on keyboard developer to understand it? No.”
CISOs do not work alone. They either inherit an existing security team, add personnel to that team, or recruit a new one. So, what does Degnan look for when recruiting her own security team members? Are, for example, security certifications important?
“To me, no. I know that’s controversial because some people spend their whole life getting a million certifications. I believe some people are great at applying theory to how things work in reality, but you don’t need to have a certification to do that. I’ve had multiple certifications over the years that I haven’t maintained, but they are a good foundation and a way to understand how things work in different areas of security, you know, in the different departments. But I don’t think it necessarily makes you a better practitioner.”
What she does look for, however, is proof of ownership and understanding of any claimed achievements. If a candidate’s resume claims to have built a specific process, she might ask for details. “Walk me through the thought process that got you there, and how did you do it?” she said. The purpose is not directly to challenge the candidate’s claim, but to discover how well they understand the cause of the need and the solution they created for it.
This approach could but does not exclude keen newcomers who haven’t yet had any opportunity to build anything. “I would never exclude that type of person. But it’s not always possible to include them. It largely depends on the size and maturity of the team you’re building. Large teams can advocate for more junior people that you can grow and shape. Small teams tend to be super lean, and you need to concentrate on acquiring a candidate that can immediately shore up one or more of the domains you need to cover.”
Regardless of the method and reasoning behind recruiting individuals, she keeps one eye on the end product: a single team with a single culture of cooperation. “It is important,” she explained, “to have the right people on the team that are not simply curious and qualified for their own position but will also work together for the team. That’s very important because we’re all in the trenches together, pushing the same rock up the same hill.”
In this process, she doesn’t specifically seek diversity in team member selection. Diversity is likely to come naturally within a team built for functionality. Gender, background, and whether someone is neurodivergent or neurotypical are irrelevant to the purpose of building the best possible cooperative team, and she neither seeks nor rejects any candidate on diversity reasoning.
One issue that faces every security practitioner is ‘burnout’. The dictionary definition is ‘mental or physical collapse caused by overwork or stress’. Working in security embraces both causes: the work is always-on, crises occur at any hour of any day, and failure to remediate any crisis could adversely affect the company and everyone working for it. Burnout is often described as rampant within cybersecurity, with some surveys suggesting it affects between 50% to 70% of practitioners.
Recovery is possible, but it takes time. But then, what? A return to the same conditions that caused the burnout in the first place: overwork and stress? Preventing future or recurring burnout can only be achieved by improving the working environment of overwork and stress. Stress cannot be eliminated because it is caused by adversarial third parties over which we have no control. Overwork could be reduced by increasing the staffing levels; but it is rare for any CISO to have the budget to adequately do so. And, ironically, the more successful the CISO, the less likely they are to receive funding for more staff.
The cause of burnout is cybersecurity itself. The CISO cannot eliminate it. All a CISO can do is attempt to manage the symptoms as they become, or before they become, apparent. Today, AI can help.
“I think burnout comes from everything being urgent,” explains Degnan. “Everything’s on fire all the time, and obviously in security, there’s an infinite amount of work. Part of the role of the CISO, or any leader, is deciding what not to do. So, I try to give very clear priorities. Automate the work you know machines should be doing in this day and age. Reserve humans for judgment and creativity in the problems where context really matters. And I’ve always been a big advocate for telling people to take time off. If you feel you need an extra day, take the day, especially now when we have the ability to build redundancy into workloads with AI. AI is pretty exciting. It gives you greater flexibility in reducing burnout.”
She goes further in time off. “My philosophy has always been that everybody should work wherever they’re going to do their best work. If someone is having a rough week and can’t come in to work, they shouldn’t. I would be happy to take the heat for it in that scenario.”
To be a successful CISO, she believes the two most important character traits are personal resiliency and communication skills. For the first, “In the face of the constantly evolving and changing concerns that are always there, you must be able to pick up the stick and keep walking every day.” That’s not just for yourself; it’s the image of strength you need to convey to your team.
Communication skills include the ability to receive information from one source and translate and deliver that information to a different destination. “You’re sitting between different levels of technical understanding among teams, executives, customers, and in some cases regulators. The board, if you report to it, is a prime example. You must have the communication skills able to translate the potential effect on the business of subtle and technical security issues into language the non- or less-technical business managers can really understand.”
For the CISOs with a planned career path, advice from mentors along the journey is common and important. Degnan had no visible path and received no specific advice. Instead, she learned from her own experiences. “The best lesson I ever learned was to never underestimate yourself,” she explained. “There will always be someone who can go deeper or be more technical in any domain, but you can still understand the strategy and the programs better than you credit yourself.”
But while she had no mentors, she is now a mentor for her security team. So, what advice would she give them in their career path? In specifics, it varies between individuals. “More generically, I have two pieces of advice. Firstly, always dive as deep as you can and know your domain, so you are comfortable when talking about it with other people. Secondly, understand the importance of communicating and partnering across the aisle. We’re not here just to look busy; we have to partner with other teams in the business to add the value of security understanding to what they are doing.”
This is perhaps the single greatest lesson to be learned from Patti Degnan’s philosophy. Security is not an island – it is a partnership with the entirety of the business. Deep understanding of the domain, and constant cooperation within the security team, and from the team to the entirety of the business, is what leads to successful cybersecurity.
