articles.title: iPhone 20 Pro : de nouvelles images confirment le design incurvé de l'écran
articles.text:
Pour les 20 ans de l’iPhone, Apple préparerait un changement esthétique que plusieurs fuites décrivent depuis quelques mois. Des échantillons de verre de protection viennent donner une forme bien réelle à cette hypothèse, avec un écran légèrement arrondi sur chacun de ses quatre côtés.
Et si le prochain grand changement de design de l’iPhone se jouait sur quelques millimètres de verre ? Depuis plusieurs semaines, les rumeurs prêtent à Apple l’intention de revoir les contours de l’écran de son modèle anniversaire. Les dernières images relayées par Ice Universe apportent un nouvel élément à ce dossier : des protections d’écran dont la forme correspond précisément à cette description.
Un premier aperçu concret de l’écran incurvé de l’iPhone 20 Pro ?
Sur la vidéo publiée par le leaker sur X, le verre présente des courbes discrètes sur ses quatre côtés. Les angles sont arrondis et les bordures paraissent particulièrement fines. L’ensemble donne un aperçu de ce que pourrait être l’écran du futur smartphone, sans pour autant permettre d’en connaître les dimensions exactes ni de confirmer son apparence définitive.
Ice Universe a également accompagné sa publication d’un commentaire sur Weibo, où il évoque la fin des protections faciles à installer et l’arrivée d’une prise en main plus confortable. Par conséquent, les accessoires devront eux aussi s’adapter à un écran qui ne s’arrête plus sur des contours parfaitement plats.
Des rumeurs qui se suivent… Et qui se ressemblent
Il est nécessaire de rappeler que ces pièces ne sont pas des composants officiels fournis par Apple. Elles seraient issues de premiers essais de fabrication réalisés à partir des informations disponibles sur le futur appareil. Les fabricants peuvent ainsi tester de nouvelles méthodes de production avant de connaître les dimensions définitives du produit.
Ce n’est d’ailleurs pas la première fois que de tels échantillons apparaissent. Le 7 octobre dernier, un compte avait publié sur Weibo des photographies de deux protections de tailles différentes, présentées comme des concepts inspirés des fuites. Plus récemment, Ice Universe avait partagé une vidéo d’un modèle décrit comme un verre de protection incurvé en 3D sur ses quatre côtés.
Ces nouveaux échantillons livrent aussi un indice important sur un autre élément de la façade : la Dynamic Island. Sa découpe semble conserver des proportions proches de celles de la version réduite apparue sur l’iPhone 18 Pro. Cela correspond aux prévisions de Ross Young, analyste spécialisé dans les écrans, qui estime que ce format devrait être maintenu jusqu’en 2027.
La Dynamic Island conserverait les dimensions de l’iPhone 18 Pro
Vous l’aurez compris, la courbure du verre serait donc la principale évolution visible sur ces prototypes. Elle pourrait cela dit compliquer la pose d’une protection intégrale car, contrairement à un accessoire destiné à une surface plane, celui-ci devrait épouser les quatre bords arrondis sans perdre son ajustement.
Une autre fuite, publiée par Fixed Focus Digital, va dans le même sens. Le leaker affirme que les futurs modèles anniversaire utiliseraient un verre comparable à celui de l’iPhone Air, mais avec des courbes plus prononcées sur chacun des côtés
Pour rappel, la marque à la pomme préparerait ces iPhone anniversaire pour l’automne 2027. Le nom iPhone 20 Pro reste encore hypothétique à l’heure où nous rédigeons ces lignes. Et si les échantillons donnent corps à la piste d’un écran incurvé, ils ne constituent pas encore une validation du design final par Apple.
Source : MacRumors

articles.title: Instagram now lets you edit your stories after you post them
articles.text:
Instagram’s latest update will allow you to edit your Stories without losing your views, likes, or replies. You can now edit the text, music, stickers, and drawings for up to 15 minutes after sharing your Story, Instagram head Adam Mosseri has announced.
Instagram now lets you edit your stories after you post them
You can edit the text, music, stickers, and drawings in your Stories for up to 15 minutes after sharing.
Reverse engineer Alessandro Paluzzi first spotted Instagram working on this feature in April, but now it’s official. Previously, you had to delete and repost your Story to fix a typo or add a song that you forgot to include.
You can edit your post by opening your Story and selecting the three-dot menu in the bottom-right corner. From there, tap “Edit Story” to start making changes.
In addition to editable Stories, Instagram announced that it’s launching new fonts, colors, and shapes for stickers, as well as presenting them on sticker sheets that are supposed to be easier to browse. The platform is also making changes to the way you select multiple photos and adding new blur, colors, and gradient background options.

articles.title: Build Training-Ready Physical AI Datasets with Two Prompts in NVIDIA Cosmos | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
World model accuracy starts with high-quality, diverse training datasets. Yet capturing rare defects, nighttime incidents, and other challenging scenarios is costly and time-consuming. Turning raw data into training-ready datasets adds complexity, particularly when using disconnected tools and manual processes for curation, labeling, generation, and evaluation.
NVIDIA technology is helping developers more easily build high-quality, diverse training datasets at scale for physical AI. NVIDIA Cosmos is an open platform of frontier models, datasets, frameworks, and skills for world model development. As part of this platform, NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory (CDF) is a collection of five cloud-native blueprints and six composable skills to accelerate data curation, processing, and synthetic data generation (SDG). Frontier AI agents can be used to orchestrate these blueprints, enabling prompt-to-data without human steering.
This post walks you through how to curate and augment datasets or create anomalous events for physical AI model training with just two prompts in Cosmos. It features five different use cases.
Set up and configure Cosmos blueprints and skills: Prompt 1
Cosmos Data Factory contains five reference blueprints for common tasks. All five blueprints run using the CDF Orchestration core skill, which coordinates workflow steps, deploys the required services, and manages execution on your cluster.
To set it up, enter the following prompt into your coding agent:
| Example prompt: “Clone the CDF Orchestration repository, then run orchestration preflight and setup.” | 
|---|
Preflight checks your environment without making changes and flags anything missing. Once those checks pass, setup prepares your environment to run the blueprints.
Run the blueprint for your training data use case: Prompt 2
This section features five training data use cases for running the blueprint, including example prompts:
- Generate driving scenarios for autonomous vehicle (AV) training
- Augment image attributes for search and re-identification
- Augment videos across weather, lighting, and environments
- Generate rare event videos for model training
- Generate defect images for visual inspection
If you already have footage or images and need to curate and add more variety, the first use case in this section covers generating driving scenarios, varying clothing attributes in person images, and transforming videos across weather, lighting, and environmental conditions. The augmentation use cases expand the variety in your existing data, but some training gaps call for creating entirely new events or defects.
Your model might need to recognize a leaking product or a defective circuit board, but your dataset may contain few examples or none. Waiting to capture enough rare cases can take years, and staging them can be dangerous or expensive. The last two use cases cover generating rare event videos and defect images from images or 3D assets to fill these gaps.
Use case 1: Generate driving scenarios for AV training
The Autonomous Vehicle Dataset Generation blueprint helps you search large databases of driving scenarios and generate novel datasets for downstream model training and validation tasks. NVIDIA Cosmos Curator extracts metadata for your video dataset inputs, and NVIDIA Cosmos Dataset Search finds relevant videos through those embeddings. The retrieved videos are passed to NVIDIA Cosmos3-Super-Image2Video style transfer, and Cosmos Evaluator checks the generated videos for physical plausibility.
| Example prompt: “Search for driving scenes similar to our input video.mp4, transform them into rainy, snowy, and foggy while preserving layout and motion, and check physical plausibility.” | 
|---|
Use case 2: Augment image attributes for search and re-identification
The Image Attribute Augmentation reference blueprint generates variations of person-crops with controlled attribute changes such as clothing type, accessories, and color. An LLM turns your selected attributes into structured modification prompts, used to generate the augmented variations of the source image. Cosmos Evaluator confirms that the requested clothing attributes appear. The blueprint then auto-labels the results with clothing attributes and search queries for person search and re-identification.
| Example prompt: “Augment the person crops in <input-bucket>, three clothing variants per person, and write the output to <output-bucket>.” | 
|---|
Use case 3: Augment videos across weather, lighting, and environments
The Video Data Augmentation reference blueprint transforms your existing footage across weather, lighting, and environmental conditions while preserving scene structure. A vision language model (VLM) describes your source video and combines that with your requested conditions into a structured prompt, which Cosmos3-Nano uses to generate the augmented variant.
Cosmos Evaluator checks each generated clip for motion artifacts that aren’t in your source, confirms that the conditions you asked for actually appear, and scores whether the motion is physically plausible. Next, the blueprint auto-labels both your source and generated videos with detection, tracking, and captions. It then provides you with a training-ready dataset.
| Example prompt: “Run video data augmentation on the videos in <input-bucket>, create 3 augmentations for yellow lighting, dim lighting and red table. Write the output to <output-bucket>.” | 
|---|
Use case 4: Generate rare event videos for model training
The Event Video Generation reference blueprint uses a source image to create videos of rare events, such as fires, falls, or shoplifting. A VLM combines its description of your scene with your requested event into a structured prompt. Cosmos3-Super-Image2Video generates the clip while preserving the source viewpoint and layout.
Cosmos Evaluator checks whether the event appears and whether motion looks physically plausible, retrying failed clips. Passing clips are auto-labeled with detections, tracks, captions, and semantic annotations for downstream training.
| Example prompt: “Run the Event Video Generation blueprint on the image in <input-bucket> to generate 3 clips: normal traffic, stalled vehicle, and collision at the intersection. Write the output to <output-bucket>.” | 
|---|
Use case 5: Generate defect images for visual inspection
The Defect Image Generation reference blueprint creates defective examples from clean inspection images or 3D USD assets of parts such as circuit boards, glass panels, or metal surfaces. For 3D assets, NVIDIA Isaac Sim renders inspection images and masks, and Qwen-Image-Edit creates realistic clean reference images, called golden images.
Cosmos 3 Super uses these images, defect masks, and your requested defect types to generate defects while preserving the surrounding part. It ships fine-tuned for printed circuit boards (PCBs), glass, and metal, with further fine-tuning skills available for other use cases. You get golden images, synthetic defect images, and manifests tracing each result to its source and generation settings.
| Example prompt: “Run the Defect Image Generation blueprint and generate shift structural defects for images in <input-bucket> with full board coverage. Write the output to <output-bucket>.” | 
|---|
How to use core agent skills and tools for specific tasks like curation, search, and labeling
The blueprints outlined in the previous section are built from six core agent skills: Auto Labeling, AnomalyGen, Augmentation, Curation and Retrieval, Simulation, and Orchestration. You can use these skills independently or combine them to build a workflow around your own data and goals.
- Auto Labeling: Turns raw video and images into annotated datasets with detection, tracking, captions and scene understanding.
- AnomalyGen: Creates realistic defect images from a handful of examples, with masks, for visual inspection.
- Augmentation: Generates visual variations of your video and images using Cosmos models, for conditions you can’t capture.
- Curation and Retrieval: Finds clips and images in a large collection, using Cosmos Curator and Cosmos Dataset Search.
- Simulation: Renders photorealistic, fully labeled images from 3D scenes using Isaac Sim and Omniverse Replicator.
- Orchestration: Runs reference blueprints on your cluster, deploying the services each one needs and scaling them.
| Example prompt: Clone the auto labeling repo https://github.com/NVIDIA/cdf-auto-labeling/tree/main. Perform video auto-labeling to label my videos at <input-bucket>. Save outputs to <output-bucket>. Use the locally deployed model at <endpoint> for VLM and LLM.  | 
|---|
For workflows focused on curation and retrieval, use Cosmos Curator to process and auto-label raw video and multimodal data, and Cosmos Dataset Search to find targeted training scenarios across large datasets. Cosmos Curator now supports multicamera video, IMU, and GPS inputs, plus initial lidar support in its sensor library. Reusable Python processing components and Managed Ray on Slurm orchestration help teams connect sensor observations, test curation strategies, and use spare GPU capacity.
Planned expansion includes additional lidar devices, radar, and other sensor types. Cosmos Dataset Search, now open source under the Apache 2.0 license, combines metadata, scene semantics, spatial relationships, and temporal behavior through multi-embedding retrieval and adaptive agentic reranking (early access). Its modular APIs and agent skills retrieve relevant video segments for training datasets or the augmentation blueprints above.
Generate training data up to 60x faster and 45x cheaper
Cosmos Data Factory skills and blueprints turn hard-to-collect training data into a compute workload you control. The NVIDIA team measured daily throughput on a cloud server with eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Series GPUs at roughly $40 per server-hour, or $960 per day, then divided daily cost by output to estimate cost per asset.
- AV dataset generation: Generates ~130 edge-case clips/day at $2.66 in GPU compute per clip, about 45x cheaper than a fleet crew costing $125 per scenario collected on the road.
- Image attribute augmentation: Augments ~42,649 annotated image pairs/day at $960/day, or $0.023 per pair, about 10x cheaper than the $0.25 average for third-party purchased data.
- Video data augmentation: Augments ~305 annotated clips/day at $3.15 per ~5-minute clip, about 7x cheaper than the $22 average we’ve paid for third-party data.
- Defect image generation: Dropped dataset assembly time from two months to one day, a 60x speedup.
- Event video generation: Generates ~384 annotated clips/day at $2.50 each and ~4 minutes per clip, creating scarce training examples of fires, fights, and falls without waiting for or recreating dangerous real incidents.
With Cosmos, training gaps become generation jobs with a measurable compute budget. Note that these figures cover compute only; source data preparation, setup, agent use, storage, and human review may add costs.
What results and projected outcomes are organizations reporting with Cosmos?
Several organizations are using Cosmos skills and blueprints to improve testing, detection, and search accuracy across autonomous vehicles, visual inspection, and robotics while targeting lower costs and effort.
- Improving recall on real-world anomalies by up to 24% with synthetic data and estimated 1,400x return on data-generation cost at an offshore oil and gas site.
- Targeting up to 85% less manual engineering effort in automated optical inspection (AOI) program generation – with 40% fewer false calls.
- Reducing repeated physical test drives by up to 90% and shortening AI regression test cycles by up to 85% (expected).
- Going to market in under two weeks with Cosmos Curator compared to an estimated six months (time required to build an equivalent pipeline in-house).
Get started with NVIDIA Cosmos
To accelerate data curation, processing, and synthetic data generation for your application, check out NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory blueprints and composable skills. Start with a blueprint that matches your use case, follow the setup guide, and use your AI agent to run the workflow with your data. Customize your pipeline with individual skills to generate high-quality, annotated training datasets.
To learn more, join us on November 19 for the livestream, Build Training-Ready Datasets in Two Prompts. Learn how to use Cosmos to curate and augment datasets for AVs, robotics, and vision AI agents. Featuring Voxel51 and Encord, the livestream will highlight how Porsche uses Cosmos Data Factory through the Voxel51 platform and how Encord worked with ANYbotics.

articles.title: WoW Forever : Blizzard suspend des comptes après l'exploitation d'un bug à 100 pièces d'or par heure
articles.text:
DansWorld of Warcraft Forever, tout coûte cher, surtout quand on n’a pas beaucoup d’or. Et le jeu n’est vraiment pas généreux quand il s’agit de donner des récompenses en validant des quêtes. Du coup, les joueurs et les joueuses courent après l’argent pour se payer la monture épique, monter leurs métiers et s’équiper décemment.
Blizzard avait déjà reconnu que l’économie du jeu posait problème. D’ici à un éventuel ajustement, les braves qui arpentent Azeroth cherchent des astuces pour se remplir les poches facilement et rapidement. En lisant des guides en ligne, en se passant des astuces, en faisant des affaires à l’hôtel des ventes… et parfois en abusant de bugs.
Il y avait justement une gruge que des petits malins avaient fini par voir : dans le Repaire des Noiregueules (Blackmaw Hold), un donjon de niveau 55 à 60, il a été découvert une salle d’une trentaine d’ennemis non élites (des monstres ordinaires, censés rapporter peu) dans laquelle on pouvait obtenir par erreur le butin d’un ennemi d’élite.
D’après les calculs du site spécialisé Wowhead, en enchaînant ces combats en boucle, il était tout à fait possible de dépasser les 100 pièces d’or par heure, et certains acharnés ont prétendu en avoir ramassé des milliers. Au regard de l’économie de WoW Forever, ces centaines ou ces mille pièces d’or constituent une vraie fortune.
Cette arnaque a existé jusqu’au week-end des 14 et 15 novembre, jusqu’au moment où Blizzard a publié un correctif pour faire sauter le bug au cours du 16 novembre.
Quelques centaines de comptes gelés
Mais le studio américain ne s’est pas arrêté là.
Dans un message publié ce mardi 17 novembre sur ses forums, Kaivax, responsable communautaire, a indiqué que les fonctions économiques des comptes de « quelques centaines de joueurs » qui avaient compris qu’il s’agissait d’un bug et farmé ces ennemis pendant des heures, c’est-à-dire tués en boucle pour amasser du butin.
Les sanctions ne s’arrêtent pas là : Blizzard est aussi en train de retirer cet or excédentaire des comptes ou de l’hôte des vente, y compris celui tiré de la revente des objets. Quant à celles et ceux qui ont vraiment trop abusé de ce bug, Blizzard a également appliqué des suspensions ponctuelles. Il n’est pas précisé si des suspensions définitives ont été décidées.
Il faut dire que la pression était forte : sous l’article de Wowhead comme sur Reddit, beaucoup réclamaient le retrait de l’or. Des internautes suspectaient même des streamers de couper leur diffusion pour farmer tranquillement, à l’abri des regards et pour éviter de partager l’astuce, et accessoirement pour ne pas attirer l’attention de Blizzard.
En revanche, ceux qui ont fait le donjon quelques fois sans rien savoir ne risquent rien.

articles.title: Fatehpuria Hygiene secures Rs 100 Cr in first equity fundraise
articles.text:
Fatehpuria Hygiene secures Rs 100 Cr in first equity fundraise
The company will use the funds to expand into more than 50 cities over the next 24 months and strengthen its warehousing, distribution and AI-enabled supply chain infrastructure.
Fatehpuria Hygiene, a trading, supply chain and fulfilment company, has raised Rs 100 crore in its first equity fundraise, led by investor Madhu Kela.
The company said it plans to use the capital to strengthen its nationwide presence and build a technology-driven supply chain ecosystem. It aims to expand into more than 50 major cities over the next 24 months and develop an AI-enabled, integrated supply chain network.
The expansion strategy will focus on strengthening warehousing infrastructure, enhancing technology capabilities, scaling distribution networks and developing end-to-end fulfilment solutions to meet the evolving requirements of brands and retail platforms.
Founded in 2017 by Gautam Fatehpuria, the company has established a warehousing, distribution and fulfilment network across 16 states. Its clientele includes Unilever, Wipro, Kimberly-Clark, Flipkart, Amazon, Myntra, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Blinkit, DMart, Meesho and FirstCry.
“Over the years, we have grown by focusing on strong execution, operational efficiency and long-term partnerships with leading brands and commerce platforms. This fundraise is an important validation of the business we have built and the opportunity ahead. We see significant potential in transforming India's supply chain ecosystem through deeper technology integration, stronger infrastructure and more efficient fulfilment capabilities,” said Gautam Fatehpuria, founder, Fatehpuria Hygiene.
“Fatehpuria Hygiene has built a strong business backed by execution capabilities, deep industry relationships and a scalable operating model. We believe the company is well-positioned to capitalise on India's growing demand for integrated, technology-led supply chain solutions,” said Madhu Kela.
As brands expand their geographical reach and adapt to changing consumer expectations, integrated warehousing, distribution and fulfilment networks are becoming increasingly important to their operations.

articles.title: HBO Max ya avisa a quienes comparten cuenta en España: o pagas el “miembro adicional” o te quedas sin servicio
articles.text:
HBO Max ha comenzado a endurecer las medidas contra las cuentas compartidas en España. El discurso no dista de lo que ya hemos visto en otras plataformas tales como Netflix o Disney +: no pasa nada si compartes, pero si lo haces que sea en la misma unidad familiar y, sino, toca pagar. Los usuarios a los que el sistema señala como residentes fuera del hogar del titular de la cuenta están viendo ahora avisos que les piden pagar por un nuevo complemento llamado "Miembro extra" si quieren seguir disfrutando del servicio. El complemento cuesta 5,99 euros al mes y conlleva varias condiciones. Bajo estas líneas te contamos todos los detalles.
Aplicando la norma. No hay nada nuevo desde el punto de vista de las políticas de HBO Max, pero es ahora cuando la medida está afectando a algunos usuarios en España. La compañía afirmaba a principios de año que introduciría límites en torno al uso de cuentas compartidas en la plataforma durante este año. Tanto los comentarios en redes sociales como nuestra experiencia propia con la plataforma sugiere que esas medidas ya han comenzado a aplicarse.
Las condiciones de HBO Max establecen que una cuenta es para el titular y las personas con las que convive. Cualquier persona que viva en otro lugar, incluso un familiar, necesita su propia suscripción o el complemento de pago, según el centro de ayuda de la compañía.
Qué están viendo los usuarios. El primer indicio parece ser una advertencia en la que se le indica al usuario que es posible que esté compartiendo su cuenta con personas ajenas a su propio hogar. Si el sistema sigue detectando ese patrón, llega un segundo mensaje que insta al usuario a suscribirse para seguir reproduciendo contenido o a verificar el dispositivo a través de un código enviado al correo electrónico del titular.
De momento todo apunta a que ninguna de las advertencias bloquea el acceso por completo, pues el sistema cuenta con cierta tolerancia. Pero nunca sabes cuándo te van a cortar el grifo del todo.
Cómo lo detecta HBO Max. La compañía afirma que determina qué dispositivos pertenecen a un hogar combinando datos de la cuenta, configuración de perfiles, datos de red e información de dispositivos, incluidas las direcciones IP, los identificadores de dispositivos y la actividad de los usuarios.
Sin embargo, no todos los inicios de sesión inusuales son penalizados. Por ejemplo, si se selecciona la opción de “Estoy viajando”, los usuarios pueden continuar reproduciendo el contenido, pero solo un número limitado de veces. Y desde BandaAncha también apuntan a que hay tolerancia con hasta dos ubicaciones, en caso de que las personas utilicen la cuenta en una segunda residencia.
Qué incluye el complemento. El complemento de miembro extra permite a un suscriptor compartir su plan con una persona que vive en otro lugar. Según el centro de ayuda de HBO Max, esa persona obtiene:
- Su propia cuenta, contraseña y un único perfil.
- Reproducción en un dispositivo a la vez.
- Las mismas características del plan que el titular de la cuenta, como 4K Ultra HD en determinados títulos si el titular tiene el plan Premium.
- La opción de heredar un perfil de adulto existente de la cuenta principal, conservando su historial de visionado y "Mi lista". Los perfiles infantiles no se pueden transferir.
La letra pequeña. Hay varios límites, como el hecho de que los miembros extra no tienen acceso a Deportes, deben ser mayores de 18 años y encontrarse en el mismo país donde se registro el titular, Solo se puede comprar un complemento por cuenta y se requiere una suscripción base.
Quién queda fuera. HBO Max afirma que el complemento solo está disponible para los suscriptores a los que factura directamente. Los clientes que pagan a través de tiendas de aplicaciones como Apple o Google, o a través de operadores de internet, móvil y televisión, no pueden comprarlo.

articles.title: Chrome 158 Patches 204 Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
Google on Tuesday announced the release of Chrome 158 to the stable channel with patches for 204 vulnerabilities, including six critical-severity bugs.
The critical flaws include three use-after-free issues in WebView, GarbageCollection, and WebAudio, out-of-bounds write defects in GPU and ANGLE, and a buffer overflow in Media.
No bug bounty reward will be paid for any of these. In fact, no reward will be handed out for 163 of the security weaknesses. Google and Xinyang Ge discovered 145 and 15 of them, respectively.
Of the remaining vulnerabilities, 62 are high-severity issues, 82 are medium-severity, and 54 are low-severity.
Google says it handed out $11,000 in rewards for five of the vulnerabilities reported by external researchers and has yet to determine the amounts to be paid for 36 flaws.
The most common type of vulnerability patched in Chrome 158 is use-after-free (51 occurrences), followed by incorrect authorization (34), missing authorization (16), out-of-bounds write/read (15), uninitialized resource (14), information leak (11), UI misrepresentation (10), improper input validation (9), and race condition (8).
Google makes no mention of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, but users are advised to update their browsers as soon as possible.
The latest Chrome iteration is now rolling out as versions 158.0.8127.36/.37 for Windows and macOS, and as version 158.0.8127.36 for Linux.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.text:
AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.
- Date:
- November 12, 2026
- Source:
- University of California - Santa Barbara
- Summary:
- Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.
The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.
Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.
"Building a model in the abstract is one thing," said Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab."
How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes
For decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.
Visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.
The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.
Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back."
The new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.
Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man
An important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.
At Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.
When researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.
Producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.
To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.
Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.
AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise
When the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.
Another important discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.
This distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.
"Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation."
The findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.
Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person
A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.
This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.
The participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.
Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.
The AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.
By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.
"A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around."
A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight
The research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration."
The project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.
Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.
Rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.

articles.title: Un tercio de los jóvenes de 15 a 22 años usa chatbots de IA como compañía, según un estudio
articles.text:
Uno de cada tres jóvenes de entre 15 y 22 años recurre a la inteligencia artificial como compañía, según un estudio de la firma de encuestas Gallup y el Digital Wellness Lab del Hospital de Niños de Boston. El informe se basa en 15.925 entrevistas realizadas en 16 países entre el 28 de mayo y el 21 de agosto.
Según Wired, el porcentaje es de 33% en el conjunto de la muestra, sube a 50% entre quienes usan IA todos los días y llega a 42% entre quienes tienen amigos que solo conocen por internet. Gallup define esa categoría como amistades con personas a las que nunca se vio en persona.
El estudio también midió otros usos. De acuerdo con 404 Media, el 82% de los encuestados usó IA para buscar información y el 68% le pidió consejo. La compañía es el uso menos frecuente de los tres. Las diferencias entre países son marcadas. En Estados Unidos, Canadá y Reino Unido, solo el 20% usa IA una vez al día o más, mientras que en Brasil lo hace casi el 40%. Japón e Italia rondan el 35%, según el mismo medio.
Más soledad entre quienes usan IA como compañía
Los investigadores observaron que los jóvenes que usan IA como compañía declaran sentirse solos con más frecuencia. Los autores advierten que los datos no permiten saber si recurren a los chatbots porque ya están solos, si la IA influye en su vida social o si otras circunstancias explican la relación.
David Bickham, director de investigación del Digital Wellness Lab, dijo a Wired que no ve el fenómeno como un déficit. “Son jóvenes que crecen en una época de IA”, explicó, y cuanto más la usan, más se involucran con su faceta social. También señaló que los jóvenes solitarios buscan conexión en los chatbots.
Andrew Dugan, investigador principal de Gallup, afirmó que no sería sorprendente que la compañía con IA se vuelva más común en los próximos cinco años. Aclaró que sigue abierta la pregunta de si los jóvenes recurren a ella por soledad o si esta puede reforzar ese sentimiento.
La calidad que los usuarios atribuyen a esa relación varía según el país. Casi la mitad de los australianos con una compañía de IA la calificó de alta calidad, frente al 12% de los jóvenes de Polonia. En la mayoría de los países predominó la calificación media, según 404 Media.
Las amistades presenciales siguen pesando más
Entre los 16 países, una mediana del 93% de los jóvenes tiene un amigo cercano en persona y el 37% tiene uno solo en línea, informó Gallup. El 41% califica de alta calidad su amistad presencial; el 26% hace lo mismo con la que mantiene solo en línea.
Gallup halló que tener una amistad presencial se asocia con mayor bienestar, algo que no ocurre con las amistades solo en línea. Quienes tienen un amigo solo en línea declaran más soledad, ansiedad y depresión moderada o grave, sin importar la calidad que le atribuyan.
Otro dato: el 72% de los jóvenes pasa su tiempo en línea viendo contenido corto, sobre todo en TikTok e Instagram, y seis de cada diez recurren a ese desplazamiento cuando se sienten solos, según 404 Media. En Estados Unidos, Instagram y Discord son dos de las plataformas más populares para hablar con amigos de internet.
En 14 de los 16 países la encuesta se hizo en línea con muestras no probabilísticas, es decir, sin selección aleatoria de los participantes. Solo en Kenia y Sudáfrica se entrevistó cara a cara con muestras representativas del país, según la metodología publicada por Gallup.

articles.title: Tesla veut produire 1 million de Cybercab par an en Allemagne, mais il reste un gros problème
articles.text:
L’annonce est tombée le 16 novembre, signée André Thierig, le patron du site : « Nous nous agrandissons ! La production du Cybercab arrive à Giga Berlin ! ». Tesla engage environ 3 milliards d’euros dans un nouveau bâtiment d’assemblage à Grünheide, près de Berlin, sa seule usine automobile européenne. Le calendrier prévoit un permis déposé avant la fin de l’année, un chantier au premier semestre 2027 et les premiers exemplaires en 2029.
Une halle deux fois plus grande que celle du Model Y
Le futur bâtiment s’étalerait sur quelque 500 000 m² au nord du site actuel, le double de la halle où naissent les Model Y. Tesla promet d’en faire « l’usine la plus avancée technologiquement au monde » de tout son réseau. L’enveloppe couvre aussi des annexes, dont une nouvelle station de traitement des eaux usées. À pleine maturité, le site assemblerait jusqu’à un million de Cybercab par an, de quoi ravir à Volkswagen et à son fief de Wolfsburg le rang de première usine automobile d’Allemagne en capacité.
L’usine a ouvert en mars 2022 sur une promesse de 500 000 voitures par an, jamais tenue : la cadence tourne aujourd’hui autour de 7 000 Model Y par semaine. Le site doit aussi lancer sa propre production de cellules de batterie au premier semestre 2027. Volkswagen, Mercedes et BMW taillent dans leurs effectifs par dizaines de milliers de postes ; quatre jours avant l’annonce de Tesla, Mercedes suspendait même tout nouvel investissement dans ses usines allemandes.
1 500 immatriculations par an pour toute l’Europe
Le Cybercab n’a ni volant ni pédales, ce qui le classe parmi les véhicules entièrement automatisés. Pour eux, le droit européen ne connaît qu’une porte : l’homologation en petites séries du règlement 2022/1426, plafonnée à 1 500 immatriculations par an et par type de véhicule pour l’ensemble de l’Union. Bruxelles promet de lever ce verrou par étapes et visait les autres usages courant 2026 ; seule la révision de mars est tombée, et elle ne concerne que le stationnement automatisé. À pleine cadence, la halle écoulerait donc en moins d’une journée de production le quota européen d’une année entière, un rapport de un à près de 700.
De l’autre côté de l’Atlantique, le Cybercab roule déjà : les courses payantes ont débuté à Austin le 3 septembre, et le registre texan des véhicules sans conducteur en recensait 573 au 10 novembre. Une poignée de clients triés sur le volet peuvent même en commander un pour 29 990 dollars, abonnement obligatoire de 299 dollars par mois compris. L’usage reste cantonné aux zones couvertes par le service. L’autorité américaine de la sécurité routière examine de son côté la manière dont Tesla a certifié un véhicule privé de volant, de pédales et de rétroviseurs.
La version supervisée du système de conduite de Tesla, rebaptisée Tesla Assisted Driving, circule déjà dans onze pays européens, et la France n’en fait pas partie. Avant qu’un Cybercab sorti de Grünheide ne vienne vous chercher en bas de chez vous, il faudra que Bruxelles réécrive son règlement et que Paris autorise, pour commencer, la simple conduite supervisée.

articles.title: „Vorhersagen abzuleiten, ist nicht gerechtfertigt“: Wie Experten den stockenden Polarwirbel und den Winter in Europa einordnen
articles.text:
Wann kommt der Winter in Europa? Experten ordnen die Folgen des langsamen Polarwirbels ein
Vom „frühen Wintereinbruch“ über den „Eiswinter“ bis hin zur „Eis-Peitsche“: Der stratosphärische Polarwirbel sorgte für aufgeregte Medienberichte und Prognosen über den Winter in Europa. Denn hoch über dem Nordpol, in rund 30 Kilometern Höhe, ist in den vergangenen Tagen etwas bisher Beispielloses passiert. Der Polarwirbel kam kurze Zeit zum Erliegen.
Wo um diese Jahreszeit eigentlich Stürme mit zunehmender Geschwindigkeit gen Osten brausen sollten, wehte nur ein schwaches Lüftchen mit etwa zwei Metern pro Sekunde – und das auch noch in Gegenrichtung. Im langjährigen Mittel lag die Geschwindigkeit des Westwindbandes Ende Oktober, Anfang November bei etwa 29 Metern pro Sekunde, der bisherige Tiefstwert lag bei etwa 11 Metern pro Sekunde.

articles.title: First Circle Capital raises $26 million to back African fintechs
articles.text:
First Circle Capital, a female-led venture capital firm focused on African fintechs, has closed its fund at $26 million, bringing fresh capital to early-stage startups building financial services across the continent.
The fund, Africa Fund I, will invest in pre-seed and seed-stage companies developing financial products, services, and technology infrastructure, particularly businesses using artificial intelligence, automation, and data to build more efficient financial services.
The International Finance Corporation (IFC), Bpifrance, Egypt’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency (MSMEDA), Axian, the Dutch Good Growth Fund, Stellar Foundation, and FSD Africa invested in the fund.
The fund’s close comes as fintech continues to attract a significant share of startup investment across Africa, even as venture capital investors become more cautious and concentrate capital in fewer transactions. African startups raised $3.42 billion in 2025, with fintech attracting $1.37 billion, accounting for 40% of total funding.
First Circle Capital is betting that the next generation of African fintech companies will emerge from problems that remain unresolved despite the growth of digital payments and lending over the past decade.
“Africa Fund I is built around a clear thesis: the next generation of African fintech leaders will be those addressing the structural challenges that continue to limit access to financial services across the continent,” Selma Ribica, co-founder and managing partner at First Circle Capital, said in a statement. “We want to identify those businesses at the earliest stages and work closely with their founders as they scale.”
Ribica, a former M-Pesa executive and fintech investor, Agnes Aistleitner, and Robert Smith founded First Circle Capital in 2021. The firm operates across Kampala, Nairobi, Casablanca, and Cape Town, with a pan-African investment mandate covering markets including Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, Uganda, Ghana, and Francophone Africa.
Its investment thesis, which it calls FinTech 2.0, focuses on insurtech, alternative lending models, interoperability and financial infrastructure, climate fintech, fintech software-as-a-service, and regulatory technology. The firm is also interested in AI-native fintech startups that build artificial intelligence and data-driven operations into their businesses from inception.
“We are particularly excited by the emergence of AI-native fintech companies,” Ribica said. “Founders now have the opportunity to build financial businesses around automation, intelligence, and software from day one, fundamentally changing the economics of delivering financial services across African markets.”
First Circle Capital says it has invested in 18 companies across African markets. Its portfolio includes TurnStay, a South African fintech building cross-border payment infrastructure for global travel merchants; Morocco-based WafR, which digitises transactions and payments through neighbourhood retailers; Scale, a card-as-a-service infrastructure company; and Orca Fraud, an AI-native fraud prevention platform for financial institutions. The firm added that it works with founders on securing follow-on funding, strategic investors, commercial partnerships, and business development opportunities
“We see a significant opportunity to back the founders addressing these challenges: making payments cheaper, expanding access to credit and insurance, strengthening fraud and risk management, improving financial operations through software, and developing innovative financial solutions for sectors such as agriculture and energy,” Aistleitner, co-founder and partner at First Circle Capital, said.
The $26 million close adds to a growing number of African-focused venture capital funds that have raised or secured new commitments this year. In August, Ventures Platform, the Nigerian venture capital firm, closed its second pan-African fund at $84 million, attracting new institutional investors including the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Norfund, Alphatron, and Ashesi University Foundation, alongside existing investors such as the IFC, British International Investment, Proparco, AfricaGrow, and Nigeria’s iDICE programme.
In October, DPI Venture Capital, Development Partners International’s venture capital platform, announced the final close of its Nclude Fund at more than $112 million. In November, Enza Capital, a multi-stage venture capital firm, announced a $21 million first close for its AI Africa Fund, targeting $60 million to invest in AI-native and AI-enabled startups across Africa.
For First Circle Capital, Africa Fund I is designed to back founders before their businesses become established players. African startups raised just $46.5 million across 281 pre-seed deals in 2025, accounting for 1.5% of total venture investment, even as the broader VC market grew by over 40%. The funding gap means early-stage founders might struggle to secure the capital needed to reach the point where larger investors are willing to back them.
“Our ambition with Africa Fund I is to build a portfolio of companies that become fundamental to how financial products are delivered across Africa,” Smith, partner and head of operations at First Circle Capital, said. “We believe the next generation of African fintech will combine deep local market understanding with increasingly sophisticated technology, including AI-native solutions that can fundamentally improve the economics and accessibility of financial services.”

articles.title: Ha entrado en vigor: los propietarios que vendan la vivienda deberán indemnizar a los inquilinos que residan en ella
articles.text:
Al vender una vivienda con inquilinos, hay que atender qué pasa con el alquiler existente. Por un lado, cambia el titular de la renta y, por otro, al comprar la vivienda, se adquieren ciertas obligaciones respecto al inquilino.
Debemos tener en cuenta la duración del contrato y el estado registral. En función de estos, puede haber que respetar el alquiler hasta cierto momento y puede ser necesario que el vendedor indemnice.
Esto viene regulado en el artículo 14 de la LAU. También existe la posibilidad de que haya que indemnizar. Esto sucede cuando el contrato es de más de 5 (o 7) años y el comprador cumple con ciertos requisitos.
Comprador debe respetar el alquiler
Los 5 primeros años (o 7 si el anterior arrendador era una persona jurídica, como por ejemplo una empresa), el nuevo dueño es sustituto del anterior arrendador. No podemos desahuciar al inquilino ni modificar unilateralmente lo que se ha firmado por el hecho de comprar el piso.
Deben contarse a partir de la fecha de inicio del contrato. Es decir que debemos respetar el tiempo que falta para llegar a los 5 (o 7) años.
En el caso de que se haya pactado un plazo mayor, la norma general es que el comprador también se vea afectado por todo el plazo. Hay una excepción en la que sí hay que indemnizar. Para ello es necesario que el comprador cumpla con los requisitos del artículo 34 de la Ley Hipotecaria (compra de buena fe y por precio a quien aparece en el Registro con facultades para transmitir, además de inscribir el derecho). No basta con que se quiera disponer de la casa.
Cuándo tiene que indemnizar el vendedor
En el caso de excepción, el comprador solo tendrá que aguantar el alquiler hasta que pasen los 5 (o 7) años. El vendedor deberá compensar al arrendatario por el tiempo restante.
La ley indica que será de una mensualidad de la renta actual por cada año que quede más allá de los 5 (o 7) años. Quien paga la indemnización que indica este artículo es el vendedor. No se trata de sumar los gastos de mudanza o relacionar el precio del alquiler con el de otra vivienda.
Por tanto, en el caso de que se firme un alquiler de 10 años y posteriormente se venda, es preciso saber si el comprador debe aguantar todo el plazo o si estamos en una situación de excepción. No basta con que la venta sea antes de tiempo.
Es importante comprobar el contrato y cómo hemos pactado con el casero. Los contratos anteriores a esta regulación siguen sometidos al régimen que les corresponda (salvo que se haya acordado una válida adaptación entre las partes).
