articles.title: Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
articles.text:
With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits.
Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
Congress is scrambling to provide legal recourse for deepfakes and online grooming.
On Tuesday, members of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hosted a hearing calling for the end of forced arbitration for online harms. Their immediate target was Roblox, which they accused of evading legal complaints about children allegedly groomed on the platform by enforcing its own forced arbitration clause against users who agreed to the terms as minors, in some cases even under the age of 10. Separately, a few blocks away, Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and Laurel Lee (R-FL) brought hotel heiress Paris Hilton to Capitol Hill to advocate for the Defiance Act, which would let victims of nonconsensual intimate deepfakes sue their creators.
“The best thing we can do in terms of enforcement is we can open up the courthouse doors,” Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO), who chairs the Judiciary subcommittee, told reporters after the Roblox hearing. “The more I see these companies evade regulations, the more I think there is nothing as powerful as a jury.” Hawley introduced a new bill with ranking member Dick Durbin (D-IL) to render arbitration agreements unenforceable for disputes over alleged child sexual exploitation or “child cyber injury,” which could include “reputational harm, mental suffering,” or death.
“The best thing we can do in terms of enforcement is we can open up the courthouse doors”
Roblox has sought to enforce its arbitration clause in lawsuits it’s facing over allegations that users were groomed on the gaming platform as minors, despite the company’s claims of protections. Roblox is facing about 180 lawsuits in a consolidated case over its alleged role in failing to protect children. Under the arbitration process, the public would not get to see legal discovery like the kind that’s come to light under recent cases against Meta. Hawley called the jury system “corruption-proof” and “an incredibly big hammer.”
Roblox has denied that it’s trying to dodge accountability. “Safety has been central to Roblox since we launched. We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat,” Roblox’s global head of public policy Nicky Jackson Colaço said in a statement. “A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company’s safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety.”
Congress has only a little more than three more weeks left in session before the end of the year, and a new Democratic majority will be sworn in come January. Republicans are expected to do their best to push through President Donald Trump’s nominees for judgeships and executive branch posts like FCC commissioner in the lame-duck session, as well as try to pass year-end bills like the National Defense Authorization Act, which often includes a range of other policy items. But some lawmakers are holding out hope that they can open up courthouses to new litigation over deepfake abuse and child predation.
Litigation has become one of the more successful ways for survivors of online harm to seek change. Congress has failed to pass many prominent child safety, privacy, and consumer protection bills, though it has begun to tackle the deepfake issue through the Take It Down Act. At the same time, attorneys general and individual plaintiffs have collected significant settlements and legal wins despite the broad scope of tech’s legal shield, Section 230. If bills like the Defiance Act or those seeking to end forced arbitration were to pass, tech companies and perpetrators of online harms could become vulnerable to a new wave of legal challenges.
“You will be amazed by how quickly the company will change its behavior once it is sued in public court”
In addition to Hawley and Durbin’s bill about forced arbitration, Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Katie Britt (R-AL), and Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced a similar bill with a slightly different approach, including explicitly covering data privacy violations. At the Roblox hearing, Northwestern University law professor Myriam Gilles, an expert on forced arbitration, said she’s testified before Congress many times on this topic, but “never expected to come before this body to talk about its use against 9 year olds.” Passing either proposal, she said, would have a profound impact. “You will be amazed by how quickly the company will change its behavior once it is sued in public court.”
The Defiance Act would let victims of nonconsensual intimate deepfakes sue their creators for damages, in an attempt to raise the cost of creating these kinds of images. Hilton visited Washington earlier this year to share how an intimate non-deepfake video of her at age 19 shared without her consent impacted her life, and she used her story to advocate for the Defiance Act. At Tuesday’s press conference, she said she would come back to Congress as many times as necessary for the bill to become law. “Some people might have thought that was the end of my fight,” Hilton said. “But when I make a promise to survivors, I keep it.”
Hilton said over 50 million people have been victimized by sexually explicit deepfakes. “For me personally, strangers have created over 100,000 AI-generated explicit images and videos portraying me in the most graphic and disturbing ways imaginable,” Hilton said. “If this can happen to someone with my resources and my platform, imagine how powerless a young girl might feel facing this completely alone.”
Hilton’s comments were followed by Elliston Berry, an advocate who said a classmate made an explicit deepfake image of her friend group “from an innocent social media post” when she was 14, and distributed it throughout her school. “In a matter of seconds, my sense of security disappeared,” she said. “For me, the Defiance Act means recognition that victims deserve to be heard, that their experience matters, and that their right to seek justice should not depend on how quickly technology advances.”

articles.title: 'Enterprises need to connect AI to the right data': Report finds over half of firms have abandoned AI projects over unclear goals
articles.text:
'Enterprises need to connect AI to the right data': Report finds over half of firms have abandoned AI projects over unclear goals
AI deployments are failing because of this reason
- Half of enterprises have abandoned agentic AI projects due to poor ROI
- Most organizations already have AI policies in place and trust AI's outputs
- Two in three have already seen moderate or significant AI overspending despite having budgets
Half (54%) of enterprises have abandoned their agentic AI projects due to unclear business value – but new data from SnapLogic blames poor ROI on data foundations and not AI capabilities.
One in two IT decision-makers feel pressured to continue investing in AI agents, often from top-down organizational pressures, but a similar number (48%) struggle or expect to struggle to see the desired outcomes.
SnapLogic's message is that enterprises may be ready to experiment with AI, but their technical readiness isn't up to speed, and it could all be down to data quality.
Enterprises are deploying agentic AI before they're ready
Some of the initial work is already being done – while previous studies have slated companies for not having a clear direction, this report reveals that 93% of enterprises have established their own AI agent policies and governance frameworks.
These policies are enabling overall deeper usage, with three in four (77%) admitting their AI agents have, or would have, full or extensive access to data and business systems to make them as effective as possible. Nine in 10 respondents also say they trust, or would trust, agentic AI outputs.
Speed of adoption could be one of the biggest inhibitors or ROI, though, because one-third (36%) now admit AI investment is progressing faster than their ability to actually govern the AI systems. Two-thirds (64%) have already seen moderate or significant overspending in this category even though 88% say they have clearly defined agentic budgets.
"Organizations are putting the governance, infrastructure, and investment in place to scale AI agents, but those foundations alone do not guarantee business outcomes," CTO Jeremiah Stone wrote.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
"Enterprises need to connect AI to the right data, applications, and workflows while gaining greater visibility into performance and cost to turn AI investment into measurable value."
The message is clear – businesses have rushed into deploying AI agents before they're technically ready, causing them to overspend to try and catch up. Looking ahead, those who succeed will likely be the ones to scale back spend and invest more time and consideration into their overall strategy, including solid data foundations.

articles.title: Ohne Explosion zum Schwarzen Loch? Forschende entdecken möglichen zweiten Entstehungsweg
articles.text:
Schwarze Löcher: Neue Studie findet Hinweise auf Entstehung ohne Supernova
Schwarze Löcher sind eines der großen Mysterien des Weltalls und deshalb Forschungsobjekt zahlreicher Studien. Ein Team von Astrophysiker:innen der Caltech-Universität in Kalifornien hat sich mit der Frage nach dem Ursprung Schwarzer Löcher befasst – und fand Hinweise, dass wir unser Wissen über ihre Entstehung zumindest erweitern müssen.
Die Studie wurde am 10. November in der Fachzeitschrift Physical Review D veröffentlicht. Die Caltech berichtet in einer Pressemitteilung über die Ergebnisse.
Erst Supernova, dann Schwarzes Loch? Nicht unbedingt
Bislang galt als sicher, dass Schwarze Löcher immer dann entstehen, wenn ein Stern stirbt, sein Kern in sich zusammenfällt und die Stoßwellen dieses Kernkollapses die äußere Hülle des Sterns zum Ausdehnen und schließlich zum Explodieren bringen. Kurz: bei einer Supernova. Ein Schwarzes Loch bildet sich dann an der Stelle, an der zuvor der Sternenkern kollabiert ist.
Neue Forschungsergebnisse liefern Hinweise, dass Schwarze Löcher aber auch beim Ausbleiben einer Supernova entstehen können. Also dann, wenn ein sterbender Stern nicht explodiert, sondern implodiert.
Neue Hinweise dank Gravitationswellen-Daten von über 300 Kollisionen
Basierend auf Daten des Laser-Interferometer-Gravitationswellen-Observatoriums (Ligo) der National Science Foundation, mit denen 2015 erstmals Gravitationswellen nachgewiesen werden konnten, „die von zwei kollidierenden Schwarzen Löchern ausgingen“, wurden weitere Kollisionen dieser Art untersucht. In Zusammenarbeit mit dem Virgo-Detektor in Italien und dem Kamioka-Gravitationswellendetektor (Kagra) in Japan konnten seither über 300 weitere Kollisionen Schwarzer Löcher beobachtet werden.
Den Wissenschaftler:innen fiel dabei auf: „Die überwiegende Mehrheit der verschmelzenden Schwarzen Löcher im Universum hat etwa die zehnfache Masse unserer Sonne“, sagt Katerina Chatziioannou, Physikprofessorin der Caltech und Mitglied des Ligo-Teams. „Aber warum sind Schwarze Löcher mit beispielsweise 14 Sonnenmassen so selten?“ Das Team vermutet, dass verschiedene physikalische Prozesse bei der Entstehung Schwarzer Löcher ihre Größe beeinflusst.
Kleine und große Schwarze Löcher drehen unterschiedlich: Was das über ihren Ursprung aussagt
Auch bei der Rotationsgeschwindigkeit der Schwarzen Löcher gibt es Unterschiede. Diese soll ebenfalls davon abhängen, wie genau das jeweilige Phänomen entstanden ist. Auffallend ist, dass sich die häufig auftretenden kleineren Schwarzen Löcher anders drehen als ihre selteneren großen Geschwister.
„Unsere Daten deuten darauf hin, dass diese Gruppe Schwarzer Löcher einen gemeinsamen Ursprung haben könnte – sie könnten eine besondere Unterpopulation darstellen, die nicht zur Supernova wurde“, so die Co-Autorin der Studie.
Warum weitere Forschung nötig ist
In der Theorie ist die Idee des Schwarzen Lochs ohne vorangegangene Supernova schon länger gut gestützt. Das Team der Caltech wollte überprüfen, „ob diese Idee mit den Gravitationswellendaten übereinstimmt“. Das tut sie. Die Wissenschaftler:innen betonen jedoch, dass weitere Forschung dringend nötig ist, vor allem da der Nachweis der Entstehung ohne Supernova schwierig zu erbringen sei.
„Wir können in den Himmel schauen und versuchen, historische Aufzeichnungen massereicher Sterne zu untersuchen, die nicht explodiert sind. Das ist jedoch schwierig, da sie einfach verschwinden, ohne zu explodieren, und einen dunklen Fleck am Himmel hinterlassen.“
Da Schwarze Löcher jedoch in „einigen der extremsten Umgebungen des Universums“ entstehen, sei es sehr aufregend, neue Hinweise auf ihre Entstehungsprozesse zu entdecken.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI is Rockstar at its best and most frustrating
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI feels both refreshingly new and stuck in the past.
On the one hand, Rockstar’s long-running open-world crime franchise has finally grown up thanks to a more mature and emotionally-charged narrative. But on the other hand, some dated mechanics and mission design make the experience drag in places. Still, it’s a remarkable accomplishment that’s greater than the sum of its parts — the sort that certainly none but Rockstar could make.
Above all else, GTA VI succeeds on the strength of its leads. It’s a sweeping 60-hour Bonnie & Clyde-style epic that focuses on veteran-turned-drug runner Jason Duval and gig worker and recent inmate Lucia Caminos. Notably, the latter is the series’ first non-optional female protagonist, and she is every bit the star as Jason. In fact, she’s easily the more compelling of the two.
Where Jason can sometimes feel overly stoic and passive, Lucia is vivacious, determined and thoughtful. An early mission, which lets you see what led to her incarceration, depicts her as a sympathetically desperate lead who you want to root for even as she continues to make questionable life choices. All the while, her actress, who I wasn’t permitted to reveal per (excessive) embargo restrictions even though she was just nominated for a Game Award, delivers a wonderfully charismatic and effortlessly naturalistic performance.
It’s through Jason and Lucia that Rockstar’s noted Red Dead Redemption II inspirations are most pronounced, with GTA VI‘s dense five-chapter structure really allowing you to fully live with the duo. In between their criminal exploits in the main missions, you’ll be able to take on pretty much every activity in the sprawling Florida-inspired state of Leonida with both characters. This includes everything from intense bank robberies (more on those later) to minigames like mini golf and billiards and even simply sitting on the couch and chatting.
As I guide Jason and Lucia through their daily routines, they truly feel like living, breathing people. The way that they lean in for a passionate kiss or playful love tap. The way that they work out together, cheering each other on as they power through gruelling reps, before sharing two protein shakes for recovery. The way that watching TV or taking a shower can sometimes spontaneously turn into lovemaking.
The GTA games have always been about satirical deconstructions of the so-called “American Dream,” but getting to inhabit Jason and Lucia so intimately during their everyday lives makes those themes more meaningful than ever. It’s so effective, in fact, that I sometimes found that the main story was getting in the way of that lovely dynamic. For one, the supporting cast of characters is largely disposable, the sorts of thinly written caricatures you encountered in previous games. Take Jason’s old friend Dre’Quan; I spent so many missions helping him with his nightclub business, yet there’s nothing more to him or their relationship. Similarly, Jason’s boss, Brian, is just a generic drug runner whose only memorable quality is that there’s a great character actor playing him.
GTA VI can get so caught up in some of these subplots that it occasionally loses sight of the main driving force behind the narrative. At a certain point, the story can feel meandering, taking numerous detours from Jason and Lucia’s end goal — which I’m also not allowed to reveal — in favour of forgettable side characters. This can feel even more like a slog during extensive walk-and-talk sequences where your character simply moves forward at an incredibly glacial pace while someone else is chatting with them. The worst example of this, a mission that is structurally similar to several others, consisted largely of me escorting a whiny rich guy around a packed nightclub as Jason. Outside of one series of shootouts at the end, this was it — walking back and forth at a snail’s pace. “Cinematic,” sure, but not exactly engaging.
This relative lack of interactivity also pops up in some of the bigger setpieces. During one bank heist mission, moments of gunplay would be interspersed with quick cutscenes of characters moving locations or police entering the building. And in another infiltration mission, I watched a cutscene in which characters prepared a zipline before I was prompted to hold down on the stick to rappel down, only for a second cutscene to play immediately after. These constant cinematics are frustrating; yes, the game is undeniably stunning to behold, but I would like to actually play some more of these moments myself. If nothing else, the campaign does come together rather beautifully in its final stretch, which is refreshingly tighter and more stirring. I just wish the lead-up to get there felt better paced.
But of course, many people likely won’t even “roll credits” on GTA VI, and if they do, it will be over a much more stretched-out period than I had for this review. Indeed, this being an open-world game means that scores of players will sink countless hours into exploring Leonida without touching much, if any, of the story, and thankfully, that experience is a resounding success. It’s here that you get glorious, unfettered freedom, a welcome reprieve from the sometimes painfully on-rails moment-to-moment gameplay of the campaign.
From the lively, bustling streets of the Miami-esque Vice City to the sweltering flooded grasslands of the Everglades-inspired Grassrivers, GTA VI features easily one of the densest and most exquisitely detailed open worlds of all time. (Even if, rather glaringly, the game feels bizarrely out of time in how it completely refuses to even touch on the modern Trumpian climate of the U.S. in any real way outside of some cartoonish NPCs who will yell the kind of hateful language you’d hear from your average Fox News viewer.)
If anything, GTA VI really comes to life through its economy system. For various main and side missions, you’ll sometimes need a certain amount of money to progress, but how you obtain that is entirely up to you. Do you want to sneak into a trailer park and snatch some drugs from a local dealer for quick, low-risk cash? If you’re feeling a need for speed, you could always jack a high-value car and return it to a wanted buyer. Or maybe you want to do something safer and more law-abiding, like helping a farmer with his crop by flying a miniplane to hose down his fields.
But my favourite activities, without question, are heists. You start off small, only being able to rob convenience stores, pawn shops and similar small businesses. But over time, you’ll gain new equipment like sticky bombs for safes and special lights to counter marked bills that allow you to tackle bigger hits like banks. Here, the Jason and Lucia dynamic truly sings, with one of them handling crowd control while the other tries to grab as much cash as possible.
This is also where the laborious Red Dead Redemption 2-style animations actually enhance the experience, creating a rich sense of tension as your character slowly loads stacks of cash one-by-one into a duffel bag as your partner anxiously calls on you to hurry up because the police are on their way to catch you. It creates an electrifying risk-reward element, challenging you to weigh when enough is enough — whether you sneak out earlier with a smaller haul for a potentially clean getaway or dare to take more and end up facing the cops guns a-blazing.
These heists lead to some truly dynamic sequences that make full use of the meticulously crafted open-world. In fact, one of my favourite GTA VI memories so far stems from what I thought would be a simple bank robbery in Vice City. Strapped for cash, I risked having Lucia stay longer in the vault to nab some extra dough, much to Jason’s chagrin. After I finally loaded all of the bags and handed one to Jason to better manage the load, we rushed outside to our getaway vehicle just as police arrived and started shooting at us. But because I waited too long, the cops had set up roadblocks that funnelled us to a pier area, forcing us to abandon our ride and hide in a mini yacht.
Unfortunately, it moved slower than molasses, so the Coast Guard quickly discovered us, leaving us to mow down a nearby police cruiser and steal that. To escape the large police search radius, I frantically steered us to the next landmass, which I soon realized was a small rich person’s island completely disconnected from land. Amid police radio chatter saying they tracked the stolen vehicle to this island, we snuck around the guards and found a ferry, ultimately taking us to the mainland where I was able to use my phone to hail a ride to a contact where I could fence the stolen cash for a huge profit. Naturally, we ended the day with a well-earned night of R&R at the crib. All in all, it was an absolutely thrilling experience, and one that came organically from me reacting on the fly to the game’s intricate open-world design and wanted systems.
Those highs are ultimately what define my 80-plus hours with GTA VI. The larger story could be uneven, but it’s that relationship between Jason and Lucia that I came to really love. From the quiet moments of them going about their days to their pulse-pounding, action-packed criminal escapades, I couldn’t get enough of seeing these two together. And with Leonida itself being such a phenomenal setting, I can’t wait to keep going back for many more years to come.
GTA VI launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19.
Image credit: Rockstar Games

articles.title: Essai Linktour Alumi : j'ai conduit la voiture sans permis qui ne joue pas les voiturettes
articles.text:
Sur le marché de la voiture sans permis électrique, deux marques servent de repères. Citroën vend son Ami à 8 190 €, avec un habitacle réduit au strict minimum. En face, Aixam, le spécialiste historique, demande 13 999 € pour une e-City Pack. Linktour veut se glisser entre les deux avec l’Alumi, lancée en France le 16 juin 2026 par cette filiale de Shandong Weiqiao Pioneering, un groupe chinois du textile, de l’énergie et de l’aluminium.
Lors d’une présentation à Paris à laquelle Numerama a été conviée, la marque s’est présentée comme le « premium accessible » du segment. C’est à cette occasion que j’ai pu prendre le volant des deux versions de la gamme Linktour.
Commençons par un petit rappel des forces en présence. Il y a d’abord l’Alumi de base qui est un quadricycle léger (catégorie L6e). En raison de sa réglementation, cette version est bridée à 45 km/h et se destine ainsi aux jeunes automobilistes qui peuvent la conduire dès 14 ans avec le permis AM. Au-dessus, on trouve l’Alumi Elite, qui bascule dans la catégorie des quadricycles dits lourds (catégorie L7e). Pour la conduire, il faut le permis B1, accessible dès 16 ans, et il est possible de rouler avec sur le périphérique.
Côté autonomie, Linktour annonce 120 km pour la première et 180 km pour la seconde, selon le cycle WMTC, la norme d’homologation des deux-roues et des quadricycles. La recharge se fait sur une prise domestique (AC), en 4h pour l’Alumi et 4h30 pour l’Elite. Sans surprise, il n’existe pas de recharge rapide (DC) sur ce genre de voiture.
La Linktour Alumi fait oublier la voiturette
L’Alumi ne mesure que 2,69 mètres de long, et pourtant on y trouve étonnamment beaucoup de place. L’accès à bord est facilité par de grandes portes (sans encadrement s’il-vous-plaît), tandis que la cabine est capable d’accueillir deux grands gabarits sans que les deux se gênent ou se sentent étriqués.
Pour parfaire l’habitabilité, le coffre offre un volume très généreux de 320 litres, engloutissant pas mal d’affaires. Les grandes vitres et le toit panoramique (de série dès l’entrée de gamme) offrent une excellente visibilité, ce qui fait vraiment la différence en ville. Par ailleurs, on ne sent pas tout petit face aux autres véhicules sur la route, renforçant cette sensation de « vraie » voiture et qui rassure les occupants.
Surtout, la présentation intérieure fait toute la différence face à l’Ami et consorts grâce à des matériaux plutôt flatteurs pour le segment, toutes proportions gardées. En revanche, j’ai trouvé qu’il manquait un vrai rangement entre les deux sièges. J’aurais bien vu un bac de rangement histoire de poser un petit sac. Il y a bien un espace au-dessus de la planche de bord, mais il n’est pas très profond et les affaires peuvent aussi se balader pendant la conduite.
Facile à conduire en ville
Au volant, l’Alumi se conduit facilement, même sans direction assistée sur la version L6e. C’est seulement lors des manoeuvres qu’il faudra sortir un peu les muscles, mais une fois en mouvement l’effort est bien moindre. Le moteur électrique (8 ch sur l’Alumi, 14 ch sur l’Elite) permet de suivre le flot de la circulation avec réactivité, et on ne se traîne pas au démarrage d’un feu rouge. Naturellement, le gabarit permet de se faufiler entre les voitures sans encombre, par exemple lorsqu’un carrefour est complètement bouché.
Point notable, l’insonorisation est plutôt soignée et le système audio est correct. Le gros bémol au niveau de la conduite est finalement la faiblesse du freinage régénératif. Il est d’ailleurs tellement peu prononcé sur la version sans permis qu’on fait quasiment de la roue libre au lever de pied.
Côté construction, Linktour a choisi un châssis en aluminium au lieu du châssis tubulaire habituel, et la carrosserie est vissée plutôt que collée. Remplacer un élément abîmé devrait donc être plus simple (j’y reviens un peu plus bas).
Une voiture déjà bien équipée
La version sans permis de la Linktour Alumi démarre à 10 690 €, soit 2 500 € de plus qu’une Ami. Sur le papier, l’Alumi offre bien plus d’autonomie que l’Ami pour un prix inférieur à celui d’une Aixam, laquelle n’est pas plus endurante non plus. Pour la version Elite de l’Alumi, l’ABS et le droit au périphérique justifient une bonne partie des 4 000 € d’écart avec la version de base.
À 10 690 €, l’Alumi standard (sans permis) embarque de série les vitres électriques, un compteur numérique de 5 pouces et un chauffage simple. On trouve Apple CarPlay et Android Auto, une caméra de recul, un grand écran central de 10,25 pouces à partir de la finition intermédiaire Plus à 12 690 €. Sur la version haut de gamme Pro à 13 690 €, l’Alumi gagne la climatisation, le chauffage à deux niveaux (au lieu d’un), le volant multifonctions et un port USB-C 60W.
Dès 14 990 €, l’Alumi Elite (avec permis) reprend la dotation du modèle de base et ajoute notamment l’ABS, le démarrage sans clé ainsi que la direction assistée. Enfin, pour 16 990 €, le niveau Elite + hérite des équipements de la version Plus de l’Alumi sans permis.
| Modèle | Catégorie | Permis | Autonomie | Prix | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Linktour Alumi | L6e | AM (14 ans) | 120 km | 10 690 € | 
| Linktour Alumi Elite | L7e | B1 (16 ans) | 180 km | 14 690 € | 
| Citroën Ami | L6e | AM (14 ans) | 75 km | 8 190 € | 
| Aixam e-City Pack | L6e | AM (14 ans) | 75 km | 13 999 € | 
Un réseau encore en construction
Linktour dit avoir trouvé une centaine de clients depuis juin. 90 % des immatriculations concernent la version L6e (sans permis), et c’est la finition la plus haut de gamme qui se vend le mieux. La marque mise également sur la catégorie L7e, un marché qui va « exploser » nous explique un porte-parole. Et l’Alumi a une la place à prendre : Renault a arrêté la vente de son Mobilize Duo au 1er janvier 2026. Linktour vise aussi les flottes d’entreprise et les auto-écoles. Une auto-école du Loiret va justement servir d’ambassadrice. Une version cabriolet et des versions utilitaires, avec plus d’espace de chargement, sont prévues.

articles.title: Zipline hires Uber executive to lead African expansion
articles.text:
Zipline has appointed Uber executive Anthony le Roux as its Head of Operations for Africa, effective January 2027, as the autonomous delivery company expands its distribution network through government partnerships across the continent.
le Roux, who has spent 13 years at Uber, will oversee a planned rollout of at least 20 distribution centres, known as “nests,” over two years.
His appointment comes as Zipline embarks on its biggest expansion in Africa. Executing that growth strategy will mean overcoming complex airspace approvals, unreliable off-grid power infrastructure, and sovereign payment risks while scaling its AI-powered medical delivery network across key markets, including Nigeria and Côte d’Ivoire.
le Roux told TechCabal that the company has signed agreements covering 10 centres in Côte d’Ivoire, with additional locations under negotiation. Le Roux declined to identify prospective markets before negotiations were concluded.
“What we’ve formally announced and have been formally agreed upon is 9 new nests as our distribution centres, and that’s in Côte d’Ivoire,” he said in an interview on Friday, November 13.
Zipline describes the nest distribution programme as its largest African buildout yet. The company projects that its expanded services will reach more than 130 million people, serve 20,000 health facilities and delivery sites, and support more than 800 jobs.
From Uber to aircraft
le Roux joined Uber in 2013 as general manager in Cape Town before moving to Warsaw to lead businesses across Eastern Europe. He later became regional general manager for the Middle East and Africa, based in Dubai.
In 2020, he helped build the high-capacity vehicle business that became Uber Group Transportation, an enterprise he led until his departure.
His move to Zipline follows several years working abroad, including five years based in Amsterdam. Earlier in his career, he worked in investment banking and spent a year living in Lagos.
le Roux acknowledged that aviation and fixed logistics infrastructure would present new challenges. However, he argued that building local teams, managing physical operations and navigating regulation were transferable skills.
“There’s an enormous operational component to every Uber business that you’re seeing on the ground,” he said.
Caitlin Burton, CEO of Zipline Africa and Emerging Markets, said le Roux’s operational experience would be important to delivering the expansion.
“He has a proven track record of scaling transformative technologies in Africa and beyond,” Burton said in a statement.
Zipline will prioritise markets combining meaningful population density, gaps in existing logistics infrastructure and supportive government partners, according to le Roux.
The planned network will initially focus on delivering medical supplies, including blood and essential medicines, embedding Zipline’s services within national healthcare systems. The company is already working with the Rwandan and Nigerian governments to integrate its drone delivery infrastructure into public health supply chains, partnerships that provide a foundation for its broader expansion across African markets.
“Without strong government support and backing, that’s just not going to be a feasible product to go and launch,” he said.
le Roux said Zipline could deploy the planned centres within two years, drawing on its existing African operating experience. Whether the total ultimately exceeds 20 will depend on what governments agree to commission.
For Côte d’Ivoire, he said the company already had an agreed rollout schedule. His responsibility would include delivering facilities on time, to specification and within agreed costs.
He did not provide detailed information about aviation approvals or ongoing regulatory discussions.
Healthcare first, diversification next
Medical deliveries will remain the backbone of Zipline’s African expansion, but the company is considering opportunities to carry other products once infrastructure is operational. Its broader offering already includes food, groceries and medicine.
le Roux also pointed to potential expansion in Rwanda using a different delivery system better suited to grocery-style services. However, he did not confirm a commercial rollout or provide a timeline.
Diversification, he said, is central to reducing Zipline’s dependence on government contracts. Making its delivery network integral to national healthcare systems could help sustain demand, while expanding into more countries would spread its market exposure. The company also plans to use its existing infrastructure to serve additional sectors and generate new revenue.
“Once we have the infrastructure to carry out medical and blood deliveries, we’ll obviously look at other opportunities to use that existing infrastructure to diversify revenue streams into other areas,” le Roux said. “That will help make the business model more robust and sustainable.”
But the commercial case remains untested in the details. Le Roux did not disclose delivery costs, revenue targets or the profitability thresholds needed to make the expanded model sustainable.
He added that he was recruiting three senior executives to lead deployment, service delivery and logistics, with a particular focus on talent from Africa or already operating on the continent.
According to him, local teams would handle most daily operations and pointed to Zipline’s engineering presence in Rwanda as evidence of its existing technical footprint.
“I’m looking very specifically for talent from the continent or on the continent because I want people who know how to operate across Africa,” le Roux said. “There’s such phenomenal talent that we’re speaking to as we’re going through this. I’m really excited. We’re going to get absolute world-class African operators to go and help us execute this.”

articles.title: 178 große Webseiten mit Malware infiziert: Was du wissen musst, wenn du eine von ihnen besucht hast
articles.text:
178 große Webseiten mit Malware infiziert: Was du wissen musst, wenn du eine von ihnen besucht hast
Die Cybersecurity-Expert:innen von Report URI haben einen Angriff auf einige der größten Webseiten entdeckt. Dazu zählen etwa die Seiten von Zoom, Salesforce, GitLab, Ikea, Asos, CNN, BBC, Fox News sowie Virgin Media. Insgesamt waren 178 Unternehmen und deren Webauftritte vom Angriff betroffen. Diese Webseiten haben gemein, dass sie das Marketing-Tool Optimizely nutzen.
Malware-Angriff über Optimizely: So gelang Schadcode auf die Webseiten
Mit dem Tool können verschiedene Varianten der Seiten in A/B‑Tests analysiert werden. Anhand der gesammelten Daten können Betreiber:innen ihre Seiten anpassen und so etwa die Interaktion mit bestimmten Elementen wie Werbung optimieren. Leider wurde dieses Tool jetzt zum Einfallstor für Malware. Die Seiten selbst wurden nicht direkt von Cyberkriminellen angegriffen oder kompromittiert.
Laut Report URI machten sich die Angreifer:innen JavaScript zunutze. Optimizely gibt ein Javascript-Snippet an jede:n Besucher:in einer Webseite heraus, über das bestimmte Inhalte der Seite verändert und Daten gesammelt werden. In dem Javascript-Snippet gibt es eine optionale Zeile namens „ProjectJS“, über die Kund:innen von Optimizely eigenen Code in die A/B-Test-Projekte integrieren können.
Die Angreifer:innen haben sich auf bisher unbekannte Weise Zugriff auf diese Zeile verschafft und dort eigenen Schadcode eingefügt. Der Rest des Javascript-Snippets blieb unverändert. Da die Änderung zentral auf den Servern von Optimizely stattfand, wurden die veränderten Code-Zeilen an zahlreiche Kund:innen des Unternehmens ausgerollt. Denkbar wäre, dass es eine Sicherheitslücke im System von Optimizely gab oder Login-Daten gestohlen wurden, durch die Unbefugte so weitreichende Änderungen durchführen konnten.
Was Betroffene nach der Optimizely-Attacke tun müssen
Sobald User:innen die infizierte Webseite aufgerufen hatten, wurden die Javascript-Datei und damit auch der Schadcode geladen. Insgesamt hatten die Angreifer:innen dabei vier Ziele. Zunächst hat das Skript Adressen von Krypto-Wallets auf den Endgeräten aufgespürt und sie mit den Adressen der Angreifer:innen ausgetauscht. Das passierte etwa in Notizen, Links und in der Zwischenablage. Laut Report URI gibt es schon mehrere gemeldete Fälle, in denen das geklappt hat, und insgesamt mehr als 7.000 US-Dollar entwendet wurden.
Das zweite Ziel waren Kreditkartendaten. Das Skript hat nach Kartennummern, Ablaufdaten und Sicherheitscodes auf den Geräten gesucht und diese dann über Umwege an die Angreifer:innen übermittelt. Ebenso wurden Cookies gestohlen und Screenshots übermittelt. Zu guter Letzt wurden auf iPhones und iPads die Exploit-Kits Coruna und Darksword geladen. Auch deren Ziele bestehen darin, Daten und Krypto-Währung zu stehlen.
Mittlerweile müssen Nutzer:innen keine Angst mehr haben, die gelisteten Seiten aufzurufen. Die infizierten Snippets wurden entfernt. Wer am 16. November 2026 eine der Seiten besucht hat, sollte dennoch Vorsichtsmaßnahmen ergreifen. Report URI empfiehlt, alle iOS- und iPadOS-Geräte auf die aktuelle Version zu aktualisieren. So können die Exploit-Lücken geschlossen werden. Zudem sollten End-User:innen ihre Krypto-Transfers und Kreditkartenabbuchungen im Blick behalten, um Unstimmigkeiten schnell zu erkennen und zu stoppen.
Betroffene Unternehmen sollen laut Report URI jedes Optimizely-Projekt öffnen und dort den fremden Code aus der „Project Javascript-„Zeile entfernen. Im Anschluss sollten die Zugriffsrechte für den Optimizely-Account überprüft und Login-Daten im Zweifel erneuert werden. Sollten Unternehmen in ihren Website-Formularen Kreditkartendaten abfragen, sollten Eingaben vom 16. November als gestohlen behandelt werden. Dementsprechend sollten Unternehmen überlegen, diese Informationen und mögliche Schutzmaßnahmen auch an ihre Kund:innen weiterzugeben.

articles.title: Instagram vai combater vídeos copiados até quando IA mudar imagens
articles.text:
O Instagram começou a implementar ferramenta para ajudar criadores de conteúdo a identificar e combater cópias de seus vídeos. O recurso permite revisar publicações duplicadas, ocultar reproduções não autorizadas ou direcionar o público à postagem original. A plataforma também trabalha em mecanismos para detectar casos mais difíceis de identificar, como piadas e roteiros copiados com imagens recriadas por inteligência artificial (IA).
Batizada de Content Protection (Proteção de Conteúdo, em tradução livre), a novidade aparece na área de estatísticas dos criadores. Por lá, os usuários podem consultar cópias de seus vídeos e decidir o que fazer com cada uma delas.
Em publicação no Threads, Adam Mosseri, chefe do Instagram, confirmou que a distribuição começou nesta semana. Segundo ele, os criadores poderão ocultar uma cópia ou adicionar um link que leve diretamente ao conteúdo original.
A iniciativa busca dar mais controle aos produtores de conteúdo sobre a circulação de seus trabalhos na rede social, especialmente em cenário no qual a IA facilita a reprodução e a transformação de materiais publicados por outras pessoas.
Leia mais:
- Facebook e Instagram podem ganhar limite de duas horas para adolescentes nos EUA
- Entenda por que sua busca no Instagram retorna mensagem sobre abuso sexual infantil
- Instagram começa a testar vídeos longos e horizontais no Brasil
Instagram quer identificar cópias disfarçadas com IA
O combate às cópias mais difíceis de reconhecer é um dos próximos objetivos da plataforma. Mosseri afirmou que a empresa trabalha para identificar conteúdos que reproduzem elementos de outras publicações, mesmo quando a aparência visual é modificada.
Um exemplo citado pelo executivo envolve pessoas que copiam roteiros ou piadas de outros criadores e usam IA para substituir as imagens do vídeo. Nesse caso, uma comparação visual simples pode não ser suficiente para identificar a reprodução.
Mosseri reconheceu que o sistema não conseguirá acertar em todos os casos inicialmente, mas afirmou que a empresa pretende aprimorá-lo rapidamente.
Como funciona a proteção de conteúdo do Instagram
- A Content Protection permite que criadores analisem cópias de seus vídeos diretamente na área de estatísticas do Instagram;
- Depois de identificar uma reprodução, o usuário pode optar por ocultá-la ou adicionar um link para a publicação original;
- A ferramenta começou a ser disponibilizada nesta semana, mas o Instagram ainda trabalha em melhorias para ampliar a capacidade de identificação de conteúdos copiados;
- A proposta é tornar a proteção mais abrangente, acompanhando também formas de reprodução que não preservam necessariamente as imagens, mas reutilizam elementos criativos de outros usuários.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Human Posts Beat AI Slop
articles.text:
This article is crossposted from IEEE Spectrum’s careers newsletter. Sign up now to get insider tips, expert advice, and practical strategies, written in partnership with tech career development company Parsity and delivered to your inbox for free!In one year, the number of developers working for themselves has more than doubled. Stack Overflow’s annual survey of more than 30,000 developers showed that freelancers and sole proprietors went from about four percent of respondents to ten percent.
You can read this as a polite way of saying, “I got laid off and I’m figuring it out.” But I don’t think the number can be ignored.
Whatever the case, it leads to the question I keep hearing from engineers right now: What can I do to stay employable? One tried and true answer is to build a personal brand.
But what does that actually mean?
Over the last six years, I grew my LinkedIn audience to 40,000 followers and YouTube channel to 10,000. I don’t think you should aim to be famous (unless you’re into that sort of thing) but I do think it’s worth exploring how to be discoverable online in 2027 if you want an advantage in the open market.
A personal brand is a discovery mechanism
Strip away the follower counts and the AI-generated thought leadership, and a personal brand comes down to a simple question: Does the internet know who you are? When a hiring manager goes looking for someone who has your skills, do you show up?
You can think of this as search engine optimization for your employability. Recruiters have mostly consolidated around a single platform to find people: LinkedIn.
Those 40,000 followers and millions of impressions came with barely a viral post to my name. Nobody is begging me to do sponsorships. But I rarely have trouble finding work, and far more opportunities come to me than I go looking for. That has much less to do with fame than with being easy to find.
You don’t need 10,000 followers. You need a trail of breadcrumbs.
Don’t write AI slop
LinkedIn is notorious for being overrun with AI-generated posts. It’s become a running joke. That’s good news for you, because the bar to stand out is “sound like a human being.”
Write about what you actually achieved: a hairy bug you squashed, how your team handles deployments, why you picked some obscure library, the migration that went sideways at 2 a.m. Specifics are hard to fake and easy to trust. (But be careful not to post sensitive information.)
And post a picture of yourself once in a while. People connect with faces a lot faster than with walls of text.
Hot takes, with caution
Posts with an opinion tend to outperform tutorials, but you don’t have to dunk on anyone to have one. For instance, if you work on a tech stack people love to mock (VB, .NET, some ancient Java monolith held together with prayer), try something like “What people get wrong about .NET.”
You’ll attract a few trolls in the comments—free engagement, honestly—plus people who want an actual conversation. These comments can turn into actual connections and even… friends.
A routine you can follow
Posting twice a week is not a big ask. Pick a simple, repeatable format so you’re never staring at an empty text box: what you worked on, what broke, and what you learned. Even a post that gets 10 views leaves one more breadcrumb about who you are and what you know.
Over time, the people who comment become your network. And because so few engineers post about their work on LinkedIn, you can become a big fish in a small pond surprisingly fast.
Write for the people a few steps behind you
The best audience is engineers one or two steps behind where you are now. Answer the questions you had a year ago. It helps them, it sharpens your own thinking, and every so often it turns into mentorship in both directions.
It also tells a future employer more about how you think than any résumé bullet ever could.
The engineers who grab the most opportunities are the ones employers can find. You don’t need to become an influencer to be one of them. You just need to leave enough breadcrumbs that the right person can follow them back to you.
—Brian
IEEE Xplore Digital Library Adds AI Assistant
To help researchers search through the millions of peer-review publications in the IEEE Xplore Digital Library, IEEE has released a custom AI suite optimized for STEM literature. The suit allows users to search with natural-language queries and provides overviews with reference links.
Read more here.
Systems Thinking Is Vital in the Age of AI
AI has made it easier to access information in different domains, but specialist knowledge and human judgement still serve an essential role. Today, an engineer’s core value comes from knowing how to ask the right questions—not from knowing everything.
Read more here.
The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build
In this feature article, Agility Robotics’ cofounder Jonathan Hurst tells the inside story of the company’s latest humanoid robot and offers a valuable lesson about learning to pivot. “To deliver a useful commercial product, Agility has taken a path that is very different from what I first imagined,” Hurst writes.
Read more here.
Brian Jenney is the owner of Parsity, an online education platform that helps people break into AI and modern software roles through project-based learning and one-on-one mentorship with senior developers. Parsity helps career changers transition into software by focusing on practical skills, real-world systems, and the kind of experience companies actually look for.
Outside Parsity, Brian works a senior software engineer in the SF Bay Area.
Brian is also a father of three, and when he’s not working with students or building programs, you might catch him running around Lake Merritt in Oakland, California.

articles.title: GTA 6 launch live — review roundups, Metacritic score, and everything you need to know, plus ask me anything after 100 hours of gameplay
articles.text:
Live
It's finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is launching, and reviews are now out in the wild — including our own GTA 6 review!
It's a landmark day in video games, of course, but also in wider entertainment and popular culture — this is going to be a landmark moment in time, and one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time.
I've reviewed the game and spent more than 100 hours in Vice City and have loved absolutely every moment and am eager to see and hear everyone else's experiences, discoveries, adventures, and madcap shenanigans.
As we rattle toward launch tomorrow, I'm going to be here answering any questions you may have, rounding up reviews and reactions from critics, and sharing some of my favorite bits without spoiling anything!
LIVE: Latest Updates
Oh, by the way, if you haven't ordered or bought the game yet, and want to know the cheapest price or deal going, my fabulous colleague James has rounded up the best places to buy GTA 6 right now here.
Another question to answer
Rory Mellon from our sister-site Tom's Guide has asked:
"How does the new "Criminal Profile" system impact your ability to go on a rampage in the open world between missions?"
now this is an interesting question be cause I think we may only get an answer once different endings and playthroughs have been experienced; as I only know my own playthrough so far.
My playthrough was largely at the Professional end of the scale — lower levels of unwarranted violence, fewer kills, more incapacitations, and so on — so I don't know the lasting effects of a Psycho or Irredeemable playthrough.
We do know that Rob Nelson, Head of Development, has said that the system will have affects, but I might have to speculate on that a bit: I've heard rumours of cops being hotter on your tail, and areas being far more dangerous for you to return to should have you have adopted a more violent life of crime...
We're racing toward full release - have you got your copy?
Quick straw poll time! Well, literal poll, actually.
Were you waiting for reviews before committing? Have you got your copy nailed down, or are you still waiting? Let us know in the poll below!
My top pick of a controller for GTA 6
I'm still working on a dedicated guide on the controllers I've used, but to break a bit of cover, my favorite has been the DualSense Edge on PS5 Pro. Mapping R1 to a back paddle to ensure I can easily shoot while driving, and using the different trigger actuation levels, has been a godsend.
Luckily, it's the subject of a Black Friday price cut right now, and can be got for less. If you were looking to upgrade your gamepad to ensure your GTA 6 controls are personalised and fully optimised, then this is a fantastic pad to go for.
I've had my best moments and the most control in GTA 6 with Sony's DualSense Edge gamepad on PS5 Pro. I can vouch for it getting me out of holes and being a brilliant gamepad specifically for GTA 6, with the features that it offers. Now we're deep into Black Friday territory; you can save money on it too if you're aiming for an upgrade in line with GTA 6.
UK price: was £199.99 now £149.99 at Amazon
We've got a question!
Commenter Jimmywimmy has asked:
"Do the rdr2 mechanics, where you have to manually carry your loadout from vehicles and eat/ clean get in the way of the chaos?"
In short, no. The eating, sleeping, working out elements etc, have never interrupted any of the chaos or bedlam I've enjoyed in Vice City or in missions. In fact, there was a period where I fully embraced that and did a whole routine of going to the gym, recovering, sleeping, and repeating in order to get my physical stats all the way to the top. It can be incredibly satisfying. I've only occasionally had a warning about being hungry or tired, and the impact of it is never instant so you have plenty of time to finish your chaos before addressing it.
As far as the car goes, that can be a little more demanding as it really does pay to have your car nearby wherever possible for ease of stowing fyour long arms and swag. You'll not want to carry your long arms around casually as you'll draw a lot of attention so investing in a plan with your car is worthwhile; I found that having it nearby can actually complement the ability to carve out chaos, as it'll give you a place to change loadouts, outfits, and an 'out' when things invariably go base over apex.
The highest praise from another sister-site
Another sister site of ours, Creative Bloq, has also given GTA 6 a full five stars in its review.
Ian Dean calls the game "a generational release everyone should play" and "the most entertaining and emotionally engaging open world I’ve played."
TVs to make GTA 6 shine
On the topic of gear, though, I did have a discussion with my colleague James about how the game looks and performs visually in order for him to recommend some top TV choices.
It's pretty fortuitous timing with Black Friday on the horizon too, as prices will be becoming more attractive.
If you want to read more about which TV to potentially upgrade to in order to absorb even more of GTA 6's excellence, then here's James' article to peruse.
IGN gives it a 10
My peers over at IGN have loved GTA 6 as much as I have and call the game "Unprecedented. Unbelievable. Unmissable."
It's a great summation of the game, and their writer also shares a list of mad-cap things that they've experienced in the game, which are all familiar and hilarious to me.
Anyone who plays the game will have a similar experience, and you'll soon lose count of all the wild encounters you have.
Make sure you get the best gear for the job - and stay tuned for recommendations
I'm currently writing up some thoughts on the gear I used when playing GTA 6 — namely controllers and headsets that I have used throughout my review.
There's definitely something to be said about upgrading some kit for a game of this magnitude, and IO'll be recommending some bits once I've organised my thoughts.
There's a lot to take in
As I've said, I've spent 100 hours or so in the land of Vice City so have seen a whole lot — though I'm sure I've not seen anywhere near the total amount of events, encounters, and stories on offer.
Remember, if you want to ask me anything about the game to increase that hype train's speed, then get in touch via the comments below! I'd love to try and answer any questions and share any experiences based on my hands-on time with the game.
High praise from our sister-site
It's a sea of brilliance, praise, and a huge amount of funny stories that reviewers are regaling readers with, and it's fantastic.
One of my favorite reviews is from our sister-site and my old haunt, GamesRadar+, where Josh has called the game "the highest-fidelity sandbox of the generation" and that Rockstar has "built an open world of truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality" which I couldn't agree more with.
And critics elsewhere seem to agree...
My peers in the industry seem to agree with my overall view on the game too, as the Metacritic score of the game is the highest of all time, sitting at a barely believable 99!
Our review is right here
There's only one place for our own coverage to start, and that's with my GTA 6 review, which is now live!
In brief, I think this is an astounding game. It's an absolute must-play experience for everyone and probably the game of the generation. You can furnish yourself with all my takes in the review, but this is something truly special, and I'll be sharing some bits and bobs throughout our live coverage.
Greetings from Vice City's neon lights!
Hello and welcome to our live GTA 6 review embargo and reaction coverage!
I've reviewed the game and will be guiding you through today's review and critical reaction to the game and answering any questions you may have!
I'll be sharing spoiler-free bits from my experience too, as well as some recommendations on the peripherals I've been using.

articles.title: Singapur usará IA para rastrear estafas que pasan por varios bancos en pocos minutos
articles.text:
El viceprimer ministro de Singapur, Gan Kim Yong, anunció el 18 de noviembre que el país usará inteligencia artificial para detectar estafas que atraviesan varios bancos. Cinco entidades ya reúnen los datos de sus transacciones para que los modelos hallen patrones que ninguna vería sola, y el regulador financiero diseñará un sistema común.
Gan, que además preside la Autoridad Monetaria de Singapur (MAS, el regulador financiero del país), habló en el Singapore FinTech Festival, que se realiza del 18 al 20 de noviembre. Presentó tres “misiones nacionales de IA” para el sector financiero: delitos financieros, crédito a pequeñas empresas y pagos hechos por agentes de IA.
El primer frente apunta al camino que sigue el dinero robado. “Las estafas no se limitan a los confines de un banco”, dijo Gan. “El dinero de una víctima puede pasar por varias instituciones en minutos”, recogió Bloomberg. Según el funcionario, si cada entidad solo ve su tramo de la cadena, no se puede reducir el riesgo.
Por eso las entidades combinarán su información. La prueba con cinco bancos ya está en marcha, y sus datos se reúnen de forma segura para que los modelos de IA detecten movimientos sospechosos antes y permitan intervenir más rápido.
Un sistema común de detección, con diseño previsto para 2027
Esa prueba sentará las bases de lo que Gan llamó “Scam Detection Utility”, un servicio compartido para detectar estafas en todo el sector. La MAS comenzará un estudio de diseño con el plan, la gobernanza y el modelo de funcionamiento del sistema a comienzos del próximo año.
Al principio solo abarcará cuentas y datos dentro de Singapur. El viceprimer ministro dijo que, con el tiempo, podría haber oportunidades de cooperación con otros países, porque las estafas cruzan fronteras.
La MAS había descrito la prueba el 4 de mayo, junto con la agencia tecnológica del gobierno y la policía de Singapur. Según ese comunicado, los números de cuenta se codifican, de modo que solo el banco que aporta los datos puede identificarlos, y la información se borrará al terminar la prueba.
Dos misiones más: préstamos para pymes y compras por agentes de IA
La segunda misión busca facilitar el crédito a pequeñas y medianas empresas. Gan explicó que muchos prestamistas evalúan a un negocio por su historial de pagos y exigen garantías personales, un método que deja afuera a empresas nuevas con poco historial o pocos bienes.
El plan combina datos de cuentas bancarias, facturas, pagos y registros públicos, hoy dispersos y difíciles de reunir. Singapur invitará a empresas de IA a probar soluciones con datos sintéticos, es decir, creados de forma artificial, y consultará a las pymes si esas herramientas responden a lo que necesitan. Según Gan, la IA podría reducir los costos de endeudamiento.
La tercera misión explora cómo los agentes de IA, asistentes que ejecutan tareas por su cuenta, pueden hacer pagos y compras en nombre de personas y empresas. Una de las ideas es que paguen automáticamente un contrato cuando se verifiquen las condiciones pactadas, con dinero asignado a un fin concreto.
“Una mayor autonomía debe ir acompañada de una responsabilidad clara”, advirtió Gan. Los agentes deberán actuar dentro de límites definidos, y las instituciones y empresas seguirán respondiendo por lo que hagan en su nombre.
El Future of Finance Institute, un instituto del sector, coordinará las tres misiones con la industria, investigadores y organismos públicos. Bloomberg informó que el sector financiero aporta cerca del 14% de la economía de Singapur y emplea a unas 200.000 personas.
The Business Times señaló que el anuncio llega cuando las nuevas restricciones de Estados Unidos a la exportación de chips generan dudas sobre el acceso a la capacidad de cómputo que requieren las ambiciones de IA de Singapur. El próximo paso confirmado es el estudio de diseño de la MAS, previsto para comienzos de 2027.

articles.title: Gemini gardera vos chats temporaires deux mois au lieu de 72 h
articles.text:
Google conservera environ deux mois vos discussions temporaires avec Gemini, et celles que vous avez avec l’historique désactivé, contre 72 heures jusqu’ici. Avec cette mise à jour, l’entreprise vous laisse aussi garder votre historique sans que vos conversations servent à entraîner ses modèles d’IA.
Une discussion temporaire avec Gemini n’apparaît pas dans votre historique, et Google ne l’utilise ni pour personnaliser ses réponses ni pour entraîner ses modèles. Google a lancé ce mode en août 2025, et il effaçait ces échanges au bout de 72 heures, au moins jusqu’au 12 novembre, d’après une version archivée de son centre de confidentialité retrouvée par TechCrunch. Il les gardera désormais environ deux mois, et il déploiera ce changement dans le monde entier au cours des prochaines semaines. Interrogé par TechCrunch, Google n’a pas expliqué pourquoi il lui fallait vingt fois plus de temps.
Google garde vos conversations pour protéger Gemini
Pendant ces deux mois, Google utilisera vos conversations pour vous répondre, traiter vos commentaires et « protéger Google, ses utilisateurs et le public », selon son blog. Dans son centre de confidentialité, l’entreprise cite aussi d’éventuelles pannes de ses systèmes, et elle assure ne pas entraîner ses modèles avec vos discussions temporaires.
Si vous notez une réponse de Gemini d’un pouce levé ou baissé, Google récupère en outre les 24 dernières heures de vos conversations, pièces jointes comprises, y compris avec l’historique désactivé. L’entreprise conserve jusqu’à trois ans les échanges relus par ses évaluateurs humains, et vous ne pouvez pas les effacer en supprimant votre historique.
Avec ces deux mois, Google gardera vos discussions deux fois plus longtemps qu’OpenAI et Anthropic. OpenAI conserve jusqu’à 30 jours les discussions temporaires de ChatGPT, et Anthropic garde 30 jours par défaut les conversations privées de Claude. Ces entreprises peuvent toutefois conserver certaines données plus longtemps, pour des raisons légales ou de sécurité, ou pour enquêter sur un abus de leurs services.
- Multimodalité texte, voix et fichiers
- Intégration poussée aux services Google
- Applications Web, mobile et bureau
Google sépare votre historique de l’entraînement de son IA
Jusqu’ici, avec le seul réglage « Conserver l’activité », vous acceptiez à la fois que Google garde vos conversations et qu’il les utilise pour entraîner ses modèles d’IA. Pour retrouver vos anciennes discussions, vous deviez lui laisser vos messages, mais aussi vos photos, vos fichiers, vos enregistrements audio, votre localisation et les données tirées des applications Google reliées à Gemini.
Google remplace ce réglage par deux commandes. Dans la rubrique Historique, vous choisissez combien de temps Google garde vos conversations, 18 mois par défaut, et vous pouvez les consulter ou les supprimer à tout moment. Avec la seconde commande, vous pouvez refuser que vos échanges, pièces jointes comprises, servent à entraîner ses modèles.
Si vous aviez activé « Conserver l’activité », Google garde votre historique, et vous déciderez séparément s’il peut entraîner son IA avec vos conversations. Si vous l’aviez désactivé, Google coupera par défaut les deux nouveaux réglages. Vous recevrez peut-être un courriel de Google à ce sujet, mais une fois la mise à jour arrivée sur votre compte, vérifiez ces deux réglages dans la page Activité de Gemini.
Et si vous désactivez l’historique pour que Google oublie vos conversations, il les gardera malgré tout deux mois.

articles.title: James Bond : c'est surement la fin de l'humour pour 007
articles.text:
Pour Denis Villeneuve, James Bond est avant tout un tueur. Interrogé par Zach Baron pour le numéro Men of the Year du magazine GQ, publié ce mardi 17 novembre 2026, le réalisateur du futur James Bond 26 détaille les critères qui ont guidé sa recherche du nouveau 007, menée avec les producteurs et Amazon MGM Studios.
L’entretien a eu lieu avant l’annonce officielle, alors que le choix était encore « en cours » : Villeneuve n’y cite jamais Robert Pattinson.
Un assassin crédible pour James Bond
Le cinéaste exige d’abord que son James Bond soit crédible en tueur. « La première qualité, c’est que je dois croire que cet homme est un tueur, parce que plus qu’un espion, Bond est un assassin », explique Villeneuve à GQ. Pour incarner cette dangerosité, le réalisateur recherchait un interprète capable d’afficher « une colère au fond des yeux », une qualité que « tout le monde n’a pas », selon lui.
Mais cette noirceur ne doit pas étouffer le magnétisme naturel du personnage. Le réalisateur dresse ainsi le portrait-robot d’un 007 complet, à la fois redoutable et électrisant :
- Un charisme magnétique : Villeneuve voulait un homme au « panache assumé », capable d’aimanter toute une pièce dès son entrée et de porter une scène à lui seul, doublé d’une forte sensualité et d’un vrai plaisir à évoluer dans ce monde.
- Un goût pour le danger : le cinéaste imagine un espion prendre plaisir à se retrouver dans des situations périlleuses et ne rechigne pas à se salir les mains.
- Une force physique et une vivacité d’esprit : sur le plan athlétique, il exigeait un comédien solide et musclé, représentant une véritable force à l’écran, tout en affichant dans le regard une intelligence vive et toujours un coup d’avance sur le spectateur.
Avec le tandem Villeneuve-Pattinson aux commandes, et le créateur de Peaky Blinders Steven Knight au scénario, ce James Bond 26 semble prêt à tourner définitivement la page de l’ironie britannique qui a fait le sel de la franchise pendant 6 décennies
Pourquoi le casting a pris autant de temps
Denis Villeneuve est aussi revenu sur les coulisses de ce casting qui a tenu les fans en haleine pendant des mois. Si l’annonce a autant tardé, c’est tout simplement parce que le réalisateur a imposé son propre calendrier à la production.
Les producteurs l’ont approché pour réaliser le prochain James Bond au moment où il s’apprêtait à tourner Dune 3, un film dans lequel il a justement dirigé Robert Pattinson. Villeneuve les a prévenus qu’il ne s’occuperait de 007 qu’une fois son passage sur Arrakis terminé. Les essais et le choix final ont donc été repoussés de plusieurs mois.
