articles.title: London’s Perry AI raises €2 million to bring AI-powered legal intelligence to private capital funds | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Perry AI, the London-based startup building an AI-powered legal operating system for private equity and venture capital funds, has raised €2 million ($2.2 million) in a Seed funding round.
The round was led by Haatch, with participation from Antler, Syncorp Ventures, Araya Ventures, US super angel Kelsey Chase, and a cohort of strategic angel investors. The company says the Seed funding round was oversubscribed, driven by strong interest in the LegalTech space, with funding surpassing €2.09 billion ($2.3 billion) in the first quarter of 2026 alone.
“The biggest wins in AI will go to companies that go deep in markets where the stakes are high and generalist tools fall short. Private capital legal work is a textbook example. Shashwat and Vaneesa have spent nearly three decades between them doing this work, and it shows in the product: Perry AI doesn’t just review documents, it builds a living memory of every commitment a fund has made and acts on it. The early customer results are exceptional, and we’re delighted to lead this round as Perry takes its platform to the next level,” said Fred Soneya, co-founder and General Partner at Haatch.
Perry AI was founded in 2025 by Shashwat Patel and Vaneesa Agarwal, who together bring nearly three decades of private capital legal experience. Patel spent 15 years as a funds and corporate lawyer at Debevoise & Plimpton and Simmons & Simmons, advising major asset managers including BlackRock, Brookfield, and Invesco. Agarwal, an NYU School of Law graduate, built a venture capital law firm from scratch to 75 deals and a top-tier Legal 500 ranking within three years.
With Perry AI, they are building and maintaining a live legal memory for private capital markets, one capable of capturing every right, obligation, side letter commitment, and negotiated position a fund has made, across every deal. AI agents then act on that record, reviewing documents, flagging issues, preparing drafts, and coordinating in-house teams with external counsel through one shared, live workspace.
The platform covers the full fund lifecycle, from fund formation and capital deployment to portfolio and fund management, and exit. It serves both fund teams and the law firms advising them. Perry AI says law firms can also white-label the platform under their own brand, keeping clients engaged for the life of a fund rather than only during live transactions.
“I spent more than 15 years advising funds, and every deal had the same undercurrent: a scramble against the clock, in a high-stakes, regulated world, with the constant fear that something had been missed. A side letter promise, a consent or preemption right, an MFN obligation buried three deals back. Generic AI can’t take that fear away, because it doesn’t know the fund. Perry AI does,” said Patel, co-founder and CEO of Perry AI.
He added, “It remembers every position a fund has taken and acts on it, so legal teams can move fast and still sleep at night. Demand has been exceptional, and this round lets us build on our momentum in Europe and take Perry AI across the US and Asia.”
The company says funds already using Perry AI manage over €1.4 billion ($1.5 billion) in assets under management across more than 1,000 portfolio companies. Its users report working 90% faster, with deal signing times on live transactions reduced from 84 days to just 13 days,
The fresh capital will accelerate Perry AI’s expansion into the United States and Asia, while deepening its European and UK growth. The company also plans to extend the platform beyond deal execution into areas such as fund formation, secondaries, fund transfers, LP reporting, MFN tracking, and co-invest allocation, several of which are already live.

articles.title: Mehr Klicks, mehr Warnungen: Warum Apple KI-Agenten den Zugriff auf deinen Mac erschwert
articles.text:
Mehr Klicks, mehr Warnungen: Warum Apple KI-Agenten den Zugriff auf deinen Mac erschwert
Apple ändert die Sicherheits- und Datenschutzarchitektur von macOS – und das hat vor allem mit der zunehmenden Nutzung von KI-Agenten zu tun. Die kommende Betriebssystemversion 27.3 (ab Dezember erhältlich und aktuell im Betatest) stellt die zentralen Zugriffskontrollen um, die den Festplattenvollzugriff, die Bedienungshilfen und die App-Steuerung regeln.
Nutzer:innen sollen so besser verstehen, worauf eine App zugreift, besonders, wenn es sich um einen KI-Agenten handelt. Bevor User:innen einer App einen derart weitreichenden Zugriff gewähren, sollten sie verstehen, dass dadurch „alle Daten“ auf ihrem Mac gefährdet werden, erklärt Apple. Der Konzern hat die Änderung in der Nacht auf Dienstag gegenüber Entwicklern angekündigt, weil diese ihre Software womöglich anpassen müssen. macOS 27.3 liegt aktuell als zweite Beta vor. Die fertige Version wird in einigen Wochen erscheinen.
Warum KI-Tools der Auslöser sind
Hintergrund von Apples Aktion ist das schnell wachsende Angebot an KI‑Werkzeugen. Sie verlangen oft umfassende Freigaben, um einen Mac vollständig zu steuern und auf geschützte Daten zuzugreifen. Zunächst waren das hauptsächlich Entwickler-Tools wie Claude Code oder die offizielle App von ChatGPT mit teurem Abo. Inzwischen richten sich KI-Agenten aber an ein breites Publikum. Diesen Nutzer:innen dürfte oft nicht klar sein, was Festplattenvollzugriff überhaupt bedeutet: Die App darf dann praktisch alle Daten auf dem Rechner lesen.
Für Aufsehen sorgte zuletzt die Mac-Version von Metas KI-Agentensystem Muse, das in der EU noch nicht freigeschaltet ist. Laut einem Bericht des Magazins Inc. hat die App über den zuvor von den User:innen erbetenen Festplattenvollzugriff ungefragt iMessage-Nachrichten mitgelesen und daraus Vorschläge erstellt. Meta sprach von einer Funktion, die Nutzer:innen selbst aktivieren müssen. Technisch ist ein solcher Zugriff am einfachsten mit Festplattenvollzugriff möglich – oder über eine Sicherheitslücke. Mit der Freigabe kommen KI-Tools auch an interne Log-Dateien und Datenbanken, die macOS für Siri und eigene KI-Funktionen anlegt. Darin stehen unter anderem Freundschafts- und Familienverhältnisse, das Kommunikationsverhalten und die Information, mit welchen Personen man gemeinsam auf eigenen Fotos zu sehen ist. KI-Agenten könnten solche Daten auch für Trainingszwecke an ihre Entwickler weiterleiten.
macOS: Mehr Klicks, mehr Warnungen
Apple macht die Freigabe in macOS 27.3 aus diesem Grund bewusst umständlicher. Bisher ließ sich ein App-Icon einfach in die Freigabeliste ziehen. Künftig wählen Nutzer die anfragende App aus einer Liste aus. Danach zeigt ein Warndialog detailliert, welche Daten die App einsehen, ändern und ausleiten kann, sobald sie Festplattenvollzugriff oder Zugriff auf die Bedienungshilfen bekommt. Bis die Freigabe steht, sind mehrere Bestätigungsschritte nötig.
Statt der Komplettfreigabe empfiehlt Apple, nur einzelne Ordner oder einzelne Apps freizugeben. Die App-weise Freigabe ist ebenfalls neu. Zusätzlich erscheint ein gut sichtbares Icon in der Menüleiste, sobald eine App über die sogenannte App-Steuerung eine andere App fernsteuert. Bestehende Freigaben bleiben allerdings bestehen. Die neuen Regeln gelten nur für neue Anfragen durch Agenten und andere Apps. Entwickler von Backup- und Accessibility-Software können bei Apple eine Sondergenehmigung, ein sogenanntes Entitlement, beantragen, um die Freigabe weiterhin leichter zu erhalten. Einige Entwickler:innen kritisieren, dass Apple es Drittanbietern schwerer macht, auf Daten zuzugreifen, während der Konzern selbst das Siri-AI-KI-System mit einem Klick aktivieren lässt.

articles.title: Karnataka aims to become a global hub for frontier tech; Fadnavis’ vision for a new Maharashtra
articles.text:
Karnataka aims to become a global hub for frontier tech; Fadnavis’ vision for a new Maharashtra
Karnataka aims to become a global hub for frontier technologies such as AI, deeptech, and biotech, said CM DK Shivakumar at Bengaluru Tech Summit. Meanwhile, Maharashtra CM Fadnavis has shared his roadmap for a trillion-dollar, drought-free, deeptech Maharashtra by 2035.
Dear Reader,
The best of AI is yet to come.
The potential of artificial intelligence still remains unexplored, and it can help create solutions with population-scale impact, said panellists during a discussion at Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026.
Karnataka Home and IT Minister Priyank Kharge, Infosys Co-founder S Gopalakrishnan, Biocon Group Chairperson Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, and Accel India Founding Partner Prashanth Prakash stressed the opportunities in areas such as drug development, cybersecurity, IT solutions, governance and services.
At another conference across the world, Union Minister Jayant Chaudhary spoke about India’s robust startup story.
India has around 300,000 registered startups, many of which are led by women, the Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship told global tech leaders at the TIECON 2026 conference in Singapore. “Our seeds are sown throughout the country,” he said. Highlighting the market potential, he pointed out that Indian farmers are keen to use technology, and the IITs are launching deeptech funds.
Moving on, ecommerce giant Amazon plans to invest an additional $7 billion in renewable energy projects in India by 2030, as it seeks to meet growing electricity requirements and reduce the carbon intensity of power across its operations.
In other news, Pragya Misra, OpenAI’s head of strategy and global affairs in India, is taking on a new role. She will lead the firm’s business development for India and South Asia, with a focus on building partnerships that help businesses transform with AI.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Karnataka’s aim to become a global hub for frontier tech
- Fadnavis’ vision for a new Maharashtra
Here’s your trivia for today: What cloud-based gaming service did Google launch in 2019, only to shut it down in 2023 due to lack of adoption? (Scroll down for the answer)
Technology
Karnataka aims to become a global hub for frontier tech
Karnataka aims to become a global hub for frontier technologies such as artificial intelligence, deeptech, semiconductor, robotics, and biotech, said Chief Minister DK Shivakumar at the inaugural of Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) in Bengaluru on Tuesday, citing the state government’s enabling policies.
BTS, now in its 29th edition, is themed around ‘AI and Beyond’. Addressing the event, the chief minister highlighted that Karnataka has consistently been at the forefront of technology and is well placed to lead the next phase of global innovation, backed by a strong IT and startup ecosystem.
Key takeaways
- Karnataka, the CM said, accounted for two out of every five dollars earned by India through software and services exports, which amounted to around $173 billion last year.
- The state attracted $9.4 billion in FDI equity inflows in the first half of FY26, accounting for 26.7% of India’s total inflows during the period. Karnataka is home to more than 24,000 recognised startups, and nearly two out of every five Indian unicorns originate from the state, Shivakumar said.
- AI is another main focus of Karnataka’s technology ambitions, with Bengaluru accounting for nearly 50% of India’s AI and machine learning talent.
Roadmap
Fadnavis’ vision for a new Maharashtra
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis spent nearly five hours judging student presentations at the summit of The Governance Challenge 2026 in Mumbai. Six finalist teams pitched their answers to one question: what can the Government of Maharashtra do to make the state an innovation hub by 2035? The teams presented ideas on healthcare, education, farming and access to credit.
Thereafter, the chief minister, the finalists of the challenge, and Gaurav Goel, Founder & CEO of Samagra, which runs the challenge, joined Shradha Sharma, Founder & CEO, The Bharat Project and YourStory Media, for an open conversation.
Key takeaways:
- Fadnavis shared his roadmap for a trillion-dollar, drought-free, deeptech Maharashtra by 2035. The CM called Gen Z the first generation born entirely into technology, constantly connected to global best practices. Properly channelled, he said, this exposure produces bright ideas. But he stressed the need for balancing new ideas with mentoring, oversight and experience. “Innovation is a simple solution for a very complex problem,” he stressed.
- Goel explained that The Governance Challenge (TGC) was created to fill the gap in management education. Business school case studies, campus events, internships and placements all lean heavily towards the corporate and startup world, leaving students with little exposure to governance or social impact. TGC tries to change that through immersion, in the hope that the experience stays with students and later draws them towards nation building.
- Shradha Sharma called the day a glimpse of what a Viksit Bharat could look like: a chief minister who listens, and young people ready to do the work.
News & updates
- Social media curbs: Meta Platforms has fine-tuned Instagram's content recommendation systems in India to curb the visibility of sexually suggestive material and violent content, deploying more advanced AI models to identify and filter unwanted posts before they reach users.
- Funding: Redbrick Offices, which provides managed office spaces and workspace solutions, has raised about $72 million in equity across its Series A and A1 funding rounds. The company plans to use the capital to expand its managed offices portfolio and invest in technology, design and service delivery to cater to enterprise and GCC clients.
- Data centre curbs: The Trump administration plans to press ahead with efforts to block imports of Chinese data centre equipment despite pushback from Amazon, Google, Meta and other US technology companies, according to people briefed on the matter, Reuters reported.
What cloud-based gaming service did Google launch in 2019, only to shut it down in 2023 due to lack of adoption?
Answer: Google Stadia

articles.text:
Happy midweek. ☀️️
Mzansi, we’ve got our eyes on you! 🇿🇦 TechCabal is bringing you TC Mzansi, a brand-new newsletter covering Southern Africa’s tech news: big deals, big moves, and all the industry gist worth knowing, straight to your inbox.
Join the waitlist and be the first to know when we launch.
TC Mzansi, our newsletter covering South African tech is coming on November 23.
AI
Cassava seeks $1 billion to buy Nvidia chips for AI data centres across Africa
Cassava Technologies, the pan-African technology group founded by Zimbabwean billionaire Strive Masiyiwa, is in talks with investors in the Middle East and the United States to raise up to $1 billion to buy NVIDIA-made graphics processing units (GPUs) and upgrade its fibre and data-centre networks to handle demanding AI workloads. The fundraising is still under discussion, and there is no guarantee it will close.
Explain like I’m new here: In 2025, Cassava partnered with the chipmaker to build what it called Africa’s first AI factory, using Nvidia’s computing systems and software.
Cassava became Nvidia’s first Cloud Partner in Africa and began deploying its AI infrastructure in South Africa, with plans to expand into Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, and Morocco. It has also launched its AI Multi-Model Exchange, a platform that gives African developers access to different AI models and tools to build and deploy applications.
Why it matters: Africa accounts for just 0.6% of global data-centre capacity, according to the Africa Data Centres Association’s 2026 report. There is plenty of room to grow, but building these facilities requires enormous investment. Local AI infrastructure could help businesses run applications faster, keep sensitive data within national borders and develop products around African languages and markets.
Cassava is not alone. Amazon Web Services (AWS) says it has invested more than $819 million in its South African cloud infrastructure since 2018, with another $1.5 billion committed by the end of 2029.
Microsoft and UAE-based AI company G42 announced a $1 billion investment in a data centre and cloud region in Kenya in 2024, although the project encountered delays in 2026. These investments are building the cloud infrastructure that AI services depend on.

Internet
Telkom lines up to sell Amazon’s satellite Internet in South Africa
Telkom, South Africa’s third-largest telecoms company by subscribers, has signed up to distribute Amazon Leo, Amazon’s satellite broadband service. Telkom signed the agreement through Openserve, its wholesale network business, covering all three of the group’s businesses.
How it will work: Openserve will sell satellite connectivity to large businesses and eligible public-sector customers. BCX, Telkom’s IT services subsidiary, will bundle it with managed networks, cloud computing and cybersecurity services, while Telkom Business will serve small businesses in rural and remote areas.
Telkom can also use satellite connections as primary or backup links for its mobile towers, connecting sites where conventional network infrastructure is hard to deploy.
Explain like I’m new here: In July, Amazon partnered with Herotel, a local Internet service provider, to launch a residential and small-business service called evry. It marked its commercial entry into the country, with commercial availability expected in 2027.
Why this matters: The partnerships also offer Amazon a way into a market where Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite service, has struggled to secure approval. South Africa requires companies holding certain telecoms licences to include historically disadvantaged groups in ownership. This has been a major obstacle for Starlink. Amazon’s distributor-led approach allows Herotel to handle the necessary local licensing and regulatory requirements.
The deal comes as Telkom becomes more selective about where it spends money on fibre. In the six months to September 2026, its fibre investment fell by more than a third. Extending fibre into remote areas can be expensive, but satellite offers another option. There are no prices or launch dates yet, but Telkom says it will share availability details closer to launch.
Streaming
MTN: Lights, camera, data!
MTN has a new show about staying single. The telecoms giant is looking for a long-term relationship with your screen.
MTN One TV, its streaming platform, has started producing original content, beginning with 100 Ways to Stay Single in Lagos, a Nigerian series featuring Ghanaian, Nigerian, and South African actors.
The show is currently available in South Africa and Zambia, with plans to roll it out to other MTN markets. More original productions are on the way.
Explain like I’m new here: MTN has been down this road before. In 2014, it launched FrontRow, a streaming service that became VU a year later. By May 2017, VU was dead, and MTN had retreated to partnerships with other entertainment providers.
Nine years later, the telco is giving streaming another shot. It launched MTN One TV in June 2026, starting with South Africa and Zambia. The platform is free to watch and supported by advertising, but viewers still need an internet connection.
So far, it has attracted 20,000 registered users in South Africa.
What’s MTN really after? Data consumption. MTN’s digital services chief, Burak Akinci, says video is driving data traffic growth, and the company wants to profit from more than simply providing the connection.
MTN has 317 million customers across 16 markets, including roughly 170 million smartphone users. Getting even a fraction of them hooked on its streaming platform could boost its data business.
The company isn’t building a traditional film studio. Instead, it’s commissioning African productions and plans to introduce free-to-air channels and premium viewing options.
Zoom out: Netflix and other global streamers spend billions competing for viewers. MTN believes its advantage lies elsewhere: an enormous existing customer base and a direct route to their phones.
But having millions of people on your network doesn’t mean they’ll watch your shows. MTN learned that lesson with VU.
This time, I hope100 Ways to Stay Single in Lagos becomes a lasting relationship.
Capital Markets
Juice Global wants to trade Africa’s IOUs
If you’re a business waiting to get paid, you have two options: wait patiently or chase your money. Juice Global wants to introduce a third: sell the “I owe you” (IOU).
The company behind Nigerian cross-border payments platform Juicyway and payout network Nairagram has unveiled Eko Securities Exchange, a new trading platform designed to turn money owed to African businesses into investments that people can buy and sell.
Explain like I’m new here: Juice Global has spent years helping businesses move money across borders. Along the way, it discovered another problem: businesses need money available before they can complete transactions.
Eko Securities is its proposed solution, and the idea is surprisingly simple.
Here’s how it works: Imagine a Nigerian exporter expecting payment in 60 days. Instead of waiting two months, the exporter could package the money owed into an investment that someone else buys today. The investor gets the right to receive the future payment, and takes on the risk that it might not arrive.
Eko wants to make such investments easier to trade by turning them into digital tokens. It plans to start with payment receivables and other short-term debts, before expanding into corporate bonds, private company shares, and other investments.
Why it matters: Africa has roughly 29 stock exchanges and trading venues, each operating under different rules, currencies, and systems. According to the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), African companies raised just 1% of the world’s equity capital between 2000 and 2024.
Zoom out: Eko has received approval in principle from Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), but its broader ambitions still require regulatory approval. Expanding into other African markets will also mean getting permission from local regulators.

articles.title: IKEA, ASOS, Zoom… Plus de 175 sites piratés ont peut-être tenté de voler vos données bancaires
articles.text:
Comme le révèle l’entreprise de cybersécurité Report URI, les sites de 178 entreprises et organisations ont été exposés à un malware ce lundi 16 novembre 2026, entre 5 h 21 du matin et 22 heures environ (heure de Paris). Parmi les sites compromis, nous pouvons notamment citer GitLab, Transavia, Air France-KLM, IKEA, ASOS, HSBC ou encore la plateforme de visioconférence Zoom. Pour être plus précis, ce ne sont pas les sites en eux-mêmes qui ont été compromis, mais un outil externe baptisé Optimizely, qui permet à ces sites de tester plusieurs versions de leurs pages web.
Un malware capable de voler des informations bancaires
Durant environ 15 heures, les sites web compromis ont chargé sans le savoir un malware. Les internautes de passage ont donc été exposés à ce malware durant ce laps de temps. Pour y parvenir, les pirates ont injecté des scripts JavaScript malveillants dans les projets de leurs clients, en passant par la plateforme Optimizely.
Le malware, défini par Report URI comme « un kit multifonctionnel », était capable de récupérer les cookies et les numéros de carte saisis dans les formulaires de paiement du site, mais aussi de remplacer les adresses des portefeuilles de cryptomonnaies par celles de l’attaquant. Il était également capable d’installer des kits d’exploitation sur des iPhone et des iPad non mis à jour. À noter toutefois que le malware n’aurait pas pu avoir accès aux paiements effectués via des modules externes comme Stripe ou Adyen.
La faille aurait été comblée, mais la prudence reste de mise
Optimizely, la plateforme qui a été victime de cette cyberattaque, a confirmé l’incident, tout en assurant que la faille a maintenant été comblée et le code malveillant supprimé. En théorie, visiter les sites mentionnés plus haut ne représente donc aujourd’hui plus de risque.
Si vous avez consulté l’un de ces sites ce 16 novembre, Report URI conseille de surveiller vos relevés de compte et de contacter votre banque immédiatement à la moindre détection de transaction suspecte. Veillez également à mettre votre iPhone ou votre iPad à jour. Précisons au passage que Report URI estime que sa liste de sites compromis est sans doute incomplète, et donc plus importante. Nous avons ici cité les plateformes compromises les plus utilisées en France, les autres sites concernés étant peu visités sous nos latitudes (la chaîne CNN, la plateforme de streaming Peacock, Levi’s Japan, etc.).
Cet épisode nous rappelle qu’il faut faire attention à notre comportement en ligne, même lorsque l’on visite des sites réputés pour être fiables. Un site web peut être très bien sécurisé, mais rester vulnérable à cause d’un outil externe qu’il utilise et qui aurait été compromis.

articles.title: Critical Perforce Puppet RCE Exploited in Attacks
articles.text:
Threat actors have been exploiting a critical-severity vulnerability in Perforce Puppet to execute code on vulnerable servers.
Puppet is an infrastructure-as-code (IaC) and configuration management platform that uses a client-server architecture for device management.
Tracked as CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS score of 9.4), the exploited security defect is described as a deserialization of untrusted data issue in the report processing of Puppet Enterprise and Puppet Core, leading to remote code execution (RCE).
It allows clients that have a certificate signed by the Puppet certificate authority (CA) to send reports containing malicious payloads that would be executed on the server with the service user permissions, putting managed systems at risk.
“A successful attack could expose the server’s certificate-signing key, allow an attacker to issue trusted certificates, and enable changes to software and configuration delivered to managed systems on their next Puppet run,” Perforce explains in an advisory.
Unauthenticated attackers could obtain a certificate if the CA auto-signs requests without performing strong verification. Administrators are advised to turn off auto-signing and enforce strong validation to ensure only trusted systems and authorized users can receive certificates.
The security hole was patched on November 3 alongside CVE-2026-115732, a critical issue where an attacker could use a certificate with a name that extends an approved name to bypass authorization and impersonate a managed machine.
Puppet Enterprise and Puppet Enterprise Advanced versions 2026.0.1, 2025.12.1, and 2023.8.13, and Puppet Core versions 9.1.3 and 8.22.2 contain patches for both flaws.
CVE-2026-115731 was flagged as exploited on November 4 and the US cybersecurity agency CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on November 17, urging federal agencies to patch it within two weeks, in line with BOD 26-04’s recommendations.
The vulnerability also affects the OpenVox configuration management platform. A proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit targeting OpenVox was published shortly after CVE-2026-115731 was patched.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.text:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert Huber, Franz Giessibl, and Klaus Richter, along with a team at the Max Planck Institute in Hamburg led by Angel Rubio.
Watching Electrons Move at Incredible Speeds
Understanding how matter behaves at the smallest scales is essential for developing the next generation of technology. Advances in clean energy, quantum computing, and powerful electronics for artificial intelligence all depend on knowing how chemical reactions unfold, how light interacts with materials, and how electrons travel through electronic devices.
However, even the sharpest microscopic photographs cannot reveal the full picture. Scientists also need to observe how these processes change over time, effectively creating slow-motion movies of events occurring at the atomic scale.
At RUN, researchers are developing ultrafast microscopes capable of recording the movements of electrons, atoms, and molecules with extraordinary precision in both space and time. About ten years ago, scientists in Regensburg used ultrafast scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the movement of a single molecule across space and time for the first time.
Tracking individual electrons presents an even greater challenge. At these microscopic distances, electrons can move roughly a thousand times faster than atoms and molecules, with important changes taking place over just attoseconds.
To appreciate how extreme these scales are, consider that an atom is approximately ten million times smaller than a millimeter. An attosecond is one-billionth of a billionth of a second. The difference between an attosecond and a second is comparable to the difference between one second and the entire age of the universe.
Making these measurements is especially difficult because electrons do not behave like ordinary objects. Their motion follows the unusual laws of quantum mechanics rather than the familiar rules of classical physics.
Ultrafast Lasers Reveal Quantum Tunneling
To observe electron behavior at these extraordinary speeds, the researchers built a new laser system that provides much finer time resolution than earlier experiments. The system allows them to control and study the quantum motion of individual electrons directly.
In the experiments, carefully timed laser pulses drive electrons from an extremely sharp metal tip toward a silver surface. The distance they travel is only a few atomic diameters.
The researchers detect this movement by measuring the resulting electrical current. To determine exactly when the electrons move, they use two pulses of light separated by a precisely controlled interval.
Simon Maier, the lead author of the paper, explains: "By varying the time interval between the two laser pulses, we can directly observe how the electrons respond."
This approach revealed clear evidence of electron motion occurring on attosecond timescales. It showed that the laser pulses could transfer electrons within these incredibly brief intervals while allowing scientists to observe the process as it happened.
What makes the result particularly remarkable is how the electrons travel. Instead of moving like conventional particles, they behave as quantum waves. This allows them to pass through an energy barrier separating the metal tip from the silver surface, even though classical physics predicts they should not have enough energy to cross it.
This phenomenon, known as quantum tunneling, is somewhat like an object passing through a solid wall without breaking or damaging it.
"Our measurement can be understood as a high-speed camera for the electron wave packets, since you can see at what point in time the tunneling process takes place," explains Katharina Glöckl, a doctoral student and co-author of the publication.
A Surprising 500-Attosecond Delay
To understand the measurements more deeply, researchers working with Prof. Angel Rubio performed sophisticated quantum simulations of the electrons' behavior near the "space-time limit."
Their calculations closely reproduced the experimental findings and uncovered another remarkable detail. The electrons did not respond to the light field instantaneously. Instead, their motion lagged behind it by approximately 500 attoseconds.
At such extreme scales, several fundamental features of quantum physics become important simultaneously.
For example, the researchers found that the laser pulses could not be described entirely by treating light as a wave or entirely by treating it as individual particles called photons. Their effects displayed characteristics of both descriptions. This combination was essential for exploring electron behavior so close to the "space-time limit."
The team also discovered that controlling electron motion over extremely short intervals changes how the electrons are distributed in space. Quantum mechanics describes these electrons using wave packets, which represent how their wave properties extend across different locations.
The relationship between the timing of electron motion and the spatial extent of these wave packets revealed the central limitation behind the discovery.
A Hidden Tradeoff Between Space and Time
Raffael Spachtholz, another co-author of the study, explains: "The more precisely we want to pin down the electron's position in time, the more energy we need to provide. And as a result, the electron wave packet spreads out more spatially."
In other words, improving the precision of an electron's timing comes with a cost. The more tightly researchers define when its motion occurs, the more broadly its quantum wave packet spreads through space.
To examine this relationship experimentally, the team placed a single atom on the surface to confine the electron wave packets to an extremely small region immediately before the laser pulses arrived.
This setup allowed the scientists to directly measure the connection between the electrons' spatial distribution and the timing of their motion.
Importantly, even when the electrons received substantial energy from the laser pulses, their wave packets remained sufficiently localized for microscopy with atomic spatial resolution and attosecond time resolution.
The findings provide experimental insight into a fundamental space-time constraint that scientists had previously only suspected. They also make it possible to systematically investigate how changes in electron motion over time affect the spatial structure of quantum wave functions.
Could Quantum Electronics Become Hundreds of Thousands of Times Faster?
Beyond revealing a new aspect of quantum behavior, the discovery could open the door to technologies that operate on timescales far beyond the capabilities of today's electronics.
One especially promising possibility involves using precisely controlled electron wave packets to influence chemical reactions.
Transferring a single electron to a molecule represents the smallest possible transfer of electric charge. But when that electron is concentrated within an exceptionally small region of space and time, the resulting local peak current density can reach as much as 1 trillion amperes per square centimeter.
Such extreme conditions could give scientists new ways to control chemical bonds and observe how molecules change during reactions.
"In the future, we want to use such wave packets to specifically trigger chemical reactions and observe, on the relevant length and time scales, how chemical bonds can be broken or altered," explains Prof. Jascha Repp enthusiastically.
The implications could extend well beyond chemistry. Greater control over electron motion may eventually help engineers develop electronic devices and quantum information systems that operate at speeds approaching the fundamental limits of electron dynamics.
"In the long term, the insights gained could also contribute to operating electronics and quantum information processing at the intrinsic speed limit of electron motion itself -- hundreds of thousands of times faster than the currently dominant CMOS technology," adds Prof. Rupert Huber.
That possibility remains a long term technological goal rather than an achievement demonstrated in the current experiments. Nevertheless, the findings provide a new foundation for exploring how electrons can be manipulated at the smallest distances and shortest timescales.
For Repp and Huber, the results suggest that the range of potential applications is extraordinarily broad. They believe that future advances in controlling electrons at the space-time limit may ultimately depend more on human creativity than on the constraints imposed by nature.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Regensburg. Original written by Karoline Stürmer. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

articles.title: Intermarché : les 700 000 peluches du loup ne seront pas là pour Noël, mais il y aura une « très grosse surprise »
articles.text:
Il y a un an, le loup solitaire de la publicité de Noël d’Intermarché faisait pleurer une bonne partie d’Internet. Il avait même fait remonter les écoutes de la chanson Le Mal-Aimé de Claude François sur les plateformes de streaming. Faute de stock, l’enseigne avait alors promis une peluche pour Noël 2026.
En octobre 2026, Thierry Cotillard, président du Groupement Les Mousquetaires, avait donné plus de détails : 700 000 exemplaires de la peluche loup d’Intermarché devaient arriver en magasin fin novembre, avec un prix de vente de 19,90 €. Sauf que ce mercredi 18 novembre 2026, BFM Business annonce en titre qu’il n’y aura « pas de loup au pied du sapin », mais « d’autres produits dérivés » de la publicité.
Une annonce qui arrive le jour même où GTA 6 sort enfin. Pour attirer l’attention, il y a meilleur timing.
Tous les copains du loup vendus en peluche chez Intermarché à partir du 1er décembre
« Dès le 1er décembre, vous allez retrouver tous ses copains dans nos magasins », détaille effectivement Thierry Cotillard dans une vidéo publiée sur Instagram ce mercredi. Il révèle à quoi ressemblent le lapin, le hérisson ou encore l’écureuil, sous forme de peluche.
Pourquoi la peluche loup d’Intermarché ne sera pas prête pour Noël 2026
« Vous l’avez sûrement remarqué, il y a un absent », ajoute-t-il. « Sur le format standard de la peluche du loup, elle ne sera malheureusement pas disponible pour Noël. » En cause, un problème découvert lors du contrôle qualité des peluches, un fournisseur n’ayant pas respecté le cahier des charges exigé par Intermarché. Il faudra donc, pour l’instant, se contenter de la version en porte-clés.
Thierry Cotillard indique que la fabrication de la peluche loup en format standard a été relancée dès à présent, et que la précommande sera possible « dans les prochains mois » sur un site dédié, « leloup.intermarche.com ». Ce site, qui ne renvoie pour l’instant vers rien, devrait être accessible à partir du 26 novembre.
Attention, dès à présent, aux potentielles arnaques. En fin d’année dernière, de faux sites prétendant vendre la peluche du loup d’Intermarché n’avaient pas tardé à émerger. Il existe un risque de voir surgir de nouveaux sites malveillants semblables, dans les prochains jours ou prochaines semaines.
Une « très grosse surprise » arrive
À la fin de la vidéo publiée sur Instagram aujourd’hui, Thierry Cotillard annonce une « très grosse surprise », qui devrait être révélée dans quelques semaines. Peut-être une nouvelle publicité racontant la suite des aventures du loup, avec ses nouveaux amis dans la forêt ? L’espoir semble permis.

articles.title: Falha no Java coloca sistemas de governos e empresas em alerta mundial
articles.text:
Governos de diferentes países emitiram alertas sobre a vulnerabilidade crítica no Java, uma das linguagens de programação mais utilizadas do mundo. A falha pode permitir que hackers acessem sistemas de computador, roubem informações confidenciais e assumam o controle de servidores. Autoridades recomendaram que empresas e organizações instalem imediatamente as correções disponíveis.
O problema foi identificado pela Calif, empresa de tecnologia dos Estados Unidos que, no mês anterior, havia encontrado uma vulnerabilidade em outra linguagem de programação, o PHP. Desta vez, a companhia descobriu erro nas funções de gerenciamento de memória do Java.
Os alertas partiram de autoridades dos Estados Unidos, Coreia do Sul, Alemanha e Reino Unido, além da Tencent, gigante chinesa de tecnologia. A agência de segurança cibernética da Holanda também informou que estava investigando o caso.
A preocupação foi especialmente forte na Coreia do Sul, onde o Java é amplamente utilizado. Segundo a agência de notícias Yonhap, o gabinete presidencial realizou reunião de emergência com órgãos do governo na terça-feira (17) para discutir medidas preventivas contra a ameaça.
Java é usado em sistemas críticos pelo mundo
- Disponível por meio da Oracle e de kits de desenvolvimento de código aberto, o Java está presente em sistemas de informação de governos, empresas, instituições financeiras e até das Forças Armadas;
- A Agência de Segurança Cibernética e de Infraestrutura dos Estados Unidos (CISA, na sigla em inglês) afirmou que a vulnerabilidade exige a aplicação imediata de correções. O órgão, porém, não estabeleceu relação entre a falha e as interrupções recentes em serviços tecnológicos;
- A Tencent Cloud, divisão de computação em nuvem da empresa chinesa, alertou seus clientes que a vulnerabilidade no kit de código aberto, identificada como “Java4Shell”, pode permitir que invasores sem autenticação roubem informações confidenciais ou assumam o controle de servidores afetados;
- Agências de segurança cibernética da Alemanha e da Holanda disseram não haver, até aquele momento, registros conhecidos de ataques bem-sucedidos que explorassem a falha. Já a agência britânica recomendou que empresas e organizações mantenham seus sistemas atualizados;
- A Oracle lançou, nesta terça-feira, uma atualização do Java Development Kit com correções para o problema.
Leia mais:
- Falha no iOS permitia gravação de áudio sem permissão do usuário
- IA acelera ataques cibernéticos e amplia incidentes nas empresas
- Ataque hacker atinge quase 200 sites e coloca usuários de iPhone na mira
Inteligência artificial (IA) facilita a ação de hackers
A vulnerabilidade foi identificada em momento de crescente preocupação com a segurança digital. Segundo a Reuters, os avanços rápidos da IA estão dando ferramentas cada vez mais poderosas tanto para criminosos quanto para profissionais de defesa cibernética.
A tecnologia pode acelerar a identificação e a exploração de brechas de segurança. Com isso, o intervalo disponível para que empresas corrijam vulnerabilidades pode diminuir de dias para horas ou até minutos.
No mês passado, governos e companhias de diferentes países chegaram a tirar sites do ar preventivamente enquanto operadores tentavam proteger sistemas que utilizavam PHP. A medida ocorreu depois que a Calif divulgou a descoberta de vulnerabilidade na linguagem.
Empresas de segurança cibernética também têm identificado casos de hackers usando IA para realizar dezenas de invasões simultaneamente.
Por outro lado, organizações estão recorrendo à própria tecnologia para examinar seus sistemas em busca de falhas e corrigir os problemas encontrados. Esse processo também envolve riscos, segundo Karolis Kaciulis, engenheiro-chefe de sistemas da Surfshark. “Aplicar tantas correções em tão pouco tempo torna os sistemas menos estáveis”, afirmou o especialista à Reuters.
Sequência de falhas aumenta preocupação com infraestrutura digital
Os alertas sobre o Java surgiram em meio a uma série de interrupções tecnológicas registradas nos últimos dias. Entre os episódios estão uma falha na Agência de Segurança Nacional dos Estados Unidos (NSA, na sigla em inglês), problemas em serviços da Apple e instabilidades em plataformas da Microsoft.
A Apple enfrentou interrupção na terça-feira após atualização interna afetar serviços, como iCloud e Apple Pay. Os sistemas foram restabelecidos nesta quarta-feira (18).
Também houve paralisação de quatro horas e meia no tráfego aéreo dos Estados Unidos, além de problema de software no JPMorgan Chase que afetou alguns serviços bancários.
Apesar da proximidade entre os episódios, autoridades e empresas não relacionaram as interrupções à vulnerabilidade no Java. O secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos, Marco Rubio, que também atua como conselheiro de segurança nacional, reconheceu que os incidentes eram preocupantes, mas afirmou que não tinham relação entre si.
Coreia do Sul tem alta dependência do Java
A preocupação sul-coreana também está relacionada à presença expressiva da linguagem no país. Uma pesquisa da JetBrains, empresa que desenvolve ferramentas para programação, apontou que o Java representava 53% do uso de linguagens de programação na Coreia do Sul em 2021. A média global era de 30%.
No setor público sul-coreano, a participação era ainda maior: 72% do uso de linguagens de programação em sistemas de informação, segundo pesquisa do governo realizada no ano passado.
A China também possui comunidade expressiva de desenvolvedores Java. Uma pesquisa da JetBrains de 2025, voltada à linguagem, apontou que 37% dos participantes estavam na China continental. A empresa ressalta, porém, que esse número representa a composição da amostra, e não a participação desses países no total global de desenvolvedores Java.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Codes de triche GTA 6 : la liste complète et comment les débloquer
articles.text:
Vingt-cinq ans après le premier GUNSGUNSGUNS tapé au clavier dans GTA III, Rockstar n’a pas renoncé à la tradition : GTA 6 a ses codes de triche. Il y en a soixante et un, très exactement selon PCgamer.
Le temps d’une session, ils font de Vice City et du reste de Leonida un terrain de jeu sans règles. Encore faut-il les mériter : Rockstar les réserve à ceux qui ont bouclé l’histoire, et chaque code se gagne ensuite par un défi. Nous complétons cette liste au fil des découvertes.
Comment activer les codes de triche dans GTA 6 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S
Tout se passe dans le menu Progression, onglet Codes de triche. Les 61 codes y sont répartis en cinq catégories : Joueur, Combat, Générer un véhicule, Environnement et Filtres d’écran. Les habitués y chercheront en vain l’invincibilité ou la santé instantanée. Rockstar a préféré des effets plus inattendus, du flamant rose gonflable à seize filtres d’écran.
Le système est aussi bien plus exigeant que dans GTA 5. Le menu reste verrouillé tant que vous n’avez pas terminé les 91 missions de l’histoire de Jason et Lucia. Chaque code se débloque ensuite à part, en remplissant une condition précise : médailles au stand de tir, montres de collection, catégorie de défis à boucler… Bonne nouvelle, le jeu tient compte de ce que vous avez déjà accompli pendant l’aventure.
- PlayStation : Pour activer un code, ouvrez votre iFruit (comprenez le smartphone Apple de GTA) d’une pression sur la flèche haut, maintenez L1 et R1, puis saisissez la combinaison à la croix directionnelle.
- Xbox : Sur Xbox Series X|S, la manipulation devrait être la même avec LB et RB. Inutile, a priori, de tenter une combinaison trouvée en ligne avant d’avoir rempli la condition : selon les premiers retours, elle reste sans effet.
Avant de semer le chaos à Leonida, gardez en tête qu’une fois un code activé, la sauvegarde et les trophées sont bloqués jusqu’à la fin de la session. Impossible, donc, de tricher pour avancer dans les défis ou les missions secondaires.

Y a-t-il des codes de triche dans GTA 6 ?
Oui. Comme tous les épisodes principaux de la série, GTA 6 propose des codes de triche : 61 au total, utilisables en mode histoire sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Il faut d’abord terminer l’histoire, puis débloquer chaque code.
Faut-il finir GTA 6 pour utiliser les codes de triche ?
Oui. Le menu des codes reste verrouillé tant que les 91 missions de l’histoire principale ne sont pas terminées. Chaque code se débloque ensuite par sa propre condition, et les objectifs remplis pendant l’aventure comptent déjà.
De GUNSGUNSGUNS à Vice City : petite histoire des codes de triche dans GTA
Les codes de triche accompagnent la série depuis ses débuts. Dans le premier GTA, en 1997, on les saisissait en guise de nom de joueur. GTA III a installé la formule moderne en 2001 : sur console, on enchaînait les touches de la manette ; sur PC, on tapait des mots au clavier, GUNSGUNSGUNS pour obtenir toutes les armes. San Andreas a ensuite popularisé HESOYAM : santé, armure et 250 000 dollars d’un coup.
GTA IV a fait passer la triche par le téléphone, avec des numéros à composer. GTA 5 a fini par réunir les trois méthodes (manette, téléphone et console sur PC), mais a supprimé l’argent facile : aucun code ne remplissait le compte en banque de Michael, Franklin ou Trevor.
Red Dead Redemption 2 a changé de logique avec des phrases à saisir dans un menu, dont une partie se dénichait dans les journaux du jeu au fil de l’aventure.
GTA 6 fait la synthèse. Il reprend le téléphone de GTA IV et GTA 5, et des combinaisons de touches comme à l’époque de la PS2, réduites à la seule croix directionnelle. Il garde aussi le déblocage au mérite de Red Dead Redemption 2, en le poussant beaucoup plus loin.
Y a-t-il un code d’argent illimité dans GTA 6 ?
Pas illimité, mais Rockstar a fait un geste. Un code verse 250 000 dollars, pile le montant de HESOYAM, avec la combinaison ↑ → ↓ ← ↑ ← ↓ →. Sa condition de déblocage n’est pas encore connue. Et le butin ne se garde pas : la sauvegarde étant bloquée dès qu’un code est activé, ces dollars s’évaporent en toute logique à la fin de la session. Pour remplir durablement votre compte en banque, il faudra toujours gagner vos dollars à l’ancienne, en braquant des banques, en revendant des voitures volées ou en pratiquant toute autre sorte d’activités illicites.
Les codes de GTA 5 fonctionnent-ils dans GTA 6 ?
Non. Quelques effets font leur retour, comme l’ivresse, la météo, le parachute ou la Sanchez, mais les combinaisons n’ont rien à voir. GTA 6 se contente de la croix directionnelle, quand GTA 5 mobilisait aussi les boutons et les gâchettes. Et sans version PC pour l’instant, adieu TURTLE, PAINKILLER et autres mots à taper.
Risque-t-on d’être banni en utilisant des codes de triche ?
Non. Les codes sont prévus par Rockstar et ne fonctionnent qu’en solo : ils ne vous exposent à aucune sanction. Le risque concerne les mods et menus de triche utilisés en ligne, que Rockstar sanctionne depuis des années dans GTA Online.
Trophées et sauvegarde : ce que la triche vous coûte
Rockstar n’a jamais laissé tricher sans contrepartie. Dans GTA 5, le premier code activé désactivait les trophées et succès jusqu’à la fin de la session. Red Dead Redemption 2 allait plus loin en bloquant aussi la sauvegarde. GTA 6 reprend cette ligne dure : dès le premier code saisi, impossible de sauvegarder ou de décrocher un trophée jusqu’à la fin de la session.
Comment désactiver un code de triche ?
Une fois un code activé, la sauvegarde reste bloquée. Le moyen le plus sûr de retrouver une partie normale est donc de quitter sans sauvegarder, puis de recharger votre dernière sauvegarde : vous repartez sans aucun effet actif.

articles.title: Microrobots del tamaño de un grano de arroz prometen disolver coágulos 6 veces más rápido: cómo funcionan
articles.text:
Cuando un coágulo obstruye una arteria, los médicos disponen de fármacos capaces de disolverlo, pero enfrentan un obstáculo físico: si el bloqueo es muy grande, la propia masa impide que el medicamento llegue adonde debe actuar.
Investigadores de la ETH Zúrich, en Suiza, desarrollaron una solución que combina esos fármacos con microrrobots magnéticos del tamaño de un grano de arroz. Los dispositivos empujan la droga directamente hacia la obstrucción, donde la medicación sola no logra llegar.
El estudio, llevado a cabo por un equipo de la Universidad Técnica Federal Suiza, demostró que la combinación de microrobots y trombolíticos disuelve los coágulos seis veces más rápido que el fármaco administrado por sí solo. En pruebas con cerdos vivos, la zona con circulación restaurada fue el doble tras apenas 30 minutos de tratamiento combinado, frente al grupo que solo recibió medicación.
Los robots miden ocho micrómetros y están fabricados con un polímero magnético
Cada microrobot tiene ocho micrómetros de longitud —menos que el diámetro de un glóbulo rojo— y adopta la forma de un grano de arroz. Su estructura combina un polímero a base de azúcar con nanopartículas de óxido de hierro magnético. Durante la fabricación, los dispositivos se exponen a un campo magnético rotatorio que alinea esas partículas en línea recta y forma un imán interno.
Un sistema de control externo aplica luego un campo rotatorio que hace girar ese imán y provoca que el robot ruede por las paredes del vaso. Los bots no transportan droga: se liberan cerca de la oclusión junto con el trombolítico y, al desplazarse, generan corrientes que llevan el compuesto hacia el interior del trombo.
En laboratorio, el método multiplicó por seis la velocidad de disolución respecto al fármaco solo
Para validar la técnica en condiciones controladas, el equipo de la ETH Zúrich construyó una red artificial de canales similares a vasos y los obstruyó con trombos elaborados con sangre porcina. Al comparar el tratamiento con medicamento solo contra la combinación con los microrobots, la diferencia fue contundente: la disolución se produjo seis veces más rápido cuando los dispositivos participaron en el proceso.
Los resultados en animales vivos confirmaron la tendencia observada en el laboratorio. Los investigadores bloquearon arterias en cerdos y los trataron, en grupos separados, con trombolíticos solos o junto con los bots. Tras 30 minutos, el área con circulación recuperada fue el doble en los ejemplares que recibieron ambas intervenciones.
“Hasta donde sabemos, somos los primeros en demostrar en un modelo de animal grande, clínicamente relevante, que el uso de microrobots de esta manera mejora efectivamente la trombolisis”, afirmó un integrante del equipo en un comunicado de la universidad.
El trabajo se suma a una línea de investigación creciente, aunque los ensayos en humanos están lejos
Este avance se enmarca en un campo que gana terreno en la medicina. El año pasado, otro grupo de la ETH Zúrich, liderado por Bradley Nelson, publicó en la revista Science un trabajo sobre una cápsula de gel disolvente que podía guiarse por vasos y liberar un anticoagulante al calentarse mediante un campo magnético de alta frecuencia.
Otros equipos adoptaron métodos más mecánicos. Científicos de la Universidad de Twente y del Centro Médico Universitario Radboud, en los Países Bajos, desarrollaron dispositivos con forma de tornillo y pequeños imanes internos, fabricados con impresión 3D, que perforaban trombos en arterias de ovejas hasta restablecer la circulación.
En cuanto al trabajo del equipo suizo, los investigadores presentaron una solicitud de patente para sus bots. Sin embargo, los resultados aún no superaron la revisión por pares y los ensayos clínicos en humanos se encuentran en una etapa muy inicial. La investigación marca, de todas formas, un paso concreto hacia el uso de microrobots como herramienta complementaria en el tratamiento de obstrucciones vasculares graves.

articles.title: Tesla peut déployer sa conduite autonome en Finlande, mais la France résiste toujours
articles.text:
Tesla franchit une nouvelle étape dans le déploiement de son système de conduite autonome en Europe. Le constructeur américain vient d’obtenir le feu vert de Traficom, l’agence finlandaise des transports et des communications. Il pourra prochainement commercialiser son système Tesla Assisted Driving auprès des propriétaires d’environ 6 500 véhicules compatibles. La Finlande rejoint ainsi les dix autres pays européens ayant reconnu l’homologation provisoire délivrée aux Pays-Bas en avril. Mais la France reste encore à convaincre.
Tesla Assisted Driving : ce qui change pour les automobilistes finlandais
Le FSD (Full Self-Driving) de Tesla change de nom et devient Tesla Assisted Driving. Une évolution réclamée par plusieurs responsables politiques européens, qui jugeaient l’ancienne appellation trompeuse pour un système nécessitant toujours la surveillance du conducteur. « Le changement de nom aide les utilisateurs et le marché à comprendre la vraie nature du système », explique Jukka Juhola, expert principal chez Traficom.
La Finlande autorise son déploiement avant même le vote européen. L’agence justifie sa décision par ce changement de nom, mais aussi par les modifications apportées à la gestion de la vitesse. Jusqu’à présent, le FSD pouvait autoriser un dépassement de 50 % de la limitation. Cette marge est désormais réduite à 10 % et revient à zéro à chaque démarrage du véhicule.
L’arrivée de l’hiver a également pesé dans la décision. Traficom préfère laisser aux propriétaires le temps de découvrir le système avant les premières chutes de neige et l’apparition du verglas. Les caméras peuvent en effet être perturbées par la neige, la neige fondue ou les saletés. L’agence recommande notamment de garder les mains sur le volant face à une plaque de verglas, une flaque de profondeur inconnue ou de fortes rafales de vent.
Car, malgré son nouveau nom, le Tesla Assisted Driving ne rend pas les voitures autonomes. Le conducteur reste responsable de la conduite et doit pouvoir reprendre le contrôle à tout moment, y compris en cas d’excès de vitesse.
La France toujours réticente face au système de Tesla
En France, le constructeur américain est encore loin d’obtenir une autorisation. En juillet dernier, le ministre des Transports, Philippe Tabarot, avait notamment critiqué la possibilité de dépasser jusqu’à 50 % la vitesse autorisée, mais aussi le manque de garanties concernant la vigilance du conducteur lors des changements de voie, aux intersections et dans les ronds-points.
En septembre, une visioconférence avec Elon Musk a toutefois permis d’ouvrir le dialogue. Le gouvernement a depuis autorisé des essais sur route avec deux véhicules Tesla, sans pour autant s’engager sur une reconnaissance de l’homologation néerlandaise.
Tesla encore loin de convaincre l’ensemble de l’Europe
Le dossier doit désormais passer devant le comité technique des véhicules à moteur (TCMV), qui réunit les représentants des 27 États membres. Un vote était initialement attendu le 6 octobre, mais le comité ne devrait finalement pas se réunir à nouveau avant décembre.
Pour obtenir une reconnaissance européenne, Tesla doit réunir au moins 15 États représentant 65 % de la population de l’Union. Malgré onze pays favorables, le constructeur ne rassemble pour l’instant qu’environ 70 millions d’habitants sur 450 millions, soit un peu plus de 15 %.
L’Allemagne pourrait apporter son soutien après avoir obtenu les modifications réclamées à Tesla. Mais même avec Berlin, les pays favorables ne représenteraient qu’environ un tiers de la population européenne. Le constructeur devra donc encore convaincre plusieurs grands marchés, dont la France, l’Italie et l’Espagne. La généralisation du Tesla Assisted Driving en Europe n’est donc pas encore pour demain.

articles.title: Emerging cryptographic requirements and the transition to quantum-resistant security
articles.text:
Emerging cryptographic requirements and the transition to quantum-resistant security
Encryption forms the backbone of our everyday digital lives including banking transactions, healthcare and communication. However, the rise of quantum computing is challenging our assumptions about how long certain types of security will remain effective.
Imagine a scenario where confidential information that was encrypted and sent years ago is suddenly able to be decrypted. The security systems worked as intended, the information was exchanged, the encryption algorithms were considered secure and there was no evidence of a breach. However, advances in computing have made that formerly secure information vulnerable. This is a concern that is driving the discussion about quantum resistant security.
We use encryption to secure almost every aspect of our digital lives. From banking transactions and healthcare data to industrial communications and defence systems, the encryption algorithms we use to secure sensitive information have been trusted for decades. However, the rise of quantum computing is challenging our assumptions about how long certain types of security will remain effective.
While quantum computers that can crack popular public-key cryptography aren't currently available, the possibility of this is an important consideration for organisations that need to ensure long term security of data.
Understanding the threat of quantum
Cybersecurity as we know it today relies on different types of cryptography for different purposes. We use Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithms to secure data. We use public-key cryptography like RSA and elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) for securing key establishment, authentication and digital signatures.
Quantum computing presents different challenges to these cryptographic systems. With Shor's algorithm, a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could potentially solve the mathematical problems behind RSA and ECC, thus compromising systems that rely on these cryptographic systems.
With Grover's algorithm, we have the theoretical speed up for searching for keys in symmetric encryption. For AES-256, this reduces the theoretical security margin against brute force attacks, however, this doesn't make AES-256 practically breakable with current quantum computing. This is important because we need to know what types of cryptographic systems are most at risk before we can determine what we need to change.
Another concern is that attackers could potentially collect encrypted information today, and hold on to it for decryption in the future. This approach is called harvest now, decrypt later, and it poses risks for information that must be secure for many years. Sensitive defence communications, financial data, intellectual property may remain valuable for a long time after the initial transmission.
Why existing infrastructure makes the transition difficult
While replacing an encryption algorithm may seem like a simple task, the digital infrastructure we use today consists of multiple interconnected systems with different security needs.
For example, imagine an industrial facility with hundreds of connected sensors, controllers and communication devices. Some of these devices may have been installed years ago, and may remain in use for another decade. Others may have limited processing power, memory or network connectivity.We need to consider carefully when introducing new cryptographic mechanisms to these systems.
With post-quantum cryptographic algorithms we may need larger keys, signatures, or more processing compared to current public-key cryptographic mechanisms. These differences can impact communication bandwidth, memory usage and processing performance. For real-time devices, any changes in computational requirements may impact the system design.
Thus, we need to consider the entire security architecture. This includes device authentication, key management, communication protocols and hardware compatibility. It's not just about updating software to make it quantum resistant.
What do emerging cryptographic standards mean?
We are starting to see the shift towards post-quantum cryptography. The US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) finalised three post-quantum cryptographic standards in August 2024. These are: ML-KEM for key establishment, and ML-DSA and SLH-DSA for digital signatures.
These standards provide organisations with defined cryptographic mechanisms designed to resist attacks from both conventional and quantum computers. However, implementing these standards isn't just a matter of replacing cryptographic algorithms.
We need to identify vulnerable cryptography that we use, understand how encryption keys are generated and exchanged, and consider whether existing systems can support the requirements. Alternative approaches like out-of-band key distribution, and quantum key distribution are also being explored. These approaches offer different security properties, but come with practical considerations such as infrastructure, cost, scalability and interoperability.
There's no one size fits all approach that meets all operational requirements. The right architecture depends on the sensitivity of the information, devices involved and environment where communication occurs.
Building cryptographic agility into security systems
One of the most important things organisations can do to prepare is to build cryptographic agility. This involves designing systems that can adapt to changes in cryptographic algorithms and protocols without major infrastructure changes.
● Firstly, organisations need to understand their cryptographic dependencies. What cryptographic algorithms are being used? Where are the keys being stored? How are devices authenticated? What systems may be challenging to update?
● Secondly, prioritise. Systems protecting sensitive long-lived information, or systems in critical infrastructure may need earlier planning for migration.
Using hybrid cryptographic approaches (using both existing classical mechanisms and post-quantum cryptographic algorithms) can help in managing the transition while still being compatible during the migration process.
For connected and embedded systems, security should also be considered when designing hardware and software. Devices that are expected to be in use for many years should support secure updates and be adaptable to changing cryptographic mechanisms where technically possible.
Preparing before the threat becomes imminent
Transitioning to quantum resistant security will be a gradual process. With existing infrastructure, operational constraints and evolving standards, organisations will need to carefully plan for migration strategies.
This is especially challenging for sectors like banking, telecommunications, manufacturing and defence, where we often have sensitive information and connected infrastructure with long operational lifecycles.
We don't need quantum computing to be an imminent threat to start preparing. Information encrypted today may need to be secure for decades. Systems deployed today may be in use long after the cryptographic requirements have changed.
The focus should be on understanding our current vulnerabilities, considering emerging standards and building systems that can adapt to the changing landscape of cryptographic technology.
The future of cybersecurity will be as much about being able to update and maintain trusted security as it is about the strength of the encryption algorithms we use.
~ By Srinivas Shekar, Co-Founder and CEO, Pantherun Technologies

articles.title: La rectificación de Franganillo por su agresiva entrevista con Sánchez evidencia que esta es la campaña más tensa vista en televisión
articles.text:
Una entrevista al presidente del Gobierno en plena campaña, emitida en la edición de noche de Informativos Telecinco, reunió a 997.000 espectadores. A la mañana siguiente, el periodista Carlos Franganillo, que la condujo, llegó a pasar por dos programas de su cadena para pedir disculpas por unas formas que se consideraron excesivas, y que son buen ejemplo de lo bronco que está siendo el paso por medios de los distintos candidatos de cara a las elecciones.
Qué pasó. Franganillo entrevistó a Pedro Sánchez el lunes 16 de noviembre en la edición de las 21:00 de Informativos Telecinco, la primera de la ronda que la cadena ha preparado con los candidatos. Al día siguiente, en 'La mirada crítica', admitió ante Ana Terradillos que hubo “una gestión de tiempos que se me escapó de las manos”. Por la mesa entrevista pasaron temas como la amnistía ("Hice de la necesidad virtud"), la promesa de construir 100.000 viviendas más y la DANA, sobre la que Sánchez repitió que "el señor Mazón no quiso una intervención ni ceder el mando".
El conflicto. En la entrevista se percibieron dos choques distintos. El primero fue de tiempo: cuando Franganillo pidió respuestas más cortas, Sánchez replicó: "Usted habla y yo también tengo derecho a hablar". Más tarde insistió: "Me deja terminar esta cuestión y luego ya me pregunta lo que quiera".
El segundo choque fue con las temáticas. Al entrar a la cuestión de Ceuta y a la entrada masiva del 30 y 31 de julio, el periodista aludió a la falta de reacción preventiva y Sánchez le cortó con un "a lo mejor usted está mal informado". Según se excusó el presidente, el Gobierno trabajaba con Marruecos "desde el 8 de junio para poner una frontera física". El tono contrasta con el de su paso por ‘La Revuelta’ en octubre, cuando admitió ante Broncano que “podríamos haberlo gestionado mejor”.
Si ha molestado, pues perdón. La autocrítica de Franganillo del día siguiente se limitó al cronómetro. Sobre Ceuta, el periodista insiste en que "no fue una mala información por mi parte, lo tengo que decir con toda humildad", y recordó que el propio Sánchez culpó a grupos mafiosos tras el asalto. El 31 de julio, desde Ceuta, el presidente atribuyó en efecto la avalancha a las "redes de las mafias". Horas después Franganillo repitió estas ideas en 'El programa de AR', aunque reconoció que hubo más tensión de la que él habría querido.
Las audiencias. La entrevista consiguió un 7,8% de cuota y 997.000 espectadores. No superó a sus rivales: en la misma franja, Antena 3 Noticias 2 sumó 2.325.000 y el Telediario de La 1, 1.754.000. Algunos medios han calificado la entrevista de "insólito pinchazo", ya que hasta ahora el paso de Sánchez por televisión ha tenido cifras mucho mejores. Eso sí, hay letra pequeña (que no amortigua demasiado la debacle de Mediaset): los audímetros de Fifty5Blue, la antigua Kantar Media, solo miden televisión lineal en directo, así que los cortes que Telecinco colgó el martes en Mediaset Infinity quedan fuera de ese 7,8%.
Sánchez a sus anchas. El resto de la gira de Sánchez por el prime time se mueve en otras cifras. Su paso por 'La Revuelta' el 22 de octubre congregó a 4.387.000 espectadores. El 9 de noviembre, en La Séptima, una cadena con menos de una semana en antena, logró 2.160.000 frente a la entrevista de Broncano a Abascal. Desde el 22 de octubre suman 11.175.000 espectadores con una media de 2.235.000, muy por encima de la de Franganillo.
Past tense. Los dos protagonistas ya habían vivido previamente una escena muy similar. El 18 de febrero de 2019, Franganillo recibió a Sánchez en el Telediario en su primera entrevista desde que anunció el adelanto electoral. Por entonces hizo un 9,2% con 1.672.000 espectadores. Con cualquiera de las dos cifras, siete años y un cambio de cadena después, el mismo formato pierde entre 675.000 y 853.000 espectadores, lo que dice mucho del delicado momento que atraviesa Mediaset.
Campaña accidentada. Desde que se anunciaron las elecciones, el calendario mediático del presidente se ha convertido en una auténtica carrera de obstáculos. Su aparición en ‘Salvados’, prevista para el 1 de noviembre, se cayó porque la grabación se suspendió tras el accidente ferroviario de Urda, y finalmente se emitirá el domingo 22. Con los debates ha pasado algo parecido. El 22 de octubre, el PSOE aceptó un cara a cara con Feijóo en Mediaset para el lunes 16. Ese lunes, Sánchez acabó en el plató de Telecinco, pero frente a Franganillo: el duelo con Feijóo se cerró al final para el jueves 19 en la Academia de la Televisión, con María Casado de moderadora.

articles.title: Telegram sur Android a renforcé sa sécurité mais des chercheurs ont contourné le nouveau filtre
articles.text:
Dans une vidéo de la société de sécurité NebuSec, un widget envoyé par un bot dans une conversation Telegram ouvre la calculatrice d’un téléphone Android, malgré le filtre que la messagerie a ajouté la semaine dernière à son application.
Telegram laisse ses bots envoyer des widgets depuis le 9 novembre. Ces petits blocs interactifs s’affichent dans le message, et leur code JavaScript s’exécute sur votre téléphone. Deux jours plus tard, le compte V12 a affirmé sur X que n’importe quel message Telegram permettait d’exécuter du code à distance. Telegram a alors placé dans un processus à part le moteur QuickJS, qui fait tourner le JavaScript des widgets sur Android. Avec un filtre seccomp, un mécanisme du noyau Linux, l’application bloque ou enregistre certaines requêtes de ce moteur au système, appelées appels système. Selon The HackerNews, mes chercheurs de NebuSec affirment avoir exécuté du code en dehors de ce filtre, par deux méthodes différentes.
Telegram laisse passer la plupart des appels système des widgets
Dans le code source de Telegram pour Android 13.2.2 (7303), l’entreprise ne bloque que quelques dizaines d’appels système, dont ptrace, bpf et mount, et laisse passer tous les autres. Ses développeurs n’ont pas filtré ioctl, l’appel qui sert à dialoguer avec les pilotes du matériel. Ils ont en outre réglé le filtre en mode audit, d’après le code examiné par The Hacker News. Dans ce mode, l’application empêche toujours le moteur de lancer un nouveau programme, mais elle se contente d’enregistrer les autres appels interdits, avant de les laisser passer. Un commentaire des développeurs prévoit de garder ce réglage « jusqu’à ce que les journaux des appareils indiquent que le moteur ne les génère plus ». Rien ne dit si la version installée sur votre téléphone utilise ce réglage.
Dans sa documentation, Telegram promet aux développeurs un environnement isolé, sans accès au réseau. Mais selon NebuSec, ces règles sont inscrites dans le code de QuickJS. Il suffit d’une faille d’utilisation après libération (use-after-free) ou d’écriture hors limites dans le moteur pour qu’un script lise et modifie la mémoire du processus, et la protection ne sert plus à rien. Et Telegram fait tourner tous les widgets dans un seul processus. Un widget détourné partage donc sa mémoire avec les widgets de tous les autres bots, ajoutent les chercheurs.
Leur première méthode exploite une faille des widgets que Telegram n’a pas prise en compte dans son filtre. La seconde associe une faille couverte par le filtre et une faille du noyau. Toutefois, les chercheurs ont mené leur démonstration sur un serveur de test de Telegram, car seuls des bots autorisés envoient aujourd’hui des widgets sur le service ouvert au public. Ils ne disent pas jusqu’où leur code peut aller, vers vos messages ou le reste du téléphone, ni si vous devez d’abord lancer le bot ou toucher le widget. NebuSec garde les détails techniques pour plus tard, ne mentionne aucun identifiant CVE et ne dit pas si elle a prévenu Telegram.
Telegram restreint les widgets sans publier de correctif
Sur le service ouvert au public, Telegram ne laisse plus que des bots autorisés envoyer des widgets, et NebuSec a dû passer par un serveur de test pour sa démonstration. « Oui, actuellement, les bots classiques ne sont pas autorisés à utiliser de widgets, même dans les conversations privées », confirmait la semaine dernière un contributeur du projet telegram-bot-api sur GitHub. Telegram n’a pas indiqué quels bots gardent ce droit, ni si la restriction a été levée depuis. Les chercheurs ne mentionnent aucune version corrigée, et le code source publié par l’entreprise s’arrête cette semaine à la version 13.2.2 (7303).
Telegram avait assuré avoir corrigé le problème montré dans la première vidéo de V12, et déployé le correctif chez tous ses utilisateurs. Son patron, Pavel Durov, a ensuite répondu aux signalements d’exécution de code dans les applications Android et Windows. « Personne ne peut être piraté simplement en recevant un message », a écrit le PDG sur sa chaîne Telegram. Selon lui, il faut d’abord lancer un service tiers, et Telegram a corrigé ce service côté serveur. En avril 2024, l’entreprise avait aussi bloqué depuis ses serveurs une faille zero day de son application pour Windows, née d’une faute de frappe de ses développeurs.
Mais Pavel Durov a publié son message avant la démonstration de NebuSec, et les chercheurs ne disent pas si vous devez lancer le bot, ou toucher le widget, pour que leur code s’exécute.
