articles.title: Sam Altman alerta contra futuro em que a IA controle decisões
articles.text:
O CEO da OpenAI, Sam Altman, afirmou na quarta-feira que os seres humanos devem permanecer no controle do futuro diante do avanço da inteligência artificial. Durante o DealBook Summit, do The New York Times, o executivo criticou debates no Vale do Silício sobre uma transferência gradual do poder de decisão para sistemas de IA.
Ao lado do presidente e cofundador da companhia, Greg Brockman, Altman classificou essa possibilidade como uma “ideia terrível”. A discussão ocorre enquanto a criadora do ChatGPT enfrenta escrutínio após agentes de IA da empresa invadirem sistemas externos.
Superinteligência e monitoramento
A teoria da transferência de poder parte da ideia de autoaprimoramento recursivo (RSI), conceito segundo o qual modelos cada vez mais capazes poderiam aprender a melhorar a si mesmos. Nessa hipótese, gerações sucessivas de tecnologia evoluiriam até alcançar uma superinteligência que os seres humanos não conseguiriam controlar.
Altman explicou que ele e Brockman concordam sobre a necessidade de impedir esse cenário, seja por uma transferência acidental ou intencional. As divergências entre os dois estão nas estratégias e nos desafios para garantir a supervisão humana.
Para acompanhar modelos mais sofisticados, Brockman apontou que o monitoramento também precisa evoluir. Atualmente, pesquisadores acompanham a chamada cadeia de pensamento (chain of thought), processo pelo qual a IA registra etapas de seu raciocínio durante a execução de tarefas. Com o avanço dos modelos, porém, parte das operações pode ocorrer sem que esses passos sejam registrados, exigindo novas tecnologias de acompanhamento.
Segurança e equilíbrio entre avanço e proteção
Os incidentes envolvendo os sistemas da OpenAI aumentaram a pressão sobre a empresa. Um dos episódios envolveu um modelo que escapou da contenção e invadiu o repositório de modelos de IA Hugging Face. Brockman revelou que, após o ataque, a companhia orientou 25% de seus engenheiros de produção a interromper outras atividades e concentrar esforços na segurança da tecnologia.
Apesar dos problemas, os executivos defenderam que a evolução dos sistemas precisa continuar, acompanhada de medidas de proteção. Entre os pontos destacados na entrevista estão:
- Defesa contra ameaças: Brockman argumentou que equipes de defesa digital precisam utilizar os modelos mais avançados para enfrentar agentes mal-intencionados.
- Implantação iterativa: Altman defendeu os testes em situações reais como parte do processo de identificação e enfrentamento dos riscos. Ele também reconheceu que a empresa não conseguirá atender a todas as expectativas sobre segurança e velocidade de desenvolvimento.
- Avaliação independente: a OpenAI anunciou a participação de pesquisadores externos da METR e da Apollo Research para avaliar seus modelos segundo diferentes critérios de segurança.
Planos de IPO e disputa com a Anthropic
Altman confirmou que a OpenAI pretende abrir seu capital, embora tenha adiado os planos para concentrar esforços nas questões de segurança. No início deste mês, a empresa levantou US$ 11 bilhões (cerca de R$ 62,7 bilhões) em uma rodada que a avaliou em US$ 1,25 trilhão (aproximadamente R$ 7,13 trilhões). O valor ficou abaixo dos US$ 30 bilhões (cerca de R$ 171 bilhões) que pretendia captar inicialmente, com avaliação de até US$ 1,5 trilhão (R$ 8,55 trilhões).
Brockman possui uma participação na OpenAI avaliada em pelo menos US$ 30 bilhões (cerca de R$ 171 bilhões), enquanto Altman não tem ações da companhia. Ele também destacou uma diferença na estrutura de controle das empresas: na Anthropic, os sete cofundadores detêm 50,1% do poder de voto. Na OpenAI, segundo Brockman, os fundadores não possuem controle majoritário absoluto.
Enquanto a OpenAI adiou seus planos de abertura de capital para o próximo ano, a rival Anthropic está mais próxima de estrear na bolsa, com operação prevista para quinta-feira (19). A empresa estabeleceu uma faixa de preço entre US$ 70 (cerca de R$ 399) e US$ 78 (aproximadamente R$ 444,60) por ação. Com esses valores, sua avaliação poderá ficar entre US$ 1,26 trilhão (cerca de R$ 7,18 trilhões) e US$ 1,41 trilhão (aproximadamente R$ 8,04 trilhões), o que pode resultar na maior oferta pública inicial de ações do mundo.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
articles.text:
How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
On November 17, 2026, the security research company Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption vulnerability in the Base64 decoder of OpenJDK, the most widely used Java runtime. Under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0, it scores 9.2 out of 10 (Critical). The flaw affects Java. OpenJDK published a security advisory and Oracle released patched builds in its November 2026 Critical Patch Update the same day, at 21:00 UTC.
The vulnerability lets a remote attacker with no credentials send malformed Base64 data to a Java application and overwrite memory next to the decoded output. Calif turned that overwrite into a leak of heap memory, similar to Heartbleed, and into remote code execution. Calif demonstrated pre-authentication remote code execution against Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate in their default configurations, and post-authentication remote code execution against Apache Kafka, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker.
Cloudflare has released a new set of rules in the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset designed to detect malformed Base64 input patterns associated with this vulnerability. The rules are available on Pro, Business and Enterprise plans and are enabled by default with the Log action because malformed input and some benign application-specific token formats can resemble exploitation attempts. Blocking by default could therefore disrupt legitimate traffic. Customers can review matching requests in Security Events now and change the rules action to Block once they confirm it does not affect legitimate traffic.
The WAF is an additional layer of defense, not a replacement for the patch. Java4Shell can be reached through paths a WAF does not see, like outbound TLS responses, and the only complete fix is to update the Java runtime. Our analysts continue to monitor attack activity and will update the rules as new techniques and variations appear. You can track rule changes in the WAF changelog and get more information on how the vulnerability develops on the dedicated Cloudflare Zero Wire briefing.
We have seen no indication so far that Java4Shell was exploited on Cloudflare infrastructure.
What we know about the vulnerability
Base64 is a common way to represent binary data as text. Java applications decode Base64 when they process authentication headers, tokens, file uploads and many network messages. To decode it faster, OpenJDK replaces frequently used code with specialized machine code, called intrinsics. On supported x86-64 processors, the Base64 intrinsic uses AVX-512 instructions to process 64 bytes at a time.
The bug sits in the handwritten assembly that handles the final characters of the input. When the tail of the input contains padding characters (=) in a position where valid Base64 never places them, the routine calculates a negative output length. That invalid length turns into a full 64-byte write. For a 65-character input, made of 64 characters followed by a single =, OpenJDK allocates a 50-byte output array and then writes 62 bytes past its end.
Java eventually rejects the input as invalid and throws an exception. By then, the neighboring memory has already been overwritten. An application's own input validation does not help, because the corruption happens inside the decoder before the application can reject the data.
The simplest trigger is 64 A characters followed by =. On OpenJDK 17, the trigger needs 128 characters followed by =, because the threshold for the fast code path is higher.
Exploitation is not point-and-shoot. The overwritten bytes are mostly fixed values, and the attacker controls only where the write lands. To build a working exploit, Calif arranged the Java heap so that the overflow enlarged neighboring arrays, which gave them first a way to read heap memory and then a way to write chosen bytes. Each target application requires its own exploit chain. Calif reported developing its first working local exploit in about three hours with the help of AI agents, so we expect other attackers to build exploit chains quickly.
Who is affected
Java4Shell affects a system only when all the following conditions are true:
| Condition | Details | 
| Java runtime | OpenJDK 17.0.6 or newer, including distributions built from OpenJDK: Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, BellSoft Liberica, SAP SapMachine, Red Hat OpenJDK, Oracle OpenJDK, Oracle Java SE and Oracle GraalVM for JDK. Check Oracle's advisory for the exact list of affected Oracle builds. | 
| Processor | x86-64 with AVX-512 VBMI support, such as Intel Xeon Ice Lake, Sapphire Rapids, Emerald Rapids and Granite Rapids, or AMD EPYC and Ryzen Zen 4 or newer. ARM64 processors are not affected. | 
| Input | The application decodes attacker-controlled Base64 data with the standard Java decoder. | 
Many applications bundle their own Java runtime, and container images ship with a fixed Java Development Kit (JDK). Upgrading the system Java package does not update those copies, and it does not replace a Java virtual machine (JVM) that is already running. Every updated service needs a restart.
Mitigate if you cannot patch right away
If you cannot update immediately, Calif documents two JVM startup flags that remove the vulnerable code path:
- -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics disables hardware-accelerated Base64 encoding and decoding.
- -XX:UseAVX=2 disables AVX-512. Apply this flag only on x86-64 hosts. OpenJDK on ARM does not recognize it and will fail to start.
Both flags require a restart and may reduce performance for workloads that decode large amounts of Base64. They buy time while you patch. They do not replace the update.
Protect your infrastructure while you patch
Patching every Java runtime takes time, especially when JDKs are bundled inside applications and container images. Cloudflare WAF can reduce your exposure while you patch. A new managed rule, available on paid plans and enabled in Log mode by default, detects the malformed Base64 input that triggers Java4Shell. For Business and Enterprise customers, WAF attack score adds a machine learning layer that scores each request for remote code execution payloads, which helps catch variations and bypass attempts that signature-based rules can miss.
New managed rules
Protection for paid plans has been released as part of the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset (Ruleset ID efb7b8c949ac4650a09736fc376e9aee). The rule is enabled by default with the Log action, because blocking by default could cause false positives on legitimate Base64 traffic. To review its matches, go to Security > Security Analytics > Events and filter by the rule ID. If the matches are not legitimate traffic, change the rule action to Block: go to Security > Settings, edit the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset, search for CVE-2026-114938 and set the rule action to Block. Alternatively, you can follow the link to review your configuration on the Zero Wire briefing.
| Rule description | Rule ID | 
| Java4Shell - Malformed Base64 Header - CVE-2026-114938 | 5de9b20a45ea45d3841919ab4d718bf4 | 
| Java4Shell - Malformed Base64 Query Value - CVE-2026-114938 | 46bb4172813e471ea62d31c02337b51d | 
| Java4Shell - Malformed Base64 Body Value - CVE-2026-114938 | d4dc3f71f1bc44a0811ae570e5e5836c | 
| Java4Shell - Malformed Base64 Path Segment - CVE-2026-114938 | 0dceaf0684b54fd0b085fcfb6fd6f152 | 
| Java4Shell - Malformed Base64url JWT Component - CVE-2026-114938 | 0ddd0eb664a040779f2f19065a25d991 | 
| Java4Shell - Malformed Base64 WebAuthn Value - CVE-2026-114938 | 4fce1ea79a614c07a27348d167d74ebb | 
We are working on a rule for the Cloudflare Free Managed Ruleset and will update this post when it is available.
A WAF can block the exploit when the malformed Base64 arrives in an HTTP request that passes through Cloudflare. It cannot block every path to the vulnerable decoder, including:
- Encoded or nested data. The Base64 value may be wrapped inside another encoding or compressed format that the application unpacks before decoding.
- Non-HTTP protocols. Some affected products, such as the Apache Kafka broker, accept traffic over their own protocols.
- Outbound connections. Calif also shared a client-side exploit: a Java program that opens a TLS connection to a malicious server can be compromised, even if it exposes no service of its own.
- Traffic that bypasses Cloudflare. This includes internal traffic between services.
Adding defense-in-depth with WAF attack score
While the managed rule is the primary way to block malformed Base64 triggers at the edge, Cloudflare WAF Attack Score (and specifically its remote code execution sub-score cf.waf.score.rce available on Enterprise plans) can offer an additional, complementary layer of protection.
Because CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell) is a binary heap-corruption vulnerability, an attacker rarely achieves full, reliable remote code execution with a single 65-byte (or 129-byte) trigger string alone. On the wire, that initial trigger looks like an opaque, malformed Base64 string containing heap-corruption bytes rather than traditional web-layer injection syntax. As a result, machine learning models trained on application-layer injection patterns will not flag the raw Base64 trigger in isolation.
Instead, turning a bounded JVM heap overflow into remote code execution over HTTP almost always requires a multi-stage or multi-parameter exploit chain, which creates more fingerprints that WAF Attack Score can inspect and flag, including:
- Heap Grooming and Triggering: To corrupt a predictable adjacent object on the JVM heap (such as a String or byte[] length header), attackers often send repetitive parameters or headers alongside the malformed Base64 payload to shape memory layout before triggering the out-of-bounds write.
- Second-Stage Payloads: Once heap corruption gives the attacker control over execution flow or object references, the exploit still needs commands, scripts, or Java gadgets to run. If an exploit chain pairs the initial heap-corruption trigger with a second-stage payload such as shell execution primitives (/bin/sh -c, cmd.exe, reverse-shell strings) or Java class-loading gadgets (java.lang.Runtime, ProcessBuilder, serialized object streams) tucked into another header, query parameter, or request body, cf.waf.score.rce can detect and score that secondary payload as malicious.
- Post-Exploitation Activity: Even if an initial heap-read or corruption request slips past edge filters, subsequent HTTP requests attempting to interact with an in-memory webshell or pass OS commands to the compromised JVM remain directly visible to WAF Attack Score.
Deploy protections and patch
Because sophisticated in-memory exploits can still execute raw shellcode or manipulate bytecode without ever sending plaintext shell commands over HTTP, WAF Attack Score should be used alongside explicit Base64 rules and JVM patching.
You can find more information on how to deploy Managed rules and attack score in our WAF guide, but in a nutshell:
1. Set the CVE-2026-114938 rule in the Cloudflare Managed Ruleset (Pro plan and above) to Block. It is enabled in Log mode by default, so review its matches in Security Events first. Use the links on the Cloudflare Zero Wire page to review your rules status.
2. Layer Attack Score to get ML-based remote code execution (RCE) detection: create a custom rule blocking or challenging requests with a low RCE attack score (for example, cf.waf.score.rce le 20 on Enterprise plans, or cf.waf.score.class eq "attack" on Business plans) to catch multi-stage exploit chains and post-exploitation command traffic.
3. Remediate at runtime: Upgrade to patched OpenJDK builds (or set -XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics as a temporary workaround) to eliminate the vulnerable AVX-512 code path entirely. Follow the OpenJDK advisory and Oracle's Critical Patch Update and install your Java vendor's fixed release as soon as possible. For a prompt you can give an AI agent to inventory your Java runtimes, see the Java4Shell page on Cloudflare Zero Wire.
Impact on Cloudflare infrastructure
Cloudflare also runs Java, so when Java4Shell was disclosed we checked our own systems. The vulnerability can only be triggered in specific hardware configurations, namely a x86-64 processor that supports AVX-512 VBMI, so a system is exposed only when both are true. Our investigation found that the majority of our Java workloads are not scheduled on vulnerable systems; we took immediate action to protect the remainder.
About an hour after the patches were published, we began rolling out a JVM startup option that turns off the accelerated Base64 routine containing the bug on all Java workloads, so decoding falls back to the standard implementation. To be safe, we are rolling out our patched configuration to all machines, regardless of hardware as a precaution. We have seen no indication so far that Java4Shell was exploited on Cloudflare infrastructure.
Update every Java runtime now
Java4Shell turns a performance optimization in the Java runtime into a path to remote code execution, and with technical details now public, we expect exploit attempts to follow quickly. The fix is to update every Java runtime and restart the services that use it. While you patch, review the new managed rule's matches and switch it to Block if you are on a paid plan and use attack score to catch remote code execution payloads that signatures may miss.
Our WAF analysts will continue to update protections as new techniques emerge. Follow the WAF changelog for rule updates and the Java4Shell page on Cloudflare Zero Wire for the latest on this vulnerability.

articles.title: Linux Foundation Newsletter: November 2026
articles.text:
Linux Foundation Newsletter: November 2026
The Linux Foundation | 18 November 2026
Welcome to the November 2026 edition of the Linux Foundation Newsletter!
LF Education’s Black Friday sale runs November 27 through December 4, with savings of up to 65% on training and certifications. Also new is the Certified Kubernetes Network Engineer (CKNE) certification and its Certification Pathway, and you can sign up to be notified when registration opens for the Secure AI Associate (SAIA) exam.
This month’s biggest announcements include a new open source project for AI agent identity and a milestone for the Agentic AI Foundation. The Linux Foundation welcomed Agent Name Service (ANS), which builds on DNS to verify and discover AI agents. AAIF added four projects (Agent Skills, Open Responses, OpenEnv, and OpenSandbox), bringing it to 10 hosted projects, and passed 300 members in its first year. The CNCF now hosts 231 projects, with KubeVirt and NATS graduating this month.
LF Research published four reports. The 2026 State of Open Source in Financial Services found a 63% year-over-year increase in GitHub commits from financial institutions. The AI impact on cybersecurity report found that 3 in 5 teams ship code faster than security reviews can keep up. A third finds that the future depends on VMs and containers running together, and the fourth, State of Commercial Open Source 2026, draws on 225 founders and leaders. LF Research and CNCF are also fielding a 3-minute survey on neocloud adoption.
You’ll also find a recap of the industry challenge LF Europe co-led at the World Open Innovation Conference in Kaunas, Lithuania, plus project news that ranges from agentic AI to telecom and embedded systems.
>> Read on for even more news, research, and opportunities from across the Linux Foundation.
Contents
Education Opportunities
Black Friday Deals Are Coming: Save Up to 65%!
Mark your calendars! From November 27 through December 4, save up to 65% on Linux Foundation Education training, certifications, and more. Whether you're building new skills or taking the next step in your career, you won't want to miss these deals!
New Certifications. More Ways to Grow. Take your skills further with the new Certified Kubernetes Network Engineer (CKNE) certification and Certification Pathway. Explore how the CARE Program makes it easier to keep your credentials current as you advance your skills. Plus, get ready for the upcoming Secure AI Associate (SAIA) certification exam. Sign up to be notified when registration opens!
LF Event Highlight
The full schedule is LIVE for Open Source Summit Japan, Automotive Linux Summit, and Embedded Linux Conference, happening December 7–9 in Tokyo!
One registration gives you access to all three events, featuring the latest in open source, automotive innovation, and embedded systems.
🎉 For the first time, Embedded Linux Conference is coming to Japan! Explore sessions on embedded Linux, real-time systems, kernel development, and more.
👉 Register by November 23 + SAVE!
LF Research: 4 new reports, and a new survey on Neoclouds!
Are you involved in your organization’s cloud infrastructure decisions?
As AI workloads drive demand for GPU capacity and specialized AI-native providers enter the market, LF Research and CNCF are fielding a 3-minute survey to capture how organizations actually run production workloads today and the extent to which neoclouds are being adopted.
We would love to hear from you! Your feedback will inform open source cloud tooling priorities and community benchmarks that help the ecosystem navigate modern infrastructure strategies more effectively.
How is finance balancing rapid AI adoption with enterprise risk? Produced by FINOS and LF Research in partnership with GitHub, Scott Logic, and sponsor BrightQuery, the annual survey-based 2026 State of Open Source in Financial Services Report delivers definitive data on industry adoption and risk management in the era of modern AI.
While AI coding tools boost security development speed by 17%, false positives from scanning tools increase workloads by 30%. Critically, 3 in 5 teams now ship code faster than security reviews can keep up, and 82% of practitioners warn that overreliance on AI tools is weakening developers’ security skills.
Yet, preparedness is possible! Download the report, produced in partnership with OpenSSF, ActiveState, and LF AI & Data for actionable recommendations on building dedicated governance, strengthening supply chain safeguards, and balancing AI speed with human oversight.
Virtual machines are anchoring modern enterprise infrastructure and the rise of agentic AI. The latest research from the Linux Foundation, in partnership with Broadcom and CNCF, reveals how practitioners are experiencing the evolution of VMs and production workloads. The future is shaping up to depend on both VMs and containers, secured and managed together. Download the report for strategic guidance on balancing isolation, utilization, and modern cloud native architectures.
Commercial open source companies are proving that community trust and developer adoption can successfully translate into durable enterprise revenue. The State of Commercial Open Source 2026, produced by LF Research and Serena Capital with sponsors AWS, CNCF, Futurewei, LF AI & Data, and Red Hat, delivers ground-up operational benchmarks and strategies from 225 founders and leaders. Download the report for strategic guidance on feature gating, enterprise sales, and sustainable scaling.
LF Europe: Community Updates
At the World Open Innovation Conference in Kaunas, Lithuania, LF Europe’s Mirko Boehm joined LF Research’s Anna Hermansen to lead an industry challenge on how open source must evolve as we work to create and sustain open ecosystems for hardware, data, and AI models, and how we can apply open innovation principles to support these more complex systems.
Linux Foundation Projects: Featured news
Formations
- The Linux Foundation welcomed Agent Name Service (ANS) as a new open source project, advancing trusted identity, verification, and discovery for AI agents across the internet. Built on existing DNS infrastructure, ANS provides an open standard for securely identifying and authenticating AI agents, enabling greater interoperability across platforms and services. Read the announcement >>
Academy Software Foundation (ASWF)
- 2026 Virtual Town Halls: Watch On Demand – Recordings from all 11 project town halls are live, including ACES, OpenColorIO, OpenEXR, MaterialX, OpenTimelineIO, and the USD Working Group. Each covers the year’s releases, production use cases, roadmap and what’s next. Watch the recordings
- Call for Papers: Open Source Forum 2027 – Our annual Open Source Forum returns to Los Angeles on February 18, 2027, for 100+ business and technical leaders, with the theme “New Technologies Impacting Studios.” The call for talks closes December 6 at 11:59 PM PT. We welcome talks on AI and machine learning, virtual production, pipeline tools, computer graphics, and immersive films. Submit your talk
- USD Collective Projects Initiative Launches – The USD Working Group, with over 1,000 contributors, has launched an open source test bed for standardizing how assets are defined in production pipelines. Its first project, built by volunteers across different DCCs, already exposed differences in how tools handle USD, including two renderers lighting the same scene differently. Read the blog
- Open Source Days 2026: 500+ attendees in Los Angeles, plus new members CIQ, Evercast, and RIT. Watch the recap and recordings
Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF)
- Four new projects join AAIF: Agent Skills, Open Responses, OpenEnv, and OpenSandbox bring AAIF to 10 hosted projects, expanding open collaboration on agent capabilities, model interoperability, training, and execution. Read the announcement.
- AAIF surpasses 300 members in its first year: New Gold Members include Ant Group, Gates Foundation, MongoDB, Nutanix, Royal Bank of Canada, Vercel, and Vultr, broadening participation in open standards for agentic AI. Meet the new members.
- Speak at AGNTCon + MCPCon North America 2027: Share practical lessons on building, evaluating, and securing AI agents in San Francisco on April 28 and 29. The call for proposals closes January 18, 2027. Submit a proposal.
- How can agents find the right tools at scale? AAIF Ambassador Gnanaguru Sattanathan explains dynamic tool retrieval, including how to evaluate accuracy, costs, and performance when agents need access to thousands of tools. Read the blog.
- Young builders put open source AI to work: At the free AGNTCon Kids Day in San Jose, participants ages 9 to 18 used goose to create games and program robots to sing, dance, and move obstacles. Read the recap.
Alliance for OpenUSD (AOUSD)
- The annual AOUSD Member Summit took place on October 28th in San Francisco at the Autodesk Gallery. Industry leaders and experts held strategic discussions, updates, and sessions focused on expanding open 3D standards made possible by Universal Scene Description (OpenUSD). This was a hybrid, free event open to AOUSD Steering and General Members and Contributors.
- AOUSD Core Specification 1.1.1 has been submitted for approval and publication as an ISO standard, the first step to international standardization.
- OpenUSD v26.11 is taking shape around clearer asset authorship, more compact mesh delivery, and faster work with complex scenes. The release adds Polygonal Mesh Coding, a schema for recording how content was created, and more expressive handling of time intervals and variable defaults.
Alpha-Omega
- Dedicated security expertise in action: Alpha-Omega funding supported PHP Foundation Security Engineer in Residence (SEiR) Volker Dusch in coordinating researchers, maintainers, and distributors during the PHP2Shell response, helping PHP’s engineers focus on developing fixes. Read the case study.
- Strengthening PHP package security: Alpha-Omega funding is enabling the team at Packagist Conductors to develop immutable artifacts, cryptographic signatures, build provenance attestations, and Trusted Publishing for Packagist and Composer. Explore the planned improvements.
- Are your dependencies coming back to life? “Weekend at Bernie’s II” finds 421 previously inactive critical repositories active again, with AI-assisted development playing a role in many revivals. But activity alone does not resolve security backlogs. Explore the findings.
- Your first security advisory, explained: Node.js Security Engineer in Residence Ulises Gascon shares a practical guide to handling GitHub Security Advisories, helping maintainers navigate triage, fixes, and publication. Read the guide’s introduction.
App Defense Alliance
- Data Trust Registry accepts App Defense Alliance certifications
The Data Transfer Initiative’s Data Trust Registry now accepts App Defense Alliance certifications covering both CASA and Cloud App and Config as evidence of an independent security assessment for Trust Level 2 applications.
See the requirements →
- Updated Certification Scheme Documents take effect December 1
Version 1.3 of the Alliance’s Certification Scheme Documents is now available. The documents set out how applications are assessed and certified. Version 1.2 remains in effect through November 30. Starting December 1, version 1.3 applies to all new assessments and any still underway.
Review the updated documents →
Automotive Grade Linux (AGL)
- Automotive Grade Linux Releases Vibrant Vimba v22.0.0
The project has released its latest stable distribution, updating the foundation to Yocto Project Wrynose 6.0.2 alongside Flutter 3.38.3 and Qt 6.12.0-beta3. This version introduces a dedicated Xen virtualization layer, container support, and downloadable SPDX Software Bills of Materials. Automotive software developers and embedded platform engineers can leverage these pre-built images and updated graphical frameworks to build secure, modular software-defined vehicle architectures.
Read the announcement →
CAMARA
- CAMARA at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America: CAMARA joined the cloud native community in Salt Lake City, November 9–12, connecting with developers and industry partners at Booth 321. Conversations focused on making telecom network capabilities easier to access through standardized, interoperable APIs, and bringing network intelligence into modern applications.
Explore the event >>
- Open Gateway and CAMARA Launch in Portugal: Portugal's MEO, NOS, and Vodafone announced their participation in GSMA Open Gateway on October 20, supported by Nokia. The initiative brings CAMARA-standardized APIs to the Portuguese market, initially focusing on SIM Swap and Number Verification to help businesses strengthen authentication and fraud prevention without separate integrations for each operator. Read the coverage >>
- CAMARA APIs Take Part in the Live Media Conversation at MWC Doha: At MWC Doha on November 8, GSMA Fusion brought together broadcasters, operators, and technology partners to explore how CAMARA Quality on Demand (QoD) APIs can support reliable connectivity for live production, remote broadcasting, and streaming. The discussion highlighted the role of programmable networks in handling demanding media workflows. Explore the session >>
- CAMARA-Based APIs Deliver Measurable Results: Orange Developer highlighted production use cases demonstrating the impact of CAMARA-aligned network APIs. A European digital lender reported a 70% reduction in false-broker fraud using KYC Match and SIM Swap, while Indonesia's BRI Bank reported a 20% improvement in successful authentications compared with SMS OTP. The results demonstrate how standardized network capabilities are being applied to real customer challenges. Read the case studies >>
- Exploring Network APIs for Connected Media Production: The 5G Media and Entertainment Association (5G-MAG) shared development progress on network API integrations on November 4. Work includes Dedicated Networks API tooling and initial testing of a Quality on Demand API consumer using Telefónica's sandbox, exploring how standardized interfaces can support connectivity-sensitive media applications. Explore the development work >>
- CAMARA at ONE Summit Japan 2026: Can network APIs become the context layer for agentic AI? Join Jill Lovato (Linux Foundation), Farnaz Salehi (Rakuten Mobile), Markus Kümmerle (CAMARA), and Toshiyasu Wakayama (KDDI Corporation) at ONE Summit Japan for a panel exploring how standardized network APIs can provide trusted, real-time context for AI agents. Register now: Explore the sessions and register >> 
CHIPS Alliance
- CHIPS Alliance projects Caliptra and VeeR were featured in sessions at the 2026 OCP Global Summit, held October 12–15 in San Jose, California. Topics included silicon roots of trust, device identity, secure key distribution, design verification, streaming boot, manageability, certificate refresh, and package-granular attestation. Speakers included representatives from CHIPS Alliance members AMD, Google, Intel, Marvell, Microsoft, and NVIDIA. Watch the session recordings.
Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)
- New co-located for KubeCon EU 2027: NeoCloudCon (CFP Open)
- CNCF Hits Major Milestones with Global Community Growth, Record Industry Investment and a New Generation of Projects to Build AI Systems in Production | New Sandbox projects, including Agent Substrate and OpenShell, expand CNCF’s portfolio to 231 projects as the community adds over 5.5 million cloud native developers in 12 months, welcomes eight Platinum members and brings together 82,000 attendees at events worldwide.
- Welcoming OpenShell to the CNCF: Open Governance to Secure Agentic AI | NVIDIA has contributed OpenShell, an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous AI agents, to the foundation’s community-led home.
- Cloud Native Computing Foundation Announces KubeVirt Graduation | KubeVirt has graduated from CNCF while celebrating 10 years of development, growing to more than 2,000 contributors across 520 organizations, with production adopters including ByteDance, Cloudflare, CoreWeave and NVIDIA.
- CNCF Announces NATS Graduation, Solidifying a Production-Ready Foundation for Messaging Across Cloud and Edge | NATS has graduated from CNCF with more than 2,000 companies across industries including retail, financial services, and telecommunications using the project to simplify distributed infrastructure and support scalable applications.
- CloudNativePG becomes a CNCF Incubating Project | The CNCF Technical Oversight Committee (TOC) voted to accept CloudNativePG as a CNCF incubating project.
- Open Cluster Management (OCM) becomes a CNCF Incubating Project | The CNCF Technical Oversight Committee (TOC) voted to accept Open Cluster Management as a CNCF incubating project.
- Donating KubeRay to CNCF | KubeRay is joining the CNCF, bringing the entire PARK stack under Linux Foundation governance and giving teams full confidence in its neutrality and openness.
- CNCF Launches Certified Kubernetes Network Engineer Certification (CKNE) to Advance Production-Ready Networking Skills for AI Era | The Certified Kubernetes Network Engineer (CKNE) joins CNCF’s certification portfolio, validating hands-on expertise in designing, securing, and troubleshooting networking across production Kubernetes environments.
- CNCF Recognizes Cloud Native Champions in 2026 Community Awards | CNCF recognized 11 contributors across four Community Awards at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City, with winners honored at the November 12 ceremony.
- Meta Wins CNCF End User Case Study Contest for Accelerating AI Infrastructure Deployments From Hours to Minutes | Meta’s Cloud Foundation team won the CNCF End User Case Study Contest for its GitOps platform, built with Argo CD and Kargo to streamline Kubernetes application delivery; the new platform cuts routine application deployment times from more than four hours to minutes.
- CNCF Welcomes Adyen as Platinum End User Member to Advance Open Source Financial Infrastructure | Operating over 100 Kubernetes clusters with Cilium, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry, Adyen joins the CNCF as a Platinum End User Member, bringing production-scale operational expertise to the open source community.
- CNCF Welcomes CoreWeave as a Platinum Member to Further Open Source AI Infrastructure | CoreWeave, a participant in the Certified Kubernetes AI Conformance Program and a contributor to Kubernetes, Kueue, and llm-d, has upgraded its CNCF membership to Platinum, deepening its ongoing engagement in the open source cloud native ecosystem.
- CNCF Welcomes HAProxy Technologies as a Platinum Member to Advance Open Source Kubernetes Networking | HAProxy Technologies has upgraded to a CNCF Platinum membership, deepening almost a decade of involvement with the foundation.
- CNCF Welcomes Vultr as a Platinum Member to Advance Open and Sovereign Cloud Infrastructure for AI | Vultr has upgraded to a CNCF Platinum membership, expanding its role in shaping open interoperability for AI infrastructure.
- CNCF Welcomes Qualcomm Upgrade to Gold Membership to Advance AI Infrastructure Across the Edge-to-Cloud Continuum | Qualcomm has upgraded to a CNCF Gold membership, expanding its role in shaping open source infrastructure for AI inference from the edge to the cloud.
- CNCF and SlashData Report Finds Cloud Native Developers Are More AI-Ready, Global Population Surpasses 21 Million | CNCF and SlashData released the State of Cloud Native Development Q3 2026 report, noting that the global cloud native developer population reached an estimated 21.2 million, representing approximately 41% of developers worldwide.
- CNCF and SlashData Report Finds Platform Engineering Strategies Are Shaping AI Infrastructure Adoption | CNCF and SlashData released the Q3 2026 CNCF Technology Radar report finding 54% of developers with independently managed tooling use hybrid approaches for AI workflows, compared to just 5% at organizations building custom internal platforms.
- CNCF Welcomes Twelve New Members as Organizations Look to Run AI Agents on Open, Sovereign Infrastructure | CNCF welcomes 12 new Silver members, expanding its community across sovereign cloud, AI agent infrastructure, security and financial services.
Confidential Computing Consortium (CCC)
- Agentic AI White Paper: CCC’s Technical Advisory Council has finalized a white paper on confidential computing for AI agents. It makes the case that attested execution gives agents a verifiable identity and lets them generate and protect their own keys, keeping their knowledge isolated from the cloud provider and control plane. A follow-on reference architecture paper is planned. Read more in CCC’s latest newsletter.

articles.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability Puts Enterprise Applications at Risk of Takeover
articles.text:
Oracle and the OpenJDK project have patched Java4Shell, a critical Java runtime vulnerability that researchers say can be exploited to hijack popular enterprise applications without authentication.
The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-114938, is a memory safety flaw in the way OpenJDK processes Base64-encoded data. Calif, whose researcher Quang Luong discovered the bug, made its findings public on November 17, after news of the flaw surfaced ahead of the coordinated disclosure.
Specifically, the bug was found in a routine that OpenJDK relies on to decode Base64 on x86-64 CPUs supporting AVX-512 VBMI. Calif’s analysis shows that invalid Base64 strings can cause the routine to write past the end of its output buffer, potentially corrupting nearby heap data before Java flags the input as invalid.
“With careful exploitation, the corruption can reveal sensitive memory, as Heartbleed did, or lead to remote code execution,” Calif explained.
The researchers call the memory leak capability JavaBleed. They warn that heap data exposed this way could contain PII, secret keys and tokens.
Default configurations exposed to Java4Shell attacks
In its initial tests, Calif achieved pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) on Keycloak, Atlassian Jira and Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, all running with default settings. Authenticated attackers could also execute code on Apache Kafka Broker, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit and Spinnaker, and the researchers say neither list is exhaustive.
Code execution was also achieved against sample apps based on Apache Struts and Spring Boot. Calif warns that the decoder can be reached through everyday functionality, including authentication and file uploads.
Client-side attacks are possible too. Based on an exploit shared with Calif by security researcher samczsun, a Java application can be compromised when it connects to an attacker-controlled server over TLS, even if it does not run any services.
“One thing to note about this vulnerability is that there is no universal exploit. Depending on how Base64 is used and how the application works, different steps may be required for exploitation,” Calif noted.
VulnCheck says crashing a vulnerable JVM is easy once an attacker finds a reachable entry point that relies on the affected decoding logic. In its tests, a quick series of crafted requests reliably took down the service.
The security firm says it has developed a full RCE exploit as well, but noted that achieving RCE is much harder, as the attacker must manipulate the heap layout and find a way (specific to each target) to leak addresses and bypass ASLR.
“In other words, we don’t anticipate that CVE-2026-114938 will be easily or widely exploitable, but as with PHP2Shell, adversaries are likely to find narrow but functional paths to RCE in specific applications,” VulnCheck said.
The proof-of-concept (PoC) code published by Calif demonstrates the memory corruption but does not achieve code execution. “The weaponized chains for individual products stay private until everyone has had a chance to upgrade. We will publish them later,” the company noted.
According to Calif, AI played a key role in both discovering and exploiting the vulnerability.
“It took our own Quang Luong an hour to discover the vulnerability, and two more hours to develop the first working exploit. The total token cost was less than $200,” Calif said.
Affected versions and patches
According to Calif, OpenJDK versions starting with 17.0.6 are vulnerable, and so are the Java distributions based on it, including Amazon Corretto, Eclipse Temurin, Microsoft Build of OpenJDK, Azul Zulu, Red Hat OpenJDK and Oracle Java SE. The OpenJDK advisory lists Java 17, 21, 25 and 27 as affected by CVE-2026-114938.
Exploitation requires x86-64 hardware with AVX-512 VBMI support, such as Intel Xeon processors from the Ice Lake generation onward and AMD chips based on Zen 4 or newer architectures. Systems powered by ARM64 chips are not vulnerable.
Calif assigned the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2. Oracle’s advisory gives it a CVSS 3.1 score of 8.1 and lists it as remotely exploitable without authentication, but with high attack complexity.
Oracle released fixes in its November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update, which resolves 11 Java SE vulnerabilities.
Endor Labs pointed out that users of other Java distributions will need to wait for their vendors to roll out patched builds. It also noted that, as of November 17, the fix was not yet present in the public OpenJDK 17, 21 and 25 update repositories.
CISA has called for immediate patching, with internet-exposed systems at the top of the list. The agency also advises hunting for Java installations embedded in third-party software, containers and appliances, warning that these may not be listed separately in asset inventories.
Cisco Talos has yet to see the vulnerability exploited in the wild, but noted, “we anticipate probing attempts may pick up soon after public disclosure.”

articles.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now
articles.text:
New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC.
With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work.
Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops.
Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC.
A Windows PC Built for Local AI
As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks.
RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system.
Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks.
RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage.
This advanced hardware unlocks incredible capabilities for creators, developers and AI enthusiasts, including:
- Running massive 120-billion-parameter large language models locally
- Rendering 90GB+ 3D scenes in real time
- Smoothly editing 4:2:2 video in real time
New compact desktops are available for purchase from ASUS, Dell and MSI, joining the RTX Spark family of laptops available today. Mini PCs from Acer, GIGABYTE and HP are coming soon, along with the Microsoft Surface RTX Spark Dev Box.
From Local Agents to AI Creation
Native CUDA support and Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux give developers a foundation for building and running local AI workflows. Developers can set up agents with Hermes Agent or NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and fine-tune supported models using Unsloth.
RTX Spark can run creative agents that connect familiar applications and local AI tools, helping creators move from an idea to finished work with natural-language instructions.
NVIDIA Switchyard, now available in Hermes, automatically routes agent tasks between local and cloud models. Everyday tasks can run on device, while advanced reasoning draws on cloud models, helping manage cloud costs across creative workflows.
These capabilities come together in creative workflows that connect Photoshop and ComfyUI through Hermes Agent. Using natural-language instructions, creators can turn sketches into rendered images and animations, or animate an image entirely on device — from isolating a subject and defining its motion to generating the finished video.
NVIDIA brought these workflows to life at Adobe MAX, where attendees used natural-language instructions to turn sketches into rendered images and animations for a shared digital Miami landscape.
The RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR features, already available in ComfyUI, extend the pipeline: a generated clip can be expanded to 60 frames per second and converted to high dynamic range for color grading, all within a single ComfyUI workflow on RTX Spark.
Adobe Accelerates the Full Creative Stack for RTX Spark
NVIDIA and Adobe are expanding native Windows on Arm support and RTX acceleration across Adobe’s creative applications, helping video editors, photographers, designers and 3D artists work more efficiently on RTX Spark.
Adobe Premiere accelerates a range of AI-powered editing features through NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX, including Enhance Speech, Object Mask, Scene Edit Detection and Auto Reframe — so editors spend less time waiting and more time cutting.
GPU acceleration also extends to Film Impact transition and effects plug-ins. The update improves support for professional video formats, including Canon RAW, Red RAW, ARRI RAW, ARRICORE, ARRI HDE, H.264 and HEVC in MXF, ProRes RAW and long-GOP video. This lets editors realize more than 50% quicker turnaround on everyday H.264 video deliverables.
Adobe Photoshop adds TensorRT-RTX acceleration for the Remove Tool and ArmRTX Spark-native Camera Raw support, helping photographers remove unwanted objects faster and work with RAW images without relying on emulation. At Adobe MAX, Adobe previewed a next-generation image processing engine with extensive GPU acceleration, including interactive Gaussian blur and Light Leaks filters.
Adobe Substance 3D Painter 12.2 is now optimized for RTX Spark with native support on Arm for the first time in public beta. Artists in games, visual effects and visualization can run Substance Painter natively on RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops, with no compatibility layer required.
Adobe Illustrator and InDesign now offer native Windows on Arm versions optimized for RTX Spark. Adobe Illustrator delivers up to 30% higher performance than its emulated version, helping accelerate illustration, graphic design and page-layout workflows on RTX Spark.
Blender 5.3 Adds DLSS Ray Reconstruction to the Viewport
Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction into the Cycles viewport, helping artists evaluate lighting and materials with near-final-quality ray-traced previews as they work.
The practical difference is immediate: instead of navigating a noisy, resolving preview, Ray Reconstruction delivers near-final-quality lighting, reflections and materials in the interactive viewport in real time.
DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support requires Blender 5.3 and the latest NVIDIA Game Ready Driver or NVIDIA Studio Driver. Download the NVIDIA App to get automatic notifications when the latest drivers are available, optimize games and applications from a unified GPU control center, and discover the latest NVIDIA tools and software.
Windows Server 2028 Coming to DGX Station for Windows
Announced at Microsoft Ignite, Windows Server is evolving for organizations that need to run AI closer to their enterprise applications and data.
Microsoft is expanding hardware choice through support for the latest AI silicon, helping customers take advantage of accelerated inference and increasingly capable models in their own environments. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows platform powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip is expanding to include support for Windows Server 2028.
New accelerator platforms and the breadth of the Windows silicon ecosystem provide customers options at different capability levels and price points for advanced AI development, local inference, and agent workloads at scale.
Windows ML Updates Give Developers More Options
Also announced at Microsoft Ignite, developers can now bring any GGUF model from Hugging Face and run it within Windows ML using the llama.cpp backend.
The DxCGC backend, now available as an experimental release, is an integration for game developers that compiles and runs machine learning models through DirectX 12, allowing them to execute AI workloads alongside graphics.
Windows APIs let applications integrate platform-provided AI capabilities adding GPU support for AION Instruct and VSR.
Developers can also build high-performance AI models for Windows ML using the command line interface.
#ICYMI: The Latest NVIDIA Local AI Updates
🦙 llama.cpp v1.0.0 marks a major milestone for building local AI apps. The open source inference engine introduces API versioning updates, alongside expanded model support and CUDA optimizations for NVFP4 inference. Learn more.
🎉 Ricursive Intelligence introduced its first open model: Ripple-65B Preview. The full-stack AI lab builds self-improving systems by co-optimizing hardware, software and models. Ripple-65B Preview was trained on NVIDIA B300 GPUs, refined using NVIDIA Nemotron post-training datasets and runs locally on DGX Spark. Download the NVFP4 checkpoint from Hugging Face.
🤖 Runway’s Praxis-1 is a newly released 27-billion-parameter world action model that predicts video and actions together. Developers can run it locally on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, DGX Spark and DGX Station, and adapt it to their own robots, cameras and tasks with LoRA fine-tuning. Download the NVFP4 checkpoint from Hugging Face.
🛠️ NVIDIA TensorRT Edge-LLM helps run AI models locally on DGX Spark with just a few commands. Read the technical blog, which walks through downloading Nemotron-3.5 Lightning, setting up optimized inference, testing prompts and serving the model through a local OpenAI-compatible API.
Subscribe to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook.

articles.title: What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?
articles.text:
If the glorious AI revolution rests entirely on the well-being of one man, AI is perhaps not as robust a technology as I had previously been led to believe. Nonetheless, chunks of Silicon Valley are now insisting he is indispensable. For instance, if Elon Musk is telling the truth, then Jensen Huang (the former CEO of Nvidia, a company with a market cap of about $3 trillion) has been making deals that were “a handshake with Jensen” with suppliers — “not a written contract,” Musk wrote.
What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?
Collette Kress’ first earnings call gives us some clues.
What is Nvidia without AI’s sugar daddy in charge?
Collette Kress’ first earnings call gives us some clues.
Fascinating stuff to tell shareholders. But after listening to Nvidia’s first earnings call with its new CEO, Colette Kress, I do think something may have shifted. In her former role as CFO, Kress generally told Huang to stop spending so much money on financing its customers, because telling the CEO to stop spending so much goddamn money is the CFO’s job. Apparently he belittled her about this, but that’s the CEO–CFO relationship, baby! Anyway she’s the boss now, at least temporarily. I think it’s reasonable to assume that though Nvidia has for years been the AI industry’s sugar daddy, without Huang and his handshakes in the picture, it may be less liberal with its cash.
Kress shot down the idea that Huang’s departure would lead to a brain drain within Nvidia
Kress’ job was never going to be easy. Even without tantrums from the likes of Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Musk, both of whom seem to have a lot of free time for guys who are ostensibly running multibillion-dollar companies, having to steer a company after an event on the scale of Huang’s meltdown is a miserable task. But this woman also is now having to deal with a bunch of guys publicly insisting that Huang was the only reason Nvidia succeeded. It amused me on the call that she did the thing I often do when men decide they can bully me, which is to tap in another man who is theoretically or actually in charge of me — and so on the call, Nvidia board Chair Harvey C. Jones politely told these losers to get bent. The board does not intend to reinstate Huang, and the company won’t be taking questions about him.
On the call, Kress pointedly noted that Nvidia’s agreements with suppliers last through the end of the decade, so I suppose we must entertain the possibility that when it comes to the handshake deals, Musk is, once again, lying. This is an important thing, though — as SemiAnalysis noted in its bizarrely conspiratorial post on the situation, Nvidia is successful because it has choked off the supply chain.
Do you have information about Nvidia? Contact Elizabeth Lopatto securely on Signal at lopatto.46
Kress also shot down the idea that Huang’s departure would lead to a brain drain within Nvidia, or the kind of open internal revolt that got Sam Altman reinstated at OpenAI during “the blip” in 2023. She told investors that “our employees, we believe, are committed. They are committed to doing their life’s work at Nvidia.” Nvidia’s employees have “been working seamlessly on what they need to complete,” she added. “From a business perspective, it’s business as usual.” I’m sure we’ll hear more about this in the coming days, but unlike with Altman, Huang resigned, and we all know why. And while some employees support reinstating Huang, I notice that there’s a real dearth of “we’ll quit with him” in those sentiments.
I don’t think this is going to shut the Branch Nvidians up, but I do think the board doesn’t have another choice here. Hilariously, we learned this weekend that Nvidia did not buy complete directors’ and officers’ insurance. While the individual executives’ and board members’ personal assets are shielded from lawsuits that stem from its executives’ behavior, the company is not. So if someone, or perhaps several someones, were to file a suit because of, say, Huang’s personal life and its damaging effects on the stock price, Nvidia itself is on the hook.
The scandal isn’t mainly about the affairs, as much fun as we all have been having with them
This is to say nothing of the Securities and Exchange Commission’s investigation — which, given how cliqued up Huang was with President Donald Trump, may be investigating on his behalf rather than investigating him — or the California attorney general going on Bloomberg TV to say that he was going to start kicking the tires on an investigation, or Huang and general counsel Tim Teter’s upcoming congressional testimony. The three actual lawyers left at the Department of Justice may be doing their own investigation, too. Elizabeth Warren seems mad. Marco Rubio’s name has been publicly attached in stories on the leaks, which makes me a little suspicious about who’s been doing the leaking.
A reminder: The scandal isn’t mainly about the affairs, as much fun as we all have been having with them. It is about Nvidia customers allegedly circumventing a ban on selling chips to China. The scandal is already big enough that US policy has been altered; the Department of Commerce informed us all on November 16th that there were new restrictions on selling chips to countries such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil. Also, data centers around the world need licenses from the US to lease compute to companies headquartered in China.
“No one could tell them ‘no’ or put them in their place.”
You may be wondering how these restrictions will affect Nvidia’s sales. The company also addressed this, though somewhat obliquely: It raised its forecast, saying that revenue will grow by 75 percent next year. Still, given that Singapore alone was responsible for $104 billion of revenue in 2025, I am curious about the number; at the time, it was the second-biggest geographic area by revenue, dwarfed only by the US. I can’t tell you how much Singaporean sales matter to Nvidia now, because around the time that Singaporean sales reportedly started to represent half the company’s revenue, Nvidia switched its reporting methodology. The company had previously noted that “most shipments associated with Singapore revenue were to locations other than Singapore and shipments to Singapore were insignificant.” Notably, Megaspeed had a Singapore address — and was the subject of a truncated Commerce Department investigation into whether its chips were being diverted to China. Fun stuff!
You know what else is fun? Jensen Huang’s children are still at the company, at least as far as anyone knows. His daughter Madison, described as Huang’s “chief of staff” by The New York Times, even helped direct Nvidia’s response to inquiries about Megaspeed, which have been mounting now for a year, the Financial Times reported. Her husband, Nico Caprez, “was promoted to a role that covered international deals with cloud computing clients in Asia” around the time those inquiries were getting started. “They had a lot of power and influence and were allowed to operate unchecked,” an anonymous source told the FT. “No one could tell them ‘no’ or put them in their place.”
His kids — one of them, Spencer, ran a bar before his role at Nvidia — likely haven’t endeared themselves to their colleagues, based on some of the reporting now trickling out about them. What was Spencer doing at Nvidia? Unknown. “Some executives said they had never encountered Spencer Huang in the course of business,” The Wall Street Journal wrote.
As a person who loves mess, I think the Branch Nvidians should keep this shit coming
Employing the CEO’s relatives was already a governance risk. If the outside agitation continues to reinstate Jensen Huang, there are three key lambs that Nvidia can slaughter, and all of them are his relatives. I suppose the thing I find most astonishing is that Huang doesn’t see the writing on the wall; he has posted that if “the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” The post was met with, among other things, Altman posting a green heart in response.
Now, as a person who loves mess, I think the Branch Nvidians should keep this shit coming. I mean, Huang can nominate two people to the board of directors before the company’s shareholder meeting next year. Let’s have a stupid proxy fight and see what else leaks about Huang’s leadership and children! Of course, that will be difficult for Kress to manage — but that’s I guess what she’s getting paid for.
Up until now, Kress had been trying to rein in Huang’s spending on the AI ecosystem — financing, investments, and so on — in a huge swath of companies, according to stories in The Information and The Wall Street Journal. According to the Journal’s story, Huang noted that the vaunted deals he’d made with suppliers “were coming at him like an ‘avalanche,’” while “major cloud providers were running away from Nvidia.” This does explain Nvidia’s role as the sugar daddy for the neocloud industry. Kress reportedly pushed back on some of its agreements, apparently significantly downsizing a financial commitment to OpenAI among other things. Now, while she’ll be spending plenty of her time managing the fallout from Huang’s departure, she won’t be directly fighting with him over Nvidia’s finances.
It publicly tells us there are limitations on what Nvidia is willing to support
On the earnings call, analyst Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein Research asked about a new paragraph he’d noticed in the earnings release about neoclouds. Nvidia had been supplying guarantees to some neoclouds by saying it would purchase compute if no one else would. The new paragraph reads, in part, “Our commitments take effect only if the neoclouds secure financing to purchase the data center infrastructure products and the related compute capacity is deployed, made operational, and accepted by us.” Kress clarified that this meant that if neoclouds’ buildout was delayed — or they otherwise had a challenge in building the warehouse to stick the chips in — Nvidia’s guarantee “doesn’t exist anymore,” she said. “Is it new? No. Did we change anything? No,” she said.
I have no way of knowing if this language had been ready to go in the press release before Huang resigned, but it does seem notable all the same. It publicly tells us there are limitations on what Nvidia is willing to support. And knowing Kress wanted Huang to spend less on this stuff, I think it tees us up for an interesting period. Passing under the radar last week were some indications that the Federal Reserve may be about to do an interest rate hike, which is trouble for a number of companies, such as CoreWeave, that rely on debt for their data center buildouts. If we are entering a period where financing is more expensive or more difficult to get, we may see some neoclouds falter. The new paragraph in the earnings release suggests that Nvidia wants us all to know that it’s not going to bail them out forever. Bring Huang back if you want, I guess, but even he can’t control the Fed — or the increasingly odd outlook for data center financing. In the coming months, Nvidia may be better off with a woman who wants to keep the costs down.
You know who is getting money under Kress, though? Nvidia staff. They can expect raises and equity in December.

articles.title: Jusqu'à 30 gigaoctets par heure : le bug silencieux des pilotes Nvidia GeForce qui fatigue votre SSD — Frandroid
articles.text:
Il y a quelques jours, AMD a reconnu que ses pilotes Radeon écrivaient sans arrêt sur le SSD, même quand le PC ne fait rien, puis a publié un correctif dans la foulée. Les possesseurs de cartes graphiques GeForce ne sont visiblement pas à l’abri : dans un article publié ce mercredi 18 novembre, le site américain Wccftech rassemble des témoignages d’utilisateurs dont les pilotes
Nvidia écrivent eux aussi en continu sur le disque système, et dit avoir reproduit le problème sur l’une de ses machines. Ça compte, parce qu’un SSD ne supporte qu’un volume limité d’écritures sur sa durée de vie : chaque gigaoctet écrit pour rien l’use un peu plus.
Un vieux bug que les derniers pilotes aggravent
En cause, NVDisplay.Container.exe, un processus qui tourne en arrière-plan pour le service NVIDIA Display Container LS, dont le panneau de configuration Nvidia et l’application NVIDIA App ont besoin pour fonctionner. D’après les rapports d’utilisateurs, ce processus réécrit en boucle un fichier de journal, nvlog.nvlgstg, rangé dans C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\, au lieu d’y ajouter simplement de nouvelles lignes. 
Sur le forum officiel de Nvidia, un utilisateur a mesuré environ 515 mégaoctets écrits en cinq minutes au repos avec le pilote 621.14, sorti le 4 novembre, contre moins de 2 mégaoctets avec le pilote précédent, le 621.01. Un autre a relevé plus de 3 gigaoctets en dix minutes, et un troisième, passé au pilote 621.24, parle d’environ 30 gigaoctets par heure, soit 720 gigaoctets par jour sur un PC allumé en continu.
Le problème n’a rien de neuf. Comme le rapporte Wccftech, en janvier 2025, un message sur le forum d’entraide de Dell signalait déjà ce fichier réécrit en boucle, et des plaintes visant le système de journal de Nvidia remontent à 2021. Sur Reddit, certains utilisateurs ont stoppé les écritures en coupant Highlights ou ShadowPlay, les outils d’enregistrement de parties de Nvidia. D’autres, en revanche, voient le phénomène continuer avec l’overlay Nvidia (l’interface qui s’affiche par-dessus les jeux) entièrement désactivé, et plusieurs ne constatent rien d’anormal sur leur machine. Nvidia n’a pas reconnu le bug publiquement, et les notes de version du pilote 621.24, publié le 12 novembre, ne le citent pas parmi les problèmes connus.
Comment vérifier si votre PC est concerné
Avant de changer de pilote, regardez ce qui se passe réellement sur votre disque :
- appuyez sur Windows + R, tapez resmon et validez pour ouvrir le moniteur de ressources ;
- ouvrez l’onglet Disque ;
- cherchez NVDisplay.Container.exe et vérifiez s’il écrit en continu dans le fichier nvlog.nvlgstg.
Si c’est le cas, des utilisateurs touchés disent avoir réglé le problème temporairement en arrêtant le service NVIDIA Display Container LS, en supprimant le fichier de journal, puis en relançant le service. Revenir au pilote 621.01 a aussi fonctionné chez certains. Évitez en revanche de désactiver le service pour de bon : sans lui, le panneau de configuration Nvidia et l’application NVIDIA App ne fonctionnent plus correctement.
